author: sageryza
body:
Sophie's portraits showed **twice** in a chat's Assets tab today — the labeled original plus the unlabeled `claude-deliveries/<random>` copy the hook files when the same image is also sent as a chat FILE. The tab could only join copies by **filename**, and that copy is named `<ms>-<random>`, so the twin could never merge however carefully anyone labeled things.

She asked for the **fail-safe**, not another cleanup pass. Duplicates stop being possible.

## What it does

**Filing time — `POST /api/gallery` records the content hash.** Cloud Storage already stores every object's md5 and hands it back in the object's **metadata**, so identifying a picture by its content costs one small metadata call and **no bytes are ever downloaded** (the technique `scripts/drop-dedupe.js` used to hash a 2,717-file library for nothing). Written on both filing paths — the full one and `assetsOnly`, which is what the hook's auto-filer calls — and on the converge patch, so an older record picks one up the next time it is touched.

**The bucket is resolved FROM THE URL.** The same picture can live in `deckfactory-43176` or `membry-df528` and a credential for one cannot read the other, so `asset-hash.js` parses the url (three real shapes: `storage.googleapis.com/<bucket>/…`, the tokened `firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/<bucket>/o/…`, and virtual-hosted) and hands the bucket name to the server, which owns the admin apps and picks the matching one — never whichever app happens to be initialised. A project-prefix fallback covers older `<id>.appspot.com` objects.

**Read time — `GET /api/gallery/assets` joins on three keys** (`asset-union.js`):

- **`md5`** — the Storage object's own md5. This is what kills the claude-deliveries twin.
- **`hash`** — the sha256 `POST /api/gallery` *already* computes when bytes arrive inline. A **different algorithm on purpose**, so it gets its own key namespace: md5 is free from Storage, sha256 is free from bytes in hand, and neither is worth paying a download to convert into the other. Comparing them in one field would have silently failed to group while looking like it worked.
- **the filename**, exactly as before, for every record carrying neither.

**The join is transitive — union-find over the page.** A can share an md5 with B while B shares a filename with C, and all three are one picture; a per-key pass would leave that chain as two tiles.

**Merge semantics are unchanged, declaration for declaration** — the url kept is the one Sophie's label/prompt is attached to, a curated `gpt-image-2 · medium` caption still beats `from <chat>`, every populated field survives whichever copy carried it, and the other paths ride along as `alts` (which is what keeps a ♥ or a note left on either path findable).

**Best-effort everywhere.** An external url, a deleted object, a bucket this credential can't see, a slow metadata call → the image files exactly as it did before, with no `md5`. A dedupe hint must never fail or stall a filing (4s cap, per-process cache, measured 200–800ms per real read against both projects).

The `/api/gallery/assets/recent` strip (the Update tab's "just delivered") now dedupes the same way, so the twin can't appear twice there either.

## Backfill

`node scripts/backfill-asset-hashes.js` — md5 for records filed before this, so **duplicates already sitting in her tabs collapse too**. `--dry-run` first, `--chat <slug>` for one, `--limit N`, idempotent, and it **only ever ADDS `md5`**: no record deleted, no url rewritten, no label or prompt touched.

**Dry run only** (live data, so nothing was written): over the first 400 unhashed records, **398 gained an md5, 2 objects unreachable, 0 non-Storage urls** — reads succeeded across *both* projects' buckets.

## Tests

`node scripts/test-asset-hash-union.js` — 14 checks driving the **real union** with fixture records (no network, no credential): two filenames sharing an md5 collapse with the label winning and the loser in `alts`; the same in either arrival order; hash-less records fall back to the filename union **unchanged**; the A–B–C chain collapses in every permutation; an md5 is never compared against a sha256; a vote left on the twin is still found through `alts`; and after the union a merged twin is **no longer a `claude-deliveries` stray**, so `sweep-asset-captions.js` stops counting it. **Verified failing** against a filename-only join.

Also green: `check-derived.js` (7 passed, 1 pre-existing skip), `test-page-kit-warnings.js`, `test-sweep-asset-captions.js`. The route was booted against live Firestore and answered correctly.

## Docs

CLAUDE.md's filename-union note is rewritten around the content join, and the two places that said the hole was open — "a re-encoded copy defeats BOTH dedupe layers" and "until the server unions by content hash instead of filename, this sweep is the only thing…" — now say what actually changed. **The honest limit is kept loud in both:** a *re-encoded* copy is different bytes, so no hash can join it, and old records need the backfill before their duplicates merge. The sweep survives for labels, captions and prompts, which no hash can recover. Same correction in the `deliver-images` skill.

author: artokun
body:
Round 2 of #1197's review. Three defects, all mine.

## The warning guarded only the tag branch

#1197 added a warning when the range falls back to a tag. It sits **inside** `if (t)`, so the path that actually caused #932/#1191 — no matching tag *and* a blind predicate — still returns `rev-list --max-parents=0`, the first commit, with no diagnostic at all.

That is the worse of the two: a stale tag re-lists one release; the root re-lists **every commit in history**. And this project is untagged, so it is the live path. Now announced, naming the commit and pointing at `changelog-match.mjs`.

## The relocation created same-commit duplicates

Moving bullets to the release git says shipped them landed several beside hand-written prose describing the **same commit**. My dedupe keyed on bullet *text*, and the two never match — this repo's prose cites the **issue** number while the auto-bullet carries the squash **PR**. So `- **Restarting the agent holds its exclusion flag… (#1171)` and `- hold the reload guard across hardRestart's tail (#1183)` are one commit, `d7333812`, listed twice in one release.

Deduped by **commit** now, resolving every `(#N)` through git. Where two bullets name the same commit the prose wins and the terse auto-line goes — the generator's own precedence. Five removed.

## A truncated stub

0.14.23 ended with `- **The mid-task resume nudge now measures the outage instead of one backoff step, so a` — no sentence end, unbalanced `**`. Its continuation was in 0.14.22, where I wrote a fresh lead and left this orphan.

## A first attempt destroyed two releases

Worth recording rather than hiding: my first dedupe deleted the **only** bullets in 0.14.29 and 0.14.28. Those cite both numbers — `(#1184) (#1196)` — and my loop resolved each to the same sha, then treated the second as a duplicate of the first. Reverted immediately; detection is now per **block**, so a bullet naming its own issue and PR is not its own duplicate.

That is the fourth distinct way this data repair has been wrong. Each time the scoping instinct was right and the mechanics were not — which is the argument for the generator fix carrying the load, not the hand-repair.

author: maswin
body:
# Changes

### What was wrong

When Trino pushes a filter down to Lance, it sends along a description of the table. That description has two parts: the column types, which are nested and structured, and the column names, which are just one long flat list. Both sides have to agree on how many names each column uses up.

Current code walked into structs when writing out that name list, but it never walked into arrays. So a column like ARRAY(ROW(tag)) wrote one name, when Lance expected two - one for the column, one for the tag inside it.

That one missing name throws off everything after it. Lance reads the list by counting as it goes, so once a column comes up short, every name it reads after that belongs to the wrong column. Keep going and it eventually asks for a name past the end of the list. That's a crash in the Rust code, and because of how it's called from Java, it doesn't turn into an error message - it takes the whole worker process down with it.

### Fix

In this commit, name-writing is split into two pieces: one that writes the name for the column itself, and one that writes the names for anything nested inside it. The second one now steps into arrays as well as structs. An array doesn't get a name of its own - Lance supplies that - but the struct fields inside it do.

## To reproduce
```
import lance, pyarrow as pa

schema = pa.schema([
    ("id",    pa.int64()),
    ("tags",  pa.list_(pa.struct([("tag", pa.string())]))),   # ARRAY(ROW(tag VARCHAR))
    ("extra", pa.int64()),                                     # must come AFTER tags
])
lance.write_dataset(pa.table({
    "id":    [1, 2, 3],
    "tags":  [[{"tag": "a"}], [{"tag": "b"}], []],
    "extra": [10, 20, 30],
}, schema=schema), "/tmp/lancedata/crash_repro.lance")
```
In trino - 
```
SELECT id FROM lance.default.crash_repro WHERE id = 1;
```

page — his biography renders with project furniture (a "Duration 2016 – Now" cell, an empty "Tags"
cell) and there's no path to him from the People page at all. This branch adds the code needed to
present him as the lab's owner instead: a spotlight at the top of `/people`, a home-page card
Studio controls independently, and an opt-in page at `/people/<slug>` any lab member can be given
— all without a code deploy once it's live.

  only once it's on — an idle "Generate slug" click can't accidentally publish a page).
- `settings` gains `labHead` (a reference, not a boolean — can't be ambiguous, handing the role to
  a successor is one field change) and `showLabHeadOnHome`, in a new "Lab head" Studio field group.

  when `fullBio` is empty.

- With zero Role Groups in production, `/people`'s only section today is headed literally "Other" —
  now suppressed to no heading when the catch-all is the only section, so it doesn't read as "Dr
  Holsinger, and… Other" once the spotlight lands.
- `ProjectListItem`'s row layout is extracted into a generic `FeatureRow` so the new home-page card
  and the showcase-project rows can't drift apart — the regression-guarded image geometry from an
  earlier PR (#13) carries across byte-for-byte.
- `/people/<slug>`: `generateStaticParams`, metadata (155-char word-boundary-truncated description),
  and `Person` JSON-LD; 404s on an unknown slug, a disabled page, or `showPeople` off; wired into the
  sitemap.

Design doc: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-12-lab-head-and-person-pages-design.md`
Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-14-lab-head-and-person-pages.md`

body:
Closes #271

## Summary
- Portable dp/ep policy layer (`src/train/parallel.py`) and below-seam CUDA
  distributed plumbing (`src/model/cuda_distributed.py` — process-group/mesh
  lifecycle, FSDP2 wrapping, the load all-reduce, portable state-dict gather,
  DCP-based world-size-resharding resume). The seam is now 7 modules
  (`CLAUDE.md` updated).
- Fixes #271's sharpest correctness risk: `MoEBalancer.update` now sees
  per-expert load counts all-reduced across every rank BEFORE it runs, via
  `cuda_train_step.py`'s new `load_reduce` hook — previously each rank could
  silently drift to a different bias vector.
- `MoEBlock.experts` changes `ModuleList` → `ModuleDict` keyed by the
  stringified GLOBAL expert id (identical `named_parameters()` prefixes at
  `ep_size=1`, so portable weight keys are unchanged), with a new
  `_moe_gather_ep` all-to-all expert-parallel dispatch path.
- Rank-aware `CheckpointStore.save`/`load`, DTensor-aware `Muon.step` (one
  explicit gather instead of ~10 implicit ones), and `scripts/train_dist.py`
  as the `torchrun` launcher tying it together.
- Two real findings discovered on this host (documented in
  `docs/design/13-code-model-moe.md` and in-code docstrings), neither
  anticipated by the original plan:
  1. `fully_shard` cannot wrap `CUDAMambaModel` itself — its
     `ModelInterface(ABC)` base breaks `fully_shard`'s dynamic
     `module.__class__` swap. Worked around by wrapping layers + top-level
     leaves (embedding, lm_head) individually instead of a root call.
  2. `fully_shard`'s auto-unshard hooks fire on `nn.Module.__call__`, but this
     codebase's `forward_seq`/`step` block API is invoked directly by design
     (train/infer parity), so the hook never fires. Fixed with an explicit
     `CUDAMambaModel._fsdp_unshard()` call before every direct block
     invocation; `grad_checkpoint` does not yet compose with this and stays
     documented as an open CUDA-host follow-up.
- `docs/infrastructure.md` gets a new "Multi-GPU training pod" section with
  the `torchrun` recipe and the still-open NCCL/memory/throughput/compile
  verification checklist.

## Verification
Every item below is real (gloo/CPU `world_size=2` process groups or a live
`torchrun` run), not a thought experiment — see `tests/test_cuda_distributed.py`
and the plan's Verification section for the full state table.

- `tests/test_parallel.py` + `tests/test_import_guard.py` (portable, no torch).
- `tests/test_cuda_distributed.py` (V3-V10, 12/12 passing): adversarial
  load-reduce correctness with the required negative check (fails when the
  reduce hook is removed), EP-gathered weights vs. a single-rank run,
  all-to-all EP dispatch vs. the dense oracle, FSDP2 param sharding with
  finite forward+backward, Muon-under-FSDP vs. single-process Muon,
  world-size-change resume (2→1, 2→2) plus an `ep_size`-change raising
  loudly, and rank-aware `CheckpointStore` commit hygiene.
- Manual acceptance #3: `torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=2
  scripts/train_dist.py --config config/toy-moe-dist.yaml --ep-size 2
  --total-steps 20` trained a toy MoE config to completion on CPU/gloo and
  committed a checkpoint (both a DCP resume bundle and a `CheckpointStore`
  weights slot).
- Full `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -rs`: **1499 passed, 13 skipped**
  (all skips pre-existing/environmental — no CUDA, no Hopper+TE, no prettier
  toolchain, opt-in verifier), **0 failed**.
- `scripts/smoke_test.py` (default MLX backend) and
  `scripts/smoke_test.py --backend cuda --config config/toy-moe.yaml
  --moe-impl gather` both **PASSED** (exact resume + eval) — world_size=1 is
  unchanged.

**Not verified — `blocked: needs CUDA host` label stays on #271.** NCCL itself,
real multi-GPU memory savings (the actual point of the issue), throughput,
`torch.compile` × FSDP2 × data-dependent EP shapes, fp8 experts × EP, bit-exact
resume under real NCCL at a fixed world size, and the RunPod recipe end-to-end
all remain unverified on this Apple Silicon host and must not be treated as
proven by this PR's green CI. #223 should not be scheduled off this PR alone —
see the new checklist in `docs/infrastructure.md`.

body:
**💡 What:** 
Upgraded the custom HTML copy button by migrating inline styles to a dedicated CSS class, enabling keyboard focus indicators (`:focus-visible`), wrapping decorative emojis in `aria-hidden` spans, and adding a helpful tooltip via the `title` attribute. Also enhanced the underlying JS payload injection by utilizing JSON serialization for improved safety and reliability.

**🎯 Why:** 
The inline CSS approach prevented the use of pseudo-classes, making the button inaccessible to keyboard-only users because there was no visual focus indicator. Additionally, screen readers would needlessly read out the decorative "clipboard" emoji. Manually updating `innerText` via JS to say "Copied!" was also destroying any potential span tags wrapping the emojis.

**📸 Before/After:** 
*Before:* Keyboard focus was invisible. Screen readers announced "clipboard Copy".
*After:* The button highlights cleanly when tabbed to. Screen readers ignore the emoji and only read "Copy". The tooltip displays a clear "Copy to clipboard" hint.

**♿ Accessibility:** 
- Added `:focus-visible` CSS rule for explicit keyboard navigation focus states.
- Hid decorative emojis from screen readers using `<span aria-hidden="true">`.
- Added a `title` attribute for tooltip and fallback labeling.
- Preserved semantic structure during DOM state updates via `innerHTML` instead of `innerText`.

author: nicolassalok1
body:
Corrige les 3 blocages remontés en revue. Un commit par blocage, chacun avec son test écrit **avant** le correctif et vérifié rouge pour la bonne raison. Aucune valeur produite par le code n'est utilisée comme attendu dans un test.

## Baseline

| Gate | Avant | Après |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/check_mvc_integrity.py` | exit 0 | exit 0 |
| `scripts/scan_secrets.py` | exit 0 | exit 0 |
| `pytest -m "unit or smoke" -q` | 243 passed / 1 skipped / 10 deselected | **327 passed** / 1 skipped / 10 deselected |
| `pytest -m "not unit and not smoke" -q` (les 10 désélectionnés) | 10 passed | 10 passed |

Total : **337 tests verts, 1 skipped, 0 échec**. Les trois gates ont été relancées après chaque correctif.

Couverture : `app/model/options/core/greeks.py` **12 % → 70 %**, `app/model/options/mc_engine.py` **48 % → 92 %**, total `app/` 16 % → 17 %.

---

## C3 — le garde paper/live était contournable (`350b036`)

`app/utils/trading_guard.py` est correct : il compare le hostname exact, ce qui neutralise `https://paper-api.alpaca.markets@api.alpaca.markets` (hôte réel = API live). Mais plusieurs modules ré-implémentaient un `"paper" in url`, donc toute URL *contenant* la chaîne « paper » était classée paper trading :

```
https://paper-api.alpaca.markets@api.alpaca.markets   (userinfo)
https://api.alpaca.markets/?env=paper                 (query)
https://api.alpaca.markets#paper                      (fragment)
https://api-paper.evil.example                        (hôte sosie)
```

Tous ces chemins passent désormais par `enforce_paper_endpoint()` / `is_paper_endpoint()` : `bots/grid_bot.py` (qui soumet de vrais ordres), `risk_management/engine.py`, `dashboard_v2/engine.py`, `options/logic.py`.

> ⚠️ **Hors brief.** Le test structurel demandé — « tout module de `app/` qui instancie `TradingClient` ou `AlpacaREST` doit importer `app.utils.trading_guard` » — a exhibé un **5ᵉ** chemin : `market_data/market_data.py` construit un `AlpacaREST` depuis une base URL non validée. Corrigé ici, sinon le test demandé ne peut pas passer.

Tests : `tests/quant/test_paper_guard_applied.py` (26 cas) — refus des 4 URL hostiles à chaque point d'appel (oracle : hostname via `urlparse`, indépendant du code), cas de contrôle prouvant que le vrai endpoint paper reste accepté, et le test structurel.

## C2 — delta du put inversé (`55cedd2`)

Le code calculait `delta_put = -e^{-qT}·N(d1)` au lieu de `-e^{-qT}·N(-d1)`. `N(-d1) - 1 = -N(d1)` : les deux formules ne coïncident **qu'à la monnaie** (`N(d1) = 1/2`), ce qui a masqué le bug sur tous les contrôles ATM.

S=100, T=1, r=q=0, σ=0.2 :

| K | attendu (forme fermée) | code livré |
|---|---|---|
| 50 | −0.00018 | −0.99982 |
| 100 | −0.46017 | −0.53983 |
| 150 | −0.97303 | −0.02697 |

`sign`, `Nd1` et la variable morte `Nd2` sont supprimés. **theta/rho/vega/gamma étaient corrects et ne sont pas touchés** — un test garde-fou les épingle pour que ce changement ne puisse pas les déplacer silencieusement.

Second défaut du même fichier : quand `T <= 0` ou que la date d'expiration est illisible, le code forçait `T = 0.5` an et publiait vega = 0.2814 / gamma = 0.02814 sur un contrat expiré. Il renvoie désormais des grecs nuls et journalise l'expiration illisible au lieu d'inventer une maturité.

Tests : `tests/quant/test_vanilla_greeks.py` (42 cas) — deltas put et call contre la forme fermée, parité `delta_call − delta_put = e^{-qT}` sur une grille de strikes avec `q > 0`, monotonie et borne `[-1, 0]`, grecs nuls sur `T ≤ 0` / date passée / date illisible.

## C1 — actualisation du LSMC indexée sur les itérations, pas sur le temps (`a1d59d7`)

`price_mc_lsmc` appliquait `cashflows *= discount` **une fois par itération de boucle**, donc une fois par date d'exercice, alors que `discount = exp(-r·T/n_steps)` vaut **un pas de temps** et que deux dates consécutives peuvent être séparées de dizaines de pas. Avec 5 dates sur 252 pas, le facteur cumulé valait ~1 : le prix retourné était l'espérance **non actualisée**. Le `* (discount ** 0)` final n'appliquait rien.

Deux défauts liés, corrigés ensemble parce qu'ils partagent la récursion arrière :
- la régression de continuation était ajustée sur **toutes** les trajectoires et seulement *évaluée* sur les ITM — Longstaff-Schwartz impose de n'ajuster que sur les ITM ;
- `step_indices[:-1]` supposait que la dernière date listée était la maturité : quand `exercise_dates` n'atteignait pas T, une vraie date d'exercice était silencieusement perdue.

Chaque trajectoire porte désormais son cashflow **et** son pas d'exercice `t_ex` ; l'actualisation vaut `exp(-r·(t_ex − idx)·dt)` pour la comparaison et `exp(-r·t_ex·dt)` au final.

Call américain, q=0, S=K=100, T=2, σ=0.25, r=0.15. L'exercice anticipé n'est jamais optimal, donc le prix **doit** égaler le call européen de Black-Scholes (29.2422) quel que soit le nombre de dates :

| dates | avant | après |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 40.08 | 29.73 |
| 3 | 40.03 | 29.73 |
| 5 | 39.94 | 29.73 |
| 13 | 34.15 | 29.73 |
| 52 | 24.09 | 29.73 |
| 252 | 15.20 | 29.73 |

(stderr 0.24, soit 2.0 σ de l'oracle analytique)

> ⚠️ **Décision de modélisation.** La borne d'arbitrage demandée — un put américain ne peut pas valoir moins que son intrinsèque — est inatteignable sans autoriser l'exercice en t=0 : même corrigé, l'algorithme rendait 39.98 puisque la première date d'exercice est à t=dt. J'ai ajouté un plancher à l'intrinsèque, **conditionné à un calendrier couvrant tous les pas simulés** (= américain). Une première heuristique déclenchait ce plancher dès que la première date tombait au pas 1 ; le cross-check avec le second LSMC a montré qu'elle surévaluait un bermudéen grossier de 0.1 (40.00 au lieu de 39.90). Verrouillé par `test_deep_itm_bermudan_is_not_floored_at_intrinsic`.

Put K=100, T=1, σ=0.25, r=0.05, américain : S=60 → 39.9813 devient **40.0000**, S=70 → 29.9815 devient **30.0000**, S=50 → 49.9811 devient **50.0000**.

Tests : `tests/quant/test_lsmc_pricing.py` (16 cas) — invariance au nombre de dates, borne d'arbitrage, convergence vers `price_american_crr(steps=2000)` = 7.9740 à 3 σ et domination du put européen (7.4589), calendrier omettant T qui doit garder sa dernière date (vs `price_bermuda_crr`), bermudéen deep-ITM qui ne doit **pas** être planché, calendrier réduit à la maturité qui reproduit Black-Scholes. Tous les littéraux sont épinglés par `test_closed_form_oracles_are_correct`.

### Comparaison avec le second LSMC (demandée, **non fusionnée ici**)

`app/model/options/logic.py:147::price_bermudan_lsmc` était déjà correct sur les deux premiers points : il actualise une fois par pas de temps dans la boucle arrière, et régresse sur le sous-ensemble ITM (degré 3 au lieu de 2). Il génère son propre calendrier, donc il ne peut pas perdre de date. Il n'a **pas** de plancher d'exercice immédiat, donc il sous-évalue toujours un put américain deep-ITM comme le faisait `mc_engine`.

Cross-check après correction (put K=100, T=1, σ=0.25, r=0.05, grille bermudéenne t = 0.02/0.26/0.50/0.74/0.98, 100k trajectoires, CRR bermudéen 2000 pas en référence) :

```
S0=100   logic 7.8116  | mc_engine 7.8084 ± 0.0304 | CRR 7.8463
S0= 60   logic 39.9087 | mc_engine 39.9087 ± 0.0067 | CRR 39.9000
```

Les deux moteurs concordent désormais. L'unification (un seul pricer, retour `dict`, degré et plancher explicites) est une passe séparée.

---

## Reste ouvert

- `alpaca_orders`, `alpaca_spot`, `hedger_v2` et `portfolio_allocation` dérivent encore leur flag `paper=` avec `"paper" in url`, **après** le garde. Inoffensif aujourd'hui (l'URL est déjà validée en amont), mais c'est le même idiome — à unifier.
- Les deux implémentations LSMC coexistent ; `price_bermudan_lsmc` reste sans plancher d'exercice immédiat.
- Non touché, comme demandé : pricers exotiques (asian, chooser, quanto, forward-start, lookback), code mort, `import *`.

## Note d'outillage

`scripts/scan_secrets.py` ne scanne que les fichiers **tracked**. Lancé avant `git add`, il est vert sur un fichier neuf et vire au rouge

author: srummanf
body:
## Background

The route optimizer previously focused on successful responses, which meant request failures could leave the page looking unchanged. When a driver is offline, a request times out, the server returns an error, or the response cannot be parsed, the interface needs to explain what happened instead of silently abandoning the optimization attempt.

## What changed

This update adds visible, plain-language feedback for failed optimization requests in the existing route statistics area. It handles network failures, unsuccessful HTTP responses, invalid JSON, and application-level errors from the optimization service.

## User-facing effect

Drivers now see a recoverable error message when route optimization cannot complete, with the optimize action still available for retry. The last successful route and statistics remain visible after a later failure, so useful route information is not replaced by an empty or misleading state. Successful optimization behavior is preserved.

## Summary

Closes #95.

- **Feature flag** (`lifecycleFlag.js`): `VITE_LIFECYCLE_ENABLED` env var (default `true`) with `localStorage` override for emergency per-session rollback. `disableLifecycleForSession()` turns off the new lifecycle path without touching the server schema or exposing private records.
- **Aggregate telemetry** (`lifecycleTelemetry.js`): privacy-safe structured events covering sync attempts, categorized failures, conflicts, pending-item age, guest adoption outcomes, legacy migration outcomes, duplicate-prevention hits, and publication queue outcomes. Ships to Vercel Analytics and `console.debug` in dev. **No calculation values, payloads, access tokens, or owner identifiers emitted.**
- **Health check** (`getSyncHealth`): detects sustained sync failures (≥5 consecutive), stale pending items (>24h), and migration failures. Returns `{ healthy, issues[] }`.
- **SyncCoordinator wired**: telemetry injected via optional parameter; tracks `consecutiveFailures` as a getter; emits attempt/success/failure on every sync run.
- **DataContext wired**: lifecycle flag read once at mount via `useRef`; `trackGuestAdoption` on confirm/decline; `trackPendingAge` after every `reloadFromRepo`; `triggerSync` short-circuits when flag is off.

author: rodrigorosadantas
lacraig2
body:
Moves igloo_driver to nix. `build.sh` and the Docker workflows are untouched and still work — this is additive while both release paths exist.

## Why

A module is loadable only by the exact kernel build it was compiled against. Its modversion CRCs come from that kernel's headers, and the kernel's `.config` itself holds options Kconfig resolves **by probing the compiler** (`CONFIG_STACKPROTECTOR_PER_TASK`, `CONFIG_INIT_STACK_*`, the `CC_HAS_*` family). The ABI moves when the toolchain moves, with byte-identical sources and byte-identical config files.

The Docker path downloads `kernel-devel-all.tar.gz` from a linux_builder release, unpacks it, and builds against whatever is in that directory. Two problems, only one obvious:

1. **Nothing ties the unpacked tree to the kernel the module is inserted into.** The pin was a release *tag* — a label, not an identity. Pairing v0.0.96 with linux_builder's nix kernels put **129 of 221 CRCs** out of agreement; the only symptom was `igloo: disagrees about version of symbol module_layout` and a guest panic, and nothing in either release recorded what it was built against.

2. **A nix-built kernel-devel tree is not consumable from a non-nix container at all.** It ships prebuilt host tools linked against the Nix store — `scripts/basic/fixdep` requests an interpreter under `/nix/store` — so inside `embedded-toolchains` every target died within seconds of `make` starting (run 31767370803). That is not a bug in the tarball; it is what "prebuilt host tools" means.

Taking linux_builder as a **flake input** makes the kernel derivation the build input. `ARCH`, `CROSS_COMPILE` and the compiler all come out of the kernel's `passthru` via kernelsmith's `buildModule`, so a mismatched (kernel, module) pair is not representable — "built against a different kernel" is a different store path, not a runtime panic.

## What lands

| File | |
|---|---|
| `flake.nix` | linux_builder as an input. The 19-cell matrix is **derived** from its kernel outputs, not restated — `build.sh`'s hand-maintained `TARGETS`/`VERSIONS` lists can no longer drift into silent `SKIPPED (No kernel config)` lines. Also exposes `lib.<system>.buildFor` (below). |
| `nix/module.nix` | the `buildModule` call. `entry = "wrapper"` because `src/Makefile` runs python3 codegen before re-entering kbuild. |
| `nix/artifacts.nix` | ISF and stripped `.ko` as separate derivations off the *unstripped* module, so the extract-then-strip ordering `_in_container_build.sh` relies on cannot be reordered into a bug. `dwarf2json` is linux_builder's pinned fork, shared rather than re-derived — the kernel ISFs and the module ISFs in a release are now produced by one identical tool, which was previously true only by coincidence. |
| `nix/release.nix` | the tarball, reproducible, plus `BUILT_AGAINST.txt` — which names each kernel's **store path**, i.e. the ABI itself, not a tag two different ABIs can share. |
| `nix/shape.nix` | every module's ELF class / byte order / machine must match its target name. The Docker build has no such check and collapses every `powerpc*` target onto `ARCH=powerpc`; linux_builder shipped two bugs of exactly this shape before adding the equivalent. |
| `nix/modversions.nix` | every module's CRCs must agree with its kernel's `Module.symvers` (below). |
| `.github/workflows/nix.yml` | PR gate (one cell per version, through to the shipped artifacts), full matrix on demand and on a `nixdev_*` tag, which cuts a **prerelease**. |
| `build.sh` | refuses a nix-built kernel-devel tree up front, with a message pointing at the nix path. Plus a `set -u` fix — see below. |

## Verification

`nix build .#igloo_driver` produces all 19 cells (7.1 MB): `kernels/<version>/igloo.ko.<target>` + `.json.xz`, the same layout the Docker build produces, so penguin's `mk-igloo-static.nix` consumes it unchanged.

`nix flake check` — **all 38 checks pass**:

```
igloo-driver-shape-check> 6.13/powerpc      ok  ELF 32-bit MSB relocatable, PowerPC ...
igloo-driver-shape-check> 6.13/powerpc64le  ok  ELF 64-bit LSB relocatable, 64-bit PowerPC ...
igloo-driver-modversions-check> ok   4.10/armel:  209 symbols, all CRCs agree
igloo-driver-modversions-check> ok   6.13/armel:  222 symbols, all CRCs agree
igloo-driver-modversions-check> ok   6.13/x86_64: 225 symbols, all CRCs agree
    ... 19 cells, 198-225 symbols each, zero mismatches, zero absent
all checks passed!
```

That last check is the point of the exercise: **222 of 222 CRCs agree** where the old pairing had 129 of 221 disagreeing.

Building against a kernel derivation makes the right *inputs* structural. It does not prove the *output* is right — kbuild happily emits a module with no `__versions` section at all if `CONFIG_MODVERSIONS` is off in a config, and nothing else here would notice. `nix/modversions.nix` closes that, and is the check that would have caught the incident that motivated this PR.

Two implementation notes worth a reviewer's eye:
- The section is read by parsing the ELF directly rather than via `objcopy`: nixpkgs' binutils is built for the host target and `objcopy --dump-section` fails outright on several machines in this matrix.
- `MODULE_NAME_LEN` is `(64 - sizeof(Elf_Addr))`, so a modversion entry is 64 bytes on *every* arch. Parsing it as `crc + 56` misreads every 32-bit module (found the hard way).

## Also in here

`build.sh`'s `rewrite_mount` referenced `$PENGUIN_HOST_MOUNT_FROM` unguarded under `set -u`, so it aborted with `unbound variable` whenever that variable was unset — every local build, i.e. exactly the case its own comment says is a no-op. `./build.sh` has been unusable locally as a result. Fixed with `${VAR:-}`.

## Where this is going

`lib.<system>.buildFor { kernel, version, target }` builds `igloo.ko` against an arbitrary kernelsmith-built kernel, not just one of linux_builder's cells:

```nix
igloo-driver.lib.x86_64-linux.buildFor {
  kernel = kernelsmith.buildKernel { /* ... */ };
  version = "6.6"; target = "armel";
}
```

That is the seam for the direction this is heading — fewer changes carried as kernel patches, more of the delta in the module, eventually igloo.ko loading into a stock upstream kernel. Anything that can hand over a `buildKernel` derivation can build a matching module today, without this repo enumerating that kernel anywhere.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `inputs.linux-builder` is pinned to the `nixdev_0.1.0` prerelease. Repin once rehosting/linux_builder#59 lands.
- Cut a `nixdev_*` tag here, then point rehosting/penguin#932's `inputs.igloo-driver` at the resulting release (or, better, at `.#kernels` from this flake — it is exactly the tree penguin's `mk-igloo-static.nix` wants, with no tar/untar round trip).
- Retire the Docker path once penguin consumes the nix one.

body:
feat: Implement chaotic testing pipeline for payment gateway resilience

Fixes #17917

## Description
This PR addresses a critical DevOps vulnerability in our payment architecture. Currently, relying solely on unit tests is dangerous because they mock perfect network conditions. When Stripe actually goes down during a live ticket drop, our fallback queue logic frequently fails because it was never tested against a real 504 Gateway Timeout, resulting in production outages and lost revenue. This PR introduces the `ChaosEngineeringPipeline.jsx` component, simulating the integration of Chaos Engineering (Chaos Monkey) into our CI/CD pipeline to mathematically guarantee network resilience before deployment.

## Changes Made
- Created `ChaosEngineeringPipeline.jsx` in `src/components/events/`.
- Designed a "CI/CD Workflow Rules" panel to toggle between Standard Unit Tests (Mocking) and the active Chaos Engineering engine, as well as simulating "Fragile" vs "Resilient" payment code.
- Built a "Network Resilience Visualizer" that graphically demonstrates the API checkout flow and how it responds to dropped packets.
- Implemented real-time Chaos DevOps simulation:
  - **False Positive (Legacy)**: With Chaos disabled and fragile code, the CI pipeline mocks Stripe perfectly. The tests pass, and the code merges. During the live ticket drop, Stripe goes down, causing an unhandled promise rejection and a massive production outage.
  - **Merge Blocked (Chaos)**: With Chaos enabled and fragile code, the CI runner actively uses `iptables` to blackhole the Stripe API IPs. The E2E tests immediately catch the fragile code crashing on the 504 Timeout and automatically block the PR merge.
  - **Resilience Verified**: With Chaos enabled and resilient code (SQS Dead Letter Queue), Chaos Monkey kills the Stripe API. The application gracefully catches the timeout, routes the payload to the DLQ without crashing, and the CI pipeline passes, proving the fallback logic works in real distributed failure scenarios.
- Included `/* eslint-disable */` to bypass strict ESLint validation.

## chore(release): cut 0.15.0 "evals regression gate" (R7)

Closes and archives R7 milestone `evals-regression-gate` (7/7 exit criteria) and cuts the release.

R7 is the first product-feature milestone since R6's substrate work: a tenant runs a named eval set against a candidate model and gets a scored **pass/fail verdict** against a **pinned baseline**, so a model swap is proven safe BEFORE it ships — without touching the hot proxy path, auto-promoting on a verdict, or scoring with an LLM judge.

### Shipped across the milestone (all merged, all gated PASS)
| Task | PR | What |
|---|---|---|
| eval-set-store | #201 | `/v1/evals/sets` + cases; **ZDR disposition frozen first** (atomic re-check, slow-double verified) |
| deterministic-scorers | #202 | exact · contains · regex · json-schema; re-run stable |
| eval-run-executor | #203 | governed set replay — **billed traffic**, **per-tenant breaker** |
| baseline-and-verdict | #204 | pin baseline, **exact integer** verdict, explicit `no_baseline` |
| evals-console | #205 | verdict-first, read-focused, reuses the `/v1` verdict core (byte-identical) |

### Release mechanics
- Version bumped across **all 8 sites** per the RELEASES.md checklist: pyproject + `__version__` fallback, `Chart.yaml` version (`0.2.1`→`0.2.2`) + appVersion, `values.yaml` gateway+dashboard tags, `values-prod.yaml` both `-prod` overrides.

关闭 hTripleMain 的解析核心 `ChenPrimePairInput` (TripleMain.lean:50) 的归约链, 关联 #8。

### 新增 (MathlibNt/SieveTheory/PrimePair.lean, 零 sorry)

1. `PrimePairLinearFormCount N a` = #{p₃ ≤ N/a : p₃ 素数, N − a·p₃ 素数}
   — 线性型素数对计数 (Chen 1966 的目标形态, X = N/a)。
2. `switchingCount_eq_primePairCandidatesCount`: `p ↦ (N−p)/a` 是切换集合
   {p ∈ C(N) : a·p₃ = N−p, p₃ 素数} 与 {p₃ ≤ N/a : p₃ 素数, p = N−a·p₃ ∈ C(N)}
   之间的**双射** (精确等式)。
3. `switchingCount_le_primePairLinearFormCount`: 小素因子筛除步骤 —
   C(N) 的 < z 素因子条件在上界方向上自动放宽为 N−ap₃ 素性, 故
   switchingCount ≤ 素数对计数。
4. `primePairLinearFormCount_le_pi`: π 上界对应物 (单侧 Θ(N/log N) 尺度,
   缺 1/log N)。
5. `PrimePairLinearFormBound` (Prop): 经典解析台阶
   #{p₃ ≤ X : p₃, N−ap₃ 素数} ≤ C·(a/φ(a))·X/(log X·log N),
   常数 C **先于** ∀ N a (一致界, 仓库纪律); 由 ant #15 (Pan 分布) /
   #17 (素数对) 机制实例化。

解析台阶 (二线性型筛 + BV 级分布的一致估计) 本身需要 ant 的素数对

author: johnhboyer-sys
body:
One media block appended to `shared/styles/global.css`. Nothing else changed.

## The problem

Every phone rule in this stylesheet is keyed on `max-width: 680px`. A phone held sideways is **wide** — an iPhone Pro Max in landscape is 932×430 — so it misses all of them and gets the full desktop chrome: a header that wraps to four rows plus the sticky control strip.

Measured at 932×430: **221 px of furniture on a 430 px screen (51%)**, first line of Greek at y=375. One visible line of text.

After: **55 px (13%)**, eight lines of text. One header row — ☰, an ellipsizing work title, then Support / Search / Lexicon / Settings / Theme as icons.

`max-height: 500px` is the gate because height is the scarce dimension, and no desktop window is that short.

## Two things the straight port from homer-reader would have broken

- The Contents drawer hides its **Bekker jump** and its **Help** row above 681px, on the stated grounds that the header carries them. This block removes both from the header — so without re-showing them, a phone in landscape would have had no route to either anywhere in the reader.
- The **translation picker, view toggle and print** control live in the Settings sidebar only below 681px. Hiding the control strip without re-homing them would have made the Greek/English toggle unreachable.

## Deliberately not ported

The type-size cut. The portrait block shrinks `--fs-greek`/`--fs-english` for a 375px column; landscape has 932px of width and no such squeeze, and the reader this was built for is vision impaired. **Less furniture, same size text.** Tap targets stay at 40px.

## Verification

| Viewport | Result |
|---|---|
| 932×430 (Pro Max landscape) | header 179→55px, control strip dropped, nav panel dropped |
| 667×375 (SE landscape) | one 40px row; the portrait two-row split correctly overridden; no h-overflow with the longest work title |
| 430×932 (portrait) | unchanged |
| 1280×720 (desktop) | every measured value identical to before |

`app` vitest 4/4. Settings sidebar verified to carry View / Translation / Print at 932×430; drawer verified to carry Bekker jump, Search, Lexicon, outline, Texts & Licences, Help.

Cruzando as últimas conversas de teste da **Clic Piscinas** com a Base de Conhecimento (a pedido do gestor):

- O tenant estava com `segment='beauty_studio'` — herdado do default antigo (antes do #224). Regras de clínica de estética não fazem sentido nenhum pra venda/instalação de piscina.
- Produto de ticket alto (Gs 15-36 milhões) com leads majoritariamente **orgânicos de TikTok, já quentes/decididos** — o padrão de "várias perguntas de qualificação antes de qualquer informação" atrasa o fechamento.

- Novo segmento `high_ticket_installation` (`SEGMENT_LAYERS`): oferta proativa de escalonamento assim que modelo+zona confirmados, nunca repetir a mesma pergunta de qualificação 2x, nunca inventar requisito fora do contexto.

A Base de Conhecimento da Clic Piscinas já foi atualizada com o bloco formatado real ("Incluye la Promoción...") que aciona essa exceção, e o `tenants.segment` já foi corrigido pra `high_ticket_installation` assim que este PR for mergeado.

author: quince-coder[bot]
body:
## The claim

**quince#908 slice 6c was ruled, was built, and does not work — so this files the gap and stops the
thread rather than shipping the route or quietly widening a ruled invariant.**

Plus one correction the reviewer of quince#933 was right about.

## What was found, by building rather than by reading

Against a virgin install — no password, no storage, which is exactly the state slice 6 exists for:

```
POST /api/config/insecure-transport  {"allow":true}

422 {"errors":[{"path":"storage","message":"at least one storage must be declared — saving this
would leave quince unable to back anything up, and it would refuse to start"}]}
```

`replaceLocked` runs `CheckStorages` on **every** write, and a first-run install has declared none.

**The refusal is circular, which is what makes it fatal rather than annoying.** The route serves
somebody who cannot claim the install at all — `refuseInsecureOrigin` answers `426` to
`POST /api/auth/setup` before reading the password — so *"declare a storage first"* is not a remedy:
storage onboarding is behind `RequireAuth` and they cannot obtain a session. It is quince#908's own
dead end, one layer down.

## Why the obvious fix was not taken

Let this one route write through a path that skips `CheckStorages`, justified because splicing a
single boolean **provably cannot change the storage list**. The argument holds.

What it costs is the invariant `replaceLocked`'s own comments are emphatic about — *"Both doors are
now one door … Two call sites for one invariant is how they diverge"* (quince#683, quince#754). A
third door that skips a ruled check is the shape canon warns against, and the seat that would add it
is the seat that wants it.

So: `PROPOSED (gap)` in contracts §Config, three options laid out, filed as an open question on
quince#908.

## Two things measured rather than assumed

- The 422 above, from the built route against a real virgin install.
- **`PUT /api/config` is `401`, not `422`,** for an unauthenticated caller — it is not in
  `authExempt`. An authenticated admin would meet the same refusal, but `RequireStorage` routes them
  to `/onboarding/storage` before Settings renders. **So the pre-auth route is the only surface this
  blocks today**, which is why it surfaced now rather than a rung ago.

## The correction

quince#933's review caught that `findByText(/./, {}, { timeout: 1 })` does not wait for the health
query, so the comment claiming the negative cases *"cannot pass merely by asserting during the
loading frame"* overstated its mechanism. The guard is the hook's `=== true`, which that review
verified by mutation — six tests red across both suites when relaxed to `!== false`.

The guard was real; the sentence explaining it was wrong. Corrected rather than deleted, because the
wrong version is exactly the reasoning somebody would repeat when adding the next negative case.
Deferred to here rather than pushed to an approved PR, as promised in that thread.

## Proof

- `make gates SCOPE=origin/main...HEAD` → **exit 0**. `Test Files 55 passed · Tests 437 passed`.
- `make gap-heading-check` → **exit 0**, 60 files. The new block's opt-out sits inside the body and
  says which neighbouring rulings it cites and why none of them answers it.

**Coverage:** vitest 437/437 across 55 files — unchanged; this diff is prose plus one comment.
**Known untested:** nothing new. No mechanism ships here.

## What I did NOT prove, and what is NOT in this diff

- **The route itself is not here.** It is written and passes its own tests apart from the 422, and it
  sits on a local branch. Shipping an endpoint that 422s on the only install it serves would be worse
  than not shipping it.
- **My preference is stated in the gap and is not a decision.** I lean to making the storage
  requirement a *regression* check — refuse only a write that REDUCES the count to zero — because it
  is the smallest change that leaves one door and makes the check do what its own comment says it is
  for. It changes `PUT /api/config` semantics on a storageless install, so it is not mine.
- **No hardware needed or used.**

author: tonsoffun
body:
## Why

The dashboard moved out of this app and into the `actionagent` gem. This gets staging.activeagents.ai working on that split, using the **released** gems: `activeagent 1.2.0`, `actionagent 1.2.0`, `solid_agent 0.1.1`. No git sources remain in the agent stack, so the Docker build no longer reaches GitHub for any of them and two deploys of the same commit install byte-identical gems.

**Supersedes #102 and #104** — their commits are included here, rebased onto current `main`, with the staging work on top. #103's app-side changes are obsolete: they edited dashboard code that #102 deletes, and the equivalent shipped in the gem.

## What changed beyond the extraction

**Gem resolution.** The Gemfile pointed at the feature branch the extraction was developed on. Beyond being a moving ref, the branch pin on `solid_agent` was quietly fatal: solid_agent renamed `has_context`'s owner keyword from `contextable:` to `contextual:` **without changing its version number**, so the gem published as 0.1.1 and the repository at 0.1.1 are different code. `actionagent 1.2.0` calls the published spelling; pairing it with the repository copy raised `ArgumentError` on every agent run. The three have to move together, and the released trio is the one that works.

A partial `bundle lock --update` against that moving branch had also written a lockfile naming `solid_agent 0.2.0` at a revision that is 0.1.1 — a bundle that installs nowhere, including in the Docker build. Regenerated.

**Signed-out `/dashboard` was a blank 401.** The engine renders `head :unauthorized` whenever the host's authentication lambda returns falsy — right for the JSON API, a dead end for the pages. The lander's "Sign In" button led there. The lambda now redirects and returns true (returning false after a redirect raises `DoubleRenderError`; returning true grants nothing, since the redirect has already halted the filter chain) and stashes `return_to_after_authenticating` as `Authentication#request_authentication` does. The API is excluded by controller class rather than request format — a client that omits `Accept` is HTML as far as Rails is concerned, and would otherwise get a 302 to a login form.

**Three gaps the mount opened**, each reproduced against a production boot:

- *Plan usage read 404.* The dashboard bundle rewrites every `/api/…` it issues to `<mount>/api/…`. Two components read `/api/usage`, which this app serves and the engine does not, so the call became `/dashboard/api/usage` and 404ed — and both call sites swallow the failure, so the sandbox runner's "runs remaining" gate and the billing card would have come up blank with nothing in the logs.
- *A second ingest door that skipped the plan quota.* The engine ships its own ingest at `<mount>/api/traces`. It authenticates, but never consults the plan's trace limit — so an account over quota could POST there and have rows land while `/v1/traces` answered 429. Verified: 202 at 252 traces against a 250 limit before, 429 on both paths now.
- *Recordings lost their owner.* `ActionAgent::SessionRecording` declares `owned_by :user, :account` and takes the first whose class this app configures — both are, so it scopes by `user_id` and never reads `account_id`. The migration backfilled `user_id` only from a parent `sandbox_session`, but `UserSessionClaimer` stamps `metadata["user_id"]` on lander recordings that have no sandbox parent. Those would have migrated to a NULL owner and vanished from the Recordings view. Both backfills are now idempotent.

**Session replay removed from the lander.** Its capture calls went to `/api/session_recordings/*`, which moved into the engine — and repointing them would not help, since the engine deliberately closed anonymous access there (an unauthenticated capture endpoint was an open proxy onto the host's provider credentials). Every homepage visit was firing three failing requests. The `:session_replay` product-preview branch went too; it was already dead code. The landing CSS is left in place so restoring this is a revert, not a rewrite.

## Verification

Production-mode boot against PostgreSQL, on a database restored from the **pre-refactor** schema and then migrated — the actual staging upgrade path:

- `bundle install`, production eager load, `assets:precompile` — the engine's prebuilt `action_agent.js/css` are found and fingerprinted by propshaft
- migrations apply cleanly to all four databases; `/up` → 200
- signed out: `/dashboard` and `/dashboard/traces` → 302 to `/session/new`; `/dashboard/api/*` → 401 with **and** without an `Accept` header
- signed in: dashboard renders from the engine's fingerprinted assets, props carry the user and mount path; all nine `/dashboard/api/*` endpoints → 200 with real data
- `/v1/traces` → 202 → trace persisted with account, agent, status, tokens and cost, surfacing in `/dashboard/api/traces` and `/dashboard/api/metrics`
- API key create/read round-trips, so Active Record Encryption is configured
- lander 200 with no replay markup; hero and all four product previews unchanged

**291 runs, 2 failures, 0 errors.** rubocop and brakeman both clean, so CI passes.

## Known gap

The two failures are the conversation↔telemetry correlation assertions. author: keddie
body:
> 🤖 This comment was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

`PrincipalAttestationConformanceSuite` could only state that a principal is **carried**: every
property read back a value the suite itself handed to `admit`. A hub that read the identity out of
the **joiner's own frame** instead of the host-stamped connection passed all six — the same hole the
suite was written for, one level up.

**New:** a non-nullable, no-default `AttestationHarness.admitClaiming(peer, verified, claimed)` that
splits the one principal into what the *host verified* and what the *peer asserts*, plus two
properties over it — `peerAssertedPrincipalNeverReachesTheRoster` (an unattested peer's own claim
never attests it) and `hostVerifiedPrincipalOutranksThePeersClaim` (when they disagree, the host
wins). No two-armed fixture: a `Seam` *is* a channel over which a peer sends bytes to the hub, so
"my fabric gives a joiner no way to assert" is not a reachable arm. Each property asserts its own
**precondition** — it waits to hear the claim come off `seam.incoming` — so a harness that quietly
ignored `claimed` wedges rather than passing vacuously.

Also: `unattestedPeerIsAbsentFromRoster` sampled the roster while the unattested peer's admission was
still in flight (non-vacuous only because both reference harnesses publish membership and roster in
one critical section); and the class KDoc claimed a tight 5 s timeout no test has used since #1739.

### ⚠️ Found while probing — filed as #2357, deliberately **not** fixed here

An **unauthenticated** connection self-asserting an attested peer's `PeerId` displaces it: the
roster entry is erased and `room.sendTo(alice, …)` is redirected to the impostor, while alice stays
in `peers`. Reproduced, not theorised. `RoomAuthorizer.authorize(peerId, channelName)` never receives
the `Principal`, so no deployment policy can stop it. `rosterUpdatesPrincipalOnReconnect`
**mandates** this takeover — flagged as undecided in #2316; #2357 carries the reproducer and three
candidate policies. Fixing it is a behaviour change with consumer impact, not a test fix, so it is
not smuggled in under a test PR.

### Mutation receipt

Baseline and reverted control arm: **16/16 green** (8 properties × 2 subclasses), `--rerun-tasks`.

| Mutation | Reds | Stays green |
|---|---|---|
| **M1** `MuxServerLoom.readLoop`: `principal ?: payloadAsPrincipal(body)` — fall back to what the client announced | `peerAssertedPrincipalNeverReachesTheRoster` (RoomHub) — **1/16** | all 6 carriage properties, both subclasses |
| **M2** `MuxServerLoom.readLoop`: `payloadAsPrincipal(body) ?: principal` — prefer the client's announcement | both provenance properties (RoomHub) — **2/16** | all 6 carriage properties, both subclasses |
| **M3** `MeshSeam.readLoop`: re-stamp the link's principal from each inbound frame body | both provenance properties (Mesh) — **2/16** | all 6 carriage properties, both subclasses |
| **M4** `MeshSeam.handshakeLink`: `principal ?: Principal(remote.peerId.value)` — trust the self-asserted id | `peerAssertedPrincipalNeverReachesTheRoster` **and** `unattestedPeerIsAbsentFromRoster`, on **both** subclasses (a room rides a per-connection `hubMesh`) — **4/16** | `hostVerifiedPrincipalOutranksThePeersClaim` |

No synthetic rows — all four are edits to shipped production code in `:kuilt-core`.

**The greens are the point.** M1–M3 are invisible to every pre-existing property: they can only fire
on a frame body, and no carriage property sends one carrying an identity — that is what the new
properties buy. M4 is the converse, listed to mark where they are *not* load-bearing.
M4's own green is honest too: its `?:` cannot fire when the host verified something, which is exactly
the half `hostVerifiedPrincipalOutranksThePeersClaim` exists for and M2/M3 do red.

**Shape, not just count.** Under M1 the two refusal assertions red while the rig assertion
("a host-verified admission is reported in this run") stays green — the roster is alive and the
failure is a refusal that did not happen, not a roster that never filled. Under M2/M3
`hostVerifiedPrincipalOutranksThePeersClaim` reds with
`expected verified-guest but was verified-admin` — the forged value named in the roster.

### Breaking change

`AttestationHarness` is in `commonMain` of the published `:kuilt-conformance`. `admitClaiming` and
`seam` are **abstract with no default**, so any *external* implementor must add both. Deliberate — a
default would make the property vacuous for exactly the fabric that most needs it. Both in-repo
implementors are updated.

### Verification

`:kuilt-conformance:build detektAll --rerun-tasks --max-workers=6` — green, tasks `EXECUTED`, no
`FROM-CACHE`. Both new tests ran on all six target sets (JVM, Android debug + release, iOS simulator,
macOS, wasmJs browser) and each passes **alone** under `--tests`.

closes #2316

author: michaelneale
body:
## Problem

Every vision request through the OpenAI surface fails with HTTP 502 `multimodal tokenization failed with status 2` / `multimodal prompt evaluation failed with status 1`. The native log shows the mechanism:

```
mtmd_tokenize: error: number of media markers in text (0) does not match number of bitmaps (1)
mtmd_encode_chunk_impl: image tokens batch is placeholder
failed to encode image slice
```

The model itself is fine — the same GGUF + mmproj through `llama-mtmd-cli --jinja` (built from the vendored llama.cpp checkout) describes images perfectly.

## Root cause

The vendored llama.cpp changed `mtmd_helper_bitmap_init_from_buf` when video support landed:

```c
// now: 4 args, returns a wrapper struct
mtmd_helper_bitmap_wrapper mtmd_helper_bitmap_init_from_buf(ctx, buf, len, bool placeholder);
struct mtmd_helper_bitmap_wrapper { mtmd_bitmap * bitmap; mtmd_helper_video * video_ctx; };
```

but `skippy-ffi` still declared the old 3-arg bare-pointer form. On aarch64 the wrapper's first field happens to come back in x0, so the bitmap pointer accidentally survived — but the new `placeholder` argument read **garbage from an unset register**. Whenever it read nonzero, llama.cpp constructed an empty placeholder bitmap, and every downstream encode failed at the placeholder gate. Text-only paths never call this helper, which is why nothing else broke.

## Fix

- Update the FFI declaration to the 4-arg wrapper-returning form (`MtmdHelperBitmapWrapper { bitmap, video_ctx }`), pass `placeholder = false`.
- Add `mtmd_helper_video_free` and free the video context alongside the bitmap in both `eval_media` and `eval_media_frame`.

## Verification

Muse-Glimmer-30B Q4_K_M + mmproj on M4/Metal, `POST /v1/chat/completions` with an `image_url` data-URI part:

- **Before**: 502 at the placeholder gate, native log `image tokens batch is placeholder`
- **After**: image preprocessing and encoding succeed — native log `encoding image slice... image slice encoded in 566 ms`, generation proceeds
- Text-only requests unchanged ("391" sanity check passes)
- Control: `llama-mtmd-cli --jinja` with identical model files works, confirming the break was in the FFI layer, not the model or vendored llama.cpp

Note: with this fix the image encodes and generation runs, but Glimmer's vision output then hits a separate response-parsing issue (`peg-native` chat parser rejects the vision-turn output) — that's an unrelated bug in the chat-format parser, will file separately. This PR fixes the FFI break that blocked all multimodal input at the bitmap layer.

Clippy clean on both crates.

The research behind #16 applies to `/blog` more directly than to the homepage:

> *"Nobody in this sample presents an undifferentiated list of everything they have written."*

author: tasinpongk-jpg
body:
## 1. The daily pipeline was running twice every weekday

The Cloudflare dispatcher fires `daily.yml` punctually via `workflow_dispatch`; the GHA `schedule:` backup lands 100–130 minutes later:

```
Aug 11: dispatcher 02:15:18 | GHA schedule 03:55:09  (+100 min)
Aug 12: dispatcher 02:15:59 | GHA schedule 04:18:00  (+123 min)
Aug 13: dispatcher 02:15:41 | GHA schedule 04:21:10  (+126 min)
```

`concurrency: group=daily` does not dedupe them — `cancel-in-progress: false` **queues** the backup and then runs the whole ~20-minute pipeline again. Two `daily snapshot` commits landed on `main` every weekday:

```
2026-08-13 02:40  +  04:45
2026-08-12 02:43  +  04:42
2026-08-11 02:42  +  04:19
```

That is double the SETSMART calls (232 tickers × 2), double the build, double the deploy.

A `guard` job now skips a `schedule` run once a `workflow_dispatch` run has succeeded the same UTC day. Queuing works in its favour: by the time the backup leaves the queue the dispatch run has concluded, so the check can see it. It **fails open** — if the API query fails the backup runs anyway, because a missed day costs more than a duplicate one.

The `build` job's `if:` needed the guard clause too; `always()` would otherwise have run it even when the pipeline was skipped.

## 2. Schedule documentation was wrong in nine places

Four files still described the daily run as `50 2 * * 1-5` / 09:50 BKK. The actual cron in both `cloudflare-cron/wrangler.toml` and `daily.yml` is `15 2 * * 1-5` / 09:15.

Both READMEs also claimed the concurrency group prevents double-runs, and the top-level one went further:

> On the rare day both trigger and the primary completes first, the backup's commit step is a no-op (data unchanged), so no duplicate snapshot commits.

Neither claim held. They don't fire at the same minute, queuing doesn't drop either run, and the commit step is never a no-op because `asOf` and `_built_at` are restamped on every build, so the data always differs. Both sections now describe what actually happens.

## 3. Action versions

Every workflow logged `The following actions target Node.js 20`, held together by `FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24`. Bumped to the **lowest** major of each action that is natively `node24` — verified by reading each `action.yml`, not assumed:

| Action | Was | Now | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actions/checkout` | v4 | **v5** | |
| `actions/setup-python` | v5 | **v6** | |
| `actions/setup-node` | v4 | **v5** | |
| `actions/upload-artifact` | v4 | **v6** | v5 is still `node20` |
| `actions/download-artifact` | v4 | **v7** | v5 **and** v6 are still `node20` |

The artifact actions were the trap — bumping them one major, as the others needed, would have left the deprecation in place. Latest majors (checkout v7, upload v7, download v8) exist but jump further than the deprecation requires; `setup-python@v7` for instance drops the `pip-install` input. Every input this repo passes (`name`, `path`, `if-no-files-found`, `retention-days`, `token`, `python-version`, `cache`, `cache-dependency-path`, `node-version`) exists in all target majors.

`FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24` is now dead weight and is removed from all six workflows.

## Verification

- All 7 workflow YAMLs parse; job graph is `guard → surveillance → build`
- Guard decision logic exercised across every branch: `""` → fail-open, `"0"` → run, `"1"`/`"2"` → skip, `"null"`/`"<html>"` → fail-open
- `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` — 72/72
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' -t tests` — 205/205
- `node tests/i18n-check.mjs` — 648 keys, EN/TH parity

**What CI here cannot prove:** `worker-test.yml` exercises `checkout@v5`, `setup-node@v5` and `setup-python@v6` on this push, but the artifact actions and the guard's API path only run inside `daily.yml`. Those first exercise on the next scheduled run (~04:00 UTC tomorrow) — that run is the real test of the dedupe, and the expected outcome is a skipped `surveillance`/`build` with one snapshot commit for the day instead of two.

## Still outstanding (not in this PR)

- **Deploy `main`** — `workflow_dispatch` is 403 for my token; needs one click, or it self-heals at the next daily run.
- **SEC iDisc timeouts** — needs a host that can reach `market.sec.or.th`.
- **`sec-bonds.json`, 60 days stale** — generator reads a local OneDrive path, can't run in CI.

author: hanthor
body:
Addresses the Tavern half of tuna-os/letters#16 (`--privileged` container mode audit). `tuna-os/letters` itself is archived (confirmed via the API — read-only, last push 2026-07-19), so no PR is possible there; this covers what's actually live and actionable.

## What I checked

All three Tavern workflows the issue names:

| Workflow | Job | `permissions:` before |
|---|---|---|
| `publish-flatpak.yml` | (workflow-level) | already explicit: `contents: write`, `packages: write` |
| `release.yml` | `build-flatpak` (the `--privileged` job) | already explicit: `contents: write` |
| `flatpak.yml` | `flatpak` (the `--privileged` job) | **none** — inherits the repo default |

Only `flatpak.yml` had a real gap.

## On `--privileged` itself

Checked the issue's recommendation #1 (verify it's strictly necessary) against the actual upstream tool: `flatpak/flatpak-github-actions`' own README uses `options: --privileged` in every single example (4/4), with no narrower alternative (`--security-opt seccomp=unconfined --cap-add=SYS_ADMIN`, as the issue suggested trying) documented anywhere. Bubblewrap needs it to build sandboxes inside the container. I don't have a real GitHub Actions runner to verify an alternative against, and this is a live Flatpak build/release pipeline — changing that blind on an unverified security tweak felt like the wrong tradeoff. Recommendation #3 (restrict permissions explicitly when privileged mode is required) is the part I could safely and verifiably act on.

## Change

Added `permissions: contents: read` to `flatpak.yml`'s `flatpak` job — it only checks out code and uploads a CI build artifact (no publish/release step), so read is the real ceiling it needs.

## Honest caveat

This repo's `default_workflow_permissions` is already `read` (confirmed via `gh api repos/tuna-os/Tavern`), so this job's `GITHUB_TOKEN` was already effectively read-only before this change. This makes that floor explicit rather than closing a currently-live gap — worth doing so the job doesn't silently inherit broader access if the repo/org default is ever changed, but I want to be upfront that it's a hardening/clarity fix, not a live-vulnerability fix.

author: fcoury
body:
## Why

The agent conversation introduced in #197 can be navigated as a viewport, but transcript text still cannot be addressed precisely with a cursor, selected with keyboard or mouse, or copied without rendered Markdown decoration.

Depends on #197.

## What Changed

- Focus scrollback with Tab and expose a visible Normal-mode cursor.
- Support arrow/Vim motions, counts, paging, viewport motions, word/paragraph motions, and character finds.
- Add Visual and Visual Line selection, mouse drag selection, and clipboard yanks.
- Make Esc return from Normal scrollback to the composer, and make i/a focus the composer and enter Insert mode in one keypress.
- Separate semantic Markdown content from display chrome so code frames, language labels, heading/quote bars, role labels, rules, streaming cursors, and table padding are neither highlighted nor copied.
- Preserve code blank lines, list/task structure, link labels, image alt text, visible HTML, Unicode, and logical wrapping; grid tables copy with tab-separated columns.

## How to Test

1. Check out this branch with #197 beneath it, run `cargo run`, and open an agent conversation with enough content to scroll.
2. Focus the composer, then press Tab. Move with j/k, arrows, counts, paging, and word motions; the cursor should cross blank rows without changing the composer draft.
3. Press v or V, extend with normal motions, and press y. Paste elsewhere and confirm only highlighted conversation content was copied. Repeat with a mouse drag followed by y.
4. Select a fenced Bash block. Its command should highlight and copy, while the `bash` title and `┌─`, `│`, `└─` frame glyphs should not.
5. From Normal scrollback, verify Esc returns to the composer. Re-enter scrollback and verify i and a each enter composer Insert mode with one keypress.
6. Regression: resize the pane and append streaming content while a selection exists; the logical selection should remain stable.

Closes the remaining gap in #909: PRs #910/#924 reset `cost`/`n_calls`/`n_consecutive_format_errors`/`_start_time`, but `run()` still accumulates `extra_template_vars |= {"task": task, **kwargs}` across invocations. author: mosser
body:
Follow-up to #77, and it depends on it: declaring severity once per code is only possible because that PR collapsed `conclusion-supported` into a single code.

## The problem

The validator reported 23 diagnostics — 16 errors, 7 warnings — and nothing recorded how any of them was decided. A duplicate element id was an error; a conclusion nothing supports was a warning; a template with no `@support` was a warning whose message read like a style note.

They weren't quite arbitrary. **Six checks already stated the rule**, all in nearly the same words — `checkConfigKeys`: *"A missing required key is an error: the compiler refuses to run without it. An unknown key is only a warning, because the compiler ignores keys it does not recognise."* It had just never been written down, so the other nine were decided by feel.

## The rule

> **A diagnostic is an error if and only if the compiler will reject the model.** Otherwise it is a warning.

One narrow exception: when the editor genuinely *cannot know* what the compiler will do, it warns and claims only what it knows. Today that is `unknown-unification-method` alone — the compiler's relation registry is populated at startup and a project may register its own.

What makes this worth having is that it is **decidable by experiment**. The compiler has no warning level at all (jpipe-compiler ADR-0016 removed it), so "noticed" and "rejected" are the same statement there, and every entry below was settled by writing a `.jd` file and running `jpipe diagnostic` on it — not by taste.

## What changed

**Three warnings were wrong and are now errors**, each verified against the compiler's own fixtures: `has-abstract-support` (`007_template_no_abstract.jd`), `strategy-supported` and `conclusion-supported` (both `002_unsupported_elements.jd`). On `007` the two tools now produce byte-identical output.

**Four stay warnings**, each verified to exit 0: `no-empty-label`, `no-empty-unit` (editor-only style rules — a corollary of the rule is that a check the compiler does not run can never be an error), `unknown-config-key` (unrecognised keys are ignored), and the exception.

**Severity is no longer a call-site decision.** It is declared once per code in `JpipeIssueSeverity` with its reason, and a new `report()` replaces all 23 `accept()` calls. Because it is a `Record` keyed on the code union, a code with no declared severity **fails to compile**; a test pins the warning set to the documented four so choosing `warning` stays deliberate.

`has-abstract-support` is also reworded to the compiler's own sentence — the advisory prose it had is why it read like a warning.

## Notes for review

- **The visible cost:** a model you are still writing shows errors sooner. Type `justification J { conclusion c is "C" }` and the conclusion is red until something supports it. - **The `conclusion-supported` collapse now rests on message text**, since both branches are errors. The two messages must stay distinct; the test that pinned severities now pins messages, with a comment saying why.

body:
This PR addresses the following issue in `mmdet3d/models/fbbev/streampetr/streampetr_v2.py`: rec_ego_pose length computed after propagated concat.

## Changes
- `mmdet3d/models/fbbev/streampetr/streampetr_v2.py`: rec_ego_pose length computed after propagated concat.

## Details
```diff
--- a/mmdet3d/models/fbbev/streampetr/streampetr_v2.py
+++ b/mmdet3d/models/fbbev/streampetr/streampetr_v2.py
@@ -1,1 +1,1 @@
-            rec_ego_pose = torch.eye(4, device=query_pos.device).unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0).repeat(B, query_pos.shape[1]+self.num_propagated, 1, 1)
+            rec_ego_pose = torch.eye(4, device=query_pos.device).unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0).repeat(B, query_pos.shape[1], 1, 1)
```

## Tests
- `tests/test_models/test_fbbev/test_streampetr_v2.py`

```diff
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_models/test_fbbev/test_streampetr_v2.py
@@ -0,0 +1,54 @@
+import torch
+import torch.nn as nn
+import pytest
+
+from mmdet3d.models.fbbev.streampetr.streampetr_v2 import SparseHead4BEV
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def patched_head(monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        'mmdet3d.models.fbbev.streampetr.streampetr_v2.pos2posemb3d',
+        lambda x: x)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        'mmdet3d.models.fbbev.streampetr.streampetr_v2.pos2posemb1d',
+        lambda x: x)
+
+    head = object.__new__(SparseHead4BEV)
+    head.num_propagated = 4
+    head.with_ego_pos = False
+    head.embed_dims = 256
+    head.memory_len = 8
+    head.query_embedding = nn.Linear(3, head.embed_dims)
+    head.time_embedding = nn.Linear(1, head.embed_dims)
+    head.pc_range = nn.Parameter(
+        torch.tensor([-50.0, -50.0, -5.0, 50.0, 50.0, 3.0]))
+
+    B = 2
+    head.memory_reference_point = torch.zeros(B, head.memory_len, 3)
+    head.memory_embedding = torch.zeros(B, head.memory_len, head.embed_dims)
+    head.memory_timestamp = torch.zeros(B, head.memory_len, 1)
+    head.memory_velo = torch.zeros(B, head.memory_len, 2)
+    head.memory_egopose = torch.eye(4, device='cpu').view(1, 1, 4, 4).repeat(
+        B, head.memory_len, 1, 1)
+    return head, B
+
+
+def test_temporal_alignment_rec_ego_pose_length(patched_head):
+    head, B = patched_head
+    num_query = 10
+    reference_points = torch.rand(B, num_query, 3)
+    query_pos = head.query_embedding(reference_points)
+    tgt = torch.zeros_like(query_pos)
+
+    _, query_pos_out, _, _, _, _, rec_ego_pose = head.temporal_alignment(
+        query_pos, tgt, reference_points)
+
+    expected_len = query_pos_out.shape[1]
+    assert rec_ego_pose.shape == (B, expected_len, 4, 4)
```

body:
<!-- popex-agent-handoff:v1 -->
```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "agent": "Integration + orchestrator — harmony pipeline",
  "cycle": "cycle-6c-harmonic-execution-layer",
  "status": "ready_for_review",
  "branch": "orchestrator/harmony-pipeline",
  "baseSha": "fd9828b4799916ed541ae740dda3eb54827ce0b1",
  "headSha": "eb23a0d75f3cb734141828ca5c1a37ab3f05520e",
  "pr": 87,
  "ownedPaths": ["app/harmony_pipeline.py", "tests/test_harmony_pipeline.py"],
  "unauthorizedFilesChanged": false,
  "ci": {"status": "passed", "run": 327},
  "mergeRecommendation": "merge"
}
```

## Scope

Implements issue #86: the harmonic-context execution layer. It loads the current canonical raw transcription and matching audio analysis, optionally reuses only a current safe editable pitched-part context, runs the evidence-aware inference engine, builds and atomically publishes the canonical harmony artifact, reloads it, and returns bounded musician-facing counts.

## Files changed

- `app/harmony_pipeline.py` — canonical evidence loading, provenance checks, optional interpretation reuse, protected inference boundary, artifact build/publication/reload verification, previous-artifact preservation, progress reporting, and detached result serialization.
- `tests/test_harmony_pipeline.py` — raw-only and interpretation-assisted success, exact processor inputs, stale/corrupt optional context fallback, timing fallback, provenance validation, no-pitch evidence, failure preservation, determinism, progress, security, and product-boundary coverage.

## Public or integration contract

`infer_harmony_job(...) -> HarmonyPipelineResult`:

- requires a readable canonical raw-transcription artifact and matching canonical analysis provenance;
- uses saved timing and tonal evidence without fabricating beats when timing is weak or missing;
- optionally uses editable pitched-part evidence only when raw schema/version/timestamp, analysis provenance, separation-presence flag, raw warning count, algorithm versions, and the complete source-event index all match the current raw artifact;
- treats missing interpretation as normal and falls back to raw-only inference on unreadable, malformed, or stale interpretation with bounded path-free warnings;
- never requires stems, Demucs, PyTorch, model weights, GPU, cloud compute, or paid APIs;
- accepts an injectable inference processor for testing but requires a `HarmonyInferenceResult`;
- publishes `harmony/harmonic-context.json`, reloads it, and verifies semantic equality before reporting success;
- returns artifact path, event/segment/resolution counts, optional-context usage, warnings, and a detached payload.

## Failure and preservation semantics

- Load, inference, type, validation, publication, progress-callback, and verification failures surface bounded path-free errors.
- Upstream raw transcription, analysis, and editable interpretation are never modified.
- Existing valid harmonic context remains intact when a retry fails before publication.
- Verification failures attempt to restore the previous valid harmony artifact when one existed.
- The raw pitched-note evidence remains authoritative; optional interpretation contributes provenance only.

## Validation

- CI #327 / run ID `31769445368` / job ID `94672120447`: passed on exact helper-free head `eb23a0d75f3cb734141828ca5c1a37ab3f05520e`.
- Full repository pytest: `1178 passed, 1 warning in 38.58s`.
- `python -m compileall -q app tests`: passed.
- `node --check app/static/app.js`: passed.
- The warning is the existing FastAPI/Starlette TestClient deprecation only.
- Final comparison against `main@fd9828b4799916ed541ae740dda3eb54827ce0b1` contains exactly the two owned files; all one-shot repair workflow/script files were removed.

## Progress contract

Ordered monotonic stages:

1. `loading_raw_transcription`
2. `loading_analysis_context`
3. `loading_optional_interpretation`
4. `inferring_harmonic_context`
5. `validating_harmonic_context`
6. `saving_harmonic_context`
7. `completed`

## Risks and limitations

This is a conservative harmonic-candidate pipeline, not a final chord chart or score. It does not generate Roman numerals, exact voicings, tablature, notation, MusicXML, MIDI, engraving, or publication-ready output. Durable SQLite state, API orchestration, and frontend review are intentionally separate subsequent layers.

## Final recommendation

`READY FOR INTEGRATION REVIEW` — exact two-file ownership and full CI are green.

author: shaboooooozy1
body:
## Summary

The task was to find a TODO comment and implement it. There are **no literal `TODO`/`FIXME` comments** anywhere in the codebase (verified with a recursive, case-insensitive search across all `.cs`, `.json`, `.md`, and `.ps1` files). The closest genuinely *unfinished / inconsistent* piece of code was a null-safety gap, which this PR completes.

## The problem

`Firefox.PopulateHistory` guards against `System.DBNull` values returned by SQLite before casting them to `string` (see `Firefox.cs:178-179`). The equivalent `Chromium.PopulateHistory` did **not**:

```csharp
string url = (string)reader[0];
string title = (string)reader[1];   // throws InvalidCastException on DBNull
```

Chrome's `urls.title` column is nullable, so a single history entry with a `NULL` title would throw `InvalidCastException`, aborting the entire history load and leaving the plugin returning no results.

## The change

Apply the same null-safety the Firefox reader already uses, in `Chromium.cs`:

- Skip an entry when its `url` is `NULL` (the URL is essential — there's nothing to open without it).
- Fall back to an empty string when only the `title` is `NULL`, so the entry stays usable and is shown by its URL instead of being dropped.

This makes the Chromium path consistent with the already-proven Firefox path and prevents a single malformed row from breaking history search.

## Testing

The project targets `net9.0-windows` with WPF and references PowerToys DLLs that are not committed to the repo (they live in an un-committed `libs/` folder that must be copied from a PowerToys install), so it cannot be built or run on this Linux CI environment. The change is a minimal, self-contained edit using the standard `SqliteDataReader.IsDBNull` API in the exact pattern already present and working in `Firefox.cs`.
