author: zarda
body:
## What

The Xcode project gains its first test target. `AppTests` is a standalone XCTest logic bundle (no host app) covering the three Swift seams of the share pipeline: the extension's sidecar writer, the App Group store behind `ShareIntakePlugin`, and the data-URL strip Vision OCR decodes through — 21 tests, driven against temp directories, run locally with `npm run test:ios`.

## Why

The Swift half of the share pipeline had zero automated coverage; every defect that shipped there (octet-stream typing, destroy-on-drain, wreckage re-walked forever) was found by reading and fixed on faith plus a hand-driven simulator session. The web gates are structurally blind to this code and three docs said so. This turns those hand checks into a suite.

## How

- The plugin logic moves out of its Capacitor shell: `ShareIntakeStore` (pure Foundation, folder passed in) carries collect/complete/clear, the wreckage sweep and the orphan grace; `DataURL` carries the strip and is shared with the Vision OCR plugin. The shells shrink to App Group lookup plus forwarding. Behavior-identical — the shipped app builds and runs unchanged.
- `ShareViewController.swift` is compiled into the test bundle directly (an extension target cannot be imported), with `stash` and `acceptedTypes` widened to internal.
- The `AppTests` target is hand-added to the pbxproj in the same synthetic-id convention as the ShareExtension target. No `TEST_HOST`, nothing linked but XCTest: booting the whole Capacitor app to test file operations buys nothing. XCUITest of the share sheet was considered and rejected — the documented manual procedure covers what fragile cross-app automation would.
- `npm run test:ios` runs the suite (destination iPhone 17; edit one string for another machine). Local only for now, by choice: CI stays untouched, and the docs say "not enforced" rather than "not covered". ADR 0040 records the trade-offs.

## Testing

- The 21 tests pin: concrete-MIME resolution for jpg/png/pdf with the octet-stream fallback, all four sidecar keys plus a fresh epoch stamp, payload bytes surviving the copy, rollback on copy failure, `.jpeg` leading the accepted types (the HEIC transcode guarantee), fetch-without-delete, wreckage and stale-orphan sweeping with the write-order grace, exact-id completion with path-traversal ids refused, clear, sidecar-only counting, and the any-mediatype strip. Suite green in two consecutive `xcodebuild test` runs and once through `npm run test:ios`.
- The full web gate list is untouched and green: lint, all six checks, 3930 unit specs, 422 date specs in each of two timezones, 326 emulator smoke specs, production build. Dev-server boot verified clean.

author: pablof7z-agent
body:
Refs #1495

## Why

The last two lane-bootstrap failure falsifiers still required `WakeLaneProbeStore`, a full `EventStore` forwarding implementation. That fake backend keeps false store substitutability alive and blocks concrete inner runtime assembly.

## Change

- add one construction-armed, one-shot Redb lane-bootstrap refusal at the existing pre-commit boundary
- prove a route-less bootstrap is a healthy no-op and does not consume the arm
- prove the staged refusal rolls back, preserves its independent route revision, and a same-store retry commits the exact lanes
- migrate both core falsifiers to real temporary Redb and the concrete #1537 read counter
- delete `WakeLaneProbeStore` and its forwarding/counter bridge

No production setting, controller, enum, setter, persistent constructor, or generalized fault framework is added.

## Proof

- deliberate neutralization: removing constructor arming makes the store and both core failure tests red
- deliberate sticky fault: replacing `mem::take` with a persistent read makes the same-store retry and second core intent red
- `cargo test -p nmp-store --all-features`

author: skylerberg
body:
`scripts/test-guards.mjs` holds 12 guards, each naming a bug, the source edit that reintroduces it, and the narrow test that must then fail. `check:all` ran only `check:test-guards:anchors`, which confirms each `find` still matches once and stops — so **the number of guards CI actually proved was zero**.

The full run did prove them, but by rewriting tracked source on disk, running vitest, and writing it back. That is why it could not go in CI, and it is what produced a spurious "the guard is stale" report for a concurrent reader during a recent audit.

## What changed

- **The mutation arrives through vite**, not through the file. An `enforce: 'pre'` transform applies the edit as the module is transformed, so no guard run writes to the source tree.
- **Four jobs at a time.** 12 guards go from 42.6s serial to ~15s; 36 would land near 40s. A pool of 4 is the knee — 8 barely improves wall time while doubling total CPU. Each job takes its own dep-optimizer cache, the separation `check:a11y` got in 4e8fb04.
- **Five verdicts** — CAUGHT, STILL-PASSED, NO-TESTS-RAN, NEVER-APPLIED, RUN-FAILED — split on whether the marker appeared and whether vitest printed a summary, so an infrastructure death no longer reads as a stale anchor.
- **`--selftest`**, and `check:all` now runs the real thing.

## Why the positive control exists

The first version of `--selftest` had three controls, all expecting a *non*-catch. Review neutered the plugin so it wrote the marker but returned the code unchanged: **the selftest passed green while the full run reported 12/12 guards dead.** A fourth control now expects an unmodified guard to still bite. Re-checked by hand — that break exits 1, and the tree restores byte-identical.

## Verification

- `npm run check:test-guards` — 12/12 caught. `--selftest` — 4/4. `--verify-only` — 0.26s.
- `npm run check` 935 files / 0 errors; `npm test` 141 files / 2772 tests, unchanged.
- Inertness proved by resolved-config comparison, not by "tests still pass": with the env unset the plugin list and cacheDir are identical to HEAD's, and a full 12-guard run leaves the `src`+`scripts` tree hash unchanged.

author: mp2ez
body:
Closes DEBUG-419

Onboarding folded the wellness-data processing consent into the granted `ConsentRecord` with `legalGate?.mentalHealthProcessingConsent ?? true`, so an unreadable gate record persisted a sensitive-data consent the user never affirmed in that session.

## This deliberately reverses DEBUG-382 — read before reviewing

`git log -S'?? true'` pins that line to `8cd0e560` ("fix: DEBUG-382 a failed legal-gate read no longer records a granted Art. 9 consent as refused", PR #282, **Done**), which replaced an earlier `?? false`. DEBUG-419's literal AC asked to restore `false`; that was **not** implemented.

DEBUG-382's finding was right, its remedy was not. Both values write a DERIVED value into a field whose sole evidentiary purpose is to record a USER ACT — one fabricates a grant, the other a refusal, and neither is what happened. `renewConsent` (FEAT-399) had already adjudicated this same field the same way and re-asks; two live paths cannot hold opposite postures on one field's provenance.

The gate invariant is *stronger* than DEBUG-382 claimed, and cuts against it: `CombinedLegalGateScreen`'s catch does not call `onComplete()`, so advancing proves the **write succeeded** — an unreadable record later is post-write destruction of unknown scope, in which we cannot know only this field was lost.

## A worse defect neither item named

`getLegalGateConsents` blind-cast `JSON.parse(stored) as LegalGateConsents`. `as` has no runtime effect, so any parseable value came back as a record — one *present but missing the consent field* left the caller's `if (!legalGate)` guard **false**, so the coalesce fired with **nothing logged at all**. The null path at least logged.

## Changes

- `OnboardingScreen.tsx` — coalesce deleted; on a null read, log at high severity and `navigation.replace('LegalGate')`. A `return`, never a `throw` — the catch below ends in `navigateNext()` and would reopen the fail-open path.
- `consentStore.ts` — runtime shape validation on every field. Null now distinguishes **absent** (legitimate, unlogged), **read_failed**, **shape_invalid**; faults log a reason and deliberately not the record contents, which are consent evidence.
- Legal citation corrected throughout to state-law sensitive-data opt-in (TDPSA/CPA/VCDPA/CTDPA) + FTC Act s5, with GDPR Art. 9(2)(a) contingent — `regulatory-applicability.md` makes GDPR conditional on serving EU users. The standard does not relax.
- DEBUG-382's suite rewritten in place with a reversal header; new 18-case suite on the read boundary; `consentInvariant` header no longer claims to underwrite a reconstruction.

Fail-closed here means **re-ask**, never blocking crisis access: LegalGate's 988 footer is unconditional and is the only crisis affordance at that point.

## Verification

`npm run precommit` against the merged tree, exit code captured under `set -o pipefail`:

```
PRECOMMIT_EXIT=0
No new lint errors. 403/427 errors across 189 files.
Test Suites: 14 passed  Tests: 320 passed   (test:safety)
Test Suites: 7 passed   Tests: 141 passed   (test:clinical)
Test Suites: 76 passed  Tests: 808 passed   (test:unit)
Test Suites: 22 passed  Tests: 273 passed   (test:privacy)
```

Plus both allowlisted suites run explicitly: `OnboardingScreen.test.tsx` 10/10, `consentStore.test.ts` 68/68.

Phase 2.5 Maestro gate correctly skipped — no safety-surface path changed (the one `features/consent/` file is a test header, excluded by the `__tests__/` filter).

author: lucasccordeiro
body:
`llvm/struct_method` is plain C — a function-pointer struct member called as
`x.update()` — so §81's scope question is answered: Phase 6 work, not one of
§63.1's C++-only arms.

`goto_convert`'s `do_function_call` accepts a symbol or a dereference as callee,
and `adjust_side_effect_function_call`'s implicit-dereference step supplies the
latter. Without that pass the `member` node arrives bare. The rewrite is driven
only by the callee's type, depends on no adjustment, and surfaces after
migration — so by §80's rule it belongs in the native walk.

The arm also unwraps an *implicit* `address_of` callee. `address_of2t` carries no
`implicit` flag, so that half is deliberately not mirrored: it would have to be
guessed, and guessing wrong is silent. If it matters it will show up as a
divergence or an error, not as a bad rewrite.

| | before this series | now |
|---|---:|---:|
| `-only` divergences | 1 808 | **1 623** |
| `-only` errors | 304 | **185** |
| sampled *real* errors | 14 | **0** |

The sample's remaining 10 are pre-existing parse failures that fail flag-off too,
so the 303-test sample is exhausted as an instrument — the full-corpus 185 is the
number to work from next.

**Gate:** default path **0 of 2 809**; shadow unchanged at **2**; `cstd` 142/142;
`llvm/struct_method` and `llvm/sizeof` pass.
`regression/esbmc/irep2_only_fnptr_callee` pins the dereferenced callee, and
disabling the rewrite reproduces the original error and fails it. The test pins
only the callee — `-only` still mislowers other parts of that function, and
freezing that would pin bugs the remaining arms still have.

Stacked on #7006. Refs #4715

author: andersondalmina
body:
An agent working in this repo had nothing to read and nothing to stop it: no description of the three-process boundary it must not cross, no CI, and tests covering only three main-process services. This adds the context, the guardrails, the sensors and the CI, wired so Claude Code and opencode both read the same rules.

## Context

`AGENTS.md` is the contract — project overview, commands, the main/preload/renderer architecture, conventions and guardrails — with `CLAUDE.md` pointing at it so both tools read one file. Three path-scoped rule files in `.github/instructions/` carry the non-negotiables of each boundary: spawn CLIs with argument arrays rather than shell strings, keep SQL inside `db.ts`, add an IPC channel across all four files or not at all.

## Guardrails

Declarative on both sides — a `permissions` block in `.claude/settings.json`, a `permission.bash` table in `opencode.json`. Recursive deletes, `git reset --hard`, force pushes, `git clean` and `chmod 777` are denied; pushing, committing, adding a dependency and anything that writes to GitHub or GitLab ask first. `rm one-file.txt` stays fine.

**The one thing to check while reviewing:** the two files resolve matches by opposite rules. Claude Code takes deny before ask before allow; opencode takes the *last* pattern that matches. `opencode.json` is therefore ordered allow → ask → deny on purpose, and putting a deny above an ask there silently downgrades it. `AGENTS.md` documents this.

The only code in the harness is a Stop hook (`.claude/hooks/verify-done.mjs`). It runs `make check` when a turn ends with a dirty tree and hands the failure back, so finishing means the checks pass. It cannot be declarative: it has to skip a clean tree and check `stop_hook_active` so a block cannot loop.

`.opencode/agents/` holds a `reviewer` and `fixer` agent written against this codebase — both `mode: primary`, so Workestrator's own board actions can be pointed at them. `.opencode/commands` is a symlink to `.claude/commands`, so `/check` and `/ipc` are one file rather than two copies. (A Windows clone with `core.symlinks=false` gets a text file and simply won't find the commands — degradation, not breakage. Noted in `AGENTS.md`.)

## Sensors

The ~1,000 lines of pure logic that had no tests now have 158, taking the suite from 17 to 175:

- `repoUrl.ts` — parses untrusted remotes; eight spellings of one repository collapse onto a single URL, GitLab nested groups, `/pull/12` trimming
- `pullRequests.ts` — every column and status-precedence rule, relative time on a frozen clock
- `selectors.ts` and `workspaceReducer.ts` — filters, the project-removal cascade, review dedup, and the two buffers bounding how much of a review is held in memory

The reducer reads `localStorage` while it loads, so those run against jsdom. `src/test/setup.ts` installs an in-memory store because Node's own inert `localStorage` global shadows jsdom's. No source file was changed to make anything testable.

## Feedback loops

Three points: opencode formats an edited file as it goes (built-in formatter, picks up the existing Prettier), husky + lint-staged fix and verify what is staged, and CI runs format, lint, typecheck and test as four parallel jobs on every PR — `fail-fast: false`, so one push reports every failure rather than the first.

Also adds the `LICENSE` the package has always claimed, a `Makefile` fronting the npm scripts, and a `typecheck` script that was missing.

## The CI found a real bug on its first run

Worth reading the last two commits, because they are not cosmetic.

`npm ci` failed immediately: adding jsdom had left the tree half-resolved. vitest 4 brings its own vite 8, whose optional `esbuild` peer wants `^0.27 || ^0.28`, and npm had deduped it onto the `0.21.5` that vite 5 hoists. `npm ls` called the tree invalid, but a working `node_modules` hid it — every check passed locally while the lockfile was unusable on a clean machine. Regenerating it fixed that.

It then failed again for a second reason: npm 10 (bundled with Node 22) and npm 11 disagree about whether that optional peer belongs in the lockfile. Neither is wrong, but a lockfile can only be one of them. CI now pins npm 11 and reads its Node version from a new `.nvmrc`, so the two environments match by construction rather than coincidence, and prints both versions since that is the first thing worth knowing when an install behaves differently in two places. CI runs on Node 24.18.0 / npm 11.19.0.

## Reviewing

Four commits, meant to be read in order:

1. Prettier-only reflow of five files that predate anyone running it — no behaviour change, split out so it is not noise inside the harness diff
2. The harness itself
3. The lockfile repair
4. The CI toolchain pin

All four CI checks pass. `make check` is green locally against a clean `npm ci`: 175 tests, typecheck clean, one pre-existing lint warning at `WorkspaceProvider.tsx:611` (a non-component export breaking Fast Refresh) left alone as out of scope.

## Why the backend half matters

The sweeps walk every active tenant in one loop with no isolation, so a schema mid-creation or behind on migrations raises and **every remaining tenant silently stops being polled**. #446 made the weather sweep newly dependent on a post-0077 table, which exposed it; the fragility predates that and both imagery sweeps share the shape.

That failure was real on `main`, not a flake — and it looked green because `backend-integration` is `continue-on-error`, so the **run** reported success while the **check** was failing.

Prod was not affected: only two tenants are active there and both carry the table. The schema at alembic `0052` is inactive so the sweep skips it — luck rather than design, which this converts into design.

author: trek-e
body:
## Fix PR

---

## Linked Issue

Fixes #3190

---

## What was broken

`/gsd:code-review-fix <phase> --auto` re-ran the review after each fix round and rewrote `REVIEW.md` in place every iteration, but the workflow's single end-of-run docs commit staged only `REVIEW-FIX.md`. So the committed `REVIEW.md` stayed at iteration 1 and contradicted the committed `REVIEW-FIX.md`, while the converged `REVIEW.md` and the `.iterN.md` backups survived only as uncommitted working-tree state that any tree cleanup discards.

A coupled defect in the same commit step defeated even the `REVIEW-FIX.md` commit: the two inline frontmatter validators exported `REVIEW_PATH` into a `node -e` body that reads `process.env.FIX_REPORT_PATH` (a name never exported into that subshell). `readFileSync(undefined)` threw, the trace was swallowed by `2>/dev/null`, and `HAS_STATUS`/`FIX_FRONTMATTER` were always empty — so `REVIEW-FIX.md` was never committed and the rendered summary had blank counts.

## What this fix does

- In `--auto` mode the single docs commit now stages the converged `REVIEW.md` alongside `REVIEW-FIX.md`, so the two committed artifacts agree. Non-`--auto` single-pass runs never rewrite `REVIEW.md` and are left untouched (the new staging is guarded on `AUTO_MODE`).
- Both inline validators (`HAS_STATUS`, `FIX_FRONTMATTER`) now export `FIX_REPORT_PATH` to match the `process.env.FIX_REPORT_PATH` their bodies read, so the status check fires for well-formed reports and the summary fields populate.
- On successful convergence the spent `.iterN.md` backups are removed so the phase directory is clean (`git status --porcelain` reports no dirty review/backup files). They are retained when the loop degrades (hit `MAX_ITERATIONS` / fixer failure) for post-mortem analysis. Backup creation is unchanged.

## Root cause

`gsd-core/workflows/code-review-fix.md` (introduced in `99c089bfb`, #1630). The `--auto` loop's single docs commit was designed for `REVIEW-FIX.md` only; the fact that the loop also mutates `REVIEW.md` was not reflected in the commit's `--files` list. The two validator sites are a copy/paste of the `REVIEW_PATH=...` pattern from the review-status parsers into scripts that read `FIX_REPORT.md`, without renaming the exported env var to match the `process.env.FIX_REPORT_PATH` the pasted body reads.

## Testing

### How I verified the fix

- `tests/code-review-fix-pipeline-regression.test.cjs` (new) — behavioral + docs-parity, mirroring the established `code-review-pipeline-regression.test.cjs` pattern. T1/T2 execute the actual validator body via the `process-seam` against a real temp `REVIEW-FIX.md` (proves the body prints `valid` when `FIX_REPORT_PATH` is wired, and silently fails when it is unset — the mis-wiring). T3–T6 are docs-parity on the deployed workflow text (env-name pairing, `REVIEW.md` staged in `--auto`, convergence cleanup).
- `npm run lint:ci` exits 0 locally (includes `lint-allow-test-rule-refs` at the bumped 300/300 ceiling and `lint-emitted-drift-ack` validating the new growth acknowledgment).

### Regression test added?

- [x] Yes — added a test that would have caught this bug

### Platforms tested

- [x] macOS
- [ ] Windows (including backslash path handling)
- [ ] Linux
- [ ] N/A (not platform-specific)

### Runtimes tested

- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Gemini CLI
- [ ] OpenCode
- [ ] Other: ___
- [x] N/A (not runtime-specific — the workflow text is copied verbatim to every runtime layout; the fix is in the shared workflow file)

---

## Checklist

- [x] Issue linked above with `Fixes #3190`
- [x] Linked issue has the `confirmed-bug` label
- [x] Fix is scoped to the reported bug — no unrelated changes included
- [x] Regression test added (or explained why not)
- [x] All existing tests pass (`npm test`)
- [x] `.changeset/` fragment added (`Fixed`, `pr: 0` until the PR number is known, then updated)
- [x] No unnecessary dependencies added

## Breaking changes

None. The commit message, commit count (still one docs commit), and non-`--auto` behavior are unchanged. `REVIEW.md` now also lands in the single `--auto` docs commit where it previously did not.

author: srummanf
body:
## Background

Route optimization can be an expensive operation because it coordinates distance lookup, solving, and route geometry work. Before this change, clicking Optimize repeatedly while a calculation was already running could start duplicate requests for the same set of stops and make the route state confusing.

## What changed

This update makes the frontend keep a single active optimization request at a time. While a route calculation is running, Optimize is disabled and shows a loading state, while Clear remains available.

The route state now also uses a generation guard so that clearing the map while a request is still in flight prevents a late response from drawing an old route or restoring cleared stats and stops.

A focused browser test fixture was added for successful completion, failure recovery, repeated clicks, and clearing before a delayed response settles. The implementation handoff recorded that syntax checks and local DOM-simulated fixture scenarios passed; a full real-browser fixture run was not available in the implementation container.

## User-facing effect

Users should see clearer progress during optimization, avoid accidental duplicate calculations from repeated clicks, and be able to clear the map without a late route response repopulating the cleared view.

author: steveweed79
body:
Asked whether the install page is a good enough test for *"has the build reached the box"*. It is — the version stamp names the file actually on the shelf, read out of the APK at publish time. But checking the headers rather than reading the config found the one thing that would have made it lie.

## The defect

```
header /index.html Cache-Control "no-cache"
```

**This never matched.** `header` runs before `try_files` — the same ordering the `@apk` matcher directly above it is built around, and the reason *that* one has to test for the file existing. A request for `/app/` is still `/` when the header is evaluated, so the header landed only on `/app/index.html`, a URL nobody types.

Measured, before:

| path | Cache-Control |
|---|---|
| `/app/` | *(none)* |
| `/app/index.html` | `no-cache` |

## Why it matters here specifically

With no `Cache-Control`, a browser is free to heuristically cache the page. So the one job it has — refresh it, read the version, decide whether today's build arrived — could be answered from memory, showing yesterday's stamp.

That is worse than having no test, because it looks like an answer.

## The fix

Matched by what it is **not**:

```
@page not path *.apk
header @page Cache-Control "no-cache"
```

The APK deliberately keeps its caching. It is forty megabytes, and revalidating it on every visit would undo the point of a stable link.

## Verification

Generated a test config **from this file** rather than a hand-copy — the earlier round of this investigation produced a false negative from a stale Caddy process serving a previous config, so the check had to come from the real thing.

| path | result |
|---|---|
| `/app/` | `no-cache` · `text/html` |
| `/app/index.html` | `no-cache` · `text/html` |
| `/app/steading.apk` | cacheable · `application/vnd.android.package-archive` |
| `/app/steading-0.9.9-99.apk` (pruned build) | lands on the page as `text/html` |

Config-only — no code, no tests, nothing to run. Takes effect on the next `deploy.sh`, which validates and reloads the Caddyfile.

+import torch

+

author: danny-avila
body:
Resolves #14812

## Summary

Uploading the same document for File Search twice embedded it twice. Every upload minted a fresh `crypto.randomUUID()` and posted the bytes to the RAG API's `/embed`, so identical content was chunked and embedded again under a new `file_id`, and each subsequent `file_search` query fanned out over both copies.

`file_search` uploads now hash their bytes and reuse embeddings that already exist for the same content.

## How it works

Uploads on the `file_search` path stream a SHA-256 of the staged file and persist it as `hash`, then look for an already-embedded record with the same content. What happens on a match depends on **who owns the embeddings** — the RAG API stamps `entity_id` as the document owner and refuses reads from any other owner, so content can only be shared between records embedded under the same one:

| Upload | RAG owner | On a content match |
|---|---|---|
| Chat attachment (`message_attachment`) | the user (no `entity_id`) | create the record as usual, but skip `/embed` and store `vectorId` — the document its chunks live under |
| Agent knowledge file (`agents`) | the agent | reuse only if the match already belongs to **that agent's** `file_search` resource, in which case the existing record is returned instead of adding a duplicate entry |

Records carrying an expiry (retention deadline or the upload TTL) are never reused as a source — their vectors are on a deletion clock the new upload doesn't share.

## Why records stay separate

The issue offers this as the acceptable shape, and it's the safer one:

> If creating a new file reference is required for each chat or agent, ideally that reference would point to the existing indexed document rather than triggering the file to be embedded again.

Each upload keeps its own `file_id` and its own stored object, so nothing about the file lifecycle changes for callers — deleting one attachment can't break another chat that happens to hold the same document.

To make that safe, `processDeleteRequest` counts the files still pointing at a vector document and clears `embedded` on any record that would destroy embeddings another one is using. Every RAG delete path already treats that as "nothing to remove", so the guard holds in one place instead of each storage strategy learning about sharing. Within a single delete batch exactly one record drops each shared document.

`resolveVectorId` is the single reader used by all three RAG read sites and both delete paths. Files that own their vectors store no `vectorId` and resolve to themselves, so **existing records need no migration** and behave exactly as before.

## Also fixed

Deduplicating query fan-out by resolved vector id in `fileSearch.js` meant pairing each response with its file at call time. That incidentally fixes result attribution: `validResults` was indexed against the *unfiltered* `files` array, so one failed query misattributed every later file's citations to the wrong file.

## Scope note

For chat attachments the file library still shows one entry per upload — that's the deliberate trade for keeping per-record deletion independent. What's gone is the duplicate embedding cost, the duplicate vector rows, and the duplicate query round trip.

## Changes

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `packages/data-schemas` | `hash` + `vectorId` on the File schema/type, two partial indexes, `findVectorReuseCandidates` and `countVectorReferences` |
| `packages/api` | new `files/vectors.ts` — `hashFileContent`, `resolveVectorId`, `dedupeByVectorId`, `pickVectorReuseSource`, `suppressSharedVectorDeletes`; `deleteRagFile` addresses the resolved document |
| `packages/data-provider` | `hash` + `vectorId` on `TFile` |
| `api` | reuse lookup wired into `processAgentFileUpload`; reference guard in `processDeleteRequest`; resolved ids + dedupe in `fileSearch.js`, `createContextHandlers.js`, `VectorDB/crud.js` |

## Testing

75 new tests, all verified red against the pre-change code:

- `packages/api/src/files/vectors.spec.ts` — 23 (real streamed hashing over temp files; reuse and suppression policy)
- `packages/data-schemas/src/methods/file.vectors.spec.ts` — 15 (real `mongodb-memory-server`; owner/hash/context/tenant/expiry scoping, reference counting)
- `api/server/services/Files/process.vectors.spec.js` — 16 (upload reuse for both owner cases, refcounted deletes)
- `api/app/clients/prompts/createContextHandlers.spec.js` — 7 (new file)
- `api/server/services/Files/VectorDB/crud.spec.js` — 4 (new file)
- `api/test/app/clients/tools/util/fileSearch.test.js`, `packages/api/src/files/rag.spec.ts` — extended

Full `api` workspace suite passes (3746 tests; the one `initialize.spec.js` failure and the `libreoffice.spec.ts` missing-fixture failure both reproduce on a clean tree).

author: echuquillanqui
body:
### Motivation

- Añadir la posibilidad de indicar el tipo de examen de laboratorio (`M`, `B`, `T`, `S`) tanto en la generación individual como en bloque para que cada orden clínica ligue una ficha de laboratorio correspondiente.

### Description

- Backend: se agregó el campo `laboratory_period` a `orders` (migración `2026_08_14_010000_add_laboratory_period_to_orders_table.php`) y validación para `laboratory_period` en `OrderController::store`, `OrderController::storeBulk` y `OrderController::update` usando `in:M,B,T,S`.
- Lógica: se implementaron los métodos `createLaboratoryOrder()` y `addLaboratoryItems()` en `OrderController` para crear una `LaboratoryOrder` vinculada a la orden clínica y poblar sus `items` con los exámenes FISSAL del periodo seleccionado; también se sincronizan los exámenes si cambia el periodo.
- Modelos/relaciones: se añadió `laboratory_period` al `fillable` de `Order`, la relación `Order::laboratoryOrder()` y la relación inversa `LaboratoryOrder::order()`; `laboratory_orders` ahora puede referenciar `orders` (clave foránea única, cascadeOnDelete).
- UI: vistas actualizadas para exponer la selección del periodo en la generación individual y en bloque y mostrar una columna `Examen Lab.` en el listado; el modal de edición recibe/actualiza `laboratory_period` y el JS rellena el campo (`data-laboratory-period`).
- Tests: se añadieron tests funcionales en `tests/Feature/FissalLaboratoryTest.php` que verifican que una orden individual genera la ficha de laboratorio con los exámenes del periodo elegido y que la generación en bloque permite periodos distintos por paciente.

### Testing

- Se ejecutaron comprobaciones de sintaxis PHP con `php -l` sobre los archivos modificados y devolvieron sin errores para `OrderController`, `Order`, `LaboratoryOrder` y la migración añadida.  
- Se agregaron tests de característica PHPUnit (`FissalLaboratoryTest`) pero no fue posible ejecutar la suite porque el entorno no tenía las dependencias instaladas (`vendor/autoload.php` ausente), por lo que `php artisan test --filter=FissalLaboratoryTest` no pudo ejecutarse en este entorno.  
- Herramientas de formateo/lint (`./vendor/bin/pint`) tampoco estaban disponibles en el entorno de ejecución, por lo que no se ejecutaron.  
- `git` y las comprobaciones de diff locales se usaron para verificar los cambios aplicados y no se detectaron conflictos de diff en los archivos modificados.

body:
Closes #63

Reframed ADR 0004 so `display ≥ title` reads as the library's shipped default (and the expectation for a text-led hero) rather than a universal invariant, and recorded the drawn-mark case — where a consumer deliberately sets `--text-display` below `--text-title` — as a sanctioned exception that breaks nothing, since no component compares the two at runtime. Also corrected the renderTokens test's name/comment to say it guards the shipped defaults against the historical swap regressing (assertion unchanged), so consumers no longer read the inversion as a contract violation.

author: wiper556
body:
シミュレーターの指摘3件。1311のスキルの作り直し、「(加勢時のみ)」の表示、人数入力欄の新設。

## 1. No.1311 蛇神幻計 が根本的に違っていた

「部隊総防御力55%上昇」なのに注記だけで自動反映しておらず、01スキル欄に手で数値を
入れる運用になっていた。そのため**個々の武将の防御%上昇**として扱われ、画面上は
「防御力が3000%上昇するスキル」に見えていた。

同型の怨龍烈牙・謀神ノ加護が既に `totalDefBoostPct` を使っているので、そちらに載せ替えた。

```
総防御力  LV10=55 / TR1=58 / TR2=62 / TR3=67 / TR4=73 / TR5=80 / TR6=84
確率      LV10=40 / TR1=42 / TR2=45 / TR3=50 / TR4=55 / TR5=60 / TR6=70
```

確率はユーザー提供のゲーム内鍛錬表で確認。**ixanary は TR1〜TR5 を一律+60% と
載せているが誤り**で、うちの武将データ（42/45/50/55/60）が正しかった。

### leaderOnly が誰にも見られていなかった

部隊長時限定のフラグはデータ側にあるだけで、総攻撃力・総防御力の集計から
参照されていなかった。小隊に置いても効いてしまう状態。集計4箇所に判定を足した。

```
部隊長に置く → 部隊防御力 × 名声補正 × (1 + 防御力上昇/100) × 総防御力上昇(+55%)
小隊1に置く → 付かない
```

## 2. 月読ノ冥略に「(加勢時のみ)」が出ない

注記を出す処理が `実発動率: -` で先に return する後ろにあり、**発動率を持たない
スキルには出なかった**。注記は発動率の有無と関係ないので、先に求めて両方の分岐で出す。

## 3. 「同じ兵種の武将数」の入力欄（神将火剣）

「自軍内で同じ兵種を指揮している武将数×12%」は防御参加武将数とは別の変数で、
部隊の中身からも計算できない。効果欄の**下**に入力欄を出して書いてもらう形にした。

- そのスキルが入っている枠にだけ出る
- ラベルはその列の兵士名（`鉄砲足軽 参加武将数`）
- **値は兵士名をキーに保持**。同じ兵士の列は連動し、違えば連動しない（弓足軽と長弓兵は別物）

既存の `variableFormula` に `sameSoldierCount` を1つ足しただけなので、同じ形の
スキルが出てきたら2行書けば入力欄が出る。

## 検査

```
check_js  0件
audit     HIGH 0件 / MID 7件(武将名の表記ゆれ、⑤の残り)
```

実機で確認: 蛇神幻計の部隊長判定、月読ノ冥略の注記、人数入力欄の表示・連動・計算
（150 + 5×12 = 210、別兵士は 150 + 3×12 = 186 で混ざらない）。

SIMULATOR_VERSION は v2026-08-14.5。

body:
## Summary

Long sessions (40k+ rendered lines) made the MiniMap viewport feel disconnected from the terminal. xterm was hard-capped at `scrollback: 20000`, so the buffer kept only the last ~20k lines while MiniMap / positions still mapped the full `total_lines`. The indicator then sat in the wrong half of the track.

This is a pre-existing main bug, not a regression from an open PR. The long session only made the coordinate mismatch obvious.

The terminal now grows scrollback *before* streaming, rewriting, or appending, so the full render stays in the buffer and MiniMap coordinates match.

## Test plan

author: prabhasg5
body:
**What does this PR accomplish?**

**PR #4067  should be merged before this PR**

*Description*

Adds `UpdateItemAtIndex` to the ListView on both Android and iOS, so an app can
change one row without rebuilding the list.

**Selection behaviour**

The replaced row stops being selected. A different item occupies that position
afterwards, so a selection pointing there no longer refers to what the user
picked. Nothing moves, so the selections around it are untouched.

`MultiSelect` needed a second rule, found while testing on the device. Dropping
the replaced row and clearing `Selection` / `SelectionIndex` with it left the
component reporting nothing selected while `SelectedItems` still held the rest
of the set — and a follow-up update driven by `SelectionIndex` then hit the
bounds check and raised an error. Reporting now falls back to the most recent
pick that remains, so `SelectionIndex` reads 0 only when `SelectedItems` really
is empty. Single selection is unchanged: replacing the one picked row leaves
nothing to fall back to.

**Both platforms**

`ListDataModel` gains a replace operation on each side — `set(index, item)` in
Java, `replace(at:with:)` for both backing arrays in Swift — along with
`lastSelection` next to the existing `firstSelection`. The unit tests mirror
each other, so the two platforms are held to the same contract rather than
merely looking alike.

**One refactor**

On Android, `AddItem` and `AddItemAtIndex` each carried the same block deciding
whether a new row should be a plain string or a dictionary, and
`UpdateItemAtIndex` would have been a third copy. That decision now lives in a
single `newRowFrom` helper, which also mirrors the `usesPlainStrings` /
`normalizedListItem` pair the iOS side already had.

author: macnite
body:
## Summary
Update firmware to support the 2026-08 hardware revision, which splits IR emitters across three MOSFET-controlled banks (one per MCP23017) instead of two. This aligns the logical bank structure with the physical chip layout and requires adding a third FET control line.

## Key Changes

- **Added third LED bank support:**
  - New `IR_LED_BANK_3_EN` constant (GPIO18, XIAO silk D10) controlling gates 20..27 (U4)
  - Updated `IR_LED_BANK_1_EN` and `IR_LED_BANK_2_EN` gate ranges: 00..07 and 10..17 respectively
  - Added `NUM_LED_BANKS` constant and `IR_LED_BANK_EN[]` array for cleaner iteration

- **Updated gate mapping table:**
  - Gates 10..13 now correctly map to `led_bank=2` (previously split between banks 1 and 2)
  - Gates 20..27 now map to `led_bank=3` (previously bank 2)
  - Each MCP23017 now maps 1:1 to a single LED bank

- **Refactored LED control code:**
  - `driveIrLeds()` now loops over all banks using the `IR_LED_BANK_EN[]` array
  - `setup()` initializes all three bank pins in a loop
  - Removed hardcoded references to individual bank pins

- **Enhanced diagnostics:**
  - `irDebugReadAndPrint()` now displays the LED bank number for each gate, making dead FET detection easier on the bench

- **Updated documentation:**
  - Clarified that `/GPIO4`, `/GPIO5`, `/GPIO6` are schematic net names only, not physical GPIO numbers
  - Added explicit mapping table showing FET → bank → gates → GPIO correspondence
  - Updated comments explaining the 1:1 bank-to-chip relationship and why all banks pulse together

## Implementation Details

The three banks are pulsed together (not per-bank) during sampling to minimize emitter on-time while ensuring all gates are correctly lit during the MCP23017 read window. The `IR_LED_BANK_EN[]` array enables clean iteration without duplicating pin names, and the updated `GateLocation` documentation clarifies how to index into it.

body:
Adds bounded read-only social listening through Meltwater Saved Searches under the existing `social.listening.read` capability.

Scope:
- Registers canonical `meltwater` provider for `social.listening.read` without changing R0 / `social.read` / no-approval / non-mutating governance.
- Uses workspace-scoped encrypted Meltwater API token from the generic provider credential store.
- Project-bound Saved Search store with fresh remote validation against `GET /v3/searches`, max 20 bindings per Project, and `projects.manage` required for bindable discovery/changes.
- Dedicated `/api/meltwater-bindings` GET/PUT endpoint with session, rate limit, payload cap, and no-store responses.
- Bounded small mention reads only: max 31-day window, page 1..10, page size 1..100, allowlisted sorting/filters, UTC request timezone, exact `POST /v3/search/{id}`, and `api.json` template.
- Requested Saved Search must be bound to the active Project; provider response `search_id` is identity-checked before Evidence is emitted.
- Initial slice deliberately excludes Saved Search mutation, exports, hooks, and streaming lifecycle APIs.

author: blakehastings
body:
Closes #304.

The model could already say "nobody knows". `rangeOfGenre` answers null for a
book no genre tag claims, `claim` in `domain/placement/rules.ts` refuses to file
one and says so, and #324 built the screens that explain it. The write path
could not produce that state, because every save stated a genre.

## What decides that a source stated a genre

Nothing new. A source either put something in the record that the ladder in
`server/classify.ts` can read, or it did not. Every rung of that ladder except
the last is grounded in something a catalogue actually said: a BISAC heading, an
Open Library subject, a Dewey number, an LC class. The last rung is grounded in
nothing, and it answered `genre/fiction` with the confidence set to `unknown`
and a sentence asking the person to fix it. That rung now answers no genre.

Nothing else about the ladder moved. A weak signal is still a signal, a
disagreement between two sources is still an answer with `unknown` beside it,
and there is no scale of definiteness anywhere: `confidence` already holds how
strongly a source said so.

The second default was `statedGenre`, which turned anything that was not the
fiction slug into `genre/non-fiction`. It reads the two slugs as themselves now
and everything else as nothing.

## The caller that default protected does not exist

Its comment said the default was the answer `Boolean(body.isFiction)` gave, kept
so a caller that had never stated a genre read the way it always had. That
caller is gone: #227 dropped `books.is_fiction`, and `isFiction` appears nowhere
on the wire, in the client, in `server/`, or in the browser suite. `asDraft` and
`asCaptureEdit` are the only things that call it, and both are fed by a client
that sends a slug. What the default did instead was file every unclassified book
into non-fiction and report nothing.

## What happens now to a book no source gave a genre

- `genreStatedBy` answers a null tag and a null range **together**, because a
  range no tag agrees with is exactly the drift it exists to prevent.
- `settleGenre` restates nothing. Not an empty claim list, which is a
  withdrawal: no statement at all. It then reads the book back with
  `rangeOfGenre`, so a book that already carries a genre tag keeps its range.
- `Store.addBook` and `Store.updateBook` take a nullable range, write the empty
  `shelf_range` a book in neither run has always carried (`CaptureQueue` writes
  the same value), and answer no placement.
- `POST /api/books` and `PUT /api/books/:id` answer `placement: null`, and
  record no derived location: there is nowhere to derive one from, and claiming
  the book is at 1A would be the same wrong answer somewhere else. A location a
  person sent is still written.
- `POST /api/placement/preview` refuses, on the same terms as a draft with no
  title. A placement is a position in one of two ordered lists and this draft is
  in neither.
- The review pane comes up with neither option highlighted, because
  `emptyDraft.genre` and `genreOfRange('')` are now null. The shelving step says
  "Nothing says whether this is fiction or non-fiction, so no rule claims it and
  there is no shelf to put it on. Go back and say which it is", instead of
  spinning on "Working out where it goes..." with every answer disabled.

A person setting it by hand is unchanged and always wins.

## No guessed tag is stripped

Every book saved before this carries a guessed genre tag, and taking those off
is a separate decision and the owner's. A save that states nothing restates
nothing, so a book that already carries a tag keeps it and keeps the range it
files into. There is a test for it.

## Following an untagged book through the app

Reported rather than fixed, because fixing it belongs elsewhere.

**Through the interface, such a book does not get shelved at all.** The shelving
step cannot name a plank, so every answer on it is disabled and the way on is
back to the field that says which it is. The book therefore stays in the queue,
which is a real list a person works through: it is the "Needs you" count on the
home screen and the whole of the queue screen. That is findable, and it is the
same place the book would be if nobody had finished identifying it.

**Reached by the API rather than the screens, a saved unfiled book is thinner
than it should be.** It is in `GET /api/books?range=all` (the empty range sorts
first, so it is at the top) and it is named on every start by the
`[tags] ... carry no genre tag` line in `applySchema`. It is not in either
`range=` listing, not in either misfile review, not on the home screen, and not
in any area's "Claimed by nothing" card, because that card reads
`books.current_area_id` and this book has never been placed anywhere. The two
screens that tell the truth about it, `ClaimedPane` and `BelongsPane`, both need
you to already be looking at the book or its area.

So the honest summary of the gap that remains: **there is no query anywhere that
answers "which books does no rule claim?"** `Store.listing`'s `tag=` filter is
purely positive and has no negation, and the only SQL that asks the question is
inlined in `db.pg.ts` and answers to a `console.error`. A collection-wide list,
and a way for `ClaimedPane` to offer an unclaimed book an action rather than
only a diagnosis, are both worth their own issue.

## Checks

`npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run lint:layers` all green.
**1853 tests, up from 1843** on `master`: ten added, none removed.

author: dorianzheng
body:
## Summary

Add local TCP and Unix listener forwarding to prepared one-shot box tunnels. This keeps `network.tunnel()` and the existing tunnel wire protocol unchanged while opening a fresh tunnel for every accepted client.

## Call graph

Before

```text
execute                    (CLI · src/cli/src/commands/network/tunnel.rs:53) — prepare one tunnel and print its URI
  └─ NetworkHandle::tunnel (Core · src/boxlite/src/litebox/network.rs:388)    — return a prepared one-shot BoxTunnel
       └─ BoxTunnel::uri   (Core · src/boxlite/src/litebox/network.rs:309)    — inspect the remote public URI
```

After

```text
execute                              (CLI · src/cli/src/commands/network/tunnel.rs:53) — preserve URI mode or parse --listen
  └─ NetworkHandle::tunnel           (Core · src/boxlite/src/litebox/network.rs:388)    — prepare the first one-shot tunnel
       └─ BoxTunnel::forward_with_bound (Core · src/boxlite/src/litebox/network.rs:347) — bind and report the canonical address
            └─ run_forwarder         (Core · src/boxlite/src/litebox/network.rs:610)    — accept with 64-relay backpressure
                 └─ relay_client     (Core · src/boxlite/src/litebox/network.rs:680)    — open a fresh tunnel and relay bytes
```

## Changes

- Add `SocketAddress` and repeatable `TunnelForwarder` lifecycle APIs while keeping `BoxTunnel` one-shot.
- Support loopback TCP, numeric IPv4/IPv6, automatic TCP port allocation, and absolute Unix stream socket paths.
- Add `boxlite network tunnel ... --listen` without changing the existing no-flag URI behavior.
- Expose the listener API through Rust, Python, Node.js, Go, and C, including synchronous wrappers and C runtime-drain callbacks.
- Bound active relays to 64, isolate per-client failures, cancel active relays on close, and clean up owned Unix sockets best-effort.
- Document the cross-SDK API and add core, CLI, binding, and lifecycle regression coverage.

## How to verify

- `UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/boxlite-uv-cache BOXLITE_DEPS_STUB=1 make fmt:check`
- `UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/boxlite-uv-cache BOXLITE_DEPS_STUB=1 make lint`
- `BOXLITE_DEPS_STUB=1 FILTER=litebox::network make test:unit:rust`
- `BOXLITE_DEPS_STUB=1 cargo nextest run -p boxlite --no-default-features --features rest -E 'test(litebox::network)'`
- `SETUP_DONE=1 BOXLITE_DEPS_STUB=1 FILTER=network_tunnel make test:integration:cli`
- `UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/boxlite-uv-cache BOXLITE_DEPS_STUB=1 make test:unit:python`
- `BOXLITE_DEPS_STUB=1 make test:unit:node`
- `BOXLITE_DEPS_STUB=1 FILTER=network::tests make test:unit:ffi`
- `SETUP_DONE=1 BOXLITE_DEPS_STUB=1 make test:unit:go FILTER='Test(NetworkTunnel|TunnelForward|ListenAddress|BoxNetwork|TunnelMethods|NetworkAndTunnel|RuntimeDoesNotStart)'`

## Risks / rollout

This is client-side forwarding only; it does not change the server, proxy, OpenAPI schema, or tunnel wire protocol. The full local pre-push integration matrix remains unavailable in this checkout because native vendor inputs are missing or mismatched; the focused rebased suites above pass, and CI remains the canonical full-matrix verification.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added local tunnel forwarding to TCP and Unix socket listeners across supported SDKs.
  * Added forwarder lifecycle controls, including address lookup, waiting, and closing.
  * Added CLI support for `network tunnel --listen`, including dynamic ports and Unix sockets.
  * Added socket address types and forwarding APIs for C, Go, Node.js, Python, and Rust.
* **Documentation**
  * Clarified that tunnels are one-shot resources consumed by either connecting or forwarding.
  * Documented listener formats, lifecycle behavior, cancellation, and multi-client forwarding.

author: guangliang2019
body:
## Summary

- catalog the required Props, Event, State, Expose core, Expose State, and Expose Event Module slices, plus Lifecycle as a Runtime-to-Adapter execution protocol without inventing a Lifecycle Module or host capability
- add first-class official Adapter Profile schema support and React, Vue, and Web Component `A-*` entities, including reviewed Module support and translated host capabilities
- catalog `HC-PROPS-SOURCE-0001`, scoped Event binding and Default Action capabilities, the complete classified Exposes Record Sink, and the new `HC-EXPOSE-EVENT-SINK-0001`
- catalog Expose Event as a required semantic Module slice that is currently co-located in `@proto.ui/module-event` while remaining distinct from the User-to-Component Event channel
- separate the physical Event facade into `EventChannelFacade` and `ExposeEventFacade`, while preserving the composite `EventFacade` for source compatibility
- add canonical `EXPOSE_EVENT_SINK_CAP` naming while preserving `EVENT_EMIT_CAP` as an exact deprecated alias
- brand Expose Event declaration descriptors so they reserve the shared Expose key namespace without being confused with structurally similar author values
- preserve those descriptors through the classified Module-to-Adapter translation record, then filter them from public `getExposes()` snapshots after the Adapter maps the signal to React callbacks, Vue emits/listeners, or Web Component `CustomEvent`s
- align Expose Event registration and retained `run.expose.emit` authority with instance lifetime across repeatable view epochs and terminal disposal
- retain the earlier Event, State, Expose, and Expose State drift fixes, reusable cataloging guide, Adapter Profile entities, and spec workspace projection improvements

## Why

Proto UI Modules expose different surfaces to prototype authors, privileged runtime/module consumers, and Adapter authors. The catalog previously lacked a repeatable way to connect those boundaries to host capabilities, official Adapter support decisions, lifecycle ownership, and executable evidence.

The Expose Event pass also uncovered a real boundary ambiguity. Existing classification contracts require outward signals to occupy the logical Expose record and shared key namespace, while official Adapter public types intentionally carry them through host-native listener or event surfaces rather than `getExposes()` values. Treating the record sink itself as the final App Maker record erased information too early; leaking the old unbranded marker exposed internal metadata too late.

This change makes that boundary explicit: Expose State publishes a classified Adapter translation record, branded signal descriptors survive to the Adapter boundary, and the Adapter public-record reader removes only those descriptors after host translation.

## Impact

- spec readers can trace Module criteria through required host capabilities where applicable, official Adapter profiles, test cases, and concrete implementation paths
- Adapter authors have an explicit required Expose Event slice and host-neutral signal sink, without being forced into DOM, framework-object, or listener-naming assumptions
- prototype authors retain one shared Expose key namespace across value, state, method, and outward signal classifications
- React, Vue, and Web Component App Makers receive host-native outward signals while `getExposes()` stays aligned with `ProtoAdapterExposes`
- structurally similar author values such as `{ __pui_expose: 'event' }` are preserved because filtering now uses a runtime brand
- the complete Exposes Record Sink is defined as a classified translation boundary rather than a prematurely finalized App Maker record
- DOM/CSS Expose State mirroring, payload portability, `options` equivalence, and missing-sink validation remain explicit draft/open questions; the standalone Expose Event package has moved into the follow-up governance plan below

## Validation

- `corepack pnpm@10.32.1 test`: 295 test files passed, 1290 tests passed; 3 existing files skipped and 34 existing todo
- `corepack pnpm@10.32.1 check:types`: 0 errors
- `corepack pnpm@10.32.1 check:prototype-catalog`: 117 declarations, 160 static authoring entries, 116 cataloged prototype entities, 0 known debt files
- `corepack pnpm@10.32.1 workspace:generate`: 522 entities
- `corepack pnpm@10.32.1 spec:docs:agent`
- `corepack pnpm@10.32.1 check:agent-doc`
- focused Expose Event, Expose, Expose State, Adapter, Runtime, prototype, and profile-schema tests: 12 files / 65 tests
- `corepack pnpm@10.32.1 release:bom` and release-asset validation
- Prettier pre-commit hook and `git diff --check`

## Coordination note

#368 (`fix: preserve Tabs roving focus targets`) is merged into `main`. This branch remains on the cataloging work line and GitHub currently reports it mergeable; when synchronizing with current `main`, preserve both the Tabs Focus `programmatic` projection and this PR's shared Event default-action, Exposes Record Sink, and Expose Event sink wiring in the nearby Adapter `runtime/modules.ts` files.

## Follow-up governance

This PR intentionally stops at cataloging the Expose Event semantic boundary and correcting the currently co-located implementation. It does not add a new public package to the already published and immutable `0.2.0-rc.7` release evidence.

After this PR has been reviewed and approved:

- start the physical extraction from a dedicated branch based on the then-current `main`
- introduce a standalone public `@proto.ui/module-expose-event` package and migrate Runtime plus official Adapter wiring there, with an explicit compatibility plan for the current `@proto.ui/module-event` surface
- make the extraction part of a new global exact-version release train rather than rewriting any `0.2.x` release BOM or evidence
- begin architecture/API-changing development with an `alpha` prerelease, advance to `beta` after the package boundary and top-level API stabilize, and reserve `rc` for builds that are genuinely release candidates

This also corrects the prerelease vocabulary used during `0.2`: internal and experimental trains that still permit architecture changes, top-level API changes, and feature additions should not be described as release candidates.

author: clarion1631
body:
## The bug `src/app/portal/contracts/[id]/PortalContractClient.tsx` imported the browser-only `dompurify` build, whose default export is a factory that needs a `window`. On the server it has no `.sanitize`, so `DOMPurify.sanitize(initialContract.body)` threw during server render: ``` TypeError: d.default.sanitize is not a function ``` This is a real client-facing page — clients open it from the emailed contract link. ### Confirmed live on production before this PR A plain HTTP fetch (no JS, so pure SSR output) of a real contract on the sanctioned "Shop" test project: ``` GET /portal/contracts/cms7psvit0001lc8m7s0s6e84?token=… → HTTP 500 → → zero contract content in the response ``` So the server render was not merely erroring into a logged warning — the route returned **500** and shipped an error document. The page only appeared at all because the client re-rendered after hydration. ## The fix Swap `dompurify` → `isomorphic-dompurify`, which uses real DOMPurify in the browser and DOMPurify-over-jsdom on the server. **Sanitization is not weakened** — the same options are passed at every call site, and the deliberate sanitize-first / inject-second ordering in `PortalContractClient` (with `escapeHtml` on `contractorSignedBy` and the signature URLs) is untouched. The same import pattern existed in five other client components that Next also renders on the server, so all six were swapped: - `src/app/portal/contracts/[id]/PortalContractClient.tsx` - `src/app/portal/estimates/[id]/PortalEstimateClient.tsx` - `src/components/ClientMessaging.tsx` - `src/components/EntityContractsClient.tsx` - `src/components/RichTextEditor.tsx` - `src/components/SendEstimateModal.tsx` `isomorphic-dompurify` declares a `browser` field, so jsdom stays out of the client bundle and only enters the server bundle. ### Second commit: hydration determinism Making these components server-render for the first time exposes a follow-on problem. Their bare `toLocaleDateString()` / `toLocaleString()` calls now run on the server too. Vercel's server is **UTC**; the client browser is **Pacific**. The same timestamp then formats to a different calendar day for any instant between 00:00 and 08:00 UTC — a hydration mismatch, and on the portal contract page those strings are injected into `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` on a legally meaningful document. Every display date in both contract components now goes through local `fmtDate` / `fmtDateTime` helpers pinned to `en-US` + `COMPANY_TIME_ZONE` (the constant the repo already uses). `companySettings` carries no `timeZone` field (`publicCompanySettingsSelect`) and `EntityContractsClient` receives no `companySettings` prop at all, so the shared constant is the deterministic source. Display formatting only — nothing stored or API-bound changed, and no `suppressHydrationWarning` was added. ## Verification - `npm run build` — clean, 0 errors (run twice: after the import swap, and again after the date fix). - Server-side sanitization behaviour checked directly under Node with the same options the app passes: | input | output | |---|---| | `

ok

` | `

ok

` | | `` | `` | | `x` | `x` | | `` | `` | | `

click

` | `

click

` | | `bi` (ALLOWED_TAGS `['b']`) | `bi` | | `

hi

{{SIGNATURE_BLOCK}}` | unchanged | | `x` | unchanged | The last two matter: the contract merge-field regexes depend on `{{…}}` placeholders and `data-merge-field` attributes surviving sanitization, or the signature blocks would stop rendering. - Production baseline captured (HTTP 500 / `__next_error__`, above) so the preview can be compared against a known-bad state on the same contract. ## Review Peer-reviewed with `codex exec -m gpt-5.6-sol -c model_reasoning_effort="xhigh"`. Verdict: *"the import swap itself is right and should fix the production SSR exception."* - **Hydration mismatch on dates** — valid, fixed in the second commit. - **Lockfile** — not applicable; `package-lock.json` is committed, it was just outside the diff excerpt sent to the reviewer. - **jsdom/browser serialization differences on unusual HTML** — acknowledged as low risk for TipTap-generated HTML; not addressed here. - **`serverExternalPackages`** — reviewer agreed it is not needed, and adding it speculatively would only add deployment variables. Codex also made a fair point worth recording: because the browser now parses server-produced HTML directly, the jsdom sanitizer is a **security boundary**, not just a perf optimization. Keeping `dompurify` and `jsdom` patched matters more after this change than before. ## Follow-ups deliberately not done here - Remove the now-indirect `dompurify` / `@types/dompurify` direct dependencies. - Introduce named policy helpers (`sanitizeContractHtml`, `sanitizeMessageHtml`, `sanitizeEditorHtml`) so the SSR-safe import lives in one place and call-site configs cannot drift. - Add e2e coverage for `/portal/contracts/[id]` — the route currently has **none**, which is why this shipped and stayed broken. ⚠️ Auto-deploy is ON — merging this ships it to production. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body:
## Why

The master never learns about a new booking.

The single channel is an Ayla-backend push into the Ayla Pro mobile app: `booking.created` → outbox → `handle_booking_created` → template `appointment_created_specialist`, `channel = PUSH`, `app_type = "pro"`. On the pilot there are **zero** active `DeviceToken` rows, and the backend dispatcher performs no fallback for `PUSH`.

Result over the entire pilot history: **26 notifications — 20 `failed`, 6 `pending`, 0 `sent`.** Not one was ever delivered to anyone, master or client.

On the bot side, none of the seven `booking.*` handlers addressed the salon at all. The MAX fan-out primitive was written for DRF-1029 and its docstring already named this ticket as its second caller — there was no calling code.

Waiting for the push channel is not an option: Ayla Pro does not exist in a working form (two of its four tabs are 15-line stubs).

## What

Deliver the new-booking notification over the transport that demonstrably works on the pilot — a plain MAX message — reusing `apps.handoff.notify.send_max_notification` (DRF-1029) instead of writing a second copy. No new transport, no new queue, no dependency on the mobile app.

**Addressing cascade, first hit wins:**

| # | Address | State on the pilot |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `CatalogMaster.linked_bot_user.chat_id` — the master personally | yields nothing: `linked_bot_user` is NULL for all four masters, `max_handle` empty |
| 2 | `Tenant.manager_chat_id` — the salon manager | field exists, currently empty |
| 3 | `HANDOFF_NOTIFY_MAX_CHAT_IDS` — fallback channel | already holds the owner's chat → the notification lands on a human on day one, no env change |
| 4 | nobody | explicit `WARNING` log — an unannounceable booking must leave a trace |

Rung 1 is implemented but inert: linking masters to their MAX accounts is a separate ticket, and when that data lands the message starts going to the right person **with no code change**. Personal delivery is exclusive by design — once a master is reachable, copying every booking to the manager and the owner as well is how a channel gets muted.

**Message content:** service, master, tenant-local time, source, appointment id. **No client data of any kind** — per the owner's decision recorded in DRF-1039 the performer does not receive the client's identity or contact.

**Wiring:** registered through `transaction.on_commit` from `handle_booking_created`, gated on the proxy actually being inserted. So a rolled-back ingest announces nothing, and a re-delivery carrying a fresh `event_id` cannot announce the same appointment twice. Every catalog read and the send itself happen in the callback — the handler's own path is unchanged, and a failure there cannot turn a *missing notification* into a *dead-lettered booking event*.

The specialist is matched on **either** mirror key (`CatalogMaster.id`, i.e. the Ayla `SpecialistProfile.id`, or `ayla_user_id`): the event contract documents `specialist_id` only as «the master assigned to the appointment» and does not pin down which of the two the producer sends. Catalog reads run under `tenant_scope` with the tenant-scoped manager, so the MKT1 boundary (cross-tenant catalog reads belong to `apps/marketplace`) still holds.

## Test plan

`apps/booking/tests/test_master_notify.py` — 26 tests:

- each rung of the cascade, including **«no address at all» → nothing sent + WARNING**;
- precedence between rungs; whitespace-only chat ids treated as absent;
- master matched by `SpecialistProfile.id` and by `ayla_user_id`;
- message content: service, master, tenant-local time (incl. a non-MSK tenant and an invalid tz), source label + unknown-source pass-through, graceful `—` for unmirrored catalog rows;
- **no client PII** — a `BotUser` with a name and a phone exists and none of it reaches the text;
- formatting makes zero DB queries;
- containment: `MaxAPIError` and an arbitrary `RuntimeError` never escape; one failing recipient does not cancel the others; the send uses the ≤5 s timeout;
- consumer wiring: send happens after commit, never before; rolled-back ingest sends nothing; exact replay ×3 and re-delivery with a fresh `event_id` each announce exactly once.

Gates: `ruff check`, `ruff format`, `mypy` clean on all three touched files **including tests**; import-boundary and red-zone AST guards pass.

Regression (Redis up, per WINDOW_PROTOCOL §5.1): `apps/booking apps/bookings apps/eventbus apps/handoff apps/catalog apps/identity tests/contracts` — one failure, `tests/contracts/test_event_idempotency.py::TestBookingIdempotency::test_booking_created_idempotent`, **reproduced on a clean `origin/dev` worktree at 273c5b2**. It is a wall-clock time bomb: the fixture books 2026-05-22, today is 2026-08-14, so #1146 skips both backdated reminders and the test's `== 2` assertion fails. Not in CI (CI runs `tests/smoke/`, the Ayla route-table contract and `apps/eventbus/tests/`), unrelated to this diff.

## Out of scope

- The Ayla backend and its notification stack — untouched. We work bot-side, on an event that already reaches the bot.
- Detector, booking client, rendering (`apps/skills/booking/lookup.py`, `apps/integrations/ayla/booking_client.py`) — untouched.
- Linking masters to MAX accounts (`CatalogMaster.linked_bot_user` is NULL for 0-of-4, `max_handle` empty). Recorded as an observation; the cascade is built so that fixing it is a data change.

Relates to DRF-1030.

author: misoto22
body:
Two things, and the second is why the first took three attempts.

## A side drawer is full width on a phone

320px on a 375px screen leaves a 55px strip of scrim: too narrow to aim
at, too wide to read as an edge, and it makes the panel look like a
desktop rail that was squeezed rather than a sheet built for the screen
it is on. Full width below `sm`, the asked-for width above it.

The width had to move from an inline style to a class for that to be
possible — an inline width beats every `sm:` variant. The classes are
written out in a lookup rather than interpolated, because Tailwind emits
a utility only when it has SEEN the literal string; `sm:w-[${n}px]`
produces no rule and every drawer would have stayed full width.

## A failing spec no longer costs the file's timeout

I tried the change above twice and twice concluded it hung the suite. It
did not. What hangs is any spec whose assertion throws before its own
`unmount()`:

  - A React root keeps the event loop alive.
  - So the file stops exiting, node waits out the whole per-file timeout,
    and then reports "the file timed out" — with the actual assertion
    nowhere in the output.

The change flipped one existing assertion (`style.width` is `''` now),
and that single failure turned into 82 silent seconds. Proved by holding
the source constant and making the same assertion fail on purpose: 82s
and no failure named, against 1.4ms and a named failure with the unmount
guaranteed.

`tests/dom.ts` now tracks every root it hands out and unmounts the
survivors in an `afterEach`, so no individual spec has to remember —
verified by re-running that deliberate failure with no per-test cleanup
at all: reported in 3ms, no timeout.

This is not Drawer-specific. Every spec file here mounts this way, so
every one of them could have swallowed a failure the same way.

669 specs pass.

body:
feat(templates): BP-04 试跑与发布蓝本版本真实落库（F178：POST trial-runs + POST versions）

这是 #991 蓝本闭环 backlog 的第四件（BP-04），也是
PROP-PROJECT-LIFECYCLE-E2E-001（track P）P4「发布版本」的实现。与它一并接线
的还有 startTrialRun——两个操作没有分开做，因为发布门槛的「已试跑」判据挂在
试跑产生的绑定记录上，没有试跑基础设施，发布门槛在真库测试里永远走不到
applied 分支。

## 做了什么

| 文件 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `migrations/20260814080000_f178_blueprint_versions_and_bindings.sql` | `blueprint_versions`（不可变快照）+ `blueprint_bindings`（试跑/套用绑定）两表、RLS、GRANT |
| `application/templates/blueprint-persistence-ports.ts` | `StartTrialRunCommand/Outcome`、`PublishBlueprintVersionCommand/Outcome` |
| `infrastructure/templates/pg-blueprint-repository.ts` | `startTrialRun()`（追加绑定，无 CAS）、`publishBlueprintVersion()`（版本号 CAS + 门槛判定 + 同事务写入） |
| `interface/controllers/blueprint.controller.ts` | `POST /blueprints/:id/trial-runs`、`POST /blueprints/:id/versions` |

## 依据等级

域/应用层早已就位且有独立单测：`domain/templates/trial-run-gate.ts`（试跑门槛）、
`domain/templates/publish-blueprint-version.ts`（组合门槛 + 版本生成，纯函数）、
`application/templates/publish-blueprint-version.ts`（编排）。缺的是仓储 + 控制器
这一层（同 F175/F174/F177 的缺口形状）。

## 与 BP-03（F177）不同：没有 T13 那类读路径缺口

`expectedCurrentVersionNumber` 对照的是 `blueprints.version_number`，而这个字段
`listBlueprints.out` 已经在返回（`BlueprintRow.versionNumber`）——客户端有合法
途径拿到它。这次前端接线不会卡在"没有读路径"这一步。

## 设计决定

- **两张表一起建**：`evaluateTrialRunGate` 判"已试跑"看的是有没有至少一条
  `kind='trial-run'` 绑定，没有真实存储就只能假装通过或永远拒绝，两者都不诚实。
- **`blueprint_bindings.kind` 现在只会出现 'trial-run' 行**：'project' 要等
  BP-08（createProject 带 blueprintVersionId）才产生，表结构现在就把闭集落成
  DDL，不是预留占位。
- **`blueprint_versions.content` 是 jsonb 冻结快照，不引用 design_facets 表**：
  版本必须不可变（I-2），若直接引用会随后续编辑一起漂移。
- **`changedDesignFacetKeys` 算法是本 feature 自己的判断**（契约只给字段形状，
  没给算法）：与上一个 published 版本的快照逐 key 比较，值不同或某 key 消失都算
  改动；首次发布没有基线，当前所有已填 key 都算改动。供人类复核，不是唯一可能
  的裁决。
- **版本比对先于门槛判定**：版本冲突不该被误判成门槛不通过，反之亦然（同
  setDurationTier 的顺序理由）。
- **不碰 `blueprints.revision` 列**：那是 BP-03（F177，PR #1208，未合并）加的，
  本分支从 main 独立分出，不依赖它是否已合入；发布的并发令牌就是
  `version_number` 本身。

## 验证

真库测试（`apps/api/tests/templates/create-blueprint-persistence.test.ts` 新增
describe block "F178 试跑与发布版本"，8 条）：
1. 没试跑直接发布 → TRIAL_RUN_REQUIRED，反证 I-3「失败不占号」（version_number
   原地不动、blueprint_versions 零行）
2. 试跑一次后发布 → 成功，版本号 0→1，蓝本转已发布，changedDesignFacetKeys 正确
3. 拿过期 expectedCurrentVersionNumber 发布 → VERSION_CHANGED
4. 发布两次 → 旧版转 archived、新版 published、版本号单调递增、
   changedDesignFacetKeys 只算真正变了的
5. 发布不存在的蓝本 → BLUEPRINT_NOT_FOUND
6. 试跑不存在的蓝本 → BLUEPRINT_NOT_FOUND
7. 试跑不计入已套用项目数（I-22）
8. 反证：两条并发试跑各自留痕，不互相覆盖（无 CAS 冲突，因为不是互斥写）

```
✓ 通过: pnpm --filter api exec vitest run tests/templates/create-blueprint-persistence.test.ts（23/23，含此前 F175/F174/F178 共 15 条）
✓ 通过: pnpm --filter api run typecheck
✓ 基础验证通过 (pnpm -w run verify:base)
✓ 门控通过 -> F178 = passing
```

## 签核

F178 追加进 templates 束 `covers:`，依 contract-design.md 的三条件规则：
UI 已签（零界面落点，空成立）/ 契约已签（只实现已签核的两条 operation）/
零新增设计面（门槛判定复用既有错误码，"已试跑"判据按 D-6 现有的"创建即算"
立场实现，未做新裁决）。只动 covers，status/confirmed_by/confirmed_at 一字未改。

Refs #991

author: v15a1
body:
# Description
Five routes: the catalog (`GET /shops/items`), the caller's order history (`GET /shops/orders/me`), and the two-step checkout — `POST /shops/checkout` creates a PENDING order, `POST /shops/checkout/confirm` settles it against an on-chain payment.

**Checkout is one transaction**: the order row, its lines, and one conditional stock decrement per line. A shortfall on any line rolls the whole basket back, so a partially-reserved order cannot exist. `totalCost` and `eventId` are accepted and ignored — the total is recomputed from live prices and the event is resolved server-side, so a client cannot name its own price. A replayed `idempotencyKey` returns the original order instead of writing a second one.

**Confirm locks the order `FOR UPDATE`** and runs verification while the lock is held, so two concurrent confirms cannot both settle. The payment must be a `transfer` to the configured master wallet, for exactly the order's stored total, and must have succeeded — presence and success are checked independently, since a transaction can be mined and still have failed. Every verification failure returns the same opaque message and logs the real reason, so the endpoint isn't an oracle for probing transaction hashes.

`SHOP_MASTER_WALLET_ADDRESS` is deliberately **not** required by `Validate()`, so a deployment with no shop still starts. But left unset, confirm refuses every request rather than skipping the recipient check — a deployment that forgot it must not hand out merchandise for free. It must match the frontend's `merchantWalletAddress` app-config row; if the two disagree, every checkout is paid and then rejected.

The catalog returns an envelope rather than a bare array because the client needs `isShopOpen` and the active event id, neither derivable from the item list. Only `VISIBLE` items are returned, so a hidden item is unbuyable rather than merely undisplayed — but items are still returned when the shop is closed, so past orders' lines resolve.

## Automation tests
- Unit tests: `go test ./internal/...` green; `go build`, `go vet` and `gofmt` clean. Coverage across four layers — model validation, repository (transactional rollback on stock shortfall, idempotent replay, `FOR UPDATE` re-read, per-user limits), service (recipient/amount/success verification and its failure modes, unset-master-wallet refusal), and handler (status-code mapping, opaque confirm errors).

## Security checks
- Followed secure coding standards: yes
- Confirmed that this PR doesn't commit any keys, passwords, tokens, usernames, or other secrets: yes — `.env.example` carries placeholders only.

## Migrations (if applicable)
No migration in this PR; the shop tables belong to the shared schema. `SHOP_MASTER_WALLET_ADDRESS` is a new environment variable, documented in `.env.example`. Leaving it unset is safe: the server starts and only checkout-confirm refuses.

## Related PRs
Overlaps #20 ("Add conference shop and wallet integration"), which implements the same feature under different filenames and also touches `main.go`, `config.go`, `models/shop.go`, `service/shop_service.go`, `repository/interfaces.go` and `clients/transaction/client.go`. These two should be reconciled — one implementation picked — rather than both merged.

Also stacked on #26, which adds the wallet balance endpoint that #20 covers as well.

body:
## Summary

- adds a native-WebSocket-first SnowLuma transport with a bounded, one-time official SDK WebSocket fallback
- bundles the exact `@snowluma/sdk` dependency into the standalone release without HTTP action replay or parallel event streams
- adds focused transport coverage for fallback selection, ordering, queue limits, redaction, action failures, timeouts, and shutdown races
- rewrites the project entry point and SnowLuma deployment documentation in Chinese, covering Docker Compose, Windows, Docker Desktop, WSL2, Linux, Termux, Baota, and 1Panel
- moves deployment documentation to stable responsibility-based paths and removes duplicate or unreferenced assets/templates
- makes the Docker/native environment templates expose the documented `SNOWLUMA_SDK_FALLBACK=auto|off` setting and updates release packaging verification

## Why

The standalone runtime previously had only the handwritten WebSocket client, while the SnowLuma installation instructions were difficult to discover from the repository entry point. The fallback is intentionally limited to startup transport selection: OneBot actions are never retried over HTTP or a second transport after uncertainty, preventing duplicate moderation actions.

## User impact

Existing SnowLuma deployments keep the native WebSocket transport by default. If its bounded startup attempts fail, the process closes it completely and tries the bundled SDK WebSocket client once; the selected client remains the only event/action transport for that process. Operators can set `SNOWLUMA_SDK_FALLBACK=off` to diagnose the native path. No data reset or migration behavior changes are introduced.

## Validation

- `corepack pnpm@10.17.1 run typecheck`
- `corepack pnpm@10.17.1 run lint`
- `corepack pnpm@10.17.1 run format:check`
- `corepack pnpm@10.17.1 run test:ci` — 155 tests passed
- `corepack pnpm@10.17.1 run package:all` — build plus both release archives and checksum verification passed
- static deployment asset tests passed; Docker CLI is unavailable in this workspace, so live `docker compose config` was not run
