author: robobun
body:
### Problem
- Every package manager subcommand (`bun install`, `add`, `remove`, `update`, `pm`, ...) aborts when its `--cwd` value is at least `PATH_MAX` bytes long (4096 on Linux, 1024 on macOS), instead of printing an error:
  ```
  $ bun install --cwd "$(head -c 5000 /dev/zero | tr '\0' a)"
  panic: range end index 5000 out of range for slice of length 4096
  $ bun install --cwd "./$(head -c 5000 /dev/zero | tr '\0' a)"
  panic: range end index 5014 out of range for slice of length 4095
  $ bun install --cwd "$(head -c 4096 /dev/zero | tr '\0' a)"
  panic: index out of bounds: the len is 4096 but the index is 4096
  ```
  (exit 134). A value one byte shorter already printed `error: failed to change directory to "...": ENAMETOOLONG` and exited 1.
- Cause: the `--cwd` block in `src/install/PackageManager/CommandLineArguments.rs` (lines 1298-1329 on main) stages the value in a `PathBuffer` of exactly `PATH_MAX` bytes with no length check. A value not starting with `.` is copied in with `copy_from_slice` and then NUL-terminated one byte further; a value starting with `.` is resolved with the unchecked `join_abs_string_buf`, which panics inside the normalizer when the result does not fit the buffer.
- The runtime's global `bun --cwd` flag has the same bug in separate code (`src/runtime/cli/Arguments.rs`); that one is fixed in #38368. This PR only covers the package manager's own flag.

### Fix
- The block moves into `change_directory`. The `.`-prefixed branch resolves with `join_abs_string_buf_checked` into `PATH_MAX - 1` bytes of the buffer; the other branch copies the value only when it leaves that last byte free. Both keep the last byte for the NUL terminator `chdir` reads. When the value does not fit, the existing `failed to change directory to "<value>": <errno>` message is printed with `ENAMETOOLONG` and the process exits 1, the same as when `chdir` itself fails.
- Why `ENAMETOOLONG` is the right answer rather than some new error: `PATH_MAX` counts the terminator, so a path of `PATH_MAX` or more bytes is one `chdir` would reject with `ENAMETOOLONG` if it could be passed at all. The check only turns away values that could never have been entered, and the user sees the same line either side of the buffer boundary (the `PATH_MAX - 1` control in the test is the kernel's own rejection, printed through the unchanged `chdir` error path).
- Why the checked join rather than a length check on the argument in the `.` branch: that branch already normalizes (`--cwd ./moo/..` enters the parent), and `join_abs_string_buf_checked` fails only when the normalized result does not fit, so that behaviour is kept. Mapping its `None` to `ENAMETOOLONG` is how the lockfile code already treats it (`src/install/lockfile/Package/WorkspaceMap.rs`).
- Messages for failures that are not about length are unchanged: a missing directory still prints the value as given (`"/nonexistent"`) or, for a `.` value, the resolved path (`"/tmp/proj/nonexistent"`).
- Verified with the new `--cwd that does not fit the path buffer` block in `test/cli/install/bun-install.test.ts`: `PATH_MAX` bytes, `PATH_MAX + 1000` bytes, the `./` form, and `bun add`, plus `PATH_MAX - 1` as the kernel-rejected control. On the current release build the four new lengths abort with the panics above and the control passes; with this change all five pass, as does the existing `should handle --cwd` test.
- Checked by hand with the debug build that `--cwd moo`, `./moo`, `moo/`, `.`, `./moo/..`, an absolute path, `""`, a missing directory and `./<5000 bytes>/..` (normalizes to the cwd and succeeds) behave as before.
- The test block is skipped on Windows: `PathBuffer` there is about 96 KiB, longer than any command line, so the overflow is unreachable.

### Background
- `PathBuffer` is a `[u8; MAX_PATH_BYTES]` scratch buffer, where `MAX_PATH_BYTES` is the platform `PATH_MAX` (4096 on Linux, 1024 on macOS and the BSDs, `32767 * 3 + 1` on Windows). `PATH_MAX` includes the NUL terminator, so the longest path a syscall accepts is `PATH_MAX - 1` bytes.
- `join_abs_string_buf(cwd, buf, parts)` is `path.resolve` into a caller buffer; it assumes the result fits. `join_abs_string_buf_checked` is the variant for user-controlled input: it normalizes into heap scratch when needed and returns `None` only if the normalized result does not fit `buf`.
- `Output::err_generic` + `Global::crash()` is how this argument parser reports every invalid flag value: it prints `error: ...` and exits 1.

author: zaba505
body:
Closes #185.

`.dagger/` loses about 2,000 lines. The image, the multi-platform publish, the tag
family, the recursive signature and the attestations are all
`github.com/z5labs/devex/daggerverse/z5labs`'s now; what stays here is the
contract checks, the release *decision*, the release notes, and the four Go
modules this repository holds.

`dagger.json`'s `go` and `z5labs` pins move together to `c10a120` — the same devex
commit avroc#223 adopted.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **All four `Ci` invocations route through `Z5labs.Go(source).…Ci`; `GoLib`
      is gone.** One `goChain` helper, so the four cannot disagree about the lint
      configuration or the race detector. `Fmt`, `Vet`, `Lint` and `Test` still
      drive the shared `go` module's `Ci` builder unchanged.
- [x] **`.golangci.yml` is in the v2 dialect**, selecting the same five linters,
      with no mention of a v1-pinned pipeline or devex#374. Note that v2's
      `staticcheck` subsumes v1's `gosimple` and `stylecheck`, so the same five
      names select more checks: five real findings came out of the switch and are
      fixed in `internal/conformance`, `internal/emit`, `internal/resolve`,
      `cmd/cpybkc-gen-go` and `.dagger/release.go`. Nothing was excluded to make
      the stage pass.
- [x] **The base image is a `Go.App` plus its two contributions.** `image()`,
      `Image`'s builder, `Publish` and `irDirectory()` are deleted, not wrapped.
      `Image` survives as an *accessor* onto the App — it is what a contributor
      exports now that there is no `publish` verb. `binary()` survives too,
      because `Binary` and `Build` still need a loose executable; the archetype
      compiles the one that goes in the image, and `checkImageBuild` reads the
      flags back out of it.
- [x] **`sign.go` is deleted in its entirety**, with the `cosignPath` pin.
      `checkProvenance` and `checkSboms` are deleted rather than rehomed, and the
      reason is written down in `.dagger/main.go`: there is no predicate of this
      repository's left to check the shape of, and a table here would be a second
      copy of somebody else's rule — the copy that stays green after the original
      moves. Same answer as avroc#223.
- [x] **`Ci`'s fan-out is sixteen goroutines down to fifteen**, with the
      `wg.Add`, the error variable and the `errors.Join` term all moved together.
- [x] **`release.go` keeps `planRelease`, `parseVersion`, `releaseName`,
      `headRefs`, the notes half and `irVersion`; loses `versionTags` and
      `publishTags`.** `Release` takes a `--registry` and a `--repository`, and
      `release.yaml` no longer passes `--builder` or `--invocation` — every
      identifying field in the provenance comes out of the exchanged OIDC token's
      claims.
- [x] **`TagScheme` still runs on every pull request**, over the cases cpybkc
      still decides, every expected value a literal. `+build` metadata moved from
      `versionTags` into `planRelease`, so it is still refused at this end as well
      as upstream.
- [x] **`ir.binpb` and the `proto/` include root arrive through `App.WithFile`
      and `App.WithDirectory`**, each with a document from `Z5labs.FileDocument`
      and `Z5labs.DirectoryDocument`, carrying an explicit `MIT` expression and no
      version. Neither document is hand-rolled.
- [x] **`ImageContract` passes on both platforms, and every row was re-derived
      against the image the archetype builds** — not edited where the old listing
      failed. The listing is still exhaustive, which is what asserts the absence
      of `/tmp` and of `/usr/local/bin`; `/app`, `/app/cpybkc`, `/home` and
      `/home/nonroot` are named rows. `checkImageConfig` now asserts all three
      pinned environment variables rather than `PATH` alone.
- [x] **`worked-example`, `companion-module`, `cli-surface`, `engine-lock`,
      `ir-artifacts`, `layout-artifact` and `build` all pass**, and `example/`
      still comes back byte for byte through the new image.
- [x] **Decided: the contract check is a gate inside `Release`.** It runs
      `checkBaseImage` — the same function `ImageContract` runs, not a sequence
      copied beside it — over the containers the App is about to push, and a
      failure means nothing was pushed. `release.yaml`'s standalone
      `dagger call image-contract` step is gone; the standalone call stays for
      pull requests, where there is no release to gate.
- [x] **`.git` reaches the build facts and not the check stages' source.** It is
      `New`'s own argument with an ignore list covering the reflog, `FETCH_HEAD`,
      `ORIG_HEAD`, the index, the hooks and `COMMIT_EDITMSG`; `appSource` is the
      only thing that folds it back in, and a `nil` directory returns the source
      unchanged rather than panicking in `Directory.WithDirectory`. `ci.yaml`
      checks out `fetch-depth: 0`; `release.yaml` already did.
- [x] **`CONTRIBUTING.md` says the pipeline does not run from a git worktree** —
      see the correction below.
- [x] **`docs/container/SPEC.md` is updated for every covered guarantee that
      changed and nothing that did not.** Five edits, listed below.
- [x] **Consumer breaks are called out as breaks.** All three are called out in
      the document, at the paragraph each one changes, with #185 cited. There are
      no release notes to write and no version to bump: `gh release list` is
      empty and the only tag is the withdrawn `v0.0.0`, so nothing has been
      published under any of these promises yet. The first release will carry them
      as its initial contract.
- [x] **The four promises were re-derived against the landed API**, not against
      the issue. `/usr/local/bin` is `appPluginDir` in `build.go` with `PATH`
      composed from it; `65532:65532` is `appOwner`, set in the one place that
      builds an image and with no `WithUser` seam; the 1777 `/tmp` was removed by
      #184 rather than asked for; the plugin directory's existence resolved into a
      document change here. Nothing is filed on devex, nothing is left to file, and
      nothing is worked around in `.dagger/`.
- [x] **`dagger.json`'s two devex dependencies move to one commit**;
      `engineVersion` is unchanged at `v0.21.8` and `EngineLock` passes.
      `.dagger/go.mod` and `daggerverse/**/go.mod` were untouched by
      `dagger develop`.
- [x] **`main.go`'s and `image.go`'s package comments are rewritten**, not left
      standing.
- [x] **`CONTRIBUTING.md`'s commands are current.** `dagger call publish` does not
      survive in any form, and the document says what to do instead —
      `dagger call image export --path=cpybkc.tar`, then `docker load`.

## The five SPEC edits

1. **The plugin directory no longer exists in the base image.** The `MUST exist
   even when empty` requirement is withdrawn, with the reason: `COPY` creates its
   destination's parents, and this project does not take that on faith — both
   worked examples are built on every pull request and one of them is that `COPY`.
   Its ownership is withdrawn with it and moved to the not-covered list; what a
   consumer actually depends on is the *file's* mode and owner, which is unchanged.
2. **The SBOM is one document per platform describing the whole image, in SPDX
   2.3 and CycloneDX**, rather than one SPDX document per executable per platform.
   The old paragraph's argument is answered rather than dropped.
3. **Attestation discovery flips to referrers-only.** A new *Discovering the
   attestations* section says outright that `cosign verify-attestation` now finds
   nothing, and gives `oras discover` with the three artifact types and the
   `org.opencontainers.image.title` annotation that picks the right document out
   of several. `cosign verify` is unchanged throughout. The mirroring section is
   corrected too — `.sig` is still a tag, `.att` is not.
4. **The IR schema is 65532-owned and read-only** — `0444` for the descriptor set,
   `0555` through the include root — rather than r

author: bdcbqa314159
body:
First half of Gap 2 (in-memory hygiene). Swaps hand-rolled/std primitives for **audited libsodium**, behind a private seam. No public-API change; all 50 tests green on debug, asan clean on the memory-critical ones.

## What's here
- **libsodium** (robinlinden/libsodium-cmake wrapper, pinned to `9b2848d` → pins libsodium via its submodule), linked **PRIVATE** to keyward. Only `secure_memory.cpp` includes `<sodium.h>`.
- **`secure_memory` seam** (`secure_alloc/free/zero/equal/random`) wrapping `sodium_malloc` (guard-paged + `mlock`'d, no swap), `sodium_free` (zeroes), `sodium_memzero`, `sodium_memcmp` (constant-time), `randombytes_buf` (CSPRNG). `sodium_init()` once via a function-local static.
- **`Secret`** now holds a hand-managed `sodium_malloc` secure buffer instead of `std::string` — guard-paged, mlock'd, zeroed on free, still move-only. **Public API unchanged** → the task-1/2 oracles pass untouched.
- **`random_bytes`** → `randombytes_buf` (replaces `std::random_device`).
- **seal/unseal derived key** → `sodium_malloc` secure buffer via `unique_ptr` with `secure_free` deleter — mlock'd and auto-zeroed on **every** return path (incl. unseal's forgery early-out).

## Scope (honest — branch 2 to follow)
Still plain `std::string`: the *stored record bytes*, the seal/unseal *blob* + recovered *plaintext*, and `PromptField` values. End-to-end secure memory is the **wire-through (part 2/2)**. This PR hardens the primitives, the `Secret` type, the key, and the RNG.

## Verification
- Full suite **50/50** on debug; **asan clean** on Secret + SecretEquals + SecretBox (17/17) — the hand-managed buffers have no UAF/leaks.
- clang-format clean. Rebased on #18.
- **CI note:** libsodium now builds on all 3 runners (slower, like FTXUI); first cross-platform proof `sodium_malloc`/`mlock` integrate on Windows/Linux.

author: gutskrd
body:
The single-quote form still failed — **exit status 127** (executable not found): a bare `sh` doesn't resolve in Render's exec context.

## Fix
Use the absolute shell path, the form Render's Docker docs prescribe for multiple commands:
```yaml
dockerCommand: "/bin/sh -c 'npm run migrate:up --workspace api && npx tsx api/src/server.ts'"
```
`/bin/sh` always resolves, and it still runs the chain: migrations, then the server.

Only `kurda-api`'s `dockerCommand` changed (`sh` → `/bin/sh`). Free plan, Postgres, Redis, `JWT_SECRET`, `APPLE_CLIENT_IDS`, and the disabled worker are all unchanged.

author: marvinbaudach
body:
*My Stats* showed Deezer's grey silhouette for several artists and then cached it
as if it were a real portrait, so the wrong image survived for the whole positive
TTL. Nine of the 162 cached portraits on this machine were that silhouette.

## What was actually wrong

**Placeholder detection matched one spelling out of three.** `is_placeholder_url`
tested `url.contains("/artist//")` — the empty path segment. Deezer also serves
the identical silhouette under the MD5 of the empty string
(`d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e`), which that substring never matches. The URL
is now parsed, the `/images/artist/<identifier>/` segment is read positionally,
and the identifier is compared against an explicit `MISSING_IMAGE_IDENTIFIERS`
list. Nothing is inferred from image content.

**The first exact name match won, pictured or not.** Deezer returns several
artists under the same name. The old loop returned the first exact match and gave
up if it had no usable picture, so a namesake with an actual photo further down
the response was never reached. Selection now ranks exact matches by
`(has picture, nb_fan)` and preserves response order on ties, and the search
limit went from 5 to 10 so the pictured candidate is inside the window.

**The `picture_xl` → `picture_big` size fallback had to survive the rewrite.**
It does; `candidate_picture_url` keeps the ordered field list and drops a field
only when it is empty or a known placeholder.

Test payloads moved into `artist_portrait/test_fixtures.rs` (`#[cfg(test)]`) and
are now full Deezer objects rather than three-field stubs — several defects here
only exist in fields the old stubs did not carry.

Production code: 297 lines under `crates/reprise-core/src/artist_portrait/`. No
GNOME code, no `Cargo.toml`, no new dependency.

## Evidence

`acceptance/deezer-placeholder-portraits/run-accept.sh` drives the real app
through *My Stats*, expands the list past the leader card, and compares rendered
portraits; all eight oracles pass and the regression check covers ranks 1–20.
Red-first proofs for each unit test and the acceptance artefacts are under
`docs/evidence/deezer-placeholder-portraits/`.

Four of the seven defects found during acceptance (F4–F7) were invisible to
reading — three reviews had passed the harness beforehand. The traps are written
up in the handover document rather than lost.

## What this does not fix

**The sentinel premise no longer holds.** On 14 Aug the live run found the
silhouette under `415714b66a5de709809dd3d05f58afe4`, an ordinary artist-specific
identifier that was still a real photograph on 13 Aug. Measured independently:
213 unique colours at 1000×1000 and RMSE 0.058 against both known variants, where
a real photograph sits at 49 000–105 000 colours and RMSE 0.35–0.87. So the list
will grow per affected artist, not once. An automatic detector is deliberately
not built — every plausible heuristic is content-based, which E1 forbids. Whether
that constraint stays is an open decision, recorded in the handover.

**Rank 10 "Oceano" now shows a namesake's face.** The more popular entry (16 388
fans) has only the silhouette; the one with 2 347 fans has a real photo, and the
rule takes the photo. This follows from E2 as agreed during the grill — the
failure mode stays cosmetic and confined to same-named artists — but it had never
been visible before the acceptance run.

**Deferred, shared file:** `cua_common_stop_daemon` in
`scripts/cua-common/session.sh` does `kill -TERM` then an unbounded `wait` with
no `kill -KILL` escalation; with a `trap '' TERM` child that `wait` never
returns and every later cleanup step is skipped (nine stray `cua-driver`
processes on the machine, the oldest ~20 h). The acceptance script fixed it in
its own `private_run_cleanup` with a 2 s bound; the shared copy belongs in its
own branch.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p reprise-core artist_portrait` — unit tests, each red before
      its fix (evidence files `red-*.txt`)
- [x] `acceptance/deezer-placeholder-portraits/run-accept.sh` — visual acceptance,
      8/8 oracles, ranks 1–20 regression-checked
- [ ] Optional after landing: `rm -rf ~/.cache/reprise/artist-portraits` to make
      the repair visible immediately instead of waiting for the 17/18 Aug TTL
      expiry. Refetching is lazy, only for displayed artists, and only if
      `module.artwork.enabled` (default off) and the online-source gate allow it.

author: lyubomir-bozhinov
body:
No corpus content touched, and that is the finding: **#11's recommended fix would have destroyed three nodes.**

## Re-derived from each node's own prompt

The quarantine holds six nodes, classified by three tickets in three sweeps. Reading each node's `change` prompt instead of the sweep that found it:

| node | ticket | ticket says | the prompt says |
|---|---|---|---|
| go-ledger | #11 | re-stub | "The ledger exercise is a **refactoring exercise** … (somewhat surprisingly) it **consistently passes**" |
| go-markdown | #11 | re-stub | "a refactoring exercise … somehow it works and **all the tests are passing**" |
| java-ledger | #23 | "the SAME content defect" | same refactoring prompt |
| java-tree-building | #23 | "the SAME content defect" | "refactor a **working** but slow and ugly piece of code" |
| javascript-ledger | #16 | not repairable, composition decision | ✅ the only correct classification |
| go-counter | #11 | author the missing test | upstream-**deprecated**, write-your-own-tests — ✅ #11 is right that it is not mechanically repairable |

**Five of six are one phenomenon**, and #16 already names it. The three-way split came from which sweep found each node, not from what the node is.

## Why "re-stub the two" is not a repair

Gutting a refactoring exercise's implementation does not restore a RED state that was lost — there was never one. It **replaces the exercise with a different exercise**, and leaves the node's `change` prompt still instructing the model to "refactor this working code" against a seed that no longer exists. The node would then lie about itself, which is a worse defect than the one being fixed.

That makes it #16's parked drop-or-exclude decision, now governing five nodes instead of one.

**The substitution is available, and this corpus already contains the precedent.** `go-tree-building` carries the identical *"refactor a working…"* prompt and the Go track ships it as `panic("Please implement the Build function")` — honestly RED, not quarantined. So the route exists; taking it is a composition decision (the prompt has to move with the seed), not a mechanical repair.

## The list is not short — checked independently

Swept all 250 prompts for the task verb rather than trusting the quarantine's own enumeration. Eight nodes matched. The two that are **not** quarantined are correctly not quarantined:

- `go-tree-building` — ships a stub, RED.
- `python-tree-building` — ships the upstream slow implementation and scores **6 failed / 7 passed** against its own suite. Measured, not assumed.

Which is the useful correction to my own first read: **the prompt does not decide RED-ability, the seed does.** The sweep stays the authority; this comment block is only its reading.

## Second defect, same block

The summary printed all of `KNOWN_GREEN` beside a count that only ever incremented for nodes the run reached:

```
RED invariant: … quarantined=3 (language=go)
  quarantined (…): go-counter go-ledger go-markdown javascript-ledger java-ledger java-tree-building
```

Three, then six names. A count that disagrees with the list next to it teaches the reader to trust neither. It now prints what it counted.

## Verification

Self-test grows a fifth property, with four mutations each caught by name:

| mutation | caught |
|---|---|
| print the whole `KNOWN_GREEN` again (the defect) | `quarantined=2 but 3 node(s) named` |
| never append to the accumulator | `quarantined=2 but 0 node(s) named` |
| never increment the count | `2 fixtures are quarantined but the summary says quarantined=0` |
| control: suppress the section entirely | `quarantined=2 but 0 node(s) named` |

The count assertion is **not** redundant with the agreement assertion: with the count stuck at 0 the section is skipped and the two agree at 0 while the coverage gap goes unreported. Its expected `2` comes from the fixture's own composition, not from what the run printed.

One more found by mutating: `grep -c` on an empty list exits 1, and under `set -euo pipefail` that killed the whole self-test with **no output at all** — a guard dying silently on the exact state it exists to detect. `wc -w` now.

Sweeps pass for go (45/45, 3 quarantined) and python (41/41, 0). `verify-attribution.sh --check` passes at 250 nodes.

Leaves #11 and #23 open — the decision they now both defer to is #16's.

author: thameema
body:
## Summary
- Hybrid recall's independent SQL arms (primary raw-turn + semantic search, plus one raw+semantic pair per grounded/wide namespace) previously ran one after another on a single held connection (`core/service.py`'s `recall_fetch`/`recall_wide_fetch`). They now fire concurrently, each on its own short-lived pooled connection, via a new `conn_factory` parameter (defaults to `None`, which is byte-identical to the original sequential behavior for every existing in-process/script/test caller).
- `MemnosMemory._dispatch_sql_jobs` pre-submits every independent arm to a bounded `ThreadPoolExecutor`, then returns resolvers in the same order the old blocking calls sat at, so every existing degrade/dedup/ordering rule (issue #41's per-arm `RECALL_ARM_FAILURES` handling, issue #2's dedup, the staleness pass) stays byte-identical — only wall-clock time changes.
- Connection-pool discipline: `jobs[0]` reuses the already-checked-out phase-B connection (no new checkout); the rest are bounded by `MEMNOS_RECALL_SQL_CONCURRENCY` (default 2 — deliberately smaller than phase 1's rerank-thread default of 4, since this cap multiplies shared, pool-wide connection pressure across every simultaneously in-flight recall, not one process's CPU budget). A connection-acquisition failure under a saturated pool (`psycopg_pool.PoolTimeout`, itself a `psycopg.OperationalError`/`DatabaseError` subclass) is already a `RECALL_ARM_FAILURES` member, so it degrades just that one arm through the existing mechanism instead of hanging or crashing the recall.

## What this verifies vs. what it doesn't
- Overlap is proven directly (two arms' queries observed in flight on distinct threads at the same wall-clock instant, against a real pool) vs. the same code path with `conn_factory=None` provably serializing, using an injected deterministic delay rather than real-query timing luck.
- Bundle parity (order, `_ns` tags, `dup_count`, degraded flags) is proven across narrow/temporal/grounded/wide recall paths.
- Pool-exhaustion handling is proven both ways: several simultaneous recalls fit a modestly-sized real pool with zero degraded arms, and a deliberately starved pool degrades exactly the one arm that couldn't get a connection. A *query* failure (not just connection-acquisition) on an arm dispatched through `conn_factory` is also proven to preserve its exception class + SQLSTATE across the thread boundary.
- **Not measured here**: the actual `sql_ms` improvement on real field data — that needs the same kind of field re-run confirmation phase 1 got before this is closed on real hardware, not just structurally correct.
- Rerank input truncation (~256 tokens), the *other* phase-2 lever from this issue's profiling, is intentionally **not** included — it changes the reranker's actual input and still needs an approved LoCoMo accuracy run before shipping, per project policy.

Fixes #12

## Test plan
Run against an isolated, throwaway `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` container (not the real `~/.memnos/config.json` or the production `:8900` server), with `HOME`/`PYTHONPATH` overridden per this repo's local-suite conventions:
- [x] `tests/test_recall_sql_concurrency.py` (new, 45 checks) — concurrency-is-real, result-parity, and pool-exhaustion coverage described above
- [x] `tests/test_recall_arm_degrade.py` (43 checks, unmodified) — confirms the `conn_factory=None` sequential path is untouched
- [x] `tests/test_recall_staleness.py` (17 checks, unmodified) — confirms the downstream staleness/rank pipeline is untouched

Only these three files were run, not the full local suite, per this change's scope (avoids incidents from running the full suite against real infra). Note: `tests/test_write_transparency.py` has a known, pre-existing local-only failure (a stale `secret://openai` config leaking into a subprocess via `~/.memnos/config.json`) unrelated to this change — not investigated here.

author: jdwillmsen
body:
Follow-up to the `truenas-iscsi` reland. The node DaemonSet got past the mount failure but hit a new one on container creation:

```
failed to apply OCI options: failed to mkdir "/usr/local/etc/iscsi":
  mkdir /usr/local/etc/iscsi: read-only file system
```

`/usr/local/etc` is part of Talos's immutable image, so `DirectoryOrCreate` cannot create the directory there.

## Why /var/lib/iscsi

Under `ISCSIADM_HOST_STRATEGY=nsenter` the driver runs the **host's** `iscsiadm` through the host namespace, so this volume is vestigial — nothing reads config from it. It only has to resolve.

Three candidates, checked on a live node with `talosctl`:

| Path | Exists on host | Resolves for kubelet | Writable |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/etc/iscsi` | yes | **no** — kubelet's own mount namespace | — |
| `/usr/local/etc/iscsi` | no | — | **no** — immutable image |
| `/var/lib/iscsi` | **yes** | yes — kubelet lives under `/var/lib` | **yes** |

## Progress so far

Each fix has moved the failure forward, which is the right direction:

- Original: `0/4` containers, `hostPath type check failed` — wrong path for Talos entirely
- Reland: `3/4` containers, mount resolved, `mkdir ... read-only file system` — right strategy, unwritable path
- This: expected `4/4`

## Test plan

- [x] `helm template` renders `iscsi-dir → {'path': '/var/lib/iscsi', 'type': 'DirectoryOrCreate'}`
- [x] `/var/lib/iscsi` confirmed present on a live node
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] **Post-merge: node DaemonSet 4/4 Running on every node**
- [ ] Post-merge: PVC create → write → delete on `truenas-iscsi`, zvol under `storage/k8s/iscsi/vols`

If this doesn't reach 4/4, the class comes out again rather than sitting broken — same rule as before.

author: pepone
body:
Closes #6605.

`PySliceLoader`'s constructor took a strong reference to its `sliceLoader` argument with `Py_NewRef` into a raw `PyObject*` member before validating it. When the argument was not callable, the constructor threw `InitializationException` and the reference was stranded: the destructor of a partially constructed object never runs, and a raw pointer member has no cleanup of its own — the mirror image of #6600 on the same error path, a leak instead of a crash.

The member is now an owning `PyObjectHandle`, like the `ThreadHook` and the other `InitializationData` wrappers, so the reference is released even when validation throws. The destructor keeps its `PyGILState_Check` assert — the handle's release still requires the GIL — since `PyObjectHandle`'s own destructor performs a bare `Py_XDECREF` with no GIL check.

author: rasaha
body:
> **Scope & non-goals**
> - Implements **GV-2E-a only** — neutral, cross-package **evidence contracts**, not an evidence authority.
> - **No** readiness scoring, **no** policy authority, **no** attribution or verification engine, **no** forecasting, **no** financial calculator.
> - **No runtime authorization** and **no authority minted**; a dataclass constructor performs no cryptographic or organizational verification.
> - **No changes to `governed-value` 0.2.0.** Its compatibility mapping is documentation-only and is **not** wired.
> - `AssessedSystemBinding` / `SubjectContext` are **excluded** (RA-owned, PR #1425 unmerged) and recorded as a **deferred dependency**; the contracts use the existing plain `tenant_id` / `subject_id` convention. No competing subject-context contract is minted.

## What this adds

A new additive module `contracts/evidence.py` in `ugence-governance-contracts`, exposing the neutral evidence vocabulary the future UVI engines share.

**Five orthogonal evidence axes** (never one linear maturity score):

| Axis | Values |
|---|---|
| `SourceBasis` | `REPORTED` · `OBSERVED` · `SYNTHETIC` · `MIXED` |
| `TransformationMethod` | `DIRECT` · `CALCULATED` · `MODELED` |
| `AttestationStatus` | `UNATTESTED` · `ATTESTED` |
| `AttributionStatus` | `NOT_APPLICABLE` · `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` · `PARTIALLY_ATTRIBUTED` · `ATTRIBUTED` |
| `VerificationStatus` | `UNVERIFIED` · `VERIFICATION_FAILED` · `VERIFIED` |

Guarantees (enforced + tested): `ATTESTED` never implies `OBSERVED`/`ATTRIBUTED`/`VERIFIED`; `VERIFIED` never implies `ATTRIBUTED` (and vice-versa); verification binds an exact declared `claim_ref`; **caller enum labels alone never satisfy the structural requirements**.

**Contracts:** immutable, digest-bound, timezone-aware references — `EvidenceReference`, `EvidenceProvenance`, `BenchmarkReference`, `AssessmentWindow`, `ForecastHorizon`, `PopulationSlice`, `ConfidenceBasis`; the neutral `MetricClaim` (reported/observed/calculated/modeled) and the constrained `MetricObservation` (source fixed to `OBSERVED`, `AssessmentWindow` required, `ForecastHorizon` impossible, never auto-elevated); `EvidenceUsageScope`; and `EvidenceContractError` (subclasses `ValueError`).

**Structural invariants:** CALCULATED/MODELED require input evidence (+ calculation/model reference); ATTESTED/ATTRIBUTED/VERIFIED require their authority-produced references (attester identity; attribution assessment + counterfactual + causal method; verification assessment + verifier identity + time); SYNTHETIC is `EVALUATION_ONLY` and cannot be attributed/verified; cross-tenant / cross-subject mixing, duplicate references, malformed digests, and invalid/naive time windows are rejected.

## Compatibility

- **Additive.** No existing public field, enum value, default, serialization, or authority meaning changed.
- Package `__version__` `0.1.0 → 0.2.0`. **`CONTRACT_VERSION` unchanged at `1.0.0`** (provider contract surface unchanged; `governance-provider-framework` asserts `== "1.0.0"`).
- stdlib-only leaf preserved; no dependency on any UVI leaf; isolated `--no-index` install preserved.
- `governed-value` 0.2.0 mapping (docs only, not wired): `EvidenceStatus.REPORTED → SourceBasis.REPORTED + TransformationMethod.DIRECT`; `AuthorityStatus.UNVERIFIED → AttestationStatus.UNATTESTED + VerificationStatus.UNVERIFIED`; current effect → `AttributionStatus.NOT_ATTRIBUTED`.

## Tests & isolated-wheel results

- **`pytest`: 87 passed** (39 new evidence unit/contract/adversarial tests + 48 existing), covering: deterministic enum serialization; valid direct/observed/calculated/modeled claims; rejection of calculated-without-input, modeled-without-model-ref, observed-with-ForecastHorizon, MetricObservation-without-AssessmentWindow, ATTESTED/VERIFIED/`VERIFICATION_FAILED`/ATTRIBUTED without required refs; `VERIFIED + NOT_ATTRIBUTED` valid; `ATTESTED + REPORTED` stays REPORTED; duplicate refs; cross-tenant / cross-subject mixing; malformed digests; invalid/naive time windows; synthetic without `EVALUATION_ONLY` and synthetic-attempting-verified rejected; caller-labels-alone rejected; identical canonical digests.
- **Isolated-wheel `--no-index` verifier: PASS** — `ISOLATED SINGLE-WHEEL GOVERNANCE-CONTRACTS DISTRIBUTION VERIFIED`, `__version__ 0.2.0`, `CONTRACT_VERSION 1.0.0`, evidence smoke-check (structural guard fires).
- **Reverse-dep safety:** `governance-provider-framework` compatibility suite **32 passed** (incl. its `CONTRACT_VERSION == "1.0.0"` assertion). (GPF integration tests that import decision-authority error on a missing `pydantic` in the sandbox — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.)

## Prerequisite note (transparency)

The GitHub API currently reports **PR #1427 (the UVI ADR) as still open/draft/unmerged**, and the ADR is not yet on the default tree. This PR was implemented per explicit direction, treating the authored ADR design as authoritative; GV-2E-a is additive, self-contained to `governance-contracts`, and has **no conflict with any merged canonical contract**. If the ADR merges with changes, these contracts may need reconciliation.

## Deferred milestones (NOT in this PR)

GV-2C (assessment context + policy schemas), the benchmark registry, `AttributionAssessment` / `VerificationAssessment` producers, GV-3R readiness evaluator, forecasting, financial valuation, and the RA-owned `SubjectContext` / `AssessedSystemBinding` binding.

## Exact changed-file scope

Entirely under `packages/governance-contracts/` (10 files): `contracts/evidence.py` (new), `tests/contract/test_evidence_contracts.py` (new), `contracts/__init__.py`, `src/…/__init__.py`, `api.py`, `public_api.json`, `verify_governance_contracts_distribution.py`, `tests/compatibility/test_legacy_compat.py` (version pin update), `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

---

## Summary
Confirmed live: an outgoing carrier confirmation SMS could match and complete the **wrong** order. Order `DEX907119529` (EVC Plus → eDahab corridor, whose own dial attempt genuinely timed out) got marked `completed` by a confirmation SMS that was actually meant for `DEX907751183` (eDahab → EVC Plus corridor) — purely because `DEX907119529` had an earlier `updated_at` and the matching query only checked amount + receiver phone across all order history, with no provider or recency check.

- **Exchange payout-confirmation** (`exchange.routes.ts`): join the candidate order's corridor down to its actual payout wallet and require the SMS's carrier (`payment_wallets.provider_label`, e.g. `Hormuud`/`Somtel`) to match, plus scope candidates to the last hour. Threaded `entry.provider` through `ExchangePayoutConfirmationRequest` in the Agent App — the Kotlin parsers already tag each confirmation with its network, it just wasn't reaching the backend.
- **Internet Store voucher-confirmation** (`orders.routes.ts`): same treatment. The Kotlin app was already sending this same `provider` field on every request; the backend was silently ignoring it.

## Test plan
- [ ] Re-run the Agent App build with these changes
- [ ] Deploy the backend and confirm a fresh Money Exchange test order completes correctly without stealing/being stolen by an unrelated order

author: valerielinc-ops
body:
Addresses #5510 (items 1 e 2). Aggregata multi-item: resta aperta.

**Il bridge di redirect che la issue chiede al punto 1 esiste gia' ed e' vivo.** Non e' stato riprogettato: e' stato *misurato*. `/en/cross-border-articles/slug-gaggiolo-traffic/` risponde **301 → `/en/cross-border-articles/gaggiolo-traffic/`**, e lo stesso vale per la coppia tedesca. Il commento in `audit-slug-prompt-leaks.mjs` che lo dava per inesistente («article pages have no `previousSlugs` bridge, that mechanism is job-board only») era gia' falso quando e' stato scritto. Quindi il residuo vero non era costruire un bridge, ma fare la contabilita' che nessuno faceva.

## Implementato

- **`KNOWN_LEGACY_LEAKS` da 17 voci a 15, e l'allowlist ora ha una scadenza.** Rimisurato da origin (non dal checkout locale, che e' stale): 15 delle 17 voci corrispondono ancora a uno slug presente nei due registri, 2 no. `slug-gaggiolo-traffic` e `slug-gaggiolo-verkehr` erano state riparate a monte — `routerBlogData.ts` oggi legge `'gaggiolo-traffico': { …, en: 'gaggiolo-traffic', de: 'gaggiolo-verkehr', … }`, senza etichetta — e la lista continuava a giustificarle senza che niente lo segnalasse. Escono.
- **L'audit ora fallisce su una voce morta, non solo su un leak nuovo.** `findDeadAllowlistEntries()` (esportata, cosi' il test asserisce *quella* e non una seconda implementazione della stessa idea) confronta ogni voce con gli slug effettivamente letti e esce **1** su quelle che non descrivono piu' niente. La direzione e' insolita — il gate diventa rosso perche' la produzione e' *migliorata* — ed e' il punto: una voce che non descrive piu' niente non e' inerte, resta armata sopra una **stringa** e copre il prossimo slug che ci finisce sopra. L'unico modo di spegnerla e' cancellare la riga, cioe' esattamente la contabilita' che non avveniva.
- **Fail-closed dalla parte giusta.** Se manca un *registro* il verdetto viene sospeso (`enforceable: false`) invece di indovinato: un registro non letto farebbe sembrare morte tutte le voci e trasformerebbe la guardia in una richiesta di cancellare un'allowlist vera. Le sitemap invece possono mancare senza conseguenze — uno slug non arriva in una sitemap senza passare da un registro, e `scripts/ci/check-blog-slugs-sitemap-sync.mjs` lo impone nei due versi — quindi il verdetto e' identico in worktree sparse e in CI (asserito).
- **Gruppo `educatore` consolidato: overrides da 8 a 28.** Le 5 varianti quasi duplicate della sezione frontaliere canonicalizzano su `frontaliere-educatore-ticino-stipendio-requisiti`, in tutti e 4 i locali. La vincitrice non e' una preferenza: e' la piu' recente (2026-07-23) ed e' l'unica con la forma `frontaliere-<mestiere>-ticino-stipendio-requisiti` che il proprietario aveva gia' scelto per `piastrellista` nello stesso file. Le righe sono generate dai registri, non digitate.
- **Regola anti-taglio rispettata e verificata live.** Tutte e 6 le pagine del gruppo (vincitrice + 5 ombra) rispondono **200**, in tutti i locali per la vincitrice: nessuna rimozione, nessun `noindex`, nessun redirect. Cambia solo il `<link rel="canonical">`/`og:url` delle ombra e la loro presenza in sitemap.
- **Le 5 ombra escono da `public/sitemap-blog.xml` (80 righe, 5 blocchi `<url>` interi).** Non a mano: con `dropShadowedSitemapUrlBlocks()`, il filtro del repo, cosi' il risultato e' quello che produrra' anche il prossimo sync. Un `<loc>` che canonicalizza altrove e' un gate duro (`audit-sitemap-canonicals.mjs`, `validate-sitemap-pages.mjs`). Stessa forma del precedente `piastrellista` (fb2b280c, 32 righe per 2 ombra). `check-blog-slugs-sitemap-sync.mjs` gira verde e ora esenta **7 articoli frontaliere** invece di 2.
- **Il test degli override non e' piu' cablato su una famiglia sola.** Costruiva i casi da un `WINNER_ID` e un `SHADOWED_IDS` di due elementi: aggiungere `educatore` lo avrebbe lasciato verde senza asserire niente sul gruppo nuovo. Ora i casi si costruiscono dalla mappa `_groups` **dentro il file di dati**, quindi una famiglia aggiunta al JSON porta con se' i propri casi, e una famiglia senza le sue `4 x N` righe fallisce invece di spedirsi mezza cablata. Da 29 a 76 test. Aggiunte due invarianti che una singola famiglia non puo' vedere: nessuna catena canonical (una vincitrice non puo' essere a sua volta ombra) e nessun id in due famiglie.

## Non implementato (ancora)

- **Le altre 5 voci di `KNOWN_LEGACY_LEAKS` restano** (`slug-traffico-da-record`, `slug-terzo-pilastro-3a-{switzerland,schweiz,suisse}`, `slug-terzo-pilastro-3a-vantaggi-2026-basilea`) — **blocked: sono una modifica a `content/`, che si ripara solo in `nanakokyobashi-rgb/frontaliere-articles`**. Ripararle qui verrebbe sovrascritto dal prossimo `pull-articles-corpus.mjs`. Sono vive e sporche davvero: verificate 2026-08-14 contro uno slug **inventato** che risponde 404 (quindi un 200 qui e' una pagina servita, non il catch-all del CDN), tutte e 5 rispondono 200 **e** l'HTML servito ripete il segnaposto in `<link rel="canonical">` e `<meta property="og:url">` — e' quello che vedono un crawler e un link condiviso, non un id interno. Con il bridge di redirect ora dimostrato vivo, il rename a monte non trasforma piu' quelle URL in 404: e' l'ordine obbligato della issue, ora sbloccato.
- **Le 3 pagine `educatore` della sezione svizzera non entrano in questa mappa** — **per scelta**: sono governate da `data/swiss-article-canonical-overrides.json`, dove `lavorare-educatore-infanzia-ticino` e' gia' una vincitrice assestata da #3010 item 1. Tirarle dentro attraverso il confine di sezione sposterebbe canonical gia' decisi, per un guadagno che nessuna misura in questa PR sostiene. Il campo e' una URL assoluta, quindi resta possibile in seguito con una decisione del proprietario.
- **Le ~180 coppie storiche misurate dal gate del corpus (#120) non sono toccate** — **per scelta**: ognuna vuole una vincitrice scelta, non un default. Quello che questa PR lascia in eredita' e' il meccanismo per farlo in sicurezza: aggiungere una famiglia a `_groups` e' ora una edit di dati che il test verifica da sola.
- **Nessun rebuild delle sitemap oltre alle 5 righe di blocco tolte** — **per scelta**: i gate duri leggono `dist/`, che si rigenera al build; `public/` e' allineato a mano come nel precedente, per non lasciare il file committato in disaccordo con la mappa nell'intervallo.
- **`tests/seo-completeness.test.ts` e `tests/sitemap-slug-integrity.test.ts` non sono stati eseguiti in locale** — **blocked: worktree sparse**. Importano build-plugin e `data/jobs.json` (quest'ultimo non e' nemmeno in git), quindi sono rossi in sparse e verdi in CI per costruzione — il corollario documentato in `CLAUDE.md`. Verificati invece in locale: `blog-slugs-sitemap-sync`, `packages-articles-confinement`, `mirror-transport-import-closure`.

### Prova per mutazione degli osservatori

Un test verde non prova niente finche' non lo si muta. Entrambi i versi, misurati:

| mutazione | atteso | esito |
|---|---|---|
| rimetto `slug-gaggiolo-traffic` in `KNOWN_LEGACY_LEAKS` (il difetto appena tolto) | rosso | **rosso** — 2 test falliti + audit CLI exit **1** che nomina lo slug |
| tolgo una riga di override del gruppo educatore (`kinderbetreuer-tessin-gehalt-2026`) | rosso | **rosso** — 4 test falliti, incluso il conteggio derivato |
| la vincitrice educatore diventa a sua volta ombra (catena canonical) | rosso | **rosso** — 6 test falliti |
| +10 righe di commento innocue in `audit-slug-prompt-leaks.mjs`, in `routerBlogData.ts` e nel test | verde | **verde** — 145 test passati, audit exit 0 |

L'ultima riga e' la ragione per cui il controllo e' **strutturale** e non una finestra a byte: `slice(idx, idx+N)` su un registro va rosso il giorno che qualcuno aggiunge un commento, e una guardia che piange sui commenti viene silenziata entro una settimana.

### Trasporto e confinamento

`frontaliere-article-canonical-overrides.json` sta sotto `packages/articles/engine/`, l'unica area del sito con trasporto **automatico** verso il corp

| Tabel | Baris |
|---|---|

| `Odp` | **0** |
| `Customer` | **0** |
| `Subscription` | **0** |
| `PppoeSession` | **1.718** — menggantung |

Itu yang sebenarnya menahan peta maupun LibreNMS, dan tidak bisa diselesaikan
dengan menulis kode.

**LibreNMS sebagian besar juga bukan koding.** Ia aplikasi tersendiri yang
dipasang lalu disambungkan — `LIBRENMS` sudah ada di `INTEGRATION_PROVIDERS`,
dan `MonitoringAlert` generik sudah mencocokkan `hostname` → `NetworkDevice`
dan `siteCode` → `NetworkSite`. Tidak perlu adapter khusus untuk alarm.

## Keputusan yang diajukan

1. **LibreNMS ke CRM atau ke `monitoring-noc`?** Saran **CRM** — di sanalah
   alarm bisa dijawab dengan "berapa pelanggan terdampak".
2. Sumber kebenaran daftar perangkat — saran **CRM**, penemuan LibreNMS
   dilaporkan sebagai "belum terdaftar".
3. Koordinat pelanggan diambil dari mana.
4. Siapa boleh melihat lapisan pelanggan di peta (data pribadi).

## Urutan

Dimulai dari **memeriksa SNMP** di router dan OLT. Kalau SNMP belum hidup,
seluruh bagian LibreNMS berhenti sebelum dimulai.

body:
The Tag and Status hooks call `seqnr.renumber` but never await it. When you create a lot of tags or statuses in one go, those loose promises pile up, the DB connection pool runs dry, and a single unhandled rejection takes the whole api-server down.

This just catches and logs the renumber error so it can't crash the server anymore.

I pulled it out of the async duplication work, where bulk creation is what made it fall over in the first place. It's a small standalone fix, so it goes straight onto branch-sprint-1.

author: rasitgueven
body:
`fehlbild_labels` trug bisher nur den Coach-Klartext. Der Elternreport braucht eine gebündelte Ebene darüber: mehrere Fehlbilder derselben Art ergeben für Eltern **einen** Satz, nicht fünf.

Gelöst über eine Ebene **darüber**, nicht durch Zusammenlegen von Slugs — die Coach-Diagnostik braucht ihre Feinheit (fünf unterscheidbare Vorzeichen-Befunde sind fünf verschiedene Übungen), der Elternreport braucht einen Satz.

## Schema

| Was | Wo |
|---|---|
| `fehlbild_familien` (`schluessel` PK, `elterntext`, `freigegeben_am`, `freigegeben_von`) | neu |
| RLS + `fehlbild_familien_read` (Leserecht admin/coach), `grant select to authenticated` | wörtlich wie `fehlbild_labels` (A20) |
| `fehlbild_labels.familie` (text, nullable) + FK auf `fehlbild_familien(schluessel)` `on update cascade` | neu |
| `lsa_fehlbild_auswertung` → `familie` + `familie_elterntext` dazu, `klartext` raus | geändert |
| `lsa_fehlbild_report` | **unverändert** (Coach-Sicht) |

Die Abnahme-Schranke ist wörtlich die aus AF3: ohne `freigegeben_am` liefert die RPC keinen Elterntext. Kein Default, kein NOT NULL — der Normalzustand einer neuen Familie ist „nicht abgenommen".

## Inhalte

5 Familien (`vorzeichen`, `gleichungen_umformen`, `rechenreihenfolge`, `einheiten_massstab`, `sachaufgaben`) und 20 Fehlbilder, alle mit `freigegeben_am = now()` und `freigegeben_von` = Rasits Admin-Profil.

**Fachliche Abnahme durch Lena steht aus.** Die 25 Texte sind von Rasit abgenommen, nicht fachlich geprüft. Rücknahme:

```sql
update public.fehlbild_familien set freigegeben_am = null, freigegeben_von = null;
```

## ⚠️ Warum `klartext` aus dem Eltern-Pfad verschwindet

Das ist die einzige Abweichung von der Spec und der Grund, sie zu lesen.

`fehlbild_labels.klartext` war bis AF3 **Elternsprache**; mit AF4 wird er der **Coach**-Satz. Aber `lsa_fehlbild_auswertung` ist die Quelle des **Eltern**-Reports:

```
lsa_fehlbild_auswertung → src/lib/supabase/lsaReport.ts:218 → ReportBody.tsx:152 → fb.klartext
```

Hätte die RPC `klartext` weiter ausgegeben, stünde nach dem Apply „x-Terme richtig zusammengefasst, die Konstante addiert statt subtrahiert" im Elterngespräch — genau das, was INV-4.3 verhindert. Deshalb verliert der Eltern-Pfad die Spalte. Der Coach-Satz bleibt exklusiv in `lsa_fehlbild_report`.

Folge: `ReportBody` zeigt bis zur Bündelung seinen neutralen Fallback. **Kein Rückschritt** — heute ist kein einziger `klartext` freigegeben, die Fläche zeigt den Fallback also schon jetzt. `familie` und `familieElterntext` sind in `ReportFehlbild` bereits da, damit die Bündelung nur noch eine Frage der Darstellung ist.

`familie` passiert die Schranke **ungefiltert**: es ist ein Gruppierungsschlüssel wie der Slug, kein Text. Hinge er an der Textabnahme, fielen die Zeilen ohne Freigabe auseinander statt still zusammenzubleiben. Wer `familie` rendert, verstößt gegen INV-4.3 wie bei einem rohen Slug — steht als Kommentar am Typ.

Der Signaturwechsel erzwingt `drop function` + `create` (Postgres ersetzt keinen Rückgabetyp, 42P13). Der Drop nimmt die Grants mit; sie werden neu gesetzt, und Fall 11 der PRUEFUNG belegt das — sonst fiele die RPC erst zur Laufzeit aus.

## Offene Punkte

1. **`teilgekuerzt` bewusst unbestückt.** Der Slug beschreibt etwas anderes als er tut: in allen 21 belegten Fällen (`bruch_add`, Klasse 6) ist das Ergebnis *gar nicht* gekürzt, nicht teilweise — `1/4 + 1/12` kommt als `4/12` statt `1/3`. Nicht umbenannt: der Slug steht in 21 `acceptance->known_errors` und in `lsa_responses`, ein Rename ist eine eigene Migration mit Datenmitzug. Fall 14 der PRUEFUNG hält fest, dass das Absicht ist.
2. **Bündelung in `ReportBody` fehlt noch.** Die Daten liegen an, die Darstellung gruppiert noch je Slug.
3. **`erklaerung` von `linearer_faktor` und `faktor_zehn_daneben`** trägt weiter die AF3-Elternprosa, während `klartext` jetzt der Coach-Satz ist. Verlässt die DB über keine RPC, sollte aber beim Durchgang mit Lena aufgeräumt werden.
4. **`term_*` liefert kein Fehlbild-Material.** 26 Aufgaben in vier Term-Skills, 0 `acceptance` — ein Drittel der Gleichungs-/Term-/Vorzeichen-Familie ist unbestückbar.

## Prüfung

`supabase/checks/fehlbild_familien.PRUEFUNG.sql`, 14 Fälle + Negativkontrolle. Kern: **Familie wird geliefert wenn freigegeben, Elterntext null wenn nicht** — bei gleichzeitig laufendem Coach-Satz, was belegt, dass die zwei Schranken unabhängig sind.

Nachgezogen: `fehlbild_auswertung.PRUEFUNG.sql` (Spaltenliste, F6) und `fehlbild_klartext_abnahme.PRUEFUNG.sql` (Textproben auf die Coach-Sicht; **Fall 7 abgelöst** — er verlangte, dass die zwei AF3-Slugs *nicht* freigegeben sind, und prüft jetzt, dass die Elternprosa nicht als freigegebener Coach-Klartext überlebt).

Beide zusätzlich in `.github/workflows/schema.yml` registriert — sie laufen gegen eine leere DB, weil die Bestückung per Upsert aus der Migration selbst kommt.

```
neuaufbau-test.sh        38 eingespielt, 0 gescheitert, entspricht dem Schnappschuss
4 CI-Prüfskripte         alle ok
npm ci && typecheck && lint && test    grün (22 Dateien, 238 Tests)
bekannt-rot.txt          unberührt
```

## Checkliste für den Apply

```sh
git checkout dev && git pull && \
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f supabase/migrations/20260814100000_af4_fehlbild_familien.sql && \
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f supabase/checks/fehlbild_familien.PRUEFUNG.sql && \
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f supabase/checks/fehlbild_klartext_abnahme.PRUEFUNG.sql && \
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f supabase/checks/fehlbild_auswertung.PRUEFUNG.sql && \
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "insert into supabase_migrations.schema_migrations (version) values ('20260814100000') on conflict do nothing"
```

Die Migration trägt eine eigene Kontrollzählung (Teil 6): 5 freigegebene Familien, 20 bestückte Fehlbilder, keine Familie ohne Label, `teilgekuerzt` unangetastet. Weicht der Datenstand ab, bricht der Apply ab statt still durchzulaufen.

Achtung: **AF3 (`20260812100000`) ist auf der Live-DB noch nicht eingespielt** — `fehlbild_labels.freigegeben_am` fehlt dort. AF3 muss vor AF4 laufen.

author: danielhanchen
body:
## Summary

#8779 made `pip_install_try()` drop the memoized torch classification alongside `pip_install()`. It has to: it is what puts the Windows AMD ROCm trio on disk, so a memo it does not clear can answer for the build it just replaced.

That fix shipped without a test. Deleting the `_invalidate_torch_runtime_probe()` line from `pip_install_try()` leaves the whole suite green, which is the wrong state for a one-line invariant that nothing else enforces.

## What this adds

Three tests, each of which fails with that line removed and passes with it:

- `test_pip_install_try_invalidates_the_cache`, the mirror of the `pip_install` case that already existed
- `test_a_real_reinstall_is_really_reclassified`, parametrised over both installers. Two real `torch` packages on disk, a real probe subprocess either side of a real call into the installer. The mocked version proves the memo was dropped; this proves the answer that replaces it comes from the venv as it is now. It also pins the half that must NOT change: while nothing has installed anything, swapping the package on `PYTHONPATH` does not move the answer.
- `test_every_installer_entry_point_invalidates`, which reads the installer entry points out of the module with `ast` (the functions that call `_build_pip_cmd` / `_build_uv_cmd`) rather than listing them here. A third one cannot be added without either invalidating or failing this test, and the assertion says why.

## Why the ast one is worth having

The memoization rests on "`pip_install` and `pip_install_try` are the only things here that change what is installed". That is true today and is not self-enforcing. Enumerating the entry points from the module means the test notices a new one instead of quietly not covering it.

## Tests

`tests/studio/install/` and `tests/python/test_install_python_stack.py`: 2606 passed. The three `test_managed_node_runtime.py` failures reproduce on `main` in this environment (they assume a particular `UNSLOTH_STUDIO_HOME` layout).

No production change in this PR.

author: tony-toubia
body:
Follow-up to #1. Adds the MRE-inspired design elements, swaps in real attributed testimonials, and reworks the core tenets.

## Content

- Em dashes replaced with en dashes throughout, including the page title.
- Real, attributed testimonials from **Tony Toubia** (AXO Solutions) and **Chris Day** (Steel Cloud Solutions), plus **Steven Nestor** (IX-Capital Partners). Nestor is a co-investment partner rather than a portfolio company, so each quote now carries a relationship tag to keep that distinction explicit.
- Hero target revenue corrected to `$10M+` so it agrees with the criteria table (these previously contradicted each other).
- Proper address is now Overland Park, Kansas. Kansas City is kept as the colloquial reference in the headline, meta description, and key facts.

## Design

- **Hero video backdrop** and **testimonial image backdrop**, both fully wired with flat fallbacks. Paths live in a `MEDIA` config block and are `null` by default, so the page makes no request and logs no 404 until real assets are supplied. `public/slt/media/README.md` documents dimensions, encoding, and file-size budgets.
- **Testimonials are a horizontal scroll-snap track** with prev/next controls that disable at each end.
- **Three light bands** (tenets, sectors, criteria) break up the dark page. These re-point the palette custom properties rather than adding override rules, so hairlines and muted copy invert automatically.
- The positioning diagram is now **four overlapping circles**, adding technology and product alongside family office, private equity, and operating business.
- The **SLT diamond mark** from the original markup is restored, at the centre of the diagram and in the nav and footer wordmarks.
- Hero key-facts table given more weight (wider column, larger values); it was reading as secondary to the headline beside it.

## Core tenets

Rewritten to read like the firm rather than investor boilerplate, grounded in published material about the founder's operating philosophy: mutual success as the organising idea, capability that compounds rather than churns, retention as the underlying asset, and a close on credit and community rather than capital efficiency. Terminology a banker expects (NRR, buy-and-build, AI-augmentable) stays on the criteria table where it belongs.

## Bug fix

The testimonial track never overflowed at tablet width, so the carousel was inert there. Percentage track sizes in `grid-auto-columns` collapse to content inside a scroll container; both breakpoints now size in `vw`.

## Accessibility

The brand gold fails contrast on cream (1.98:1), so light bands use a darkened gold. Every text style was checked programmatically against its computed background — all pass WCAG AA.

## Verification

Playwright at 1440 / 834 / 390 / 320px: no horizontal overflow, no console errors, drawer and anchor navigation working, carousel scrolling and gating its controls at every width, touch targets >=44px. Lint unchanged from baseline.

## Notes

- The media backdrops are wired but empty until footage and photography are supplied; the page renders its flat fallback in the meantime.
- Two tenets are worth a sanity check before this is treated as final: the "anticipate change rather than react to it" line paraphrases a DEG culture statement attributable to a colleague rather than to the founder, and the community half of the closing tenet is a judgment call about what belongs on a business-tenets list.

author: luinor223
body:
## Summary

Restructures the demo into a uv workspace of independently-declared packages, each service layered so the dependency rule is machine-checked. Behaviour of the demo scenarios is unchanged - `make verify` passes the same six scenarios.

## Changes

**`shared/` became four libraries.** `platform-core` (errors, ids, correlation/causation context), `platform-persistence` (pool, unit of work, outbox/inbox), `platform-messaging` (Kafka), and `contracts` (topic names, wire types). Each is installable, so a service declares only what it uses - the auth image installs no Kafka client, which is now a fact about its `pyproject.toml` rather than a claim in a README.

**Every service is layered** into `domain/ → application/ → infrastructure/ → api/`, with `command/` and `query/` split inside the application layer, ports as `typing.Protocol`, and `main.py`/`service.py` as the composition root outside the layers. Enforced by import-linter: 12 contracts, `make arch`.

**Traefik replaced the hand-rolled API gateway**, with identity moved into its own service. Routing, prefix rewriting and rate limiting are config; the auth service owns credentials, expiry, revocation and signing. Tokens moved HS256 → RS256, so only the public half is published (`/.well-known/jwks.json`) and a verifier can check a signature without being able to mint one. Auth got its own `auth_db`; Redis and the k8s manifests are gone.

**uv workspace.** Root `pyproject.toml` with `libs/*` and `services/*` as members, one `uv.lock`. `make test`/`make arch` run through `uv run`, so a fresh clone needs no install step. Images install with uv too - mounted per `RUN`, not copied in, which keeps the installer out of the runtime layer.

author: andreyaurelien
body:
Closes #3521.

## What

Mirrors in-app notifications to the operating system's notification center, as a first-class surface managed from Settings.

- **One delivery path.** `useOSNotification` is the third consumer of the shared `mc-notification` fan-out (after `useNotificationSound` and `ThemeExperienceLayer`). `McNotificationDetail` now carries `title` / `body` / `url` / `slot` / `tag`, and the producers (`useWebSocket` notification / approval / chat_done cases, `useSSE`) enrich it.
- **The note is forwarded as-is.** Banner title and body are the note's own; the owning session's title is prefixed so a multi-session user knows which session is talking. Click focuses the app and deep-links — the note's dashboard-internal `url` when present, otherwise the owning chat (`switchSlot` + `/chat`).
- **One event, one banner.** The two historical ad-hoc paths are gone: the inline `new Notification` in the approval case (which fired a second banner with a different tag when the tab was hidden) and the unread-count effect (`useNativeNotification`, which had no visibility gate and could degrade to "N new notifications"). Their regression tests were ported to the event-driven contract, including the "no aggregate body" and "per-event tag" assertions.
- **Settings.** Settings → Notifications gains an "OS notifications" section: master switch, per-category toggles (same taxonomy as sounds), Test button. Permission is requested when the switch is turned on — never at banner-fire time — and the panel reports the pending/blocked permission state. Banners fire only while the tab is hidden; the in-app surfaces cover the visible case.
- **Turn completion now reaches the OS.** The `turn` kind (previously sound-only) carries its slot, so "the agent finished" can be a banner titled with the session name.
- **i18n.** The two approval strings moved from `hooks.useWebSocket` to `hooks.useOSNotification` with every locale's translation preserved verbatim (no dead keys, deadKeys ratchet untouched). New panel/hook strings added in the 12 locales; `en-XA` and the settings registry regenerated.

## Screenshots

The new Settings section:

![settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/andreyaurelien/KiroCrew/565e8195c42027e0d1100674b249c12c458d8177/temp-screenshots/os-notifications/01-settings-os-section.png)

A bus note delivered while the tab is hidden — the recorded `new Notification()` carries the note's own title, body and tag (the proof card renders exactly what the constructor received):

![banner proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/andreyaurelien/KiroCrew/565e8195c42027e0d1100674b249c12c458d8177/temp-screenshots/os-notifications/02-banner-proof.png)

An approval frame — exactly one banner (the harness fails if the constructor is called twice for one approval), session name resolved from the owning slot:

![approval single banner](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/andreyaurelien/KiroCrew/565e8195c42027e0d1100674b249c12c458d8177/temp-screenshots/os-notifications/03-approval-single-banner.png)

Captured by `website/scripts/capture-os-notifications.mjs` (real built SPA, gateway-free, `Notification` global replaced by a recorder before boot).

## Tested

- `npx vitest run` — 1084 files, 18138 passed, 0 failed (full suite)
- New: `src/test/useOSNotification.test.ts` (12 tests: forwarding, session prefix, turn synthesis, master/per-category/visibility/permission gates, settings hot-reload, localStorage round-trip)
- Ported: `integration/AppNotification.integration.test.tsx` (6 tests, keeps the "no `N new notifications`" and per-event-tag regressions), `notificationConstructorGuard.test.ts` (throwing constructor stays contained), `UseWebSocketCoverage` approval test (asserts the enriched event and the single-banner contract)
- `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint` (0 errors), `I18N_BASE_REF=origin/main npm run i18n:check` (all green), `npm run jscpd` (0 clones), `npm run gen:settings` (registry in sync)

## Notes for reviewers

- Default is enabled + hidden-tab-only + permission-gated: users who had granted permission keep banners (now deduplicated and content-rich); users who never granted see no change until they enable it in Settings, which is where the permission prompt now lives.
- `system.approval` per-channel protection is untouched — this PR adds a surface switch, and follows the sound surface's precedent (a global surface switch may silence everything; the per-channel mute is what stays protected).
- The Electron main-process notification path (used by the updater) was considered and deliberately not used here: the renderer path keeps web and packaged behavior identical, and the permission UX is now owned by Settings. Routing through the main process for the packaged app can be a follow-up.

author: iandebruin98
body:
Duplicating a big project, or creating one from a template, used to run inside a single request and time out with "Netwerkfout" halfway through. This moves that work to a background job.

There's a new `duplicationJobs` table and a cron worker that picks up jobs one at a time (with a lock so two workers never grab the same one), keeps them alive with a heartbeat, and re-picks-up anything that got stuck. The admin just polls a status endpoint until it's done or failed.

If it fails, the worker still writes a rollback session so the existing "remove duplicated data" button keeps working. And a job that got interrupted halfway is marked failed instead of quietly running again and doubling everything.

I stacked this on #1794 so it only shows the async changes, not the template stuff. It started life as a fix for template creation timing out, but it grew into its own job queue, so a separate PR made more sense. Once #1794 is merged GitHub will point this one at branch-sprint-1.

author: ayushkbhatia
body:
`development_units` has had a public reader since Sprint 5 and **no writer, ever**. The eight rows in production arrived with the seed data. The "What's left" table on a project page renders them, and nothing in the CMS could change a price, a plot number or an availability.

Third table in this shape this week, after `article_categories` ([#356](https://github.com/ayushkbhatia/bazar-real-estate-cms/pull/356)) and `properties.description` ([#355](https://github.com/ayushkbhatia/bazar-real-estate-cms/pull/355)) — adding Arabic keeps turning into an audit of where the CMS never finished the English.

## The grid

An **Inventory** card under the development sub-page editor. One row per unit, reorderable, eleven columns scrolling sideways rather than wrapping — a wrapped row loses the thing a grid is for, which is reading down a column to spot the plot that is priced wrong.

Per row, a drawer holds the three Arabic twins and the floor-plan link. **Duplicate** copies a row minus its id and plot number, because inventory repeats: twelve "Villa A" rows differing only by plot is the normal shape, and typing that out is the actual cost of this screen.

Separate card from "Units & floor plans" above it. That one is the *catalogue* (a handful of unit types with layouts); this is the *stock*. Different tables, different cardinality, and editing a hundred plot rows inside a folding tree of unit types would be unusable.

## The fold order

`filterUnits` classified units by English word match on `unit_type` — `/villa/i`, `/town|terrace/i` — and on `lagoon_access` — `/walking/i`. Folding Arabic in first would leave every chip reading **`Villas · 0` above a full table** on `/ar`. Not an error; just wrong, and the kind that survives review.

Classification moves to `classifyUnit`, runs **before** the fold, and travels on the row. `filterUnits` becomes a membership test that works in any locale. Pinned by a spec that filters a row whose text is already Arabic — and by a second one asserting Arabic alone matches nothing, so the constraint is stated rather than implied.

## One bug found on the way

`floor_plans.id` references the table, not the development. A plan id from another project would insert happily and then render someone else's layout on this page. Checked in the action, which is the only place that knows both.

## Verified against production

On `saadiyat-lagoons` — unpublished, and the one project holding all eight rows:

- grid loaded all 8 with their real values, `8 of 200 · 6 available`
- drawer showed three `العربية — not set` twins and a layout picker offering **this project's** plans, labelled by unit type
- typed `فيلا أ` and `شمال غربي` into unit 1, saved, and confirmed via SQL that both twins persisted **with the other seven rows and every `sort_order` intact**
- cleared the test values afterwards

`lint` · `typecheck` · `test:run` (170 files, **2132** tests) · `build` green; all 78 baseline routes unchanged.

`development_units.{unit_type, orientation, lagoon_access}` move to `WIRED_EDITOR` and `WIRED_READ`.

**Noted, not fixed:** `developments.total_units` is hand-typed on the record while the grid holds the real rows, so the public eyebrow can read "6 available of 312" against 8 stored units. The card says so; deriving the total is a separate call. Recorded in FOLLOWUPS.

body:
## What

PLAN-0105 **Step 1** — `services/db/repair_case_retention.py`, the repo's first **row**-retention mechanism, plus its DB-backed unit tests.

Closes **AC-1** and **AC-9**, and the unit-level half of AC-2/AC-3/AC-4. The seven-table + disk + projection aftermath on realistic data is Step 6's scenario test (AC-10).

Step 0 was satisfied before any of this: all four SD rulings are on `main` (PR #1161).

## Design, and why each part is that way

| Part | Why |
|---|---|
| **`CASE_RETENTION_DAYS = 90`, its own constant** | LOCKED-1: an independent decision that merely *coincides* with the prompt log's number — ADR-0035 D6's regime does not reach case text. The module imports nothing from `prompt_log`, and AC-9's guard enforces that **structurally** rather than trusting the comment |
| **Three declared classification sets** | `FK_CHILD_TABLES` (the six, in deletion order), `NO_FK_REFERENCERS` (`repair_case_run_link` → **RETAIN**, SD-4), `ROOT_TABLE`. Step 4's completeness guard reads these |
| **Files removed BEFORE rows** (SD-2 (a)) | Rows-first allows a state where bytes are **unreachable AND undeleted** — nothing points at `stored_path` any more, and no retry finds them either, because the sweep finds expired cases *by row*. Files-first makes that state unconstructible |
| **`_remove_case_directory` lets non-`FileNotFoundError` propagate** | `ignore_errors=True` would swallow a real permission failure and let the caller delete the row anyway — manufacturing exactly the state above |
| **Never raises out of a case** | A pass that died on case #3 would silently stop deleting cases #4 onward. Failures are recorded and retried, per the `rotate()` contract |
| **Projection refreshed after any deletion** | `case_projection` serves from RAM, so deleted rows keep being served until refreshed — a retention leak in memory that no DB assertion would catch |

## `RetentionReport` — three numbers, not one

Shape chosen by Cray. A pass where **every case failed** and a pass with **nothing to delete** both report zero deletions, and for a compliance control those are opposite conditions. The donor sweep makes the same point about its own counters: collapsing them would make a disarmed channel look like a quiet week.

`failed_case_ids` **names** cases; `deleted` only **counts** them. The asymmetry is deliberate — a failed case still **exists**, so naming it is the pointer an operator needs to fix it. A deleted case does not, and a list of what we erased would be a residual record of exactly what the erasure was meant to remove.

## Non-vacuity probes — all three RED, and each on its named assertion

Mutation applied to the working file, RED **seen**, original restored from a `/tmp` copy (not git), restoration verified byte-identical, suite green after.

| Probe | Mutation | The RED |
|---|---|---|
| **P1 — AC-9** | plant a `prompt_log` import | `assert not ['services.engine.llm.prompt_log']` |
| **P2 — AC-1** | drop the `opened_at < cutoff` filter | `assert 2 == 1` — the 89-day case swept in |
| **P3 — SD-4** | add `RepairCaseRunLink` to the delete loop | `assert [] == ['link-1']` |

Each reddened the assertion it was aimed at, **and only that one** — the mutation changes behaviour, not just text.

The SD-4 assertion is a **positive presence check**, never the absence of a delete: that table carries no FK, so a sweep that simply *forgot* it would look identical to one that deliberately kept it. Asserting presence is what makes the ruling testable at all.

## Gates

- Full `tests/` — **4067 → 4071 passed / 8 skipped**. The delta is exactly the four new tests.
- `mypy --strict services/` — clean, **135** source files (134 + this module).
- `ruff check .` + `ruff format --check` — clean, judged on the **extracted HEAD tree** (`git archive HEAD`), not the local checkout: untracked files here would otherwise be linted and diverge from what CI sees.

⚠️ These tests are DB-backed and **skip when Postgres is unreachable**. A skip is never satisfaction — the run above executed them.

## Next

Steps 2+3 (the periodic task runner + wiring it into `lifespan` with **zero added branches**, respecting the C901 ceiling), then Step 4 (completeness guard), Step 5 (arm fleet's profile), Step 6 (the scenario test).

author: kttran-wego
body:
## The problem

`wiki-weekly` cannot run on the MCP host at all. `wiki_health` accepted only `report`, `dreaming-plan`, and `dreaming-commit` — so there was no way to plan a weekly pass or commit its cursor. Anya's copy calls `openclaw wiki health --action weekly-plan` / `--action weekly-commit`, and Hermes has no `openclaw` CLI.

## The logic was never missing

`planWeekly` and `commitWeekly` already live in `@anya-wiki/core` and are already exported. Only the adapter wiring was absent. This adds it, mirroring the dreaming actions exactly.

- **`weekly-plan`** reads lint and health, calls `planWeekly`, and records the plan plus the pre-run baseline server-side under the returned `planId`.
- **`weekly-commit`** takes that `planId`, re-reads health and lint, calls `commitWeekly`, persists the returned pipeline state, and deletes the run record so one baseline cannot be committed twice.

### Two state keys

| Key | Lifetime | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `wiki-weekly-pipeline` | durable across runs | lane cursors, backlog, last committed fingerprint — this is what makes capped lanes rotate **fairly** instead of re-selecting the same issues every week |
| `wiki-weekly-run` | one run, deleted at commit | the in-flight plan, so the model holds only an opaque `planId` and cannot hand back a trimmed or stale baseline |

### The opt-in is threaded too

`commitWeekly` gains `allowObservedRetirements`, passed to the shared commit gate. Without it the weekly pass hits exactly the stall the dreaming pass did: retiring a claim reads as damage, the commit is refused, and the cursors never rotate.

Anya passed file paths for everything (`--state`, `--lint`, `--pre-health`, `--archive-receipts`, `--journal`…). None of that crosses the tool boundary here — the server reads and writes it all internally, and `weekly-plan` takes no arguments at all.

## Two things the guard tests caught, both real

1. **`WIKI_HEALTH_WRITE_ACTIONS` did not list the weekly actions.** Both persist state, so a **declined vault** would have accepted writes through the one tool whose name reads read-only. Now listed.
2. **The action-vocabulary test pins the exact enum** and failed. Its expected value was *stale*, not wrong — so it is updated, not deleted. That test is the reason issue 1 was found at all.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm check` green — build, **571 core tests**, typecheck, mcp:build, **463 mcp-server tests**, hosts:check, plugin:check
- [x] `pnpm plugin:sync` run — the mini serves `bundles/claude-code/`, so the change would be invisible in production without it
- [ ] Live: one weekly pass on Hermes that plans, writes, and advances the cursor

## Scope

This is the last **code** blocker for retiring OpenClaw's wiki crons. The three cron prompts are ported separately in the workspace repo, and all three must cut over together — a vault has one writer, and Hermes' copy is currently overwritten from Anya's nightly at 04:30.

author: navaneethbv
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to PR #114. `lib/ical.ts` `slug()` trimmed leading and trailing dashes with `/^-+/` and `/-+$/`; PR #114 narrowed both to a single `-` to clear Sonar S8786, which changed VEVENT UIDs for any bill name with two or more leading or trailing non-alphanumerics (`"**Netflix**"` -> `-netflix-`, `"Gym!!"` -> `gym-`, `"!!!"` -> `-` instead of `bill`). A subscriber that already holds an event reads a changed UID as a second event, so that duplicates bills in existing calendars.

The S8786 finding was legitimate: `/-+$/` is unanchored at its start, so a long dash run retries at every position. Restoring the quantifiers (as the review fix in #114 did) keeps the UIDs correct but reopens the finding.

Trimming by index satisfies both: every leading and trailing dash is removed, and there is no super-linear pattern. Interior runs are deliberately left alone, since collapsing them would change existing UIDs too.

Verified identical to the pre-#114 regex trim across 14 inputs, including `"(Rent)"`, `"**Netflix**"`, `"Car - Loan"`, `"---x---"`, `"!!!"`, and `""`.

## Validation

- `npm run test:unit` (242 files, 2502 tests)
- `npx tsc --noEmit`
- `npm run lint`

The UID regression test added in #114 (`tests/unit/ical.test.ts`, "trims every leading and trailing dash from a name-derived UID") covers this and still passes.
