author: charliedowler
body:
## What changed

- add a required `source` property to `ai_writeback.started`, `completed`, `failed`, and `merged`
- map writeback origins to `chat`, `slack`, `api`, `mcp`, `review_item`, or `unknown`
- preserve the source through both Graphile worker payloads
- mark only review-driven Build-fix turns as `review_item`, while later user turns on the same thread remain `chat`

## Why

AI writeback runs from different surfaces previously converged before analytics was emitted, so the funnel could not be split by its entry point. Required, explicit source values keep every stage attributable and make unclassified paths visible as `unknown`.

## Entry-point map

- web chat -> `AiAgentService` -> `editDbtProject` / `editRepo` -> `AiWritebackService`
- Slack agent turn -> the same `AiAgentService` tool seam, distinguished by its Slack prompt
- REST -> `AiWritebackController.runAiWriteback` -> `AiWritebackService.run`
- MCP -> `McpService.run_ai_writeback` -> `AI_WRITEBACK_PIPELINE` -> `AiWritebackService.runPipeline` -> `run`
- review item `semantic_layer` strategy -> `AiAgentAdminService` -> `generateAgentThreadResponse` -> forced `editDbtProject` -> `AI_AGENT_EDIT_DBT_PROJECT_PIPELINE` -> `run`
- successful PR merge -> `AiWritebackController.mergeWritebackPullRequest` -> `AiWritebackService.mergePullRequest` -> `trackMerged`

## Merge attribution decision

`ai_writeback.merged.source` describes the latest originating writeback run associated with the pull request, rather than the later merge action. This keeps the merged stage compatible with the writeback funnel. Historical or otherwise unlinked pull requests emit `unknown`.

## Open question

The review tool's `project_context` strategy opens pull requests without emitting `ai_writeback.*`. This remains unchanged here; should those pull requests join the writeback event family in a follow-up?

author: aagam-shah
body:
## Proposed changes

* Adds `Status\Visitor::is_tracking_automattician()`, using the three signals settled on in #51217: an identified Automattician on WordPress.com Simple, and A8C-proxied requests on Simple and WoA. It sits beside the existing `is_automattician_feature_flags_only()` and delegates to it for the WoA case.
* Content Guidelines AI now tags every Tracks event it records with an `is_a11n` boolean, so internal testing can be filtered out of product reporting.
* Image Studio drops its own copy of this logic and calls the shared method instead.

Why in `jetpack-status` rather than the plugin: the package is autoloaded everywhere Jetpack runs, including on WordPress.com Simple, where extensions load through wpcom's own loader and `load-jetpack.php` never runs. That makes it usable from both an editor extension and a settings page without either one requiring the other's bootstrap. Image Studio already imported `Visitor`, so it costs it nothing.

Why now: Content Guidelines is new and low-volume. Internal testing is a visible share of the totals, and none of its events carry anything that lets us separate it — including retrospectively, since the signal simply isn't in the data.

The flag is attached once in the feature's Tracks wrapper (`_inc/content-guidelines-ai/lib/tracks.js`) rather than at each call site, so events added later pick it up without anyone remembering to.

## Related product discussion/links

*

## Does this pull request change what data or activity we track or use?

Yes — it adds one new property, `is_a11n` (boolean), to the events fired by Content Guidelines AI:

* `jetpack_ai_guidelines_generate`
* `jetpack_ai_guidelines_generate_all`
* `jetpack_ai_guidelines_accept`
* `jetpack_ai_guidelines_dismiss`
* `jetpack_ai_guidelines_upgrade_notice`
* `jetpack_ai_guidelines_read_more_click`
* `jetpack_ai_upgrade_button`, when fired from this page (`placement=content-guidelines`)

No new personal data is collected. The value is derived from signals already available server-side and records only whether the request is internal Automattician traffic. It is a reporting signal and is never used for authorization — a proxied request says something about where a request came from, not who the user is.

Image Studio's tracking is unchanged: it already sent `is_a11n`, and the shared method is behaviourally identical to the code it replaces.

The Content Guidelines event registrations will need a follow-up to declare the new property.

## Testing instructions

Content Guidelines is gated to WordPress.com platform sites (Simple and WoA), so test there.

* Build the plugin and open the Content Guidelines settings page.
* In the browser console, confirm the preloaded state carries the flag: `window.jetpackContentGuidelinesAi.isA11n`.
* Click **Generate guidelines** on any section and inspect the recorded Tracks event — it should now include `is_a11n`.
* Expected values: `true` when proxied, or when signed in as an identified Automattician on Simple; `false` otherwise. A regular user session should always report `false`.
* Worth checking the paywall path too: with no Jetpack AI plan, click a locked Generate button and confirm both `jetpack_ai_guidelines_upgrade_notice` and the `jetpack_ai_upgrade_button` click carry the flag.
* Image Studio regression check: open the Image Studio in the block editor and confirm its events still report `is_a11n` as before.

Automated coverage:

* `pnpm run test-client` in `projects/plugins/jetpack` — covers the Tracks wrapper, including the true, false, missing-global and non-boolean cases. Run locally: 17 suites / 99 tests passing.
* `Visitor_Test` in `projects/packages/status` — covers the new method. The false case is declared before the test that defines `AT_PROXIED_REQUEST`, since a constant cannot be unset once defined.

author: tamnd
body:
The compound hyphen rule asks what comes after the hyphen and not where the hyphen was written, and on page 207 of Lie 7 to 9 that took the index off a letter. The page prints "To calculate X_+ and X_-, introduce a basis". The comma after the minus stands close enough to the formula to be read into it, the word after the comma is lower case and ends where a word ends, which is the whole of what a compound word is recognised by, so the minus was moved out of the mathematics as though it were the hyphen of "X-introduce". It is the index of X, and taking it out left the underscore that opened the index with nothing after it: the page shipped as `$X_$-,introduce`, which KaTeX will not set and which hyphenates a word the page does not hyphenate.

The plus four words to the left of it is drawn from the roman font rather than the symbol font, so it never entered the mathematics on that side of the boundary and was never in any danger. The volume printed the counterexample beside the case.

A hyphen has to be written on the line to be a hyphen. One that is the whole of an index is a minus sign, part of what the formula says rather than the spelling of the word after it. Braces are dropped from an index of one character, so an index that is nothing but the minus is the one way a formula can end in an underscore and a hyphen, and the test is exactly that.

13 lines across three volumes, 7 of `lie-vii-ix`, 1 of `ts-i-ii-fr` and 5 of `ts-iii-v-fr`, every one of them a letter, a minus index and a comma. The two Algebra printings never write one and are unchanged, so their ceilings do not move. Formulae KaTeX refuses in the Lie volume fall from 68 to 56, its P04 findings from 37 to 30, and the corpus audit from 278 soft to 271.

The test is the real line, from the poppler output of that page, with the plus kept in it so that a rule which repaired the minus by refusing every hyphen next to an index would fail on the plus.

The corpus side is tamnd/bourbaki#62, which carries the 11 repaired pages and the ceiling.

author: nicolasalt
body:
## Summary

The container-side half of the companion-CLI slice (docs/262 reqs 17, 20) resolved a
declared repository's `active` symlink twice per import — once to test it existed, once
to read the manifest through it. This pins it: one `realpathSync`, and the manifest is
read out of the concrete directory it returned.

## Rationale

`active` is a symlink an activation round re-points. Returning it unresolved left every
later read following the link again, so a refresh landing between two of them could
produce one prepare result whose commands came from one generation — the skills half of
the same pass is pinned already (#2236), so the two halves of a single Plugins card could
disagree.

`realpathSync` with **no** preceding `existsSync` is the shape, not an accident: the
missing-link case is the exception branch precisely so the check and the read cannot
straddle a swap. `buildPlan` already memoizes per declared repository, so this is one
resolution per repository per pass.

**Identity is deliberately not checked here.** Whether that generation came from the
repository the declaration now names is the axis #2225 closes on the orchestrator side,
and it is unavailable on this side by construction: the generation record lives in the
orchestrator's tree and `src/server/session/` never imports from it. The container side
is guarded by activation clearing `active` for a re-pointed declaration before it
fetches. The docstring says so, because the next reader of this function would otherwise
read the two mechanisms as redundant and drop one.

This PR previously carried a docstring on `plugin-generations.ts` describing which
callers the directory-scoped readers are for. That is superseded: #2225 gives those
readers a required `expectedSource`, which states the same rule in a form the compiler
enforces, so the prose is dropped rather than left to conflict with the branch rewriting
that file.

## Changes

- `src/server/session/plugin-cli.ts` — `activeCheckout` resolves the link once and
  returns the concrete generation directory; a link pointing nowhere yields `null` as
  before. Docstring records why identity is not checked at this site and what guards it
  instead.
- `src/server/session/plugin-cli.test.ts` — two cases: the round follows a re-pointed
  `active` (pinning is per pass, not a cache, and the stale wrapper is swept in the same
  round), and a dangling `active` surfaces nothing rather than throwing.
- `src/server/orchestrator/plugin-generations.ts` — reverted to `main`.

## Test plan

- `npx vitest run src/server/session/plugin-cli.test.ts` — 13 passed.
- `npx vitest run src/server/session/plugin-runtime.test.ts src/server/session/plugin-skills.test.ts src/server/orchestrator/plugin-commands.test.ts` — 48 passed.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint:dev` — clean.

Refs planning#355

author: diegosouzapw
body:
Closes #10360.

## O bug

`tests/unit/batch_api.test.ts` **travava para sempre** no tip da base (`timeout 240 … ; exit=124`), pendurando o job `Unit Tests fast-path (4/4)` em **todos** os PRs abertos (observado simultaneamente em #10271 e #10339).

São **dois** defeitos no guard introduzido por `9da4e24013` (#10256), não um:

### 1. `instanceof Response` é nominal — rejeitava respostas reais

`instanceof` compara contra `globalThis.Response`, mas a saída padrão do OmniRoute não usa a global: `open-sse/utils/proxyFetch.ts` instala `globalThis.fetch = patchedFetch` (linha 1159) e, quando há dispatcher/proxy, despacha pelo `fetch` do **pacote npm `undici`**, cuja `Response` é outra classe.

```js
require('undici').Response === globalThis.Response   // false
new (require('undici').Response)('x') instanceof globalThis.Response   // false
```

Ou seja: uma resposta HTTP perfeitamente válida (um 401, por exemplo) era classificada como "contract violation". `BaseExecutor` — usado pela maioria dos providers — repassa essa Response direto; executores que reembrulham numa `Response` nativa (ex.: `GithubExecutor`) não eram afetados, o que provavelmente escondeu o problema na revisão.

**Fix:** `isResponseLike()` — `instanceof` como caminho rápido, depois uma sonda estrutural (brand `[object Response]` + `status`/`ok`/`headers.get`/`text`/`clone`). Um saco `{ status, ok }` continua sendo rejeitado, e há teste fixando isso: o guard **não** foi afrouxado.

### 2. A violação de contrato era classificada como falha transitória de provider

O `TypeError` não tinha `.status`, então caía no default `BAD_GATEWAY` (`chatCore.ts:3403`). Resultado: um bug **nosso** virava "provider instável" — cooldown da conexão como *rate limited*, contagem no circuit breaker do provider, e o runner de batch (que retenta 429/502/504) girando pela janela inteira de 24h num erro que nunca se resolve sozinho.

**Fix:** o erro passa a carregar `status = 500` e `code = "executor_contract_violation"`; o código entra em `REQUEST_SCOPED_UPSTREAM_ERROR_CODES` (que governa `shouldSkipConnDisable` e `shouldTripProviderBreakerForResult`) e ganha um ramo terminal no início de `checkFallbackError`. Sem retry, sem cooldown de conta, sem breaker.

## Validação (TDD — Hard Rule #18)

| Prova | Antes | Depois |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `timeout 300 node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/batch_api.test.ts` | `exit=124` (hang) | **`exit=0`, 22/22 pass** (65.9s) |
| `tests/unit/executor-contract-violation-terminal.test.ts` (novo, 10 testes) | vermelho | **10/10 verde** |
| 11 arquivos vizinhos (`normalizeExecutorResult` / `checkFallbackError` / predicados) | — | 85/85 verde |
| `npm run typecheck:core` | — | limpo |

O teste novo fixa a premissa (undici ≠ global), o aceite cross-realm, a rejeição de shapes genuinamente inválidos (`{}`, `undefined`, `{response:"not-a-response"}`) e o par status/código do erro terminal.

## Nota de escopo

`9da4e24013` está em `release/v3.8.50` mas **não em `main`** — nenhuma versão publicada carrega o defeito.

author: surdarmaputra
body:
## Summary
This PR extends the persona system to support local customization without modifying tracked files, and adds comprehensive gitignore rules for KB adapters, agent definitions, and runtime outputs.

## Key Changes

**Persona Customization Layers:**
- Added support for `personas/<name>/config.local.json` to override individual fields in tracked persona configs (merged, local wins)
- Added support for `personas/<name>/prompt.local.md` to replace the system prompt entirely for a tracked persona
- Added support for `personas.local/<name>/` directory for completely new or replacement personas (checked before `personas/`)
- Updated `bin/spawn` to resolve personas in the correct order and merge configs appropriately

**Knowledge Base & Agent Management:**
- Added gitignore entries for `kb/adapters/*`, `kb/data/*`, and `kb/INDEX.md` (user-written KB sync adapters and runtime data)
- Added gitignore entries for `.claude/agents/*` (Claude Code agent definitions)
- Added gitignore entries for `results/*` (agent result files written at runtime)
- All include `!.gitkeep` exceptions to preserve directory structure

**Documentation Updates:**
- Updated README to document the three-level persona customization system with examples
- Updated uninstall documentation to clarify what files are removed (gitignored runtime files vs. source files)
- Added comprehensive file reference table documenting all tracked and gitignored configuration files
- Clarified the distinction between shipping custom personas (in `personas/`) vs. local overrides

## Implementation Details

The `bin/spawn` script now:
1. Checks for `personas.local/<name>/` first (complete persona override)
2. Falls back to `personas/<name>/` with config merging (tracked persona with local overrides)
3. Merges `config.json` and `config.local.json` using Python to handle JSON properly
4. Checks for `prompt.local.md` and uses it instead of `prompt.md` when present

All customization files are gitignored to prevent accidental commits while allowing users to maintain local variations without modifying tracked files.

author: adexdsamson
body:
## Active-vendor role → view-only in Contract Management

Implements: *"for a vendor without PM access, they should only be able to perform view-only access — no create/update/delete — on contract management only."* Clarified to key off the **active role**: active `vendor` (Solicitation) = read-only; active `project_manager` (Vendor-PM, CLM) = full actions. A dual-access user switches to the PM role to act. **Strict**: response/acknowledgement actions are locked for an active vendor too.

### What changed
Write gates moved from `isContractVendorLike` (`isVendor || isProjectManager`) → `isProjectManager`, or excluded active vendors on non-uniform/identity gates (`!isVendor`). **Reads, endpoint/query selection, and comment loading are unchanged** — only mutation/post controls are gated.

Surfaces covered (31 write actions across 18 files):
- **Tab headers:** Create Invoice, Submit LEM, Create Change, Create Claim, Create NCR, Submit Vendor Report, Submit Rate Sheet, Issue RFI
- **Per-row / detail sheets:** Invoice edit/resubmit, LEM edit/resubmit, Change edit/resubmit + draft-CO finalize + "Send for Approval", Claim edit/resubmit, Rate Sheet edit/resubmit, RFI respond/edit/close, Deliverable submit/resubmit, Compliance policy + per-item security submit, Amendment accept/reject, CAPA submit/approve, NCR close
- **All comment composers** (posting blocked; reading kept)

### Notable
- `DeliverablesTable` previously derived vendor-ness from `basePath` (identical for vendor and PM) — now reads the active role via `useUserRole`. `NcrTable` and `RfiRowActions` gained a `useUserRole` read for the same reason.
- **FE guard only.** Vendor and PM share the same `/contract/vendor/contracts/*` mutation endpoints, so a plain vendor can still hit them via direct API. A parallel BE write-deny for `vendor`-only accounts is required to fully enforce this (tracked separately).

### Tests
- Added negative guards: a plain vendor cannot submit policies / reject amendments.
- Re-pointed existing "can write" assertions to the PM role.
- `tsc -b` clean; affected vitest suites green. (Pre-existing `DOMMatrix` env failure in `deliverables-table.test.ts` and Playwright `.spec.ts` files are unrelated — they fail identically on the base.)

author: valentinbhend
body:
## Context

This is one of seven pull requests that remove per-step overhead from the loop a
reinforcement learning agent runs against BOPTEST: five here and two in
[boptest-gym](https://github.com/ibpsa/project1-boptest-gym). Together they make
a training step **roughly 5x cheaper**.

| control signal | out of the box | all seven applied | |
|---|---|---|---|
| a held action | 23.21 ms/step | 3.52 ms/step | 6.6x |
| SAC random exploration | 32.44 ms/step | 8.40 ms/step | 3.9x |

The spread between those two rows is the controller, not the code: actions that
switch the heat pump harder make the FMU solver do more work, and that work is
untouched by these changes. Expect a figure in that range rather than a single
number. Episode resets go 490 ms to 163 ms in both cases.

Results do not change. Observations are bit-identical. With the optional coarser
warmup grid enabled the core KPIs agree to 2.1e-08; with it left at its default
everything is bit-identical. `time_rat` changes, because it is a wall-clock
measurement.

Every option added by these pull requests is off or unset by default, so a
deployment that does not ask for them behaves exactly as before.

The issues in this set: #168 (request client), #169 (in-process backend) here;
and in BOPTEST: ibpsa/project1-boptest#859 (`get_data` cost),
ibpsa/project1-boptest#858 (KPI subset), ibpsa/project1-boptest#857 (direct
stepping), ibpsa/project1-boptest#861 (log levels), ibpsa/project1-boptest#860
(warmup grid).

---

### What this does

Adds `local=True`, which runs BOPTEST's own `TestCase` in the calling process
and dispatches the endpoints the environment uses to its methods. A step then
involves no HTTP request, no redis round trip and no JSON encoding.

Worth **2.3x on a control step** on top of the options the other pull requests
in this set add — 10.3 ms to 4.4 ms — measured with a REST environment and an
in-process one constructed in the same process and driven alternately, so drift
hits both. Episode resets barely change, because a reset is dominated by the
warmup simulation rather than by transport.

**Off by default.** Nothing changes for anyone who does not ask for it.

Results are unchanged, because the code that simulates is the same code the
BOPTEST worker runs.

### Two requirements, both from BOPTEST rather than from here

* **`pyfmi` must be importable and the test case FMU must load.** The
  distributed FMUs are JModelica-built and need `libgfortran.so.4`, which the
  BOPTEST `worker` image provides and a current distribution generally does not.
  Running inside that image is the supported way to satisfy this.
* **One environment per process.** Every distributed test case FMU declares
  `canBeInstantiatedOnlyOncePerProcess=true`, which this backend honours by
  creating one `TestCase` per process. `SubprocVecEnv` gives each its own
  process, as in the vectorized example. Threads are not an alternative: pyfmi
  holds the GIL through `do_step`, so concurrent instances serialise.

`boptest_root` points at a BOPTEST checkout containing the test case FMUs, and
defaults to the `BOPTEST_ROOT` environment variable. Each environment gets a
temporary directory of its own for the files `TestCase` writes; `stop()` removes
it and is idempotent.

### Verification

Against the REST client over an identical 12-step sequence on
`bestest_hydronic_heat_pump`: the zone temperature, the heat pump power, both
reward KPIs at every step and all nine final KPIs agree to a **maximum absolute
difference of exactly 0**.

The full CI workflow passes on this branch — `test-local` 16 OK,
`test-multiaction` 1 OK, `test-vectorized` 1 OK, `test-tutorial` 1 OK,
`test-client` 11 OK — matching unchanged `master` on every job it shares.
`local=False` is the default, so those jobs exercise the REST path throughout;

body: ## Summary The follow-up promised by #2678: `.context/designs/` held four planning documents whose real value was the reasoning buried inside them. That reasoning is now a standard, and the planning tree is gone. **2,434 lines deleted, 148 written.** Nothing read those files at runtime — all four PRD-tooling commands behave identically without them. **Stacked on #2678**, which introduces the rule this PR is the first application of. ## What the guide keeps `.context/standards/PRD-Tooling-Guide.md` records what would be expensive to rediscover and easy to undo by accident: - **Two audiences, kept apart.** Epic Leads own the PRD, engineers own the investigation. The routing test — *could someone who doesn't read code answer this?* — and the rule that `/refine-prd` never emits `file:line`, class names, or time estimates and never rewrites the PRD's prose. - **Why four agents rather than one.** They split on *when they run*, not on topic: a fully net-new PRD never dispatches the two PT9 agents, because classification is per-aspect rather than one PORT-or-NET-NEW label per PRD. - **Why `/refine-prd` is a sibling command, not a `--coach` flag.** The flag was designed and rejected — it forked the prose in seven to nine places, left ~40% dead per run, and forced one frontmatter description to serve two audiences. "Just add a flag" is the suggestion that will recur, so the reasons are written down. - **Access model and degradation**, the standing invariants (inventory corrected in the same change that disproves it; no PT10 leakage in archaeology; facts answered, decisions asked), and what was deliberately dropped from the retired porting pipeline. ## What it drops The two implementation plans, 2,086 lines of task lists for work that shipped in June and July. Nothing in them that the command files don't already say — and one of them opened by instructing agents to *execute* it, with live checkboxes. ## Two things reviewers should look at **The claims were checked against the live tooling, and four of them initially weren't.** roborev caught all four on the first commit and they are fixed in the second: the sibling-resolution convention is `{ROOT}`/`PT_REPOS_ROOT` and not `~/git/`; the orchestrator hands off to `/prd-to-jira` and not to planning; the "three-way option set" was round-1 design that round 2 replaced; and the claim that the repo had no remaining exceptions was false. **That last one found a real gap.** `docs/plans/`, `docs/specs/`, and `docs/superpowers/` hold planning documents of exactly the kind #2678's rule forbids — and several were written by the Superpowers `brainstorming` and `writing-plans` skills, which default to `docs/superpowers/`. The repository's own tooling has been depositing what the rule prohibits. The guide now tells you to redirect those skills, and names those trees as the rule's one honest exception with their conversion called out as outstanding. **Cleaning them up is deliberately not in this PR** — it is a separate decision about twelve files nobody has re-read. --- AI-assisted — [session 1](https://claude.ai/code/session_01FNfvLRp2C6xTLTKv5WgUwr) - - - This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/paranext/paranext-core/2679)

author: localai-bot
body:
Wave **L2** of #607, and it **closes #686**.

L1 ported vLLM's per-modality input limits and the refusal they produce, but
nothing constructed a config on a live request — so the numbers were
unreachable, and #685's reviewer correctly recorded that the HTTP 400 arm was
*unproven end to end* and that "L2's reviewer should treat that as an owed gate,
not an inherited pass." This wave pays that.

Spec: [`.agents/specs/multimodal-track.md` §1.5](.agents/specs/multimodal-track.md)
(the L2 block now carries the outcome). Issues: #607, #686.

## The three surfaces

**1. Serve flags** — `src/vllm/entrypoints/openai/server_main.cpp`

| ours | upstream @ `5559679229bc` |
|---|---|
| `--language-model-only` / `--no-language-model-only` | `arg_utils.py:555,1276,1691` |
| `--limit-mm-per-prompt '<json>'` | `arg_utils.py:556,1279,1692` |
| `ParseLimitMmPerPromptJson` (`src/vllm/config/multimodal.cpp`) | `multimodal.py:212-236` + the DummyOptions dataclasses `:17-43` |

Both spellings of the boolean, because `_compute_kwargs` gives a bool field
`argparse.BooleanOptionalAction` (`arg_utils.py:346-348`) — a recipe that turns
the flag off explicitly must not die on an unknown argument. The dict value is a
JSON object (`type=parse_type(json.loads)`, `arg_utils.py:379-381` — the plain-`dict` branch, corrected from `:375-377` in the review round), and all
three of upstream's object spellings parse: legacy count-only, configurable
`{"count": N, …}`, and the two mixed.

Malformed input is **refused before the model load**, never defaulted — a
mistyped limit that silently became 999 is a limit that is not there. Every
refusal is upstream's own: a non-object document, a negative count
(`count: int = Field(999, ge=0)`), an unknown per-modality option on
image/video/audio (`extra="forbid"`; corrected in the review round — every OTHER
modality falls to `BaseDummyOptions`, which has no `extra="forbid"`, so its
unknown keys are DROPPED, not refused), a non-positive option (`Field(None, gt=0)`). The profiling
options are validated, dropped (only `.count` feeds `get_limit_per_prompt`,
`:335`) and the drop is **announced per key**.

`kAcceptedInertArgs` was checked first and is untouched: #606 deliberately
excluded `--language-model-only` as "a real capability gap", and L2 resolves that
by implementing it rather than by adding an entry, so that table still holds only
genuine no-ops. `.agents/specs/serve-recipe-args.md` is reconciled to say so.

**NAMED RESIDUAL**: upstream's dotted spelling (`--limit-mm-per-prompt.image 2`)
is a `FlexibleArgumentParser` feature (`argparse_utils.py:389-425`) that applies
equally to `--kv-transfer-config` and `--speculative-config`, which this server
also takes as JSON only. Adding it for one flag would be the bespoke path; it
belongs to a parser brick covering all three.

**2. C-ABI field** — `include/vllm.h`, **`VLLM_ABI_VERSION` 18 → 19**

`vllm_model_params.language_model_only` (`int32_t`) and `.limit_mm_per_prompt`
(`const char*`, the same JSON object the flag takes). Appended at the end of the
struct, following the convention v14/v16/v18 set: a versioned `/* ── … (ABI v19)
── */` block on the field, a `v19 — …` paragraph in the header's version log
stating what a zero-initialised v18 struct gets, and the JSON-string shape
following the **v9 `kv_transfer_config` precedent** — a dict-valued vLLM flag
crosses this ABI as its own JSON rather than as a fixed struct of modalities the
ABI would then owe forever. Malformed input fails `vllm_engine_load` with
`VLLM_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

Both surfaces land on `EngineParams::multimodal` → `LoadedEngine::mm_config()`,
so the flags and the ABI resolve **one** config object per engine and cannot
drift.

**3. The call site** — `src/vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_mm.cpp`

`MakeQwen3VLImageChatFn` now runs `ValidateChatMmLimits` (the port of the
`chat_utils.py:648-662` tracker) as step 0, over a `BaseProcessingInfo` folding
the engine's config with the seam's own declared ceiling,
`Qwen3VLChatSupportedMmLimits() == {"image": 1}`.

That declaration answers the question #686 left open — *"the model's own
supported limit (the `min()` fold's other operand) — today nothing declares
one"*. This seam locates a single image part and routes no video or audio, so its
honest ceiling is one image and every other modality is **absent**, which
`context.py:414-415` reads as limit 0. A user limit can only lower it, so
`--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 99}'` still refuses the second image — and then
correctly omits the `Set --limit-mm-per-prompt to increase this limit.` hint,
because raising the user's limit would not help.

## The e2e 400 test, and exactly what it distinguishes

`tests/vllm/entrypoints/openai/test_api_server.cpp`, three legs through the real
`ApiServer::handle_chat_completions`:

1. the **real production seam** (`MakeQwen3VLImageChatFn`) + a three-image body
   → `400` / `BadRequestError` / `"At most 1 image(s) may be provided in one
   prompt."`, and asserted `!= 500` and `!= 200` and no `choices` key;
2. the same server, a **within-limit** request → `200` with a real completion,
   so the 400 is a *limit* decision and not "multimodal is off"; the same seam
   then refuses three;
3. a seam throwing a **non-validation** exception → `500` /
   `InternalServerError`, so "status == 400" cannot be satisfied by a handler
   that answers 400 to every seam failure.

Plus `--language-model-only` → `400 "At most 0 image(s) … Set
--limit-mm-per-prompt to increase this limit."` with a text request on the same
server still `200`.

**RED first, behaviourally** (these are verbatim from the pre-implementation
run):

```
CHECK_THROWS_AS( mm_fn(ImageMessages(3, uri)), vllm::v1::InputValidationError )
  threw a DIFFERENT exception: "ExpandImagePlaceholders: more image placeholders than grids"
FATAL ERROR: expected --language-model-only to refuse an image request
CHECK( refused.status == 400 )                       values: CHECK( 500 == 400 )
CHECK( j.at("error").at("type") == "BadRequestError" ) values: CHECK( "InternalServerError" == BadRequestError )
CHECK( h.server.handle_chat_completions(ImageBody(3)).status == 400 ) values: CHECK( 200 == 400 )
```

### A correction to #686, recorded rather than quietly fixed

The RED run says something the issue does not. Against the **production** seam
the pre-L2 behaviour was not the truncated 200 #686 describes — it was an
**HTTP 500**: `MakeQwen3VLImageChatFn` injects one placeholder marker per image
part while routing only the first image, so `ExpandImagePlaceholders` raised
*"more image placeholders than grids"* and the client got a server fault carrying
an internal message. The truncated 200 is real for the validate-then-build seam
shape and is pinned as its own leg (the `CHECK( 200 == 400 )` above). Both are
wrong the same way — neither is upstream's refusal — so the issue's diagnosis
(first image, `break`, no refusal) stands and only its stated consequence was
understated. `.agents/specs/mm-serving.md` is corrected accordingly, as the issue
asked.

## Mutation proof

Restored with `cp` + `touch` (not `cp -a`, which preserves mtime and makes ninja
skip the relink), rebuilt and re-verified green between every mutation. All four
mutated files verified byte-for-byte identical to the working tree afterwards by
md5.

| mutation | result | caught by |
|---|---|---|
| **(a1)** flag→config: `a.multimodal.language_model_only = false;` | `test_serve_mm_limits` 8/10, 7 assertions | `CHECK(Contains(run.output, "server: multimodal limits language-model-only=ON"))`, `image=0`, and `CHECK_FALSE(Contains(run.output, "image=4"))` in the precedence case |
| **(a2)** config→engine: `mm_config_()` instead of `mm_config_(params.multimodal)` | `test_capi` 56/57, 3 assertions | `CHECK(e.mm_config().GetLimitPerPrompt("image") == 2)` |
| **(b)** call-site wiring removed from the seam | `test_openai_api_server` 54/56 **and** `test_chat_mm` 9/11 | `CHECK(refused.status == 400)` → `500`; `CHECK(j.at("error")

## Summary

Three usability fixes to the VeritaQC program reported from the field:

1. **Typeable numeric inputs.** Every QC numeric field (Result value, chart Points, new-lot mfr mean/SD, lot-changeover mean/SD, and the import assigned-value) was a spinner `type="number"` that in the reporting user's environment could only be changed with the arrows, not typed. body:
🎯 Feature: Anti-Screenshot Dynamic Barcode Overlay for Tickets

Issue: #17715

Problem

Attendees sharing ticket screenshots or posting them online allows unauthorized check-ins, leading to venue capacity issues and loss of ticket control.

Solution

Implemented a Dynamic QR Check-in Generator that:

  • Hashes user authentication details with short-lived TOTP tokens.

  • Generates new QR code frames in browser memory every 15 seconds.

  • Enables token expiration checks on check-in scanners.

Features

  • ✅ Dynamic Rotating QR Display — QR codes automatically refresh with new tokens every 15 seconds (configurable).

  • ✅ Expiration Progress Bar Overlay — Visual countdown showing the time until the next rotation.

  • ✅ Offline-Ready Ticket Verification — Tokens include expiration metadata for scanner validation.

  • ✅ Anti-Screenshot Measures

    • Watermark overlay patterns on QR codes.

    • Visibility toggle (show/hide).

    • Warning messages discouraging screenshots.

  • ✅ User Actions

    • Copy token to clipboard.

    • Download token as a text file.

Files Added

Path | Description -- | -- …/tickets/barcode/DynamicBarcodeCard.jsx | Main dynamic barcode component …/tickets/barcode/RotationProgressBar.jsx | Circular progress timer src/components/tickets/barcode/index.js | Component exports …/utils/security/barcode/dynamicTokenGenerator.js | TOTP token generation & validation src/utils/security/barcode/index.js | Utility exports

Tech Stack

  • React 18 with Hooks (useState, useEffect, useCallback, useMemo)

  • JavaScript with Web Crypto API for SHA-256 hashing

  • Tailwind CSS for styling

  • react-qr-code for QR generation

  • lucide-react for icons

Usage

import { DynamicBarcodeCard } from 'components/tickets/barcode';

<DynamicBarcodeCard
  ticketId="REG-2026-001"
  userId="user@example.com"
  eventName="Global Open Source Summit 2026"
  interval={15}
/>

Testing

  • ✅ Tokens rotate every 15 seconds.

  • ✅ Progress bar updates smoothly.

  • ✅ Copy/download functionality works.

  • ✅ QR codes are scannable.

  • ✅ Offline-ready indicators display correctly.

author: tusharbhardwaj-bk
body:
`expbkmain` and `bkmain` each produce their own macOS app, published automatically on every push to that branch, with in-app update notifications.

| Branch | App | Bundle id | User data | URL scheme |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `expbkmain` | Stage BK T3 Code | `work.beknown.bkt3code.staging` | `bkt3code-staging` | none |
| `bkmain` | BK T3 Code | `work.beknown.bkt3code` | `bkt3code` | `t3code://` |

## How the two apps stay apart

Both publish into this repo, separated only by the updater channel. `GitHubProvider.getLatestVersion` takes the first release whose `semver.prerelease(tag)[0]` equals the running app's channel, then reads `<channel>-mac.yml` from it — so the channel is the version's **first** prerelease identifier: `X.Y.Z-staging-nightly.N` / `X.Y.Z-production-nightly.N`.

Keeping `-nightly.YYYYMMDD.N` as the **suffix** is what makes this cheap: `resolveDesktopUpdateChannel` and `isNightlyDesktopVersion` still match, `release.yml`'s `!v*-nightly.*` exclusion still holds, and `DesktopUpdateChannel` stays `"latest" | "nightly"`. Only the string handed to `autoUpdater.channel` changes.

## Safety properties

- **Keyless.** Managed builds carry no Clerk key — identity comes from the device-bound pairing credential. A key mounts `ElectronClerkProvider`, which renders nothing until Clerk's Native API answers (the known black-screen failure). Enforced by the build script *and* the workflow; both fail rather than warn.
- **Exact-SHA tags.** `--source-sha` is required. Without `--target`, `gh release create` tags the default branch — an `expbkmain` release could point at `main` while holding staging code.
- **Atomic publish.** Draft → upload → verify names/sizes/upload state → verify manifest sha512 against the ZIP → flip to prerelease. A failed upload leaves a draft, never a partial release.
- **Signed or refused.** Squirrel.Mac validates against the installed app's designated requirement, so the publisher runs `codesign --verify` and refuses unsigned builds.
- **Queued, idempotent releases.** Per-channel concurrency with `cancel-in-progress: false` (cancelling mid-publish can strand a tag). A re-run of an already-published SHA is skipped.

## Update UX

Downloads happen in the background. The notification click **surfaces** the update; it does not install. Installing quits the app and stops every backend, which would discard an in-flight agent turn or terminal session on a stray click. The labelled sidebar button — which already confirms — does the restart.

## Runner security

Self-hosted runner on a public repo, holding a signing key. Guards: `push`/`workflow_dispatch` only (neither is fork-triggerable — **do not add `pull_request`**), build job `contents: read` with publish split out at `contents: write`, `persist-credentials: false`, actions pinned to SHAs, production gated on a protected environment, plus a free-space check and build-dir cleanup.

## Verification

- `@t3tools/scripts`, `@t3tools/desktop`, `@t3tools/web`, `@t3tools/contracts` and `t3` typecheck clean.
- 410 script tests, 54 desktop tests, 70 web tests pass. New coverage: per-channel counters, cross-channel isolation, identity separation across every macOS-derived directory, and that both fork channels still enable prerelease handling.
- `check-fork-markers.ts` passes (also fixes three violations inherited from `expbkmain` that were failing the `markers` job for every PR).
- `DesktopUpdates.test.ts` cannot run on the Linux dev box (no Electron binary — pre-existing, verified against a clean tree); CI covers it.

**Not yet proven on hardware:** the self-signed Squirrel A → B update. Docs mark it unproven and gate production rollout behind it. Steps 2–10 of the rollout order in `docs/operations/bk-desktop-build.md` are the remaining work.

Incorporates review from the agent that deployed the app on a real Mac.

author: 07rinat07
laker-93
body:
Half of #125. That issue asks for a `mem_limit` on prod pymix; this PR supplies the two
things needed to set one responsibly and to survive being hit by it. The compose change
is the other half — see below.

## Why not just set the limit

Two gaps, both of which would bite after the limit lands:

**Nothing reports the peak.** `process_memory()` deliberately reported only current
values (a peak counter reads flat through a leak). Correct for a leak hunt, wrong for
sizing a ceiling: today's steady state is 276 MB, but the Rekordbox import path allocates
in bursts (#126), and a limit sized from steady state OOM-kills the process mid-import.
`rss_peak_mb` (`VmHWM`) is now reported alongside, with the docstring saying which
question each answers.

**Nothing reports the ceiling.** RSS is not what an OOM kill is charged against — the
cgroup is, and it also charges page cache and every other process in the container. New
`cgroup_memory()` reads `memory.max`/`memory.current` under v2 (the droplet) and falls
back to v1. Both "unlimited" spellings are handled: v2's literal `"max"` parsed as an
integer would report a 0 MB limit and make every sample look like a 100% emergency;
v1's `2**63`-ish sentinel taken at face value gives an 8 exabyte limit and a
`used_fraction` pinned at 0.0 forever. Off Linux it degrades to `available: false`, like
the rest of memdiag.

## The part that matters after an OOM kill

All of memdiag is pull-based — it answers beautifully, but only while someone is awake to
call `/admin/memory`. Once a limit exists, the kernel SIGKILLs at the ceiling with no
warning, no traceback and no chance to flush. **The only diagnosis that can survive that
is one already written to the log before the kill.** #116 was found by hand, and what
made it expensive was that the logs from the growth period said nothing about memory at
all; the last lines before a restart are whatever request happened to be in flight.

`mem_watch_loop` joins the lifespan task group and logs one line per interval:

```
memory: rss 275.8 MB; peak 402.1 MB; anon 249.4 MB; in_use 83.6 MB; retained 56.2 MB; cgroup 300.0/512.0 MB (59%)
```

at WARNING past `warn_fraction` of the limit, naming `/admin/memory` as the follow-up
while the process is still alive to serve it. 60s in prod, 300s in dev. Three procfs
reads and a libc struct copy per pass; `python_objects` — the one genuinely expensive
call in memdiag — is never made here. Exceptions are caught and logged: a diagnostic must
never be the reason the app goes down.

With no limit set (today) there is nothing to be a fraction of, so every sample stays at
INFO. The loop is still worth running — it gives the growth-rate history #116 lacked.

## Logs that outlive the container

`initialise_logger` has had a `TimedRotatingFileHandler` since forever, with
`disable_file_handler=True` hardcoded at the only call site — which made `logs_directory`
dead config in every file. Prod now enables it against `/subbox/logs`, on the existing
host bind mount.

This matters because of a Docker detail that cuts the wrong way: the json-file log
**survives a restart** (the container id is unchanged, so the file is appended to, and an
OOM restart keeps both runs) but **not a `docker compose up -d`**, which recreates the
container and discards its log. That includes the deploy applying the `mem_limit`, and
any later deploy made to investigate an incident. A file under `/subbox` survives the
container, the image and the deploy.

An unwritable directory degrades to console-only with an ERROR rather than crash-looping
the app — pymix runs as uid 1000 against a host-owned mount, so this is a permissions
mistake worth being defensive about.

Prod's `LogConfig.Config` is also `{}` — no `max-size`, no `max-file`, so that json-file
grows unbounded. Fixed in the compose PR.

## Testing

280 pass. 5 failures, pre-existing and identical on `main`: 3 recorded by c6fb714, plus
the 2 memdiag tests that need procfs and fail on any Mac.

New tests cover the sampler's two per-pass decisions (what the line says, whether it
warns) including the no-limit and non-glibc cases, plus both cgroup "unlimited"
spellings and the invariant that peak ≥ current.

## Sequencing — read before merging the compose PR

1. Merge, release and deploy this.
2. Let prod serve a real Rekordbox import, then read `process.rss_peak_mb` from
   `GET /admin/memory`. That is the transient high-water mark the limit has to clear.
3. Set `mem_limit` to roughly 2x it, in laker-93/traefik's `droplet` branch.

Note for #125: the issue says to change `../subbox`'s droplet branch. **pymix is not in
that repo** — `origin/droplet` there holds only `docker-compose/{beets,filebrowser,navidrome}`.
The pymix service is defined in **laker-93/traefik**, branch `droplet`. The compose PR is
laker-93/traefik#3.

Closes nothing on its own; #125 closes with the compose change.

author: hejin0-0
body:
PROMPT:

A single-player 3D obstacle-course game in the browser: plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with Three.js, no build step and no binary assets. Five stages and four games — race, hunt, survival and final — plus six characters that differ only in paint.

Level content is data. A stage is a plain object of decks, obstacles, checkpoints, pickups and hazards, and declares which games it can host; a mode owns what wins, what loses and what the HUD shows. Game runs the simulation and asks, so neither has a branch per the other.

test.html is the gate. It boots the real page in a hidden frame and checks the physics assertions, six fairness rules over every stage, five scripted bot playthroughs per stage-and-game pairing, each mode's lose path against a declared expectation, and that all six characters produce byte-identical runs.

The fairness rules are not style guidance. Each one is a bug that shipped once and had to be found by automated play — a sweeper that owned the whole runway so there was nowhere fair to time the next jump, checkpoints respawning inside a rotating bar, a slider landable in 20% of its cycle, pickups guarded by a shove or sitting where the hazard's own answer never goes.

author: jasleenkaur-qed42
body:
## What does it do?

Extends `plugin::upload.breakpoints` so each entry can be either:

- a **number** — existing behaviour (`width` + `height` = value, `fit: 'inside'`)
- a **Sharp `ResizeOptions` object** — e.g. `{ width: 1000 }` or `{ height: 1000, fit: 'inside' }`

Generation skips a breakpoint when the source already fits the constrained axis (width-only objects no longer resize portrait images solely because height exceeds the number).

## Why is it needed?

With numeric breakpoints, Sharp always gets a square box, so the **largest side** is clamped. Landscape `1200×500` → `1000×416` (expected); portrait `500×1200` → `416×1000` (often unwanted). Callers need width- or height-only control.

Fixes #24221

## How to test it?

```bash
yarn workspace @strapi/upload test:unit --testPathPattern='responsive-parallelism|image-manipulation|upload/uploadImage'
```

Manual: enable responsive dimensions, set `breakpoints: { large: { width: 1000 } }`, upload landscape and portrait images, confirm formats.

## Related issue(s)/PR(s)

- Fixes #24221

author: nikitaxgusev
body:
@skip-pr-bot

## Motivation

Today the smoke vs nightly scope for the AINIC runner is baked into the
workflow YAML (a SMOKE_SUITES variable plus bash that splits tests into groups
by suite-name patterns). Any coverage change therefore needs a workflow-file
approval, which is a slow bottleneck. This PR moves the scope decision into the
test-runner JSON config so coverage can change without touching the workflow,
and renames the runner and config to match repo conventions.

## Technical Details

test_runner framework:
- Add `--scope {nightly,smoke}`: `smoke` runs only suites with `"smoke": true`,
  `nightly` (or unset) runs all enabled suites.
- Suite `name` is now optional (the `config` key is used as the suite id); add a
  per-suite `smoke` flag and a config-level `test_binary_dir` that is inherited
  via `extends` and applied as a per-test default. `schema.json` updated to match.

AINIC config (`configs/ainic.json` renamed to `configs/mi355x_ainic_tw_roce.json`):
- Matches the `mi<gfx>_<fabric>` naming of the other configs.
- The A/B/C group labels are replaced by two categories derived from `is_gtest`:
  `gtest-tests` (`gtest_base`) and `rccl-tests-sweeps` (`rccl_tests_base`). Each
  base carries its own `test_binary_dir` (`GTEST_BIN_DIR` vs `PERF_BIN_DIR`), so
  the execution lane is derived automatically and no per-suite lane flag is
  needed. Suite entries are now just `{config, enabled, smoke}`; the readable
  title lives in each config `description`. Internal test IDs are unchanged.
- Fixes `gin_enable_gate` / `gin_ainic_backend`: their old suite names lacked
  "Component", so they landed in the perf lane and were skipped. Lane is now
  derived from `is_gtest`, so they run as gtests.

## Summary

- remove the `githubWebhookAutomations` and `userFriendlyAutomationMessage` registry keys
- permanently expose the GitHub workflow job, pull request review, deployment status, and issue comment automation entry points in Platform and CLI
- permanently use human-readable automation messages and agent-facing event context in the API queue path
- remove rollout-only feature reads, fallback prompts, override setup, and true/false test matrices
- keep the old persisted automation-message marker read-only so already queued payloads are normalized without leaking rollout metadata; new payloads no longer write it or branch on it

## Terminal state and basis

Both switches are `fully-rolled-out`.

- rollout decision: `c24a2fb503dbdc725c7dfc2a75257e39c5140195` (`feat: roll out automation feature switches`, #27142) changed both registry entries to globally enabled
- cleanup request: remove both globally enabled switches and retain their enabled behavior

## Commit archaeology

### `githubWebhookAutomations`

- introduced by `6e20502a92bb6cc5eea35a98d6583fd8c949cd1d` (`feat: add github job, review, deployment, and comment automations`, #22904)
- the parent did not expose the four new GitHub webhook automation kinds
- the enabled path exposes and accepts those kinds; the disabled path filtered them from CLI/Platform and rejected CLI creation
- this PR keeps the enabled path and removes only the visibility/validation gate

### `userFriendlyAutomationMessage`

- introduced by `5c13a78454fb78da731ba59b5ebe56c532f8c608` (`feat: add user-friendly automation messages`, #26963)
- the parent used a technical trigger in the visible turn plus an automation-specific system append
- the enabled path uses a natural display message and supplies full event context through the agent user prompt
- this PR keeps the enabled path and deletes the legacy prompt/system-append fallback

## Search and cleanup coverage

Second-pass searches covered:

- both exact keys, enum members, camel/kebab/snake variants, and registry descriptions
- `githubWebhookAutomationsEnabled`, `githubWebhookEventKind`, `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_EVENT_KINDS`, and the disabled-workspace error
- `workflowAutomationPrompt`, `workflowAutomationAppendSystemPrompt`, `workflowAutomationEventUsesUserFriendlyMessage`, the prompt-variant option, and the rollout marker
- related Platform props, CLI guards, API org-scoped override configuration, fixtures, and test overrides

Remaining GitHub webhook automation names are the permanent service implementation, not feature-switch gates. The only user-friendly rollout artifact retained is the reserved persisted marker reader for already queued payload compatibility; it is no longer written and cannot select a fallback path.

## Knip

- baseline: clean for `apps/api`, `apps/cli`, `apps/platform`, and `packages/core`
- after cleanup and after rebase: clean for the same four workspaces
- no cleanup-related unused files, exports, types, dependencies, or binaries

## Tests updated

- deleted the Platform disabled-state creation-entry test
- changed the Platform positive test to exercise GitHub issue-comment creation without a feature override
- removed API `UserFriendlyAutomationMessage: true` setup from event-specific tests
- rewrote the queue test to verify friendly prompts unconditionally across queue drain
- updated context serialization coverage to verify permanent agent/display messages and read compatibility for already persisted rollout markers
- removed core rollout-matrix assertions for both deleted keys

## Validation

Passed locally:

- Prettier on all changed files
- `git diff --check`
- lint for `api`, `@okouai/cli`, `@okouai/app`, and `@okouai/core`
- type checks for `api`, `@okouai/cli`, `@okouai/app`, and `@okouai/core`
- targeted Vitest: Core feature-switch, CLI workflow automation, and Platform workflows page suites — 173 tests passed
- final exact-key/helper searches and full diff review against both introducing commits and their parent behavior

Not run locally:

- API targeted Vitest suites. Standard API test setup could not connect to the local test database (`ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:5432` / `::1:5432`); 25 context tests were skipped at suite setup. The PR pipeline should run the affected API service and route tests with PostgreSQL available.

author: wxy
body:
## Problem

The spend-surge alert fired with an amount that disagreed with both the dashboard and the official DeepSeek API.

Root causes:

1. `PricingCatalog.costUSD` billed cache tokens additively on top of input tokens, even though every parser stores cache as a *subset* of input. DeepSeek cache pricing is ~1/120 of input pricing, so context-heavy Codex sessions were overcounted ~50x.
2. The alert read `SUM(usage_event.cost_usd)` (a token x price estimate), while the dashboard reads `balance_snapshot` deltas (real money). Subscriptions were not the issue here, but the alert should never depend on token estimates.

## Changes

- `costUSD`: treat cache tokens as a subset (`max(0, in - cache)`) instead of additive.
- New one-time `CostBackfill`: recomputes existing `estimated` `usage_event.cost_usd`.
- `SpendAlertService` spend-rate check now uses `StatsService.balanceDailySpend` (the same source as the dashboard): today's local calendar-day spend vs the prior 7-day median, excluding subscriptions.
- Cold-start guard: require 3 days of history before a rate alert can fire.
- Balance-drop check now measures from the last snapshot at-or-before the 24h boundary instead of the first in-window snapshot.
- Updated the pricing unit test for the corrected cache semantics.

## Verification

- `swift build` passes.
- `swift test`: 137 tests, 0 failures.

author: emrahyigit
body:
## Summary

Two changes that both narrow the product to what it is actually for.

**Strong Bullish Momentum is retired.** The product hunts reversals, and a coin already advancing has nothing left to turn around. Continuation stops being a declared state — the engine resolves that structure to neutral, and the momentum component score that existed only to classify it goes with it.

**Predictions save again, under one rule, on one leaderboard.** Saving had been silently broken since 2026-08-09, and when a call did save it never reached the screen the user was watching.

## Momentum removal

Engine, now `market-state-v4-reversal`:

- `bullish_momentum` leaves the state union; both classification branches go (the `>=70` entry and the `>=60` hysteresis hold)
- the `bullishMomentum` score and its `momentumRaw` ingredient are deleted; the raw candle descriptors they fed on (`nearHigh`, `volumeExpansion`, `buyParticipation`, `upsideAtr`, `bullishCloseFraction`) stay as diagnostics
- the scoring-version bump makes `scan-market` rescore the prior candle under the new rules, so change badges stay apples-to-apples

Database (`20260814200000`) drops the `bullish_momentum` columns, narrows six check constraints to the seven remaining states, and rewrites stored rows: history to neutral so the scenario replay keeps a contiguous series, current rows deleted for the scanner to repopulate, journey events and notifications nulled. Alert selections drop the state; a trade config left empty by the removal falls back to `bullish_confirmation`.

iOS loses the dashboard momentum carousel, the scanner and scenario filters, the metric row and its copy. A+ now belongs solely to a 75+ confirmed rebound. Stored alert selections are cleaned on launch so the retired state cannot linger and be rejected on every sync.

## Prediction fixes

**The gate.** `signal_predictions` carried a `guard_prediction_window` trigger that accepted a vote only while the coin's newest `breakout_signals` row still read `pre_breakout`. That lifecycle was retired with the Market State rework, so the gate quietly closed the feature — 20 of 723 signals still carry the status. The trigger is dropped and uniqueness moves off the journey onto `(user_id, symbol, prediction_day)`: one call per coin per UTC day, the same rule the daily game already enforced.

**The split.** The chat's Holds/Fails bar wrote `signal_predictions` while the dashboard leaderboard read only `daily_predictions`, so a chat vote could never place. Both surfaces now post to the `daily-prediction` function and write the same `daily_predictions` row. A chat vote additionally records its journey for the accuracy badge, and that secondary write can fail without dropping the call that counts. Every breakout signal is `direction = 'up'`, so holds maps to up and fails to down.

**Error reporting.** A rejection carries the server's own code and message instead of a blanket "could not be saved". A transport failure names itself (timeout, offline, TLS). The leaderboard refresh moved out of the submit `do`-block, so a saved call can no longer be reported as a failure. The Apple-account requirement is shown on the composer before the tap rather than after it, and a missing profile row returns `PROFILE_REQUIRED` instead of a foreign-key 500.

## Already applied to production

The three migrations and the `scan-market`, `sync-user` and `daily-prediction` functions were deployed and verified during this session, so this PR documents state that is already live:

- 111 history rows rewritten to neutral, 40 current rows deleted, 8 journey events and 1 notification nulled, 62 profiles' alert selections cleaned
- the first v4 scan rescored all 100 coins on 15m with no momentum state: 65 neutral, 12 selling_dominant, 11 breakdown_risk, 9 seller_impact_fading, 3 buy_side_absorption
- the current day's 4 chat votes were backfilled into the leaderboard at the first closed 15m price at or after each vote

Note that `supabase db push` does not work on this project: remote `schema_migrations` holds 34 versions with no local files, so migrations are applied by running the `.sql` directly.

## Reviewer notes

- `20260814220000` is deliberately scoped to the current UTC day. 15m history does not reach further back, so an older vote would be stamped with today's price as its entry. Six such rows were inserted by a first pass and removed.
- ROBOUSDT sits outside the scanned top-100, so its backfilled entry price comes from `symbols.current_price` rather than a closed candle.
- Retiring the state widens Neutral. Coins that read Strong Bullish Momentum now read Neutral rather than moving to another state.

## Testing

- 50/50 Deno tests pass; the two momentum tests are replaced by one asserting that pure continuation without reversal context stays neutral
- `deno check` clean on every changed function
- iOS builds for device and is installed on the test iPhone
- Prediction saving verified end to end: previously blocked inserts now succeed, and the leaderboard shows the 4 real calls

- Follows the [failed-test investigator's latest

harness setup rather than a determinate break.

author: thomasgorisse
body:
Closes #2958

## What changed

`MaterialsDemo.PbrSection` mounted both PBR subject nodes (bundled + streamed) without `autoAnimate`, so both inherited `SceneScope.ModelNode`'s `autoAnimate = true` default. `DemoSettings.qaMode` freezes the orbit yaw (`DemoHelpers`) but not model animation, so the section's QA determinism contract — the one #2926 built it around — was one notch weaker than its sibling `ModelViewerDemo`, which passes `autoAnimate = !DemoSettings.qaMode` deliberately.

Both call sites now pass `autoAnimate = !DemoSettings.qaMode`.

## Challenge verdict

The issue's prescribed cause **held under probe**, and the probe also confirmed its own "measured impact: none" claim, which is what decided the shape of the fix:

- `SceneScope.kt:274` — `autoAnimate: Boolean = true`, confirmed; the two call sites passed nothing.
- `DemoHelpers.kt` — every `qaMode` read is a yaw freeze (`:347`, `:440`, `:492`, `:709`); nothing touches animation. Confirmed.
- Parsed `assets/models/khronos_toy_car.glb` directly: **0 animations, 0 skins**. The three streamed `materials` slugs all declare `hasBakedAnimation = false`. So no frame, on any device, in either mode, can distinguish the fixed build from the broken one — the defect is real but latent.

One divergence from the issue text: it asked for the fix plus "a `MaterialsSubjectsTest` assertion that pins the intent". A value assertion cannot pin it (the contract lives at a Compose call site, and the parameter is read once at node creation, so no pure-value test observes it). The guard is therefore asserted on the source of `MaterialsDemo.kt`: every `ModelNode(…)` carrying `scaleToUnits = MaterialsSubjects.FRAMING_UNITS` must also carry `autoAnimate = !DemoSettings.qaMode`. Verified both ways — green as committed, and **red when the parameter is deleted from one call site** (negative probe run, `AssertionError` quoted the offending call). A guard that cannot fail would have been a fake green.

## Gates

- `:samples:android-demo:compileDebugKotlin` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL
- `:samples:android-demo:testDebugUnitTest` (full module) — BUILD SUCCESSFUL
- `:arsceneview:testDebugUnitTest` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL
- `pre-push-check.sh --quick` reported `ShadowReceiverPlaneContractTest` red; traced to `Expected …/tools/GenerateFilamat.sh` — an artifact of the lean sparse checkout, not of this diff. Re-ran with `tools/` restored: green. No `arsceneview` file is touched here.

## Self-review (5 angles)

- **Correctness** — matches the sibling exactly. Reading `DemoSettings.qaMode` (a `mutableStateOf`) inside the scene content lambda adds a snapshot read, but `ModelNode`'s `remember(engine, modelInstance)` is not keyed on it, so a runtime toggle recomposes without rebuilding the node. That is deliberate: re-keying would destroy and recreate nodes that only *borrow* their entities — the exact teardown defect #2939 fixed in this very block. The QA harness sets `qaMode` before launching a demo, so the creation-time read is the one that matters; documented at the call site rather than left implicit.
- **Threading** — no Filament work added; `autoAnimate` is evaluated during composition on the main thread. No coroutine, no lifecycle change.
- **API consistency** — no public API touched. Named argument, sibling's idiom and ordering.
- **Minimality** — 2 functional lines + 1 import in `main`; the rest is the comment and the guard test. No dead code, no unrelated churn.
- **Cross-platform** — `DemoSettings.qaMode` is Android-demo-only harness state; no iOS/Web/`llms.txt`/skill surface is implicated, so nothing to mirror or defer.

body:
Refactors the monolithic `app.js` by extracting 10 reusable components into `source/shared/components/`, fixes a sync-blocking form submission bug, and standardises all page buttons through a single `SubmitButton` renderer.

## Task 1 — Sync form fix
Removed the early-return error in `bindAsyncFormSubmit` that blocked all form submissions while syncing. SyncEngine's last-write-wins conflict resolution makes the guard unnecessary.

## Task 2–3 — Universal `SubmitButton` component
New `submitButton.js` renders a fully-structured button (`.btn-icon` + `.btn-label`) so `enhanceButtons()` post-processing is skipped (`data-icon-skip="1"`). Buttons embed `data-orig-label` / `data-icon-default` so `setSyncing(false)` can reliably restore state. All `<button class="btn …">` strings in `app.js` replaced with `SubmitButton.render({text, icon, theme, submit})`.

## Tasks 4–12 — Extracted components

| Component | File | Replaces |
|---|---|---|
| `MenuBar` | `menuBar.js` | nav HTML + React nav in `attachNav` / `renderWithReact` |
| `Snackbar` | `snackbar.js` | `_pushSnack` / `_removeSnack` / `renderSnackbar` |
| `SiteHeader` | `siteHeader.js` | auth-chip in `attachNav` / `renderWithReact` |
| `WeightChart` | `weightChart.js` | `_attachWeightChart` |
| `Leaderboard` | `leaderboard.js` | leaderboard card in `renderOverview` |
| `WeekPager` | `weekPager.js` | week-nav div in `renderOverview` |
| `DataTable` | `dataTable.js` | user list table in `renderUsers` |
| `SyncButton` | `syncButton.js` | inline sync retry button + state in `renderSyncSettingsTab` |
| `InviteQRCode` | `qrCode.js` | `_renderInviteQR` + QR lazy-load logic |

Each component is an ES module in `source/shared/components/` imported at the top of `app.js`. No behaviour changes beyond the sync form fix.

## Summary

- **Generators** (Tasks 2-6): seeded Python generators producing synthetic subscription, engagement, kit-delivery, and business data, with delivery-timing and state-distribution *shape* resampled from the real, public Olist Brazilian E-Commerce dataset — never its actual identities. Includes a deliberately injected "problem state" (worse kit delivery) for the root-cause narrative.

body:
## Summary
- Adds a second `docker run` to `scripts/integration-test.sh`, after the existing full-featured run tears down, mirroring `k8s/deployment.yaml`'s exact security profile: root startup, `--cap-drop=ALL --cap-add=SETUID --cap-add=SETGID`.
- Factors the existing health-poll loop (wait for `docker inspect` health status, fail with logs on stop/timeout) into a `wait_healthy()` function so both runs share it.

## Why
This is the gap that let #88 slip through undetected: the existing test always ran with Docker's default (unrestricted) capability set, so a capability the reference k8s manifest is missing never shows up in CI — it only surfaces once someone deploys with the restricted profile for real. This run reproduces that profile directly, so a future regression (e.g. a new s6-rc service needing a capability we don't grant) fails CI with the same `s6-applyuidgid: fatal: unable to set supplementary group list` signature instead of only showing up at deploy time.

author: mcereal
body:
## Summary

`runtime/capsule.toml` declared all 35 `sfn-sources` unconditionally, and 8 of them import the `sfn/crypto` capsule. Every Sailfin binary therefore compiled the whole TLS 1.3 stack: a `print`-only hello-world staged **69 modules, 38 of them crypto**, for a program that cannot reach a socket.

This is the root cause of the nightly self-host regression. It was never a self-host failure — where the triple-pass completed it reached a clean fixed point (`stage2 == stage3`, 0 module diffs). It was wall time, surfacing as two different symptoms: macOS blew the 180-minute cap, and Linux tripped the pass1 smoke hang guard at 58.99 s without ever reaching the self-host check.

Touches the build driver, the capsule resolver, and the TLS diagnostics module boundary; no language surface.

Design: `docs/proposals/design-notes/runtime-demand-driven-sources.md` (§0 records the six places the design was wrong and what this does instead).

Fixes SFN-882

## Changes

**Manifest**
- `runtime/capsule.toml` — new last-in-file `[sfn-source-gates]` table keyed by canonical effect name; `net` gates 8 TLS/socket/HTTP/WebSocket/serve entries. Placement is load-bearing: `toml_get_string_array` scans header-to-header, so a section before `[build]` would truncate `sfn-sources` under the pinned seed and break `make compile`.
- `compiler/capsule.toml` — `[build] full-runtime = true`, so the compiler binary keeps the full runtime surface by construction rather than resting on `entry.sfn` continuing to declare `[clock, io, net]`.

**Driver / resolver**
- New `compiler/src/build/runtime_selection.sfn` — the demand set, the selector, `runtime_demanded_dep_specs`, the dead-strip invariant, and the env toggles.
- `capsule_import_scan.sfn` — `collect_effect_tokens`, a deliberately raw scan (no string/comment skipping): over-retention costs compile time, under-retention breaks the link.
- `toml_parser.sfn` — `toml_get_sfn_source_gate`, `toml_get_build_full_runtime`.
- `runtime_capsule_resolver.sfn` — `RuntimeCapsuleArtifacts.sfn_source_gates`, resolved to absolute paths at parse time, as records rather than a parallel array (target conditioning rewrites `sfn_sources`, so positional alignment goes stale).
- C1 `capsule_resolver/reachability.sfn`, C2 `build/runtime_objs.sfn`, C3 `build/link.sfn` + `build/link_contract.sfn`.
- Narrowed `runtime_capsule_from_root` fallbacks in `cli/commands/build.sfn`, `cli/commands/run.sfn`, `build/tensor_ir_link_harness.sfn`.

**Runtime**
- New `runtime/sfn/platform/tls_status.sfn` — the TLS diagnostics surface (two process-global slots, the error/alert name tables, the four accessors), extracted crypto-free and left **ungated**. See reviewer note 1.

**Tests** — new `runtime_source_gates_test.sfn` (7 manifest invariants), `runtime_demand_driven_sources_test.sfn` (7 acceptance), `gated_builtin_effect_rows_test.sfn` (the class guard); 2 added to `runtime_dep_link_contract_test.sfn` and 2 to `runtime_tls_skeleton_test.sfn`.

**Docs** — `docs/status.md`, `site/.../advanced/capsules.md`, the RCA tracked-work table, and the design note.

## Validation

- [x] `sfn fmt --check` clean on every touched `.sfn` file
- [x] `sfn check` (fast static analysis) passes
- [x] `make compile` — compiler self-hosts (`make clean-build` first; structural)
- [x] `make check` — full triple-pass self-host + suite, green: **unit 305/305, integration 55/55, e2e 327/327, capsules 88/88**
- [x] Regression coverage added (20 new tests across 5 files)
- [x] CI green on `788150c0` — 46/46 checks

Measured cold, 4 vCPU / 15 GiB, `sfn run examples/basics/hello-world.sfn`. The control is the same binary on the same box via the escape hatch, so this is apples-to-apples:

| | control (`SAILFIN_RUNTIME_SOURCE_GATES=off`) | gated | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| wall | 79.45 s | **22.33 s** | **3.56x** |
| peak RSS | 1,915 MB | **361 MB** | **5.31x** |
| modules staged | 69 | **28** | |
| crypto modules | 33 | **0** | |

That the control reproduces the pre-change artifact set exactly (69 / 33) is itself the escape-hatch acceptance test.

## Notes for reviewers

**`sfn build -p compiler` is deliberately unaffected** — it retains everything, so `make compile` gets no faster. The win lands on everything the freshly built compiler then builds, which is the entire CI regression surface. The pinned seed ignores the gate section, so this bundles: one PR, no `seed-blocker`, no seed cut (`.claude/rules/seed-dependency.md`).

Six things the design note did not anticipate, in descending order of how easily they could have shipped broken:

1. **A zero-effect builtin resolving into a gated module could not link.** `tls.last_error()`/`tls.last_alert()` are deliberately effect-free (SFN-822: pure accessors over a process-global slot; adding a `net` row would force `[net]` onto assertion helpers, and `typecheck_builtin_allowlist_test.sfn` exists to assert they stay callable without one). They lower into `tls.sfn`, which this PR gates. So `fn main() [io] { print(tls.last_error()); }` passed `sfn check` and then failed with `undefined symbol: tls_last_error_name`, reported as an **ICE**. The reference is live and reachable from `main`, so `--gc-sections` cannot remove it. Every in-tree caller pairs the builtin with `[net]`, which is why the acceptance suite was green. Fixed by extracting the crypto-free `tls_status.sfn`; ungating `tls.sfn` instead would drag the 33-module crypto closure back and erase the win. `gated_builtin_effect_rows_test.sfn` is now the standing guard, verified by negative control.

2. **The reachability filter's fail-open guard defeated the change, silently.** On a positional build the runtime roots are the only class that produces edges — `tls.sfn` naming `sfn/crypto` is how the capsule entered the retained set at all. Closing the gate empties every class, so the guard concluded "root discrimination is wrong here" and retained the *unfiltered* set: demand computed correctly, gate closed, and all 33 crypto modules still compiled. Fixed by distinguishing well-defined-and-empty from never-derived (`_cr_selected_runtime_root_count`). §11 correctly predicted the link contract would be the sharpest hazard and that it fails *loudly*; this one failed as a change that merely did nothing, and only the required measurement caught it.

3. **The gate is sound only when the link dead-strips.** `--gc-sections` is what removes the prelude's uncalled `serve` wrapper along with its reference into gated `serve.sfn`. Two link paths skip it — the msvc ABI, whose `lld-link` rejects the flags, and any host without `nm`. Both now retain everything, decided at demand time so the link contract and the dep-staging loop cannot disagree.

4. **`sfn test` opts out on both sides.** That path does not dead-strip, so gating produced an undefined `sailfin_runtime_serve` in *every* test binary. Nothing is lost: the pooled runner already amortises the runtime, and the win is paid by the nested builds e2e tests spawn. Forcing `"*"` at the resolver rather than only at the link keeps C1 and the link on one demand set.

5. **Sub-effects are load-bearing.** `http.get` requires `[net.http]` and `websocket.*` require `[net.ws]`; only `serve` uses bare `[net]`. Matching raw tokens against the gate key would close the gate on any HTTP program. Every token and every `[capabilities] required` entry normalizes through `effect_root()`.

6. **The `sfn check` guard.** The demand scan is skipped when the consumer declares no `runtime_root` — the `sfn check` shape. `check` never links, and an unconditional extra read pass over every resolved source would tax rung 1 of the validation ladder for a consumer that does not exist there.

The blocking §5.4 investigation passed before implementation started: a bare `serve(...)` with no `net` effect *is* rejected, so the feared effect-enforcement hole is not live. The diagnostic is `E0400`, not the `E0402` the design predicted.

author: fw-bot
body:
Before this commit, the hoot test "keep banner for messages received while scrolled up" failed at random on runbot:

```
Failed to find 1 of ".o-mail-Thread-banner:has(:text('1 new message'))"
(Timeout of 10 seconds). Found 0 instead.
```

This happens because the test waits for the scroll position it sets in the DOM only, while the thread copies that position to the record on the scroll event, one animation frame later. Bob's message can arrive in between, when the record still says "bottom": the counter the banner reads stays frozen at 0 and the message is marked as read on arrival, so the banner never shows.

This commit waits until the record holds that position before posting.

author: mchaarawi
body:
The per-dkey throttling held split IODs back on a private io_next chain
and issued each successor from the completion callback of its
predecessor. That had three problems, all reported on the PR:

  - params->io_task was assigned before tse_task_register_comp_cb(), so
    the failure path completed the task and then completed it again from
    err_iotask, after tse_sched_process_complete() had already dropped
    the final reference and freed it.

  - A deferred split was never handed to tse_task_schedule(), so it was
    on none of the scheduler lists. Cancellation only walks those lists,
    which left the split uncompleted, the parent dependency count
    non-zero, and the task plus its io_params leaked.

  - The successor was scheduled with instant == true from inside a
    completion callback, so a split that completed inline ran the next
    one nested. Depth scaled with the number of splits of the dkey.

Express the throttling as a real scheduler dependency instead: register
each split as a dependency of the previous split of the same dkey and
schedule every task up front. A chained split has a non-zero dependency
count, so the scheduler parks it on the init list and runs it once its
predecessor completes. Only one RPC per dkey is still outstanding, but
every task stays visible to the scheduler and no split runs nested.

Chaining now keys off an explicit flag set where the inner loop breaks
on the tiny extent cap, rather than on two consecutive IODs merely
sharing a dkey, so out-of-order ranges that revisit a dkey are no longer
serialized needlessly.

Also document that a dkey may now be updated by more than one RPC, so a
failed write can leave it partially updated, and warn when the tunables
disable splitting.
