author: bryanfrd
body:
Closes #11.

git-lfs probed the locking endpoints, found nothing, and fell back to `lfs.locksverify false`. Nothing broke — which is the problem. A Unity team keeps working, unaware that two artists can open the same scene and one of them will lose the afternoon. Binary assets cannot be merged, and this is the only mechanism Git offers.

All four endpoints from the specification: `POST /locks`, `GET /locks`, `POST /locks/verify`, `POST /locks/{id}/unlock`.

## Identity had to come first

A lock belongs to somebody, and until now the server resolved a permission but never a name. `GET /user` gives the login behind the token, cached like the permission but on its own — deliberately **not** on the transfer path, so a push of two hundred objects still costs one API call rather than two. Only the three lock endpoints that need a name pay for it.

`Permission` gains `Admin`, read from the `admin` flag GitHub already returns in the repository response. Only the owner can release a lock; anyone else needs `--force`, and force needs admin — the same person who could rewrite the branch anyway. A colleague on holiday with a scene locked is a real situation, and that is its escape hatch.

## Storage, without a database

One file per lock at `$LFSX_STORAGE_ROOT/.locks/{org}/{repo}/{id}.json`, the id being a digest of the path. Two useful consequences: unlock by id opens one file with no index to maintain, and *taking a held lock is refused by the filesystem itself* — `create_new` fails with `AlreadyExists`, so the mutual exclusion is atomic rather than a check followed by a write that races.

`.locks` sits outside the object tree, and namespaces may no longer begin with a dot, so no repository can ever be routed into it. GitHub does not allow such names anyway.

## Tests

Five on the store, eight through the HTTP API — a held lock is refused with the holder's name attached, the owner can release, a third party cannot, force is refused to a writer and granted to an admin, `verify` splits ours from theirs, a read-only token cannot lock at all.

And the one that actually convinced me, in `ci/e2e.sh` with the real client: `git lfs lock`, `git lfs locks` showing the path, a second `git lfs lock` that must fail, then `git lfs unlock`. The e2e also flips its old assertion — `locks/verify` returning a clean 404 was the documented fallback, and now it must answer 200.

That last one caught a real gap on the first run: the e2e stub forge served `/repos/{org}/{repo}` but not `/user`, so locking failed with "these credentials do not grant that access" while the permission was fine. Exactly the kind of thing a handcrafted request would not have reproduced.

author: johnitvn
body: ## Summary Harden the intent gate so that "proven" means: implemented + executable proof + actually discoverable by the test runner + not skipped/disabled. Add behavioral proofs for the two contracts that previously had only source-evidence. ## Intent proof changes | Change | Before | After | |--------|--------|-------| | Status derivation | Self-attested (`status` field in manifest) | Computed from evidence types (`proven` ↔ has executable evidence) | | Evidence discoverability | Not checked | Executable evidence paths must match a vitest include pattern | | Test integrity | Not checked | All test files scanned for `.skip`/`.only`/`fit`/`fdescribe`/`xit`/`xdescribe` | | Contract C status | `documented` | `proven` (behavioral: schema conformance + tag invariance) | | Contract J status | `documented` | `proven` (behavioral: judgeEdge↔evaluate parity + explain↔evaluate parity) | | `unprovenIntents` | 2 | **0** | ## Files changed ### `src/intent/intent.test.mjs` (+625 lines) **Manifest validation gates (7 new tests):** - Every evidence type must be in the taxonomy - Every evidence path must resolve to an existing file - Executable evidence paths must match a vitest include pattern (discoverability) - Executable evidence files must contain no `.skip`/`.only` patterns - No test file in the suite contains `.only` (suite-wide scan) - Declared status must agree with computed status (not self-attested) - Source-evidence and documentation types are never counted as executable proof **Contract C behavioral proofs (2 new tests):** - Analysis output conforms to the frozen contract schema — calls `analyzeTypeScript`, asserts `Object.keys` matches the contract (no verdict/policy fields) - Analysis output is invariant under project tag changes — same source text produces same output regardless of project tags **Contract J behavioral proofs (3 new tests):** - author: fabio-gos-sonarsource
body:
## The defect

`strings.TrimSpace` does not remove U+FEFF — the BOM is not Unicode whitespace. So the first line of a BOM-prefixed file reads as U+FEFF followed by its real content, every `strings.HasPrefix` test in `scanFile` misses, block-comment state is never entered, and the entire leading licence header is counted as code.

Visual Studio writes a BOM by default, which makes this the dominant counting error on .NET repositories — and it is invisible on most benchmark corpora, because no other language in the five repositories I swept is affected.

## Measured effect

On SonarSource's `sonarlint-visualstudio`, over the **exact 1,157 files SonarQube analyses** (file list read from `api/measures/component_tree`, hard-linked into a tree containing nothing else, GoLC exclusions off — so scope is identical on both sides and only the counting engine is under test):

| | ncloc |
|---|---:|
| SonarQube | 41,578 |
| GoLC before | 62,565 — **+50.5%** |
| GoLC after | 41,871 — **+0.7%** |

1,785 of its 1,950 C# files carry a BOM followed by a 19-line header: **33,917 lines** across the repository attributed to code. GoLC reported 7,691 comment lines where the true figure is 28,377.

Across a five-repository corpus (sonar-enterprise, sonarqube-webapp, llvm-project, sonar-skunk, sonarlint-visualstudio) scanned at SonarQube's own file-level scope, the total moves from **+2.5% to +1.5%** of ncloc — 2,049,118 → 2,028,422 against 1,998,879 over 14,821 files. The other four projects are unaffected and already sat within 2%.

## The change

Four lines: strip the BOM from the first line before the prefix tests. Only the first line — U+FEFF elsewhere in a file is a zero-width no-break space and is content, so stripping it globally would silently drop real characters. A test case covers that boundary.

## Tests

`TestScanCountsCommentsOnBOMPrefixedFirstLine` covers seven cases: BOM + multi-line header, the same header without a BOM (must count identically), BOM + line comment, BOM + self-closing block comment, BOM + code, BOM alone as a blank line, and a BOM-like rune on a later line that must **not** open a comment.

- `go test ./...` — pass
- `go test -tags=engine .` — pass
- `GOLC_RESULTS_PORT=<free> go test -tags=resultsall .` — pass (the default 8090 is held by Docker locally; that failure is pre-existing and reproduces on an unmodified tree)
- `go vet`, `gofmt` — clean
- `sonar analyze` on both files — no issues

Server-side Vortex analysis could not run: the `sonar` CLI and MCP server authenticate to `sonarcloud-demos`, while this project's key lives in `sonar-solutions`, so both report "Project not found".

author: mikelward
body:
Follow-up to #505. Applied across every sibling repo.

## The failure

Every Codex finding missed today was missed the same way: **a paginated list read somewhere other than its end.** `get_reviews`, `get_review_comments` and `get_comments` all page oldest first, so a middle page is indistinguishable from the latest one.

Four incidents, one cause:

- a P1 sat unanswered for two hours (it was a top-level comment, invisible to `get_review_comments`);
- a second went unseen while its PR was merged;
- a superseded review was reported as the current verdict, twice, because page 2 of 3 read as newest;
- ten PRs were told there was "silence to recover from" and asked for a re-review, while a finding was already sitting on one of them.

## The rule

> **Read findings to the last page, and in both places.** `get_review_comments` returns only inline threads, so a top-level comment is invisible to it — read `get_comments` too. Both, and `get_reviews`, page oldest first, so the newest is on the LAST page: `hasNextPage` is the only thing that says you have seen it.

## Testing

Documentation only — no `src/` or `api/` change.

body:
**What is this feature?** Adds analytics instrumentation for the two dashboard "plan" editing interactions that were previously untracked: switching between tabs and expanding/collapsing rows. It introduces a single `DashboardInteractions.trackSectionNavigated(...)` helper that fires a `dashboards_section_navigated` event with `{ item: 'tab' | 'row', action: 'switch_tab' | 'expand_row' | 'collapse_row', isEditing }`. **Why do we need this feature?** User feedback asked for the ability to tweak a dashboard before building it — switching tabs/rows, moving elements, and deleting elements — and to "track user interactions to see how useful this feature is". Moving (`trackMoveItem`) and deleting (`trackDeleteDashboardElement`) elements were already instrumented, but switching tabs and expanding/collapsing rows were not. This closes that gap so the team can measure how users navigate and reorganize a dashboard's sections, including while shaping it in edit mode (`isEditing`). **Who is this feature for?** The Dashboards squad / product analytics, to evaluate usage of the new dynamic-layout (tabs/rows) editing experience. **Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**: Tracked in Linear (Armin Grafana project). Linear could not be updated automatically in this run because the Linear integration is unauthenticated — see the Slack thread. **Special notes for your reviewer:** - Tracking is wired at the user-click sites (`TabItemRenderer.onChangeTab`, `RowItemRenderer` collapse button), not the model methods (`switchToTab` / `onCollapseToggle`), because those are also invoked programmatically (e.g. `scrollCanvasElementIntoView`). This keeps events tied to genuine user intent. - Tab clicks are only tracked when the target tab is not already active. - Tabs/rows layouts require `dashboardNewLayouts`, which is GA/on-by-default. - Tests: new `TabItemRenderer.test.tsx` and extended `RowItemRenderer.test.tsx`; `yarn jest` (7 tests) and `yarn typecheck` pass, ESLint clean. Please check that: - [x] It works as expected from a user's perspective. - [x] Covered by unit tests.

author: 0x13omb3r
body:
## Summary

Phase 3 of the founder-confirmed 6-phase program (2026-08-14): agent verdict
surface. Agents get verdicts, not page bytes — resolution and DANE outcomes
become a first-class, evidence-carrying `hns-verdict/1` result over both the
MCP and CDP surfaces.

- **Schema** (`src/network/hns/verdict.zig`, new): name, resolution_path
  (spv/doh/os), resolver detail (doh endpoint, or spv sync height + chain
  time via hnsd's own Hesiod status channel), dane outcome (matched /
  mismatch / absent / lookup_failed / off) with the matched record's
  usage/selector/matching-type + SPKI digest, a `verified` flag true only
  on the spv path, timestamps, and an evidence block. Never any key
  material.
- **MCP**: new `verdict` tool — resolve + TLSA check only, no page fetch.
- **CDP**: new `LP.getHnsVerdict` command (same primitive), plus an
  additive `hnsVerdict` field on `Network.responseReceived` /
  `Network.loadingFailed` for names outside the ICANN root — absent
  entirely, byte-identical to upstream, for everything else.
- **Fail-closed inheritance**: the surface only reports what the DANE
  engine already decided. The standalone check drives the exact same
  `http.Connection` arm/verify path a real fetch uses
  (`CURLOPT_CONNECT_ONLY=2`, stopped after the TLS handshake); the passive
  CDP attachment reads back an already-completed connection's state. A
  mismatch that blocked a connection is reported as blocked, with the
  evidence — never silently downgraded.
- Additive-only engine changes: `tlsa.zig`/`spv.zig` gain a richer
  `LookupOutcome` (failed vs. confirmed-absent) via new `*Detailed`
  functions; the existing `lookup`/`lookupTlsa` (used by the live DANE
  engine) become thin wrappers with unchanged behavior. `HttpClient.zig`
  gains a `Transfer._dane` snapshot, captured before the connection is
  released/reused. No ICANN-path or TLS-default code touched (grep-audited
  in the PR diff — zero hits on `ssl_verify|insecure|verify_host|CURLOPT_SSL`
  outside pre-existing lines).

## Test plan

- [x] `zig fmt --check` clean on every changed file
- [x] `make build` — clean, Build OK (v8 snapshot + release-fast browser)
- [x] `make test` — **1141 of 1141 tests passed** (baseline was 1125; 16 new:
      schema pin, one per dane outcome, spv-vs-doh `verified` distinction,
      MCP `verdict` tool integration tests, CDP `LP.getHnsVerdict` +
      `Network.responseReceived` additive-field integration tests)
- [x] ICANN regression grep on the diff: zero hits on
      `ssl_verify|insecure|verify_host|CURLOPT_SSL`

## Self-review

Claude-authored; the Codex review gate is suspended per the master repo's
CLAUDE.md (founder directive, 2026-08-04) — this PR merges on green
`repo-checks` (if configured for this fork) plus the review discipline
below, not an independent review.

Checked against the tree, not just against the diff:
- `hns_tlsa.DaneState` fields (`armed`, `verified`, `count`, `recs`) are
  accessed from `verdict.zig`/`HttpClient.zig` without needing to name the
  private `Rec` type — confirmed this compiles (`make build`) and the new
  tests exercise it.
- The `LookupOutcome`-returning `*Detailed` functions were verified to
  preserve exact `lookup`/`lookupTlsa` behavior (0 on both failure and
  empty) via the full test suite staying green with no regressions from
  the pre-existing baseline.
- `Transfer._dane` capture points (`materializeResponse` for success,
  the failure branch of `processOneMessage` before `removeConn`) were
  chosen to run *before* the connection is released back to the pool and
  reset — verified by reading `Network.zig`'s conn-reuse path, not assumed.
- Stated scope boundary (not silently absorbed): the passive CDP
  attachment (`fromObservedConnection`) cannot distinguish a failed TLSA
  lookup from a confirmed-empty one, both leaving `DaneState` unarmed
  identically — it reports `absent` with an `evidence.detail` note saying
  so. The active MCP/CDP standalone check does not have this limitation.
- `matched` reports the first usable TLSA record in a set (real
  `.0xtestrun` positions mint one record per name today); a genuinely
  multi-record RRset isn't disambiguated back to "which record matched" —
  flagged in `docs/hns-agent-verdicts.md`'s open items, not hidden.

body:
Yukon submission `4e0be0c2-074a-496c-94dd-4d0087454714` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/lighter-prover-challenge at `7477de7794c4e91ccddcff1af5837039c08bc796`.

Current best score: 30.7380852237325. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
the PR is merged automatically if the submission is accepted, and closed with the result otherwise.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: Grok 4.6

# Lower exclusive streamed-Merkle admission from 2^20 to 2^17

## Attribution

Exact model: Grok 4.6.
Agent: Grok Build TUI.
Effort: high.
Account: scarletbright.
Date: 2026-08-14.

Benchmark: `eigenlabs/lighter-prover-challenge`.
Ranked: 2500 transactions, five sequential cold workers, M4 Pro 48 GB.
Tip: `a955674` / commit `7477de7` at **30.7380852237325** tx/s.
Fat `poseidon2.metallib` is 1,225,264 bytes and is byte-identical to
the promoted tip. Shader source is unchanged.

Marker: `stream-floor-17-1786717000`.

## Base

Keeper: IFFT-v2 + perm-inv-merge `ca01578` at **30.5595318884001**
(−0.178 vs tip). Perm-inv-merge stays. This fire changes one
admission constant on the exclusive-phase streamed Merkle path.

`07d84db` INV_BATCH 256 scored **26.320** (slow-class) and is not
in this archive. `INV_BATCH` stays 128. No Horner / OpeningSet /
FRI PoW / metallib / TMPDIR / decode-overlap / cached-coset.

## Why this axis

`build_merkle_tree_shared_streamed` overlaps each 8-column LDE
fill with the previous group's GPU absorb, collapsing a
commitment to `max(fill, hash)`. During exclusive GPU phases
(pre-exec, final block, and — importantly — the chain spine
when a path has claimed the exclusive flag) the promoted gate
is `leaf_count >= 2^20`.

Chain-step Zs and quotient trees are `2^17`-leaf shapes. They
miss that gate and run fill-then-hash serially on the
sequential spine **while the GPU stream is idle**. The tree's
own comments record a GPU-vs-CPU break-even far below `2^17`
(GPU wins ~2× at 262,128 permutations, the `2^17` width-8
shape). Admitting those trees costs nothing when nothing else
is on the stream.

The non-exclusive admission (`2^19` and idle-gated) is
unchanged, so pipelined tx trees keep today's occupancy
behavior.

A public 30.67-class family on this board (bot66) included this
floor change in a larger stack. That note is untrusted; this
archive implements only the exclusive-floor constant against
the 30.560 keeper.

This is not the ready-LDE stream isolate (`46356eb`, 29.771)
which changed how mixed ready/missing columns fill. This fire
does not touch `from_coeffs_with_ready_ldes`. It only lets
already-streamed `from_coeffs` admit `2^17` exclusive trees.

## Mechanism

One site: `build_merkle_tree_shared_streamed` in
`vendor/plonky2/plonky2/src/hash/poseidon2/metal.rs`.

```
exclusive: leaf_count >= 1 << 17   // was 1 << 20
non-exclusive: unchanged (1 << 19 && idle)
```

Absorb kernel, parent kernel, group size 8, and leaf bytes are
unchanged. A declined stream still falls through to fill-all +
classic build. Wrong absorb is a Merkle-cap / FRI mismatch.
Fail-closed.

## Files

| file | change |
|---|---|
| `vendor/plonky2/plonky2/src/hash/poseidon2/metal.rs` | exclusive floor `2^20` → `2^17` |

IFFT-v2 and perm-inv-merge remain as in `ca01578`. No circuit
width change. Metallib untouched. `MAX_BUFFER_SETS` still 1.

## Host-class reading

| official score | reading |
|---|---|
| verify-fail / worker crash | stream disagreed; drop |
| 24–29.4 | slow/mid; next on 30.560 |
| 29.5–30.55 | fast, did not pay versus 30.560; drop |
| 30.56–30.73 | paid; keep as base |
| ≥30.738 | promote |

Local `./benchmark.sh` is correctness-only. This host is AGXG16S
(M1 Max); the ranked metallib applegpu slice is AGXG16C (M4 Pro)
and is not reloaded here.

## Value-exactness checklist

- Same `poseidon2_absorb_pass` kernel, same group order.
- Same parent hashing over the same leaf digests.
- Challenger still observes the same cap layout.
- Non-exclusive `2^19` idle gate is untouched.
- `leaf_width >= 16` and power-of-two `leaf_count` still apply.

## What this is not

It is not ready-LDE streaming. It is not GPU-NTT commitments
(`GPU_NTT_COMMITMENTS` stays false). It is not INV_BATCH 256,
fuse-gpu-quot, drop-preproof, narenas, skip-ifft, Horner,
OpeningSet, FRI PoW, decode-overlap, or metallib.

## Commands

```
# worktree = IFFT-v2 + perm-inv-merge + this floor
# metallib 1225264 unchanged
# rm -rf vendor/plonky2/target
yukon submit eigenlabs/lighter-prover-challenge \
  --note-file submission-note-stream-floor-17.md \
  --model "Grok 4.6"
```

## Learning

INV_BATCH 256 verified at 26.320 (slow class). The invert merge
is still the only fast-class pay since IFFT-v2. The remaining
0.178 to the tip is on the order of a tenth of a second per
worker. Hiding fill behind absorb on the chain spine's `2^17`
trees is a different axis from another invert grouping.

## Reproducible narrative

Starting point: `ca01578` at 30.560 after INV_BATCH 256 26.320.
Hypothesis: exclusive `2^20` starves `2^17` chain trees of a
stream the GPU is idle for. Approach: lower that floor to
`2^17`. Tradeoff: more absorb groups on the exclusive stream;
if that queues behind a leftover job, the spine stretches and
we drop. Implementation is one comparison. Measured result is
the official score of this submission.

## Caveats

- Exclusive phase must actually be true for chain tails. If a
  path does not claim it, those trees still use the
  non-exclusive `2^19` idle gate.
- Mixing this floor with a change to the absorb kernel would
  be a second cause. This archive does not touch the shader.

The archive is one cause, fail-closed, legal on the 30.560
keeper, and independent of the Horner / opening / metallib /
TMPDIR families.

author: jason-shen
body:
This pull request introduces a significant refactor to how conversational context is handled and transmitted throughout the agent pipeline and LLM interfaces. The main goal is to ensure that the text field always contains only the caller's exact words, while contextual information (such as retrieval chunks, rolling summaries, barge-in text, and per-turn notes) is sent in separate fields. This prevents context scaffolding from polluting the agent's persistent conversation history and clarifies data boundaries for downstream consumers (including external agents and stateless LLMs). The change is thoroughly documented and covered with new and updated tests.

**Key changes:**

### Core context separation and data model updates

* Introduced a new `Turn` struct to encapsulate a user utterance and all associated context (e.g., `Context`, `InterruptedText`, `Summary`, `Note`). This struct is now used throughout the LLM and pipeline layers, replacing the previous string-based interface. (`internal/llm/llm.go`, `internal/llm/agent.go`, `internal/llm/openai.go`, `internal/llm/ollama.go`, `internal/pipeline/agent.go`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-15e84642b9ee7cbb81fbfc09f439cc544bcabb6fc29b0835f8a31c77802d6aebR31-R65) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7ebdd8c58baf4f93114fddbbacce6d3f43a7ee34634089d0b89052abca0ac8d5R101-R121) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b784602960fcf6fb9fb45f82224c87527cf99d94d1276502b1520a04c898eda2L138-R141) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-d7410c57c6fd8c938d791257f4c6a51e2ec0ad9ca5856362d678bce2b7ce6b57L117-R119) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-f7a5228cef5de0e6d0f63ca5af285d6403c836d7292e4f6a1ef337dff4d36c03L115-R134) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-f7a5228cef5de0e6d0f63ca5af285d6403c836d7292e4f6a1ef337dff4d36c03L166-R189) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-f7a5228cef5de0e6d0f63ca5af285d6403c836d7292e4f6a1ef337dff4d36c03L202-R211)

* Updated the agent request payload and its documentation to include new optional fields: `interrupted_text`, `context`, and `summary`, and clarified the semantics of the `text` and `system` fields. (`internal/llm/agent.go`, `docs/bring-your-own-agent.md`, `docs/bring-your-own-agent.zh-CN.md`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7ebdd8c58baf4f93114fddbbacce6d3f43a7ee34634089d0b89052abca0ac8d5L32-R46) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e1025d02cdf88a9784f92a7b9489589108dfa3dc6f4e2c7d6eb954ad2f862415L37-R56) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c9deb5efe8f32f9a990cfeddf192a49735182c7cfd1989dccbcbb6a0311b7ab7L37-R56)

### Pipeline and LLM interface refactor

* The pipeline now constructs a `Turn` object for each user utterance, ensuring that context is passed separately from the user's words. The `Prompt` field is used for providers that require context to be folded into the message (e.g., OpenAI, Ollama), while external agents receive the context in dedicated fields. (`internal/pipeline/agent.go`, `internal/llm/llm.go`, `internal/llm/agent.go`, `internal/llm/openai.go`, `internal/llm/ollama.go`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f7a5228cef5de0e6d0f63ca5af285d6403c836d7292e4f6a1ef337dff4d36c03L115-R134) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f7a5228cef5de0e6d0f63ca5af285d6403c836d7292e4f6a1ef337dff4d36c03L166-R189) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-f7a5228cef5de0e6d0f63ca5af285d6403c836d7292e4f6a1ef337dff4d36c03L202-R211) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-15e84642b9ee7cbb81fbfc09f439cc544bcabb6fc29b0835f8a31c77802d6aebR31-R65) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-7ebdd8c58baf4f93114fddbbacce6d3f43a7ee34634089d0b89052abca0ac8d5R101-R121) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-b784602960fcf6fb9fb45f82224c87527cf99d94d1276502b1520a04c898eda2L138-R141) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-d7410c57c6fd8c938d791257f4c6a51e2ec0ad9ca5856362d678bce2b7ce6b57L117-R119)

### Testing and validation

* Added comprehensive tests to verify that context fields travel beside the user's text (not inside it), and that plain turns omit all optional context fields from the wire payload. Updated all existing tests to use the new `Turn` struct. (`internal/llm/agent_test.go`, `internal/llm/openai_baseurl_test.go`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-25b6d72edcf9914991fb65defa92d4a8888def19772731b39a68639f05023ddbR97-R173) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-25b6d72edcf9914991fb65defa92d4a8888def19772731b39a68639f05023ddbL45-R46) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-25b6d72edcf9914991fb65defa92d4a8888def19772731b39a68639f05023ddbL83-R84) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-2380952a3d3b6a748678ecc95c9b839ed644545fe0529c16ac17656ad7e4d069L64-R64) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-2380952a3d3b6a748678ecc95c9b839ed644545fe0529c16ac17656ad7e4d069L83-R83)

### Documentation updates

* Expanded and clarified the documentation for both English and Chinese audiences, detailing the new request fields, their purpose, and best practices for agent developers. (`docs/bring-your-own-agent.md`, `docs/bring-your-own-agent.zh-CN.md`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e1025d02cdf88a9784f92a7b9489589108dfa3dc6f4e2c7d6eb954ad2f862415L37-R56) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c9deb5efe8f32f9a990cfeddf192a49735182c7cfd1989dccbcbb6a0311b7ab7L37-R56)

---

These changes make the agent interface more robust, prevent context leakage into user history, and provide a clear contract for both stateless and stateful LLM providers.

author: emprex
body:
## Purpose
Consolidate the authenticated AgentRiskLayer experience around the customer’s AI agent and the decision flow: agent → posture → why → next action → proof.

This is a source-level workspace refactor, not another DOM/CSS overlay. It replaces the previous `workspace-ux.js` / `workspace-ux.css` rearrangement layer and keeps the public marketing site structurally separate.

## Customer-facing changes
- One authenticated navigation vocabulary: Overview, Assess, Findings, Evidence, Runtime, Settings, Help.
- Agent-centred dashboard with current server-recorded deployment evidence where linked, latest declared assessment posture, one next action, grouped history and secondary admin/account content.
- Assessment grouped into five human phases while preserving the existing questionnaire and unknown-information semantics.
- Assessment result reordered to posture → reasons → next action, with findings progressively disclosed and technical evidence retained below.
- Control Intelligence entry reframed as Deployment evidence; server-recorded deployment decision first, technical provenance collapsed, and no inferred HOLD/PROCEED when no decision exists.
- Inspector presented as observed evidence tied to an explicit assessment context.
- Runtime/remediation and signed-in Help use the same application shell.

## Security / trust boundary
No backend, database, migration, authentication, billing, Stripe, email, runtime-policy, evidence-service or assessment-engine files are changed. Server-side workspace/project/tenant authorisation remains authoritative. Client-side selected project/assessment is navigation state only.

Declared is not observed. Missing information is not a vulnerability. Inconclusive is not failed. No positive or negative deployment decision is fabricated when the server has not recorded one.

## Validation evidence
Feature-branch validation on the same product source:
- changed-module JavaScript syntax checks: PASS
- `npm run check`: PASS
- commercial workspace contract tests: PASS (8/8)
- Playwright Chromium responsive acceptance: PASS at 1440×1000 and 390×844 for Dashboard, Result, Assessment, Deployment evidence, Evidence, and signed-in Help; no horizontal overflow or browser/page errors in the fixture journey
- full regression: 391 total — 389 pass, 1 fail, 1 skipped

The sole regression failure is the known pre-existing `tests/control-intelligence.test.js` case `manual review can confirm applicable with a reason when the snapshot has no structured facts` (`expected applicable`, `actual undefined`), previously reproduced on the pre-refactor baseline. This UX change does not alter that backend path or its semantics.

Temporary validation workflow and browser fixture were removed from the branch after validation and are not part of this PR.

## Production acceptance
Do not call this commercially accepted solely from merge/deploy. After deployment, verify the exact SHA, health/readiness and the real production journey visually on desktop/mobile.

author: gambithovzla
body:
## Por qué

Un Brier suelto no se puede leer. **0.25 es exactamente "predecir 50% en todo"**, y la línea de cierre de-vigueada normalmente puntúa mejor que eso. Las tarjetas de modelo llevan tiempo mostrando ~0.24 como si fuera precisión, cuando es indistinguible de un volado.

Los números actuales en producción: NFL moneyline 0.2397, NFL spread 0.2450, NFL total 0.2371, MLB moneyline 0.2414, MLB over/under 0.2441. Ninguno tenía una referencia contra la cual leerse.

## Qué añade

Cada entrenamiento calcula ahora dos forecasts de referencia sobre **las mismas filas** del test, y reporta la diferencia pareada con IC bootstrap:

- `vs_base_rate` — la media del train repetida en cada fila (el piso que no requiere información)
- `vs_market` — la línea de cierre de-vigueada (la barra que importa)

`beats_reference` es `true` **solo cuando todo el IC95 queda bajo cero**, así que un slate afortunado de 77 partidos no puede leerse como edge.

Las referencias que no se pueden construir honestamente devuelven `unavailable` en vez de un default plausible. En particular, las filas de pre-training MLB quedan **excluidas** de la referencia de mercado: sus odds se rellenan con una expectativa pitagórica derivada de las mismas features que entrena el booster, así que compararse contra ellas es compararse consigo mismo.

Nota de interpretación que quedó documentada en el código: en **spread y total el Brier del mercado es ≈0.25 por construcción** — la casa mueve la línea hasta que ambos lados son ~50/50. Ahí "cerca del volado" no significa perderle al mercado, significa ser indistinguible de él. El de-vig solo muerde de verdad en los moneyline.

## Cuatro defectos que salieron al cablear esto

**1. Una línea pasada como precio.** `train.py` mandaba `odds_ou_total` a `kelly_roi` para todo mercado con línea. Esa columna es `DECIMAL(4,1)`: el número de cierre (8.5 carreras), no una cuota. El simulador leía `8.5` como `+8.5` — probabilidad implícita del 92%. `runline` se liquidaba al precio de *moneyline*. Ahora los precios se resuelven por mercado, y los mercados sin precio almacenado caen a un supuesto explícito de −110 que marca el ROI como no confiable en vez de esconderlo.

**2. Los modelos NFL se liquidaron a −110 asumido.** El frame de nflverse trae `spread_close`/`total_close`, no precios, así que la columna faltaba y caía a −110 en silencio. Para spread es razonable; para moneyline es grave, porque liquidar un favorito de 14 puntos a −110 fabrica ganancia sistemáticamente.

**3. Fuga de calibración.** El calibrador Platt se ajustaba con `X_calib=X_test, y_calib=y_test`, y `brier_test` se computaba sobre esas mismas filas. El comentario afirmaba que no se doble-contaba; sí se doble-contaba. **Los Brier reportados hasta ahora son optimistas.** La rebanada de calibración se corta ahora de la cola de la ventana de entrenamiento; donde los datos no alcanzan para apartar una, `calibrated_on_test` lo dice en la tarjeta.

**4. ROI desacoplado del Brier.** El ROI volvía positivo en modelos sin edge demostrable — así es como un +60.4% ATS convivía con un Brier de volado. Reproducido con datos sintéticos: ROI +5.5% y +8.0% en modelos cuyo IC de edge cruza cero limpiamente. La métrica ahora viaja con la procedencia de sus precios (`roi_odds_source`, `roi_trustworthy`).

## Dónde se ve

- Logs de entrenamiento: una línea de veredicto por referencia y por mercado.
- HUD admin (`/admin/ml-control`): bloque `¿HAY EDGE?` en cada tarjeta de mercado, con los avisos de ROI sobre precios asumidos y de calibración sobre test.
- `manifest.json` → `/calibration` → `mlModelHealth.js`.

## Tests

16 nuevos en `ml/tests/test_market_baseline.py`: matemática de de-vig, rechazo del cero como precio, exclusión de odds sintéticas, que **sí** detecta un edge real, y que **no** confunde un volado de 77 filas con edge. Los 109 tests de Python pasan. Build del cliente limpio.

## Después del merge

`docs/admin-and-ops.md:437` — sin volumen persistente, Railway borra `artifacts/` en cada redeploy. Los picks caen al validator legacy hasta que corra un retrain, así que **hace falta disparar `retrain-weekly.yml` con `market=all` una vez que el deploy termine.**

Un límite que la instrumentación no arregla: los tres mercados NFL comparten los mismos 77 partidos de test. El IC es por mercado; tres veredictos sobre el mismo slate no son tres pruebas independientes.

author: mikelward
body:
Follow-up to #192. Applied across every sibling repo.

## The failure

Every Codex finding missed today was missed the same way: **a paginated list read somewhere other than its end.** `get_reviews`, `get_review_comments` and `get_comments` all page oldest first, so a middle page is indistinguishable from the latest one.

Four incidents, one cause: a P1 unanswered for two hours (a top-level comment, invisible to `get_review_comments`); a second unseen while its PR merged; a superseded review reported as the current verdict, twice, because page 2 of 3 read as newest; and ten PRs asked for a re-review on the grounds of silence while a finding was already sitting on one of them.

## The rule

> **Read findings to the last page, and in both places.** `get_review_comments` returns only inline threads, so a top-level comment is invisible to it — read `get_comments` too. Both, and `get_reviews`, page oldest first, so the newest is on the LAST page: `hasNextPage` is the only thing that says you have seen it.

## Testing

Documentation only — no script behavior touched, so `make test` was not run, per this repo's own carve-out.

author: ioansl
body:
The platform grew a per-user plan — five apps on the free tier, enforced on both paths that create one (a `deploy` to a new name, and `fork`). The skill said nothing about it, so an agent's only knowledge of the rule was a single error string.

## The line

> **Five apps per account on the free plan.** `app limit reached: 5 of 5` means the account is full, not that anything is broken: `deploy` to a *new* name and `fork` both refuse there, while redeploying an app that already exists never does. Retrying is pointless — `destroy` something first, and the slot is usable immediately. `list_apps` is how you see what is taking the five.

It says the two things the error cannot: that redeploying an existing app is unaffected, and that a retry will never clear it. Wording follows what the live platform actually does, verified against `api.spacesagents.com` rather than against the design:

- 6th app via `deploy` → refused, message intact through the MCP layer
- 6th app via `fork` → refused identically, which is the path that would otherwise walk around the cap
- redeploy of an existing app *at* the cap → healthy in 256 ms
- `destroy` then immediately `fork` → succeeded, so the freed slot is usable at once

## Versions

Both `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` to **0.2.0**. `/plugin update` compares manifest versions and not commits, so bumping one of them ships nothing.

## Not in this PR

The MCP server needs its own npm publish for the improved `logs` description. This plugin doesn't pin it — `.mcp.json` runs `npx -y spacedock-mcp` — so that arrives on its own once published, with no plugin release required.

body:
`paths-ignore: ['**/*.md']` on both the push and pull_request triggers.

Every file under `docs/` is markdown (24 of 24) and no crate pulls one in with `include_str!`, so a markdown-only commit cannot change what fmt, clippy or the tests see. 07ecd07 was a one-file doc edit and still spent ~1m52s on a Zig build and a full workspace test run.

The filter is `**/*.md` rather than `docs/**` so it also covers AGENTS.md and the skill docs, and so a non-markdown file landing under `docs/` later runs the build instead of silently skipping.

Mixed commits still run — `paths-ignore` skips only when every changed file matches. `main` has no required status checks, so a skipped pull_request run leaves nothing pending.

This PR touches only the .yml, so CI running here is itself the check that the trigger still fires.

### Motivation

- Prove the full PGO profile-generation path for the pinned Mullvad Browser Alpha Windows x86_64 Firefox build and produce verified profile inputs for the next stage. 
- Ensure the baseline build remains unchanged while enabling an explicit overlay-only PGO-generation target and enforce correct cross-PGO instrumentation evidence. 
- Run training natively on a Windows hosted runner using the exact upstream `profileserver.py` and preserve raw LLVM profiles and jarlog for deterministic merging. 
- Persist an immutable, machine-readable profile artifact set bound to upstream provenance and toolchain identities for Stage 4B consumption.

### Description

- Add a manual Actions workflow ` .github/workflows/pgo-stage4a.yml` with three jobs: `pgo-generate` (Ubuntu), `pgo-train` (Windows), and `pgo-merge` (Ubuntu), artifact handoff via `upload-artifact`/`download-artifact`, and prerelease-publish logic. 
- Introduce an overlay patch `patches/firefox-pgo-generate.patch` that adds an overlay-only RBM target `pgo-generate` and conditionally injects `--enable-profile-generate=cross` into Firefox's configure invocation without enabling profile-use. 
- Add helper scripts: `scripts/prepare-pgo-generate.sh` to apply the overlay safely, `scripts/run-pgo-generate.sh` to build only the instrumented Firefox target and validate configure/build evidence, and `scripts/resolve-pgo-provenance.sh` to resolve and capture the exact Firefox repository/ref and `profileserver.py`. 
- Add `scripts/train-pgo.ps1` to run the exact upstream `profileserver.py` natively on Windows with explicit `LLVM_PROFILE_FILE` and `JARLOG_FILE`, and to enforce non-empty `*.profraw` and jarlog outputs and fail on profile errors. 
- Add `scripts/publish-pgo-profile.py` to immutably publish `merged.profdata`, `jarlog`, and a provenance manifest to a technical GitHub prerelease and treat the registry file as the final commit marker, rejecting conflicting publications while allowing byte-identical resume. 
- Add structural unit tests `tests/test_pgo_stage4a.py` that verify baseline isolation, explicit cross-PGO selection, generate/use mutual exclusion, native exact-source Windows training, rejection of empty profraw/jarlog, use of restored matching `llvm-profdata`, and registry-last publication semantics.

### Testing

- Ran `python3 -m unittest tests/test_pgo_stage4a.py -v` and all 7 Stage 4A tests passed. 
- Ran the existing test suite `tests/test-baseline-workflow.py`, `tests/test-binutils-input.py`, `tests/test-build-rbm-workflow.py`, and `tests/test-rbm-release-artifacts.py`, and they all passed.

- Did not execute the multi-hour PGO build or run the Windows-hosted training at scale in this environment, and `gh` was unauthenticated here so a PR could not be opened from this environment; PyYAML was not available in the environment for additional YAML validation.

author: suijinn
body:
ROADMAP の **P3-6「アドレスバーと、パス入力の補完」** を実装しました。

## 何ができるようになったか

タブバー直下のパンくず行が、`Ctrl+L`（またはパンくずの後ろの余白をクリック）で**そのまま入力欄になります**。打てば打った先のフォルダが候補に出て、`Tab` / `↓` で採れます。

- 開いた瞬間は**全選択**。次の一手はたいてい別のパスを打つか貼るかなので、消す作業を挟ませない
- **入力欄の外を押したら畳む**（打った文字は捨てる）。押した先の操作自体は普通に実行される
- 候補は**フォルダだけ**を**フルパス**で表示。隠しフォルダは名前を打ち始めていれば出す
- `Escape` は先に候補だけ畳み、もう一度でパンくずに戻る

入力欄の編集操作も足しました（`Prompt` に選択範囲を持たせたので、名前の変更など**他の入力欄でも同じように使えます**）。

| | 単独 | `Shift` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `←` `→` | 1 文字。選択があればその端に畳む | `anchor` を残して伸縮 |
| `Ctrl+←` `Ctrl+→` | パス 1 区切り | 同じ幅で伸縮 |
| `Home` `End` | 端へ | 端まで選択 |

`Ctrl+A` で全選択、選択したまま打てば置き換わります。

## 設計上の判断（レビューで見てほしい点）

**パンくずと入力欄を 1 行に統合したこと。** パスの読む形と書く形なので、同じことを言う行を 2 段重ねません。専用の帯を出し入れする作りだと、目を向けたその瞬間に窓の中身全部がずれます。元からある行を借りれば下の一覧は 1 ピクセルも動かず、これはテストで検査しています。

**列挙は `PathComplete` の外。** 冷えたネットワーク共有は 1 回の `FindFirstFile` で数秒ブロックするので、要求は他と同じく `DirectoryLoader` を通り、結果は `App::PumpLoader` が流し込みます。トークンはタブのものと別に持ち、打ち続けている間に届いた古いフォルダの答えは黙って捨てます。**同じフォルダは 1 回しか列挙しません**（`C:\Users\ab` と打つと 1 つのフォルダに対して 3 つの前置が生まれるため）。

**キャレットが末尾にないときは補完しない。** 補完が足すのは文字列の末尾なので、途中にキャレットがあるまま候補を採ると後ろが消えます。

**フォーカス色を Windows のアクセント色に揃えました**（ダーク `#4CC2FF` = WinUI が暗いテーマのフォーカス枠に使う値、ライト `#0078D4` = 既定のアクセント色）。従来の彩度を落とした青は、灰色で通した画面の中でただの灰色に見えていました。`test_theme.cpp` の検査を「彩度が低いこと」から「無彩色でないこと」へ反転させています。一覧の行の選択（`rowSelected`）は無彩色のままです ─ 「選んである」と「キーボードがここにいる」は別の問いなので。

**入力欄の選択には専用色 `textSelection` を足しました**（ダーク `#2F5D8E` / ライト `#CCE8FF`）。文字色は変えないので（1 回の `DrawText` で描くため）、通常の文字色が乗って読める明度に限られます。

## 挙動が変わる点

`Ctrl+L` 直後に打つと、従来のようにパスへ追記されず**置き換わります**（エクスプローラーと同じ）。追記したいときは `End` か `→` で選択を畳んでから。

`ui.path_label`（「パス:」）は削除しました。その行に入っているのがパスであることは中身が言っているので、語を置けばその幅だけパスが削れます。

## テスト

339 件すべて通過、Doxygen 警告ゼロ（既知の japanese 通知のみ）。

- `tests/test_pathcomplete.cpp`（新規 14 件）… 候補の切り出し・大小無視・隠しフォルダ・巡回・遅れて届いた列挙の扱いなど、補完の判断を端から端まで
- `tests/test_app.cpp` … 補完の非同期経路、1 フォルダ 1 回の列挙、`Escape` の二段階、選択と矢印キー、外クリックでの畳み
- `tests/test_appui.cpp` … パンくず↔入力欄の切り替えで行が動かないこと、候補一覧の位置とクリック、外クリックの範囲
- `tests/test_pathutil.cpp` / `test_theme.cpp` … `PrevSegment` / `NextSegment` / `IsAbsolute`、フォーカス色と選択色の条件

## 未確認

実機 GUI での見た目は確認していません。特に `#4CC2FF` の明るさと、入力欄の選択色（アクセントよりやや紫寄りの色相）は、実際に見てから微調整の余地があります。どちらも `settings.ini` の `[theme.dark]` で再ビルド無しに試せます。

author: chalbert
body:
Three captures that existed only in one session conversation and would have been lost. No code.

## 1. The gate outruns the agent foreground window — a phase-B blocker

A `test:unit` shard takes ~150–350s; the agent tool foreground window is ~120s. The run is auto-backgrounded, the agent stops at end-of-turn, and its work sits **uncommitted**. **Eight occurrences on 2026-08-14**, every one recovered by hand, none reported by any signal — the lane just looks idle.

**Not addressable by wording.** Every brief carried *"run it in the FOREGROUND and WAIT"* and the agents **did** — the harness backgrounded it anyway. Later briefs said "poll rather than stop"; one agent then looped three times.

This blocks #3102 phase B: *"queue and supervise engine failures"* assumes the engine can finish one unit of work unattended, and that a failure looks like a failure rather than like silence. Filed with the approach fork named, not picked — the interesting option is taking the gate out of the agent arc entirely, since CI already runs the same suite with no timeout.

## 2. The golden-corpus miner is 12 fixtures behind

Re-mining and committing silently drops the difference, including the `reexec-*` and `subshell-closer-*` fixtures. The #2997 build caught it and restored them; **the drift remains.**

A deleted golden fixture is a deleted guarantee that deletes **silently** — the suite goes green because the assertion that would have failed no longer exists. Filed with **diagnose before fixing**: regenerating without knowing why they went missing loses them the same way.

## 3. De-risk the risky part during preparation

Added to the story-preparation checklist. Every preparation told to verify its own card claim first changed the outcome:

- **#3015** measured the proposed pattern set at **1,276 of 3,319 files** and retired three families that would have reddened a third of the board
- **#2967** proved both gaps live by mutation, and found the second already shipping at two call sites rather than hypothetical
- **#2996** reverted the code under a regression test and watched it pass anyway

Each cost one probe and removed a whole review round. A POC belongs in preparation when the risk is that the *approach* is wrong; it belongs nowhere once the approach is known.

`check:standards` 0 errors.

Pricing was duplicated — `_cmd_models` had its own hardcoded list, separate from the defaults baked into `estimate_cost`. It now lives once in `MODEL_PRICING`, and both the listing and the new estimates read from it, so they can't drift.

Two details worth keeping:

- `model_pricing` matches the **longest** known prefix, so a deployed name like `gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18` resolves correctly and `gpt-4-turbo-preview` prices as `gpt-4-turbo` rather than as `gpt-4`.
- An unknown model returns `None` and the CLI prints `unknown (no published rate for 'x')`. Substituting a default would quote one model's rates for another — worse than admitting the rate isn't known.

Sub-cent costs print to 4dp; at 2dp every run reads `$0.00`, which tells the user nothing.

`info` gains a per-100-runs column because per-token rates are hard to reason about — "$0.08 per hundred runs on gpt-4o-mini vs $10.80 on gpt-4" is the comparison someone picking a model is actually making.

`batch --schema` documents the output fields without needing a paid run first, and records the guarantee a consumer depends on: every input item yields a record, failures carrying `error` instead of `content`, so line counts always match.

## Also closed

**#24 (`--no-stream`) — closed as not applicable.** There is no streaming to disable: `grep -rn stream src/` returns nothing, and the CoV pipeline is inherently multi-call, so the answer only exists after the last call. Shipping the flag would imply streaming is the default and that this turns it off. Reopening as a request for streaming itself would be reasonable.

Tests: 57 passing, 6 new covering the prefix rules and the unknown-model path.

body:
## Зачем

Разбор реферальной программы по живым данным прода нашёл дефект, который **уже сработал**: комиссия начислялась по факту оплаты и не отменялась, если заказ после этого проваливался. На проде это одна строка — $0.80 на заказе в `failed`, — но механика бьёт тем сильнее, чем больше объём.

Это именно дефект, а не трактовка: остальная система уже считала `failed` НЕ покупкой (оборот сети, витрина партнёра, выборка пропущенных начислений), и только ledger продолжал платить. Судьба денег партнёра зависела от гонки — успел inline-путь начислить до провала или нет.

Спека: `docs/spec-2026-08-referral-fixes.md`.

## Что сделано

**Отмена начислений** — `reverseAccrualsForOrder` пишет компенсирующую строку `reversed` (append-only, инвариант 1). Гасит по **статусу заказа в БД**, а не по месту вызова: точки вызова глотают запрещённый переход, и заказ, ушедший в `completed`, иначе лишался бы комиссии безвозвратно.

**Гонка** — `NOT EXISTS` не защищает под READ COMMITTED (inline-путь и крон не видят чужую незакоммиченную строку). Добавлен частичный UNIQUE `referral_accruals_order_reversal_idx` (**миграция 0030**) + `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`. Ключ включает `payment_id`: у заказа с двумя успешными платежами одна отмена гасила бы две строки.

**Двойное гашение** — самореферальный реверс в `consumeLinkToken` дедуплился по `created_at` и не видел отмену провалившегося заказа. Предикаты согласованы.

**Набор статусов** — `failed`/`refunded`/`cancelled`. `refund_requested` НЕ входит: возврат ещё могут отклонить, а гашение необратимо.

**Сверка в обе стороны** — бэкстоп в ежечасном `referral-recovery` ловит расхождение, даже если новую точку перехода в `failed` забудут подключить. По итогам финального ревью добавлена зеркальная выборка: заказ **состоялся**, а комиссия погашена — партнёру недоплачено. Путь реальный (`markOrderFailed` гасит и при неизвестном исходе топапа). Только сигнал: автокомпенсация в append-only ledger'е рискует двойным начислением.

**Наблюдаемость** — DM владельцу с дедупом 60 мин на три случая: промах inline-вызова, отрицательный баланс, недоплата партнёру. Штатные возвраты оператора гасятся молча, чтобы денежный алерт не стал фоном.

**Рефакторинг** — один источник дефолтной ставки (`DEFAULT_REFERRAL_RATE_L1_BPS`) и понятия «покупка состоялась» (`PURCHASED_ORDER_STATUSES`, жил шестью копиями).

**Кабинет** — отрицательный месяц показан явно (подпись + другой цвет), формулировка про ручную выплату вынесена в один модуль.

Попутно в ветке — алерт на статус провайдера вне контракта (инцидент 14.08, Freekassa вернула `status: 7`). К рефералке отношения не имеет, вынесен отдельным коммитом.

## Проверка

- `pnpm typecheck` — зелёный
- `pnpm lint` — 0 ошибок
- Тесты: **web 984, db 118 (PGlite), types 183, agent 40** — все зелёные
- Code-review и QA прогнаны отдельно, все находки закрыты или занесены в BACKLOG с обоснованием

Миграция 0030 проверена на прод-данных: в ledger'е 6 строк, все `accrued`, дублей по ключу нет — `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` ляжет чисто.

## ⚠️ После мержа

**Миграция 0030 требует ручного применения на прод-БД** — деплой миграции не применяет. Команда и предпроверочный SQL — в спеке (T-8). `/api/ready` сделает деплой красным, если забыть.

После первого прогона `referral-recovery` историческое расхождение гасится само — ручной SQL не нужен.

author: vandyckmed-droid
body:
## MOM

Was an average of four raw-return percentiles. Now the average of two annualised return-over-volatility ratios:

```
mom = mean( annualised return(250,20) / annualised vol(250,20),
            annualised return(125,10) / annualised vol(125,10) )
```

Dividing by the volatility of the same stretch is what separates the score from a return column — it asks what the climb cost, not only how far it went.

## Returns lose their skip

A 3 month return is now the plain move over three months, checkable against any other source; the same for every window and for the placings computed on them. The skipping that momentum needs now lives inside momentum instead of being spread across the whole table.

## R/R removed

Subsumed by a MOM that is itself risk-adjusted.

## Three sorts, and only three

MOM, market cap, volatility.

## Nothing is ranked at build time

Every score and placing is computed against the rows actually on screen. Filtering the Top 300 down to technology re-ranks that field of 64 rather than showing standings from a field of 300 — verified: DELL 99→98, MU 99→96, AMD 98→93 as the field narrows.

The published `mom` is an absolute ratio; the 0–100 beside a row is its percentile among what is displayed. That also disarms the outliers — SNDK annualises a genuine 30-bagger into a ratio of 20, and as a percentile it simply takes the top slot instead of flattening everyone else. Scores are floored so 100 belongs to the leader alone.

## Defaults

The app opens on the Top 300, no sector filter, best MOM first, every time. Only the watchlist is remembered, being the reader's data rather than a position in the app.

## How the data was rebuilt

Formulas changed but prices did not, so `scripts/remetric.py` replays the pipeline's own functions over the committed `history` — one definition, in `build_snapshot.py`, applied to existing files with the validate-then-atomically-write invariant intact. No refetch, same data date. Its range guard is deliberately loose (±100) because a real 30-bagger annualises into the 20s while the failure it guards against — dividing by a volatility rounded to nothing — lands in the thousands.

## Verification

Chromium, phone size: chips are MOM/CAP/VOL with MOM active, best in view scores 100 and worst scores 0, a sector filter rescales both ends, no skip markers survive on any return window, both MOM windows show on the ticker screen, and 100/100 rows still draw their logo. No console errors.

body: ## Summary - Define `tryRoot` from `rootWithRemainder`: `some b` when the remainder is `none`, otherwise `none`. - Define `root` from `rootWithRemainder` when `Power e a` holds. A nonzero remainder is impossible in that case (`rootWithRemainder_some_power`, via the Peano theorem and `rootWithRemainder_toPeano`). - Prove `root_toPeano`: `(root e a h).toPeano` is `Peano.root` of the embeddings. - Prove `tryRoot_toPeano`: `Option.map toPeano (tryRoot e a) = Peano.tryRoot e.toPeano a.toPeano`. ## Definitions ```lean def tryRoot (e a : Decimal) : Option Decimal := match rootWithRemainder a e with | (b, none) => b | _ => none def root (e a : Decimal) (h : Power e a) : Decimal := match hres : rootWithRemainder a e with | (b, none) => b | (b, some r) => False.elim (rootWithRemainder_some_power a e b r h hres) theorem root_toPeano (e a : Decimal) (h : Power e a) : ∃ h2, (root e a h).toPeano = Peano.root e.toPeano a.toPeano h2 theorem tryRoot_toPeano (e a : Decimal) : Option.map toPeano (tryRoot e a) = Peano.tryRoot e.toPeano a.toPeano ``` ## Testing - `lake build` — success (46 jobs) - `lake env lean scripts/check_axioms.lean` — 8293 declarations; axioms `{propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}` only - Scratch `#eval` of `tryRoot` / `root` (printed as `Nat`): | expression | result | | --- | --- | | `tryRoot 1 5` | `some 5` | | `tryRoot 2 9` | `some 3` | | `tryRoot 3 8` | `some 2` | | `tryRoot 2 2` | `none` | | `tryRoot 2 8` | `none` | | `root 3 (2 ^ 3)` | `2` | | `Peano.tryRoot 2 9` | `some 3` (matches decimal) |

author: mikelward
body:
Part of a fourteen-repo pass over the agent guides. **Two commits**, split on review — the allowlist change and the verdict change are independent, with different blast radii.

### 1. `docs: Point the global allowlist at what the loop performs`

The rule named a category of tool — MCP entries yes, `Bash` entries no — which was wrong in both directions. Twelve of the thirteen sibling repos have no `Bash` entries at all, so it warned about widening a grant that was never there; and a session rooted above several repositories loads none of their repo-local settings, so the watch stalled at a push prompt with nobody there to answer. It now names what the loop performs — the scheduler entries, the GitHub reads and writes, and `git push` — and states the cost where the rule is: any repo the account opens can push, comment and merge unprompted.

### 2. `docs: Cut the Codex verdict rules back to the invariant`

> **Read the Codex verdict, don't infer it.** It reacts to the PR body (`issue_read` → `reactions`), not to a review thread, whose `Useful?` bar reads true on any PR it has commented on. `eyes` means reading, `+1` means clean, and Codex revokes it on push — so a visible one belongs to the visible head, and `+1` with green CI is a merge. The count names no author, so leave PR-body reactions to Codex: nobody else's is revoked, and a review is the attributable form, naming the commit it read. Findings arrive as review comments, as a top-level comment, or as a review — read `get_review_comments`, `get_comments` and `get_reviews` to the last page, since all three page oldest first — and they block the merge until fixed or rebutted; an acknowledgement is not an answer. Nothing from Codex since the push, five minutes on, means it never picked it up — comment `@codex review`, once.

## How it got here

It began as a **trim**. Each round of review had been answered by appending that round's incident to the rule, until the verdict guidance was an essay carrying four anecdotes, an API tour, and two further bullets saying what one clause could say — in a file every session loads whole. Three bullets became one, about 1.4 KB lighter. Codex and the repo owner asked for that independently.

The trim then cut too far, and the next review round put three things back, each with a concrete failure attached:

- **The reaction count is anonymous.** Dropping the "leave PR-body reactions to Codex" convention wasn't neutral: a human's `+1` is *not* revoked by a push, so without that line an ordinary thumbs up reads as a current-head verdict. Restored with its reason, beside the fact that a review is the attributable form of the same verdict.
- **`get_reviews` belongs in the sweep.** A clean pass can arrive as a review with no findings and no reaction, so reading only the two comment endpoints can leave a verdict already given looking like silence.
- **"Answered" is not "fixed".** These guides accept acknowledgement noise as a reply, so `good catch, will do` would have cleared the gate with the defect still in the diff. It now takes a fix or a rebuttal.

And one bug that predated the trim: the recovery condition was unsatisfiable. Old reviews and comments outlive a push, so "no reaction, no review, no comment" is never true on a PR with any history, and `@codex review` would never have fired on a push Codex missed. Scoped first to the push — then to **Codex**, because the guides' own reply order (push, then reply) and CI's own PR comments both guarantee post-push activity from someone else.

## What it deliberately does not fix

Two limits, stated rather than papered over. Both were raised as findings and both are answered on their threads:

- **The verdict has no author.** `issue_read` returns an aggregate; `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{n}/reactions`, which does carry a `user`, returns **403** through this sandbox's egress proxy. So the convention is the mitigation, and a review naming the head is the stronger signal whenever one exists. Requiring that review unconditionally is declined: a clean pass often posts no review at all, which would gate every clean PR permanently.
- **The head can move between reading the verdict and merging.** `mcp__github__merge_pull_request` has no `sha` parameter, so the expected-head guard the REST API supports isn't reachable from here. Read head, reaction and CI in one pass and merge immediately — a narrowed window, not a proof.

## Testing

Documentation only — no product code, no behavior change. Nothing in `src/` or `legacy/` is touched, so the setuid path is unaffected.

author: trek-e
body:
## Fix PR

---

## Linked Issue

Fixes #1884

---

## What was broken

`withPlanningLock` swallowed a `platformEnsureDir` (mkdir) failure creating `.planning/`
in a `try { ... } catch { /* ok */ }`. The subsequent lock write then failed with ENOENT
(parent directory missing), and ENOENT is in `PLANNING_LOCK_RETRY_ERRNOS` (added for a
Docker overlay-fs race), so the retry loop spun the full 10-second budget and threw a
phantom "held by a live process" contention error — misattributing a real filesystem
failure (unwritable disk, full disk, read-only FS) to a nonexistent concurrent writer.

## What this fix does

The mkdir call now propagates its failure immediately, with the real errno and message,
instead of being swallowed. The normal path (`.planning/` already exists or is
creatable) is unaffected, since `mkdirSync(recursive: true)` never throws on an existing
directory. The genuine Docker overlay-fs ENOENT race on the lock *write* (with
`.planning/` present) is unaffected and still retries as before — proven by a dedicated
regression test.

## Root cause

The swallowing `catch { /* ok */ }` predates the TS migration (carried over verbatim from
the original hand-written `.cjs`, per ADR-457's byte-for-behaviour port) and has no
recorded rationale — a defensive "best effort" habit rather than a deliberate decision.
Per `docs/adr/1411-resolution-provenance.md`'s 2026-07-26 amendment (part of epic #1879,
"distinguish absent from corrupt/permission-denied"), this is the one site in that epic's
cluster that legitimately throws under ADR-227's genuinely-fatal carve-out — its defect
was throwing the *wrong* error after swallowing the real one, not that it threw at all.

## Testing

### How I verified the fix

`gsd-test` (remote dockerized matrix runner) on `linux-node24`, three checkpoints:

| Commit | Contents | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `dcde255d7` | test only, no fix (RED) | `failed` — 33622 total, 4 unique failures: the 3 new regression-test cases requiring the fix, plus their parent-describe rollup |
| `259c408b6` | test + fix (final, post-rebase onto `next`) | `passed` — 33645/33645, 0 failures |

An intermediate RED run against an earlier base caught 2 unrelated
`tests/lint-allow-test-rule-refs.test.cjs` failures (a file-count ceiling gate). Diagnosed
before dismissing: confirmed via a control run against a clean `origin/next` checkout, in
isolation, that this was transient upstream drift on `next` between fetches (the ceiling
had already been bumped upstream, moments apart from this branch's fetch) — not caused by
this diff. Resolved by rebasing onto the fresher `next`; absent from every subsequent run.

`npm run lint:ci` and `npm run build:lib` both green locally.

### Regression test added?

- [x] Yes — added a test that would have caught this bug

`tests/planning-lock-mkdir-failure-1884.test.cjs`: EACCES and ENOSPC creating
`.planning/` are surfaced immediately (not folded into a 10s phantom timeout); the thrown
error is not branded `lockTimeout`; the normal (creatable) path is unaffected; and a
transient ENOENT on the lock *write* (the genuine pre-existing race) still retries and
succeeds. IO failure is injected via `t.mock.method(fs, 'mkdirSync'/'writeFileSync', ...)`
(never `chmod 0o000`), and a fake clock proves fail-fast without a wall-clock assertion.

### Platforms tested

- [ ] macOS
- [ ] Windows (including backslash path handling)
- [x] Linux
- [ ] N/A (not platform-specific)

The `gsd-test` matrix ran `linux-node24` only for this change. The fix is a plain
`fs.mkdirSync` error-propagation change with no platform-specific branching; CI's
Windows/macOS lanes cover it further.

### Runtimes tested

- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Gemini CLI
- [ ] OpenCode
- [ ] Other: ___
- [x] N/A (not runtime-specific — engine-internal read/lock path)

---

## Checklist

- [x] Issue linked above with `Fixes #NNN`
- [x] Linked issue has the `confirmed-bug` label
- [x] Fix is scoped to the reported bug — no unrelated changes included
- [x] Regression test added
- [x] All existing tests pass (verified via `gsd-test`, the repo's remote matrix runner —
      not `npm test`, which is hard-blocked locally per `CONTRIBUTING.md`)
- [x] `.changeset/` fragment added (`Fixed`)
- [x] No unnecessary dependencies added

## Breaking changes

None to any return value or the normal path. One error case changes shape: creating
`.planning/` on an unwritable/full/read-only filesystem now throws the real `fs` error
(e.g. `EACCES`) immediately, instead of a `lockTimeout: true` "held by a live process"
error after a 10-second hang. A caller audit (`get_impact` on `withPlanningLock`'s 8
direct callers, plus a repo-wide search for `.lockTimeout` and "held by a live process")
found no caller reads either signal — all callers propagate the error unmodified.

### Motivation

- Users sharing the same browser saw the last-selected workspace bleed across accounts because the active workspace was stored in a single global key `fluxa-workspace` instead of being tied to the authenticated user. 
- The provider could also resolve a membership fallback from previous render data before the user's preference was applied, causing role/organization to flip after navigation or refresh.

### Description

- Add `src/lib/workspace-preference.ts` with helpers `workspaceStorageKey`, `readWorkspacePreference` and `writeWorkspacePreference` to centralize per-user workspace storage using `fluxa-workspace:<user.id>`.
- Update `WorkspaceProvider` (`src/lib/workspace.tsx`) to store selection as `{ userId, organizationId }`, load the per-user preference on auth changes, apply the selection only when it belongs to the current user, and persist changes with `writeWorkspacePreference` when `switchWorkspace` is called.
- Update invite acceptance (`src/routes/convite.$token.tsx`) to write the invited organization into the accepting user's per-user preference instead of the old global key.

author: jonathan-nam
body:
Stacked on #413 — review that one first, this PR's base is its branch so the diff here is the two Settled commits alone.

The pipeline gets its last stage: **Drop Ledger → Sale Ledger → Settlement Ledger → Settled**. One direction. The first three ask something of the reader; the last asks nothing and only records, which is what lets them stop carrying finished rows.

### What Settled holds

Both kinds in one list, because "what happened to this drop" is one question however the drop divided. A reader looking for a night knows the boss and the week, not which pipeline the app filed it under.

- Money drops that paid out or were taken, with what there was to split and your side of it.
- Coupon nights, filed by the **act** that closed them and never by their status. A piece drop settles through the tranche ledger, so its status stays `PENDING` for ever; reading it would file every night the account has ever had as unfinished.

Not a second reader. Every field comes off `buildDropLog`'s entries, which is `splitOf()`'s money and `couponGapOf()`'s pieces. What this adds is which act finished a row, read off the settlements rather than worked out.

Three things worth calling out:

- A night closed with two people is **two records**. One night's coupons sit in as many piles as there were people bending down, and closing the books with Bro says nothing about Jared.
- A settlement records one write-off for the whole act, so a row's share is that figure over the drops it closed, remainder on the first row, adding back up to exactly what was entered.
- The money total is what there was to **split**, never the sum of the amounts as entered. Same total and same reason as the Drop Log's.

The one control reopens a settlement, returning the night to the Settlement Ledger where every other correction already lives. Orphans (a settlement naming a drop the pool no longer has) are counted on screen rather than absorbed.

### What leaves the worklists

- A pile whose every night is closed is held back from the Sale Ledger. Held back rather than dropped: a mistyped tranche re-prices what a settlement was agreed on, and that card is still the only place one can be taken off. It comes back behind **Record a sale**.
- The card's "N settled" count and its "fully settled" header line both go. Both said less than Settled now says in full, and two places saying it is two places to disagree. `queueOf` no longer returns `closed`; nothing else read it.

The **Drop Ledger is untouched** and stays the whole log. A drop that sold is still in it with its figures, because that is where the account's earnings are read and a month whose drops had all been settled would otherwise total zero.

author: gianfrancopiana
body:
## What

The gateway now forwards the client's `anthropic-beta` features and denies only the family that can move spend outside the ledger (`fallback`), instead of forwarding an allowlist of two.

## Why

Found by running Gumhead against the deployed gateway. The first real turn failed:

```
API Error: 400 context_management: Extra inputs are not permitted
```

The runtime sends eight beta features today:

```
claude-code-20250219, interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14, thinking-token-count-2026-05-13,
context-management-2025-06-27, prompt-caching-scope-2026-01-05,
mid-conversation-system-2026-04-07, advisor-tool-2026-03-01, effort-2025-11-24
```

The allowlist forwarded one of them, so its body — which carries `context_management`, `output_config`, and `thinking` — reached Anthropic without the headers that authorize those fields. Confirmed against production: the same body succeeds without `context_management` and fails with it, whether or not the caller sends the beta headers, because the gateway strips them either way.

An allowlist of client feature flags cannot hold: the list grows with every runtime upgrade, and each addition breaks the pet with an error naming a field nobody set by hand.

## Why this is still safe

Enforcement was never the header — it is the body validators, and they are unchanged:

- `fallbacks`, `speed`, and `inference_geo` are rejected outright (unweighted pricing paths).
- Server-side tools are rejected (they bill per use outside the token ledger).
- `max_tokens` is bounded, and buffered outputs are capped.

A beta header grants nothing unless the request also carries the corresponding field, and every field that matters for spend is refused with a named error. The `fallback` denial stays because that one runs extra models server-side.

`GUMHEAD_DENIED_ANTHROPIC_BETAS` tunes the denials without a deploy.

## Tests

- The runtime's real eight-beta header must survive verbatim.
- A denied beta is dropped while the rest pass through.
- 51 examples, 0 failures; rubocop clean.

## Verification

Verified end to end against production before and after: the token comes from the seller's Gumroad login, the runtime is pointed at `/v2/gumhead`, and no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` exists on the machine. Buffered calls already returned 200 with real usage; this fixes the full agent turn.

body:
Four blockers first. `python-louvain` was pinned but never imported, and it fails to build against modern setuptools -- so a clean `pip install` died before it reached anything else. Community detection has always used the NetworkX built-in; the pin is gone and a comment says why.

"Fraudster fights back" flowed into the plan but not into the replay that animates it, so ticking it changed nothing on the panel a judge watches. It now reaches both timelines. On S1 recovery moves 39.5% -> 25.6% with ten transfers rerouted, and the caption under our own column says so, comparing against a passive run this console actually produced rather than a constant.

The harm limit spent 94% of its travel on a no-op. Range is 0.05-2.0 with a quadratic map putting the interesting band in 70% of the pixels, regime ticks you can click, and a live line reading the plan's *composition* -- 18 step-up verifications, 13 freezes + 1 hold, 25 full freezes -- because the count alone hides the behaviour that makes the control worth having.

Then the framing. A navy portal shell -- masthead, classification strip, breadcrumb, footer, 140px in total -- wraps the dark console without restyling it. The crest is drawn here rather than borrowed: no State Emblem, no RBI mark, and the non-affiliation notice appears in the footer and on every page of every document issued. No saffron anywhere, because it sits a few degrees from the amber reserved for money at risk.

And the artifact. The solver already produced an ordered, timed, reason-coded plan; now it issues one. `/api/freeze-order` groups by holding bank, because eight institutions each act only on their own accounts, and the PDF is a formal memorandum with masked identifiers and a plain-English justification column -- "why was my customer's account frozen" is the first question a bank asks. It is byte-identical for identical inputs, which took pinning both the document timestamp and the /ID that ReportLab derives from the output buffer's memory address.

Also: a live policy switcher with a head-to-head strip that accumulates during the demo; an intake form that runs the full pipeline on any account, proving the six scenarios are not hardcoded; an append-only audit trail; the p(mule) distribution instead of a saturated 100% mean, with the conditioning caveat said where the number appears; an idle canvas that reads as waiting rather than broken; the freeze plan lifted above the fold at 1366x768; one-command `demo` targets; a four-minute beat sheet; and a bundle split that takes the first chunk from 966 kB to 294 kB.

External validation is written but not run: AMLSim ships no generated data and the Kaggle export needs a token. Limitations gains an item saying so plainly rather than omitting it.

63 tests -> 82. Typecheck, build and browser console all clean.

author: blairham
body:
Closes #3.

**Signal posture for the interactive shell:**
- `signal.Notify` (never `Ignore` — ignored dispositions survive exec and would make children immune to Ctrl-C) held for the session; SIGINT cancels the per-command context so **pure-builtin loops** (`while :; do :; done`) stop too; external children get their SIGINT straight from the terminal (same process group until #5)
- SIGQUIT: swallowed for the shell, kernel-default for the child; SIGTSTP untouched until job control (#5)
- Prompt-time signals drained before each run so a stale SIGINT can't cancel the next command

**The bug this flushed out:** mvdan's `Runner.Exited()` reports true after a context cancellation, not just after `exit` — the first cut returned there and Ctrl-C killed the whole shell. Interruption now surfaces as an `errInterrupted` sentinel checked before `Exited()`; probe-verified that the runner stays reusable with state intact (no `Reset`, which would wipe vars/cwd).

**Verified under a real pty:** `sleep 5` + Ctrl-C → child dies, no spurious error, fresh prompt; Ctrl-\ inert at prompt; session continues; `exit` still works. Unit tests cover builtin-loop interruption, SIGQUIT non-cancellation, sentinel mapping, drain semantics; race-clean.

Ctrl-C *at the prompt* was already handled by #2 (raw mode makes it a key event); SIGWINCH re-render likewise. This closes the remaining scope.

author: frederick-douglas-pearce
body:
Closes #33.

## What this changes

The acceptance gate is last after #31, but the merge candidate can still change after it certifies. Nothing in the engine said those verdicts expired — and this failure looks like success: every gate genuinely passed, just not on the code being merged.

**Prevalence, measured at plan time** (corpus pass over the 20 `done` rows in this run's ledger): **3 of 20 iterations (15%)** hit a currency re-run — #60, #29, #32. All three were caught by the human noticing, never by a rule. That 15% also **discharges the issue's own falsifier**: if the gate re-ran on more than half of issues, F5's frequency argument — the whole basis for #31's reorder — would collapse. It does not.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Status |
|---|---|
| **AC1** — invalidation rule enumerates the sources it covers, incl. CI fixes and merge-gate-driven changes | Met, as a **source-agnostic** rule with the sources as illustrative examples (`loop-engine.md` → Gate-outcome invariant) |
| **AC2** — the round cap is explicitly a handoff to the human, never a terminal state | Met at the Fresh-re-check bound |
| **AC3** — acceptance must be green before merge, stated in the engine | **Already met by the tree** (`:661`, gate-table Merge row) — recorded, not restated |
| **AC4** — what a source-changing acceptance-gate fix re-arms (proposed in #31's hand-off comment) | Met: it **escalates**, as the rule; the three things a re-arm would need are stated as the reasons none is offered |

## Design notes

**Currency is folded into the existing Gate-outcome invariant, not minted as a third named invariant.** The architect blocked the new-invariant approach and was right twice over: step 10 already attributed the idea to Gate-outcome, and "Currency invariant" collides with plan-currency (#89), which `:320` already calls "in the same family as #33."

**The source list is `sufficient, not exhaustive`.** A closed list is this repo's recurring enumerable-assertion trap — and the architect's review caught that my closed list had already missed one: with strict branch protection, bringing a branch up to date changes the merge candidate after acceptance certified it, and no one authored the change.

**The two hand-off pointers the tree already owed to #33 (`:584`, `:614`) are discharged in place** rather than in a new region — they were a debt, so paying them is not accretion.

**`HERMETIC_TEST_CMD` turns out to be the worked precedent** — a test added at step 8 or 10 already re-arms a step-6 trigger journalled `n/a`. The new clause anchors on it rather than inventing a mechanism, and reuses its "re-arm" vocabulary.

**SKILL.md's fail-safe list gains the currency clause but *not* the round-cap clause**, deliberately: a partial load that reads a cap as terminal over-escalates (safe), while one that merges on a stale verdict under-gates (not safe). Only the second belongs in that list.

**README trust-model section updated in the same PR** per the standing convention, with the `This arrives with v0.2.0` marker so a reader on the installed 0.0.1 does not believe the protection is live.

## Gates

- **Tests:** 138 passing.
- **Security review: skipped** — `loop.config.md` §4 scopes it to diffs touching `hooks/`, the repo's only executable attack surface. This diff is `skills/` + `README.md`.
- **Class B (mutation):** the limit case is expected to fire — Route `code`, alters behavior, adds no test. Disposition at the merge gate.

author: leowilkin
body:
Deleting an event 500'd — Sentry [ATTEND-5V](https://hack-club-hcb.sentry.io/issues/ATTEND-5V), `DELETE /admin/events/assemble`.

`Event` destroys its `participant_events` before its `incidents`, so the `incident_participants` join rows were still holding a foreign key to a participant event when it went away:

```
PG::ForeignKeyViolation: update or delete on table "participant_events" violates
foreign key constraint "fk_rails_ea6deabc8e" on table "incident_participants"
```

`ParticipantEvent` had no `incident_participants` association at all, so nothing cleaned them up. Auditing the rest of the foreign keys pointing at `participant_events` turned up the same gap in three more places, each of which would have been the next error:

- `slack_blast_recipients` — blasts are destroyed after participant events
- the inbound side of roommate preferences and exclusions — someone else naming you as preferred/excluded also holds a foreign key to you, and only the outbound side was covered
- `incidents` and `notes` — now `dependent: :nullify` rather than `:destroy`. They're a record of the event, not of the enrolment, and the event destroys them itself moments later.

`hospitality_acts` also has a foreign key to `participant_events`, but it has no model and no migration in the repo — nothing writes it, so it can't hold rows. Left alone.

## Testing

New spec in `spec/models/event_spec.rb` builds an event with all five kinds of pointer and destroys it. Reverting the model change reproduces the production error exactly; with it, green.

Fixes ATTEND-5V
