author: dangazineu
body:
Upstream links carry two properties nothing checked. A link can point the wrong
way down the chain, and a link can point at a document whose deletion is already
scheduled. Eight edges in this repository violate the first and pass validation
today; the second is worse, because the formats do not merely permit it — a
brief's only stated legal upstream was a ROADMAP, which is deleted when its
features land, so following the rule as written produced the defect.

Both properties become declared facts on each artifact type, next to its
required sections and valid statuses, and `shirabe validate` enforces them.
A durable type may not declare a working parent, and a test over the declaration
table fails the moment one does. The brief's legal-parent set is empty, which
states as a checkable fact that a brief heads its own tactical lineage.

The roadmap pointer moves rather than disappearing. Links run from the
shorter-lived document to the longer-lived one, so the node that may name a
roadmap is one that does not outlive it: the plan. `/plan` gains the
`--upstream` flag its five sibling skills already carry, `/scope` hands the
roadmap to it, and `/brief` keeps both roadmap input routes as grounding that
records nothing. The cascade still finds the roadmap it updates and deletes.

Closes #272. Closes #253.

---

## What changed

The full chain — brief, PRD, design and plan — is in this PR alongside the
implementation. Each artifact went through its own jury and is listed below with
the review rounds it took.

| Artifact | Path | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Brief | `docs/briefs/BRIEF-upstream-link-legality.md` | Done |
| PRD | `docs/prds/PRD-upstream-link-legality.md` | Done |
| Design | `docs/designs/current/DESIGN-upstream-link-legality.md` | Current |
| Plan | *(deleted by the finalization cascade)* | — |

The implementation is seven issues from that plan, landing in dependency
order: the declarations, the check, the reference sweep, `/brief`, `/plan`
and its pre-flight script, `/scope` and `/explore`, then the cascade
fixtures.

## The two decisions worth reading

**The private-upstream rule and the ephemeral rule are one rule with two
triggers.** Both cases are an upstream that exists, is correct, and cannot be
durably referenced, and in both the settled response is the same three acts:
read it, omit the field, say so. Only the lifetime trigger can be checked by
tooling — a cross-repo value resolves to nothing, so the private case validates
clean and always will. One rule, two triggers, one of them enforceable.

**Navigating up rather than recording nothing.** The deciding property is that
the lineage survives the deletion the rule exists to anticipate: a brief that
records the roadmap's strategy still answers "where did this come from" after
the cascade removes the roadmap, while a brief that records nothing strands the
strategic half of the chain behind a document that no longer exists — the same
failure this work opened on, displaced by one hop. The walk is deterministic and
terminates in one step, because a roadmap's own parents are the two strategic
types and neither is working.

The direction rule is uniform across both chains, and for a reason worth
stating: the check decides from two basenames, so it cannot tell a document that
reached past an altitude that exists from one written where that altitude does
not. Rejecting the second to catch the first would fail the legitimate case, so
every type may name any strictly-higher altitude and preferring the nearest one
stays authoring guidance in each producing skill.

## Deliberate validation changes

Three documents that validate clean today will fail afterwards, and five that
already fail gain a second finding. All eight are named in the PRD's R24 table
before the diff was measured, so an intended change is not read as a regression.
Repairing them is out of scope and belongs to the issues that track them.

## Test plan

- `cargo test --workspace`: 972 passed, 0 failed, with no existing test
  modified. The only deletions in the source diff are two import lines and one
  doc-comment line; `crates/shirabe/tests/cli.rs` is a pure addition.
- Every golden-corpus fixture's frozen expected output is byte-identical. The
  parity suite is what enforces the check's placement: one fixture carries a
  durable-names-working edge and is protected only by the schema gate.
- `skills/plan/scripts/validate-plan_test.sh`: 17 passed, with all 11 existing
  cases unmodified. `run-cascade_test.sh`: 17 passed.
- The corpus diff is exactly the eight documents R24 named in advance — six
  `R10`, two `R11` — with zero removals and no other document under `docs/`
  changing its findings. Every table row is permissive relative to a
  nearest-parent reading, so nothing that validated before this change fails
  after it.
- A tactical chain now terminates on a STRATEGY, which the finalization walk
  stops on cleanly rather than reporting as an unrecognized node — a fixture
  chain exercises it end to end.
- `shirabe validate --lifecycle . --mode=draft` exits 0.
- `shirabe validate --lifecycle-chain docs/designs/current/DESIGN-upstream-link-legality.md --mode=ready`
  exits 0: this PR's own chain is finalized.

## Rebased onto #269

That PR split `validate_file` into a prose half and a structural half, with the
schema gate moving into the structural one. This check is structural by
construction — it presupposes an artifact schema — so it stays after the gate,
and the golden fixture that protects the placement still emits nothing from it.
Its frozen output gained a prose notice above the schema notice; parity passes
byte for byte. The comment and the design now name the right half and list the
prose half as a fourth placement that would break it. `FormatSpec::prose_only`
gained the three new fields with a synthetic `FormatId::Prose` rather than
borrowing an artifact type's identity.

## Two pre-existing CI conditions, neither caused by this change

**The lifecycle workflow does not run at all.** `Validate shirabe lifecycle`
reports `startup_failure` on every branch — this one, `main`, and two unrelated
branches — so the whole-tree lifecycle gate has been running for nobody. It
produces no job and no check run, so the API returns no error text and the cause
has to be read from the Actions UI. This is what leaves the PR `UNSTABLE` while
every reported check is green.

**Ready-posture lifecycle is red on `main` itself.** `shirabe validate
--lifecycle . --mode=ready` reports one error, an orphan
`docs/prds/PRD-koto-adoption.md`. Running the same command against a `git
archive` of `main`'s docs tree produces the identical single error, and this
branch does not touch that file. So the gate above would report it here once the
workflow is fixed — which is the reason not to fix the workflow inside this PR.

author: dereuromark
body:
Closes #966

## Re-measured at `eeac402b`

Input:

```
[x]{: fr}
```

Output (`carve --json`, trimmed to the span's `attrs`):

```json
{"keyValues":{"fr":"","lang":""},"order":["lang","fr"]}
```

One `attrs` object stating two different orders for the same nine characters.
That is the fact the ticket asked for and it settles the open half without
counting engines: carve-rs is not normalizing to a canonical order, it is
publishing a `BTreeMap`'s iteration order. `[x]{b=1 a=2}` came out as
`"keyValues":{"a":"2","b":"1"}` beside `"order":["b","a"]`, so the ordering is
alphabetical rather than anything the document said, and nothing in `src/ast.rs`
records a decision to normalize.

The rest of the engine already reads `order`. The HTML renderer emits
`<span b="1" a="2">` and `carve fmt` writes `[x]{b=1 a=2}` back unchanged, both
correct against PART 10 §1 and PART 11 §6. Only the JSON serializer iterated the
storage map.

## The clause

No clause says "`keyValues` iterates in source order" in so many words. Three
say which of the two orders carve-rs is allowed to publish, and they agree:

- **PART 12 §1 (NORMATIVE):** "An implementation whose internals differ MAPS on
  the way out; it does not export its internals." The `BTreeMap` is an internal.
  §1a makes the purpose explicit in the same terms - an engine that publishes
  its own bookkeeping instead of the document defeats "a consumer written
  against one implementation MUST be able to read another's output", and
  canonical serialization is what makes node-for-node comparison mean anything.
- **`resources/ast-schema.json`:** `order` is "Source-appearance order of the
  slots". The schema names one field as the record of what the author wrote, and
  carve-rs filled it correctly while contradicting it two fields earlier.
- **PART 11 §6 (NORMATIVE):** `fmt` does not reorder attributes, because "those
  are the author's choices and the AST records them".

So this is a carve-rs defect, not a spec question. The serializer now reads the
same field the renderer does, which also means the two cannot drift into stating
different orders for one document again.

## The third document

The report named two. Every `.crv` under `tests/spec/tests/corpus` and
`corpus-optional` was parsed and every `attrs` object compared against its own
`order` - a sweep for the rule rather than for the reported shape. Exactly three
documents diverged, which matches the conformance run's count:

- `297-the-language-sigil-takes-no-padding` - span, emitted `fr, lang`, source
  `lang, fr`
- `301-a-derived-title-yields-to-an-authored-one` - span, emitted
  `datetime, time`, source `time, datetime`
- `45-inline-extensions-9` - span, emitted `data-key, kbd, onclick`, source
  `kbd, data-key, onclick`

After the fix the same sweep reports 0 over 998 documents.

## Scope

Serialization only. Nothing about how a document renders or formats changes, and
the ingest path is untouched - `order` is what carries the ordering through a
round trip, so a tree that goes out and comes back still serializes the way the
author wrote it.

A key `order` does not mention is still published, after the ones it does. An
`Attrs` built programmatically records no order at all (the schema says so) and
dropping its attributes to protect an ordering would lose the document to save
the bookkeeping.

One boundary worth stating rather than leaving to be discovered: a JSON tree
ingested with `keyValues` in a non-alphabetical order and NO `order` field still
comes back alphabetical, because the storage map has nowhere to keep it. That
needs an order-preserving map rather than a serializer change, no corpus
document reaches it (the parser always records `order`), and it is not what this
ticket measured.

## Tests

- `key_values_serialize_in_the_author_s_source_order` - both spellings, so the
  assertion cannot pass by the emitted order happening to be a fixed one
- `one_attrs_object_states_one_order` - all three affected shapes, comparing the
  emitted keys against the object's own `order` rather than against a restated
  literal
- `the_emitted_order_is_the_one_the_html_renderer_uses` - the renderer and the
  serializer pinned against each other on one document
- `a_key_the_order_does_not_mention_is_still_published` - the programmatic
  fallback
- `source_order_survives_a_json_round_trip`

author: zarmstrong
body:
## Summary

- order active category campaigns by their actual deadline across Twitch inventory and fallback sources
- preserve configured category order when `CategoryCampaignOrder.ORDER` is selected
- preserve fallback-backed category eligibility when Twitch omits that campaign from a channel response
- add regression coverage for mixed-source ordering and fallback eligibility

## Root cause

The category filter ranked every Twitch inventory campaign ahead of every fallback campaign before comparing deadlines. This placed an earlier-expiring fallback campaign such as DJs after later-expiring inventory campaigns even with `CategoryCampaignOrder.EXPIRATION` configured.

After discovery selected DJs first, startup performed a channel-level campaign lookup. Twitch returned an available but empty campaign list because the account-ineligible DJs campaign was not exposed there. That empty response replaced the positive fallback eligibility with `(0, 0)`, removing every DJ candidate before the minute watcher selected a stream.

## Impact

Time-sensitive Drop categories are selected according to the documented nearest-deadline behavior regardless of campaign source. Fallback-only campaigns remain eligible through startup when their official Drops-enabled directory result and external campaign index agree, while empty Twitch responses remain authoritative for categories without fallback evidence.

## Validation

- full test suite: 591 passed
- focused category ordering and eligibility tests: 11 passed
- pre-commit hooks: trailing whitespace, end-of-file, large files, isort, Black, and flake8

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
Hardens view counting, earnings attribution and anti-fraud to production grade, without changing the Normal Campaign Flow, the CPM formula, ads, withdrawals, referrals, notifications or auth/RLS.

## 1. Architecture inspected first

Read the full pipeline before changing anything: `api/views/record/route.ts`, `lib/{earnings,fraud,view-schema,rate-limit,request-ip,cpm,finance,tasks,unlock-token,geo,chart-data,admin-server}.ts`, every migration `0001`→`0019` (especially `credit_view_earning` in `0008`, the `views` table in `0001/0012/0014`, `record_view_with_ip_check` + `rate_limit_entries` in `0017`, the `0019` repair), all 13 `from('views')` call sites, the admin/creator dashboards, and `supabase/functions/fraud-check`. Baseline: **26 files / 271 tests green**.

## 2. The duplicate-view rule

**1 IP + 1 campaign = max 1 earning-eligible view per rolling 24h. Same IP + a different campaign is fully independent.** The key is `(campaign_id, ip_hash, eligibility_window_start)` — campaign-scoped, so a shared NAT/university/office IP keeps earning on every campaign it hasn't already been paid for. There is no site-wide per-IP rule and no global IP block anywhere.

Traffic view and earning-eligible view are now separate concepts: every request that passes campaign validation is *recorded*; only rows that also clear security checks and the 24h window are *paid*. Non-eligible rows are stored with `earnings = 0`, a safe `traffic_category`, and `earning_eligible = false`.

## 3. How the admin sees paid and non-paid

New `AdminTrafficQuality` panel on the admin dashboard and the admin campaign page: Total Views, Valid/Paid, Non-Paid, Duplicates, Bot/Fraud Blocked, Earnings, plus a per-category breakdown and a 14-day trend. Fed by two SECURITY DEFINER RPCs (`admin_view_traffic_summary`, `admin_view_traffic_daily`) that both re-check `is_admin()` in SQL. Categories are coarse buckets (`duplicate_24h`, `bot_or_automation`, `vpn_or_proxy`, …) — no raw IP, no `ip_hash`, no fingerprint, no fraud score, no threshold in the admin UI.

## 4. Creator privacy

Creators see only business metrics: Total Views, Valid Views, Valid Rate, Earnings, Avg CPM, countries. The "Invalid Views" card and the red invalid-views chart series are gone; the recent-views panel is valid-only. No duplicate notification, no "rejected" message, no reason string, no count of hidden traffic.

The visitor response is byte-identical for a paid view and for a duplicate/bot/VPN/capped view (`{unlocked, payoutEligible, earning}`), so a creator cannot infer the rules from their own browser. DB-side, `creator_campaign_traffic` (security_invoker) filters out every hidden category.

## 5. Concurrency

`record_view_with_ip_check` does the window check and the INSERT in **one transaction** — never SELECT-then-INSERT. It takes a `pg_advisory_xact_lock` on `sha256(campaign||':'||ip_hash)`, and underneath sits the real guarantee: a **partial unique index** `uniq_views_paid_campaign_ip_window ON views (campaign_id, ip_hash, eligibility_window_start) WHERE earning_eligible AND ip_hash IS NOT NULL`. A losing racer catches `unique_violation` and re-inserts as `duplicate_ip_24h` with earnings 0. Tested at 2 and 5 concurrent requests: exactly one paid every time.

## 6. Bot/fraud improvements

New `src/lib/bot-detection.ts`:
- Envelope validation (405/415/413/400 for method, content-type, payload size) with a byte-level re-check so a lying `Content-Length` cannot smuggle a large body.
- Automation detection: Selenium/Playwright/Puppeteer/PhantomJS/HeadlessChrome, `sec-ch-ua: headless`, non-browser clients, missing/short UA.
- **Risk-only** signals for missing Accept/Sec-Fetch headers, client-hint mismatches and impossible UA/OS combos.
- Behavioural scoring (frequency abuse, rapid campaign switching, reload patterns, instant completion, abnormal session length) raises risk rather than blanket-blocking, so shared IPs stay legitimate.

`src/lib/fraud.ts` gained datacenter-range detection and a rewritten local heuristic. The server-observed `user-agent` header is authoritative; `body.userAgent` is never read. Rate limiting stays on the existing distributed `check_rate_limit` chain (per-IP 60/min plus per-campaign 12/min keyed on the *hashed* IP), so another serverless instance is not a bypass.

## 7. Files changed

**Modified (14):** `api/views/record/route.ts`, `lib/{earnings,fraud,view-schema,admin-server}.ts`, `admin/page.tsx`, `admin/campaigns/[id]/page.tsx`, `dashboard/page.tsx`, `dashboard/analytics/page.tsx`, `dashboard/campaigns/[id]/page.tsx`, `c/[slug]/UnlockClient.tsx`, `components/AnalyticsCharts.tsx`, `tests/database-security.test.ts`, `tests/user-agent-security.test.ts`

**New (9):** `lib/view-eligibility.ts`, `lib/bot-detection.ts`, `components/AdminTrafficQuality.tsx`, `supabase/migrations/0020_view_traffic_attribution.sql`, and five test files.

The two touched tests were **strengthened, not weakened**: the migration-count assertion was pinned to `^0019_`, and the UA tests encoded the *old, weaker* `header || body.userAgent` fallback. The rewritten route never reads `body.userAgent` at all, so the tests now assert the stronger contract (no fallback in either direction, and `userAgent` is not destructured from `parsed.data`).

## 8. Migration

One additive migration, `0020_view_traffic_attribution.sql`. **No old migration was edited.** It adds:

- Three columns on `views` (`traffic_category`, `earning_eligible`, `eligibility_window_start`) plus a backfill.
- Two IMMUTABLE classifier functions mirroring the TS module.
- A BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger that derives those columns and **forces `earnings = 0`** whenever a row is not eligible.
- The partial unique index and three support indexes.
- A replaced `record_view_with_ip_check` (same name/signature).
- A `CREATE OR REPLACE` of `credit_view_earning` whose financial logic is byte-for-byte the same — the only change is that counters increment only for creator-visible categories.
- Three admin RPCs, the creator-safe view, and a final `REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON views FROM anon, authenticated`.

## 9. Existing systems verified untouched

The CPM formula is unchanged — `earning = (CPM × creator_level_multiplier) / 1000`, asserted numerically in the new tests (5 × 1.25 / 1000 = 0.00625). Country CPM, trusted `cpm_country_code`, level multipliers, per-view and daily caps, the earnings ledger, referral commission, holding period and `recalculate_creator_level` all run through the original code paths.

Untouched entirely: `lib/ad-revenue/*` (Adsterra/Monetag — no impression or click behaviour changed), withdrawals, notifications, auth/RBAC/RLS, campaign create/edit/destination, and the Normal Campaign Flow. The removed 4/5-page custom flow was not restored.

## 10. Test results

```
npx tsc --noEmit   → clean, 0 errors
npm run lint       → 0 errors, 11 warnings (all pre-existing)
npm test           → 31 files / 469 tests passed   (baseline 26 / 271)
npm run build      → success, all routes compiled
git diff --check   → clean
```

New coverage:
- `view-attribution` (23) — walks the exact spec timeline: A paid → A+2h duplicate → B paid → C paid → B duplicate → A+25h paid again, plus concurrency, ledger zero-credit and hashed-IP keying.
- `record-view-route` (63) — spoofed UA, 16 smuggled financial/security fields, malformed/oversized/wrong-method payloads, rate-limit abuse, identical responses across five block reasons.
- `bot-detection` (48)
- `admin-traffic-analytics` (46) — admin aggregation plus a comment-stripped source audit of every creator surface.
- `view-eligibility` (17)

---

## Deploy note

Migration `0020` is committed but **has not been applied to any database**. It must run against Supabase before the new admin RPCs and the partial unique index take effect. Until then the admin loaders degrade gracefully to empty aggregates rather than erroring, and duplicate protection falls back to the existing `0017` advisory-lock path.

body:
## Problem

## Description
The report currency default is inconsistent across three surfaces:
- `ReportPreview.tsx:45`: `const reportCurrency = currency || INR;`
- `ReportExport.tsx:132`: `const [baseCurrency, setBaseCurrency] = useState(INR);`
- `reportUtils.ts` (authoritative fallback): `currency = reportData.currency || USD` (multiple sites)

## Expected Behavior
A single default (`USD`) everywhere, matching `CurrencyManager`'s default and `reportUtils`, so the same report renders in the same currency on every surface.

## Actual Behavior
A saved/exported report with an empty `currency` shows **INR** in Preview and PDF/CSV (`reportUtils` falls back to USD), so the same report shows different currencies depending on surface. Worse, `ReportExport` initializes `baseCurrency=INR`, so a brand-new user who never opened `CurrencyManager` (which defaults base to USD) gets reports labelled INR while their transactions were entered in USD — a silent mislabel of every figure.

## Proposed Fix
```ts
// ReportPreview.tsx
const reportCurrency = currency || USD;
// ReportExport.tsx
const [baseCurrency, setBaseCurrency] = useState(USD);
```

## Fix

fix: unify report currency default across Preview/ReportExport/reportUtils (Closes #1268)

## Files changed

- src/components/reports/ReportExport.tsx  | 2 +-
- src/components/reports/ReportPreview.tsx | 2 +-

## Testing

- Change is scoped to the issue; reviewed against surrounding code for correctness.
- Type checking / lint could not be executed locally (node_modules not installed in the working copy), so a CI typecheck is recommended on the PR.

Closes #1268

author: derand
body:
Closes #62.

A book's format was the last dot in its name and nothing else, so a book whose
name ends in anything unfamiliar did not exist: invisible in Browse, and "Wrong
file format, could not find supported extension" when opened from a file manager.

**Google Drive saves an FB2 as `book.fb2.xml`.** That is how books arrive on this
device — a folder of them was sitting there, every one refused — and the intent
filter added in #61 made it worse in the most confusing way available, since
`text/xml` is in it: the app offered itself for exactly those files and then
declined them.

## The name is enough

No file is read. The last extension when it is one of the seven, and failing that
the **second-to-last**.

The position is the whole of the care here:

```
як конвертувати .fb2 в .epub.html.xml
                            ↑     ↑
                   second-to-last last
```

An HTML page about converting books. Only the second-to-last counts — never a
known extension found anywhere in the name — or this would be handed to the FB2
parser. Its second-to-last is `.html`, which is what it is. By the same rule
`book.fb2.xml.bak` is **not** a book: two unknown extensions is a file that has
stopped saying what it holds. Both are tests.

Taken deliberately: `book.epub.bak` now opens as EPUB, and shows up in Browse for
the same reason. The user tapped that file.

## One resolver, for what were five copies

The three parsers, the image loader, the Browse listing and the sort by file
format each carried the rule. Browse mattered most: it filtered on `endsWith`
against the same seven strings, so without it a file that opens from a file
manager would stay invisible in the library it belongs to — and a listing that
disagrees with the parser offers files it cannot open. Sorting by format now
sorts a `*.fb2.xml` with the other FB2s rather than under "xml".

## Deciding by content is deliberately not here

A `PK` header, `%PDF-`, a `<FictionBook` root — nothing on the device needs it
yet, and it cannot be done on the Browse scan: that walks the whole tree, and a
read per file is a ContentResolver round trip, over a network for a cloud
provider. Worth doing when a file appears that its name cannot answer for.

author: cpmadrid
body:
Closes #304

Documentation only — no code, no behavior change. #304 was decided on
2026-08-13 ([decision comment](https://github.com/Sassy-Dog/solador/issues/304#issuecomment-5287183534)):
**`tauri-plugin-updater`**, not Sparkle. This is the docs reconciliation that
was all that remained of it. Part of #15.

## What changed

**`docs/VERSIONING.md` §5 (Tags)** — rewritten. The old block sent the reader
to "the §7 macOS row" for Sparkle's two-key mapping. Replaced with:

- A **"Mapping onto the update feed"** subsection naming `tauri-plugin-updater`
  and stating which number is the comparison key. The manifest has exactly one
  `version` field and the default comparison is `update.version > current`
  ([v2 docs](https://v2.tauri.app/plugin/updater)), so the marketing CalVer is
  the **sole** comparison key.
- The property that makes a single key safe, which Sparkle never needed and
  which was therefore written down nowhere: **CalVer is monotonic under semver
  ordering** — `2026.8.40` < `2026.9.1` < `2027.1.1`, every lower-field reset
  paired with an increase in the field above it. Includes why the **non-padded**
  month is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: semver forbids leading zeroes in
  numeric identifiers, so `2026.08.1` would not parse as a version at all.
- "generated — never hand-edited" kept, now applied to the updater manifest.
- The stale `#15 (signing / notarization / Sparkle)` parenthetical now points at
  the two issues that actually own that work, #306 and #308.
- The Sparkle mapping is **kept as a labelled superseded block** — this repo
  keeps provenance deliberately — and it is the only place either word survives.

**`scripts/publish.sh:179`** — one log line, `signing/notarization/Sparkle)` →
`signing/notarization and the update feed)`. Wording only. This line sits in the
unreachable block below the line-24 refusal; the `DerivedData` residue in that
same block is **#306**'s and was not touched.

## Correction to the issue body

The issue says the build number has *"no release-artifact or update-feed
consumer"*. **That is now half-wrong** and was not written that way here: #303
(PR #322) gave the build number a real build-time consumer — it is stamped over
`CFBundleVersion` and asserted back out of the artifact on every bundle,
precisely because Tauri's config has one version field and would otherwise write
the marketing version into both plist keys. So §5 says, narrowly, that the build
number has **no update-feed consumer**, and names its two real ones
(`CFBundleVersion`, and §5's own `mac-direct/<version>-<build>-<UTCts>` channel
tag). "No consumer" unqualified would be exactly the class of false claim this
issue exists to remove. The new §5 cross-references the Consumers section #322
rewrote rather than restating or contradicting it.

## Scope was smaller than the issue's list

The issue targeted 10 references across 4 files. **#303 (PR #322) merged first
and already cleaned `CLAUDE.md` and `scripts/build.sh`** — both were verified
clean and were not touched here. Only 5 references remained, in 2 files.

## Verification

`git grep -niE 'sparkle|appcast' -- . ':(exclude)Cargo.lock'` after the change —
all four surviving hits are inside the one paragraph explicitly labelled
`**Superseded:**`:

```
docs/VERSIONING.md:120:**Superseded:** this section previously mapped Sparkle's two keys per the §7
docs/VERSIONING.md:121:macOS row — `sparkle:version` = build number (the comparison key),
docs/VERSIONING.md:122:`sparkle:shortVersionString` = marketing version (display only), appcast
docs/VERSIONING.md:123:generated. Sparkle is macOS-only and was inherited from the deleted SwiftUI
```

Other gates (exit codes checked directly, not through a pipe):

- `./dev lint; echo "EXIT=$?"` → `EXIT=0`
- `bash -n scripts/publish.sh` → `0`
- `shellcheck -S warning scripts/publish.sh` → `0`

## Out of scope, deliberately

- The updater implementation itself (`plugins.updater`, minisign `pubkey`,
  `bundle.createUpdaterArtifacts`) is **#308**.
- The `DerivedData` residue in publish.sh's unreachable block is **#306**.
- #15's own body still contradicts itself on the signing-key type at line 39;
  that is operator work, recorded in #304 for resolution alongside #305.

author: aniruddh-alt
body:
## What
Adds one shared remote inference engine per worker process for generating simulated-user replies.

## Why
Creating a new inference engine for every conversation wastes resources, while sharing an in-process model would force concurrent conversations to run one at a time. The simulator therefore needs a reusable remote engine with early validation for unsupported configurations.

## How
The simulator loads its configuration once per worker, reuses the resulting remote engine, and rejects local model engines before they load weights.

Predecessor: #2610 · Successor: #2612

## Testing
Unit tests verify remote-engine reuse and confirm that missing, local, or otherwise non-remote engines are rejected before use. Standard lints clean.

author: noorallah
body:
`generate_sample_data.py --reset` could not finish. Its `delete_order` was a hand-maintained tuple naming **108 models for a 169-table schema**, so it died on whichever foreign key the missing 61 happened to violate first. It had gone stale four times that anybody noticed — settlements, physical counts, sales returns, quotations — and each repair was a guess at an order somebody worked out by reading error messages.

## The tuple is gone

`Base.metadata.sorted_tables` already knows the dependency graph. Reversed, it *is* the delete order, and it cannot go stale — a table added tomorrow is in it the moment its model is imported.

`PRESERVED_TABLES` names the fourteen exceptions and says why each survives:

- **`alembic_version`** — clearing it would make the database look unmigrated.
- **The business-profile catalogue** (5 tables) — seeded by migrations and nothing else. Deleting it loses the seven `is_implemented = false` flags `20260810_0059` set, which `seed_business_profiles` does **not** restore. Verified: 7 of 22 are still marked after two resets.
- **8 tables the function clears afterwards** with rules a generic pass cannot express — platform admins survive, system roles and permissions survive, the audit trail is truncated because it is append-only.

## The hand list was not the whole story

The delete was also **unqualified**, while the seed session runs with `search_path = platform, firm_shared, public`. A table existing in both — `product_valuations` is one — resolved to the *platform* copy, which is empty, while the firm_shared rows survived to break the next foreign key.

That is why the list appeared to work for years: **it worked for tables that live in one schema only.** Each schema is now cleared by name, in full, before the next.

**Proven by running the generator twice**: the second `--yes` succeeds, which it could only do if the first run's reset cleared everything. A `reset` leaves nothing behind except the fourteen preserved tables and the six `seed_uom_reference_data` immediately re-seeds.

## One list of model modules

`app/core/database/all_models.py`. `alembic/env.py`, `tests/conftest.py` and the seed script each kept their own copy, and `CLAUDE.md` carried a standing instruction to keep two of them in step by hand — the shape of a rule that gets forgotten, and it was: that is how the reset fell 61 tables behind. `test_schema_registry.py` fails the build if a module under `app/*/models/` is missing from it.

**475 backend tests** pass (2 new), `ruff`/`black`/`mypy` clean across the tree.

## Two things this uncovered, left open

Both are written into `docs/BACKLOG.md` §12 and `CLAUDE.md`.

**`seed_multi_firm_demo.py` cannot seed a genuinely clean database** — nobody had one before, because the reset never worked. It asked for UOM codes `GRAM` and `TABLET` the baseline catalogue never had (**fixed here**: `TABLET` joins the catalogue below `STRIP`, and `GRAM` becomes `G`, the code the catalogue uses). It then fails the mandatory-attribute check against `CategoryAttributeRule` rows it has just written itself. That one I did not chase — it needs someone to work out which attribute the rule requires that the product does not supply, and it is not this change.

**The generated dataset does not balance.** `verify_sample_data.py` reports customers owing 885,000.00 against a receivable control account of zero: the generator sets `customers.opening_balance` directly and nothing posts a journal. Same defect class as `CustomerService.post_receivable_transaction`. Fixing it needs a decision about the counterpart — opening balance equity, the way opening stock got one in `20260814_0080`.

## 先订正前提:「存量工厂关不掉模块」**不成立**

客户在画布里关模块 → `toggleModule` → `saveModuleConfig` → **`getOrCreateDraft`**,行写进 **DRAFT** 版本;而门禁条件 2 要 **PUBLISHED**。⇒ 不发布就不生效。

**而发布是可达的**:`POST /config/publish` 存在,web-admin `canvas-editor/CanvasHeader.vue` 里有**「立即发布」按钮**。⇒ **存量工厂完全能做到「关掉且生效」——判据第 2 条成立。**

## 真正缺的是**判据第 3 条**

| 出口 | 说的话 | 问题 |
|---|---|---|
| 四态 tag | `ROLLOUT`「灰度中 · 接口已开放」 | **准确但不完整**,听着一切正常 |
| `/module-gate-status` | `NO_PUBLISHED_CONFIG`,`needsAttention=false` | 与「客户什么都没配」**完全同一句话** |

两者库状态相同,**含义相反**。**坏掉的样子和正常一模一样。**

## 做了什么(全部是可见性,**零行为变更**)

1. `ModuleGateStatus.Reason.PENDING_PUBLISH` —— 无 PUBLISHED **且**未发布草稿里有 `enabled=false` 的行时报它,`needsAttention=true`,**列出是哪些码**,`detail` 写「请到『画布配置』点一次『立即发布』」。
2. `ModuleSwitchService.describe()` 把它写进 **`stateDescription`** —— features 页**已经**在渲染这个字段作 tooltip ⇒ **零 `.vue` 改动**就到达用户。另加 `pendingPublish` 布尔字段。

### ⛔ 没动的三处(边界)

**发布语义** / **四态枚举** / **四态那份数据的 `needsAttention` 口径**。要不要让「未发布」在界面**报红**是产品决定 —— 数据已备好,**改一行**,位置写在代码注释里。

## 顺带修掉一个「写了但没接上」

`ModuleGateStatus` 是 **record**,Jackson 默认**只序列化 record 组件**。实测:**补 `@JsonProperty` 之前,`/module-gate-status` 的响应里根本没有 `needsAttention` 字段** ⇒ 自 #106 它诞生起**没有任何消费方读得到它**,而且躲过了 #106 的四条断言。

## 验收

`PendingPublishVisibilityTest` **4/4**,真实 MVC 路由 + 真 `FactoryConfigServiceImpl` + 真 `ModuleSwitchService`,只桩 repository。含**两条阴性对照**:什么都没关时不能报;草稿里**只有 `enabled=true`** 的行时**不算**。

**变异 5/5 红**(含「拿掉 `@JsonProperty` 让它又变回不可见」)。既有:`ModuleGateInertnessTest` 4/4 · `ModuleSwitchEntryTest` 5/5 · `ModuleEnabledInterceptorUserAccessTest` 3/3 · 迁移闸 1/1+3/3 · 七道闸全 EXIT=0。**无迁移。**

## 🔴 我自己踩的两个坑

1. **第一版变异 5 条里 1 条是绿的** —— 我改了 `needsAttention()` 却**没有断言守着它**。补上断言后才挖出更深的问题:那字段**压根不在 JSON 里**。
2. **我把 #105 的 `ModuleSwitchEntryTest` 弄红了一次** —— `describe()` 新增了对 `describeModuleGate` 的调用,那测试里它是**没打桩的 mock 返回 null**。真实现永不返 null,所以**补桩**是对的修法。

## Why

The market page price can read higher than wallets/aggregators (e.g. $160 vs ~$148 for 50,000 LUKO). This is **not a bug**: the site computes price from the **live LUKO/USDC Aerodrome pool reserve ratio** (USDC ÷ LUKO, taking 1 USDC ≈ $1), which GeckoTerminal's own per-pool quote confirms exactly. Wallets and aggregators show a token-level USD price that **lags** the pool on a thin market ($553 liquidity), so they differ briefly after a trade. This PR makes that transparent and verifiable instead of surprising.

Every USD figure on this page is derived from it — no third-party price feed. This is the pool's current price; wallets and aggregators can lag it briefly on a thin pool, so their numbers may differ.

## Problem

- Managed warehouse dashboards cannot tell which duckgres queries come from customers and which from our own pipelines.
- The register workflow, copy workflows, SQL shadow path, and materialization all connect as the org-root user, the same username customers copy from connection details.
- Duckgres now echoes the client's `application_name` startup param into its `query_initiated` / `query_completed` / `query_failed` analytics events (PostHog/duckgres#1072), but our callers never set one.

## Changes

- `make_duckgres_conninfo` and `connect_to_duckgres` gain a keyword-only `application_name` defaulting to `"posthog"`, forwarded on both the org-root and service-credential branches.
- Call sites pass caller slugs: `ducklake-register`, `ducklake-copy`, `ducklake-copy-modeling`, `events-backfill`, `endpoints-shadow`, `materialization`.
- The facade wrapper passes `application_name` through so out-of-product callers can tag themselves.
- The `"posthog"` default means even an untagged internal caller stays separable from customer clients, which send their own value (`psql`) or none.

> [!NOTE]
> This is a labeling convention for analytics, not a security or billing boundary — clients can send any `application_name`. Billing attribution stays on the validated `duckgres.query_source` GUC. Safe to merge before or after the duckgres PR; until it deploys, the tag is simply ignored.

- Extended conninfo tests assert the default and explicit overrides on both auth branches, and the `endpoints-shadow` / `materialization` slugs at their call sites — no prior test pinned any application_name, so an accidental drop of the param was previously invisible.
- Not run: live duckgres connection checks; the tag's end-to-end effect depends on the duckgres PR above.

None — internal telemetry attribution only.

author: the-data-is-a-lie
body:
Closes #81 (sheet half). The backend half is committed on `feat/loot-endpoint` in
`Pathfinder_Char_Creator` and **awaits a human `deploy.ps1`** — this PR does not.

## Why it can merge before the deploy

The 💰 **Treasure…** button ships `hidden`. `SheetLootUI.init()` runs one `GET /generate_loot`
after `?backend=` has been applied and reveals the button only if that answers `{ok:true}`. Against
today's deployed backend the probe 404s and nothing appears; the moment the endpoint deploys, the
button shows up with no second release here. The probe is cached as a promise, so ten dialog opens
are one request, and it hits a limiter-exempt route that generates nothing.

## What it does

CR + campaign track → the backend's parcel (coins / gems / items against Paizo's per-encounter
value table) → tick what you want → **add to any character in your library**, including one you do
not have open. Plus *Copy as text* for pasting into notes.

## Two decisions worth keeping

- **Writing to a character that is not open had no precedent in this repo.** The open character
  must go through `SheetRoster.saveCurrent` — its in-memory object is the authority and a library
  write would be overwritten by the next auto-save. Anybody else is `SheetLibrary.get` → mutate →
  `SheetLibrary.save`, which never touches `SheetApp.current`. Both paths are in `commit()`.
- **Loot lands carried but not equipped.** `addInventoryItem` defaults to `equipped: true`, which
  would silently move AC and attack numbers the moment a GM added a pile of armor to a character.
  Item ids also get a sequence suffix — that function stamps ids from `Date.now()`, and six items
  added in a loop land in the same millisecond (the collision #93 hit with buffs).

## Verified

Playwright against a local backend (`?backend=http://127.0.0.1:5099`), **11/11, 0 page errors**:
probe reveals the button · dialog opens · CR 10 fast roll returns a 8,200 gp parcel · items and
coins land in a **second, unopened** character (0 → 6 items, 5 → 1,545 gp) · nothing auto-equipped ·
ids unique · every item priced · the open character is not switched · and against a backend without
the endpoint the button **stays hidden**.

Backend: `Backend/scripts/tests/test_loot.py` is 379 checks, and the full suite is 14/14 green with
the golden payload unchanged.

author: trentkm
body:
An attach snapshot taken while the PTY has delivered half an escape sequence hands a fresh replica the tail with no head — printed as text at the cursor. Claude Code rewrites the terminal title constantly; the tail of `ESC ]0;Claude Code BEL` is the literal string "Claude Code", which is how it kept materializing on an agent's input line in Stormlight (and why session titles sometimes rendered as a bare `�` — the same tear seen from the other side).

`readLoop` now holds back each read's incomplete trailing sequence/rune and prepends it to the next read, so the emulator, snapshots, resize repaints, and subscriber broadcasts only ever see whole sequences. Bounded holdback; a dying child's remnant is flushed torn rather than lost.

Reproduced by `TestAttachMidEscapeSequenceDoesNotLeakTheTail`; the scanner is table-tested in `TestCompleteBoundaryHoldsBackTornTails`.

body:
Three new staged sketches under \`firmware/3D model/Gam/cube-bringup/\`,
implementing Phase 0.2/0.3/0.4 against real cube hardware for the first
time — the panel bring-up never exercised 3-wheel CAN contention or an
IMU jitter budget, so none of this could be adapted, it's new code
written in the same house style.

  in sequence, 60s. Re-run for all 3 wheel IDs before Stage0b.
- **Stage0b_ThreeMoteusLatency** — three wheels, one 400 Hz loop, pooled
  latency histogram + dropped-cycle counter. Pass: p99.9 < 2.0ms, zero
  drops, 10 min.
- **Stage0c_IMUJitter** — BMI270 at 800 Hz ODR polled at 400 Hz, checks
  every poll gets fresh (non-repeated) data. \`bwp\`/group-delay left as
  an explicit TODO — that's a datasheet lookup, not something firmware
  can determine on its own.

README in the folder documents run order and what's still open after
these three pass (per-wheel \`kMoteusId\` re-run, the \`bwp\` datasheet
lookup, and \`kWheelSign\` — untested here, that's Phase 1.3).

Not merged into anything downstream yet — no control code, no estimator,
no gains. Pure bring-up instrumentation, meant to be flashed and run on
the bench before Phase 1.

author: annejan
body:
Post-mortem fix for the one thing that went wrong deploying v1.0.0 to production.

## What happened

`/projects/{slug}` returned 500 with `could not find driver`. The licence list is
a Sushi model backed by an **in-memory SQLite** database, and the host had no
`pdo_sqlite` — Ubuntu packages it separately as `php8.4-sqlite3`.

Nothing declared that requirement, so it surfaced as one broken page in
production rather than as a missing prerequisite at install time. Every other
page worked, which made it easy to miss.

## Two parts to the fix

**1. Declare what we use.** `composer.json` listed `gd`, `gmp`, `fileinfo`,
`json`, `zlib`, `mbstring` — but not the four the code actually reaches for:

| extension | used by |
| --- | --- |
| `pdo_sqlite` | `App\Models\License` via Sushi |
| `pdo_mysql` | the database |
| `phar` | `PublishProject` building egg archives with `PharData` |
| `curl` | Guzzle, outbound HTTP |

**2. Turn the runtime check on — this is the part that actually matters here.**

Composer defaults `platform-check` to `"php-only"`, so
`vendor/composer/platform_check.php` only guarded the PHP version. And because
releases ship a **prebuilt `vendor/`**, `composer install` never runs on the
server that is missing the extension — so declaring it would have changed
nothing for this deployment.

With `"platform-check": true`, that same host now fails the very first request
with:

```
Your Composer dependencies require the following PHP extensions to be installed: pdo_sqlite.
```

Verified by patching the generated check to report `pdo_sqlite` absent and
confirming the message.

## Notes

- The Docker image is unaffected: `php:8.4-cli` has `pdo_sqlite` built in, which
  is exactly why CI, the browser tests and my local runs never caught this.
- The README now lists the extensions and calls out `pdo_sqlite` as the easy one
  to miss.
- Cost is a handful of `extension_loaded()` calls per request.

270 tests, phpstan level 8, phpcs and REUSE all pass.

## Production is fine

`php8.4-sqlite3` is installed and the site is healthy — full sweep of `/`,
`/projects`, `/projects/{slug}` ×4, `/badges`, `/users`, `/login`, `/register`,
`/api`, `/up`, `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml`, `/eggs/*`, `/basket/*`, `/v2/*` all
200. This PR is so the next person does not have to find it the same way.

body: ## Why The last two `main` runs of this workflow never published `latest`: both hung in the QEMU-emulated `linux/arm64` leg of `pnpm turbo run docker-build` and were killed by the 90-minute job timeout ([run 31757295680](https://github.com/hexclave/hexclave/actions/runs/31757295680), and the earlier run for the fix's merge commit). In the stalled logs the arm64 step stops emitting output entirely — no OOM, no error — while the amd64 leg of the same step finishes in ~73s, and a `dev` build of a neighbouring commit ran the same emulated step in 8.5 min. So it's an intermittent emulation hang, not legitimate build time. Consequence: `stackauth/server:latest` has been stuck on the Aug 12 build, so the self-hosted key-stability fix (#1950) never reached customers. ## What Split the single multi-platform job into a matrix that builds each platform on a native runner (`ubicloud-standard-8` for amd64, `ubicloud-standard-8-arm` for arm64) and drop the QEMU setup step. Because two jobs must not race on the same moving tags, the platform jobs push **untagged, by digest** and a final `merge` job assembles the manifest: ``` build (amd64) ─┐ push-by-digest → server@sha256:… build (arm64) ─┴─→ merge: docker buildx imagetools create --tag server@amd64digest server@arm64digest ``` Tag semantics are unchanged — the `merge` job reuses the identical `docker/metadata-action` rules (`latest` on `main` only, branch tag off `main`, unprefixed sha, `\d.\d.\d`), so it emits one `--tag` per generated tag against one multi-platform manifest. Push gating is unchanged too: non-push events build both platforms with an empty `outputs:` (no registry credentials needed) and skip `merge` entirely. Per-ref concurrency is kept, with its comment updated to say the tag move now happens in `merge`. The merge script refuses to assemble a manifest from anything that isn't exactly two `sha256:<64 hex>` digests rather than silently creating a malformed reference. No caching in this PR, and no changes to the Dockerfile or application code. ## Testing Workflow-only change, so it can only be exercised by running on a branch: YAML parses, `git diff --check` clean, and every `steps.*`/`needs.*` reference and the tag loop were checked by hand (`actionlint` isn't installed here). The arm64 runner label is Ubicloud's documented native arm64 8-vCPU Ubuntu 24.04 alias; this repo hasn't used it before, so the first `dev` run is the real proof that the label resolves. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/a9ac9b0a226a4043ba1d627d46fee263 Requested by: @N2D4 --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes release publishing for `stackauth/server` images; wrong merge logic or digest handling could break or mis-tag production Docker images, though tag rules and push gating are preserved. > > **Overview** > Replaces the single QEMU-based multi-platform Docker build with a **matrix** that builds `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` on native runners (`ubicloud-standard-8` / `ubicloud-standard-8-arm`), removing QEMU setup. Platform jobs no longer push release tags directly; on push events they **push by digest only** and upload digests as artifacts. > > A new **`merge` job** downloads both digests, validates exactly two `sha256:` references, and runs `docker buildx imagetools create` to publish the same metadata tags (`latest`, branch, sha, semver) as one multi-platform manifest. Per-ref concurrency comments are updated to reflect that tag moves happen in merge. Non-push runs still build both platforms without registry push and skip merge. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit fd42720f37e8d00c163719a89a013fcb8e74b00e. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot). --- ## Summary by cubic Builds server Docker images natively per platform instead of via QEMU, preventing intermittent arm64 hangs that were blocking `latest` and `dev` tag publication. Previously one job built a multi-arch image under emulation and pushed tags; now each platform builds on a native runner and pushes by digest, then a merge job assembles the multi-arch manifest and tags. - Runs a matrix: `linux/amd64` on `ubicloud-standard-8` (30 min timeout) and `linux/arm64` on `ubicloud-standard-8-arm` (45 min). - Removes `docker/setup-qemu-action`; keeps `docker/setup-buildx-action` and `docker/login-action`. - Each platform uses `docker/build-push-action` to push an untagged digest (`push-by-digest=true`); digests are exchanged via `actions/upload-artifact`/`actions/download-artifact`. - A `merge` job validates exactly two `sha256:<64 hex>` digests and runs `docker buildx imagetools create` to publish one multi-arch manifest per tag from `docker/metadata-action` (tag rules unchanged: `latest` on `main`, branch tag off `main`, unprefixed SHA, `\d.\d.\d`). - Concurrency remains per ref; tag movement happens only in `merge`. Non-push events build both platforms without pushing and skip `merge`. - No changes to Dockerfiles, application code, or caching. Written for commit fd42720f37e8d00c163719a89a013fcb8e74b00e. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved container image builds for both amd64 and arm64 platforms. * Added validation to ensure platform digests are correctly formatted and complete. * Improved image publishing reliability by combining platform-specific builds into multi-platform images.

author: ionfwsrijan
body:
## Problem

## Description
`calculateCategoryTrends` (`src/lib/insightsUtils.ts:505-510`) builds the monthly interval with `end: now`, so the final trend point is the **current, still-running month**. `filterByPeriod` then only sums transactions up to today for that point.

## Expected Behavior
The trend series should contain only completed months (or the current month should be annualized/excluded) so the last point is comparable to prior full months.

## Actual Behavior
The last point is almost always far lower than the preceding full months, drawing a misleading "spending dropped" line at the right edge of the 6-month chart. Meanwhile `topCategories` is computed against `endOfMonth(now)` (treating the current month as complete), so the chart and the category ranking are internally inconsistent.

## Proposed Fix
```ts
const now = new Date();
const endWindow = endOfMonth(subMonths(now, 1)); // last fully-elapsed month
const startWindow = startOfMonth(subMonths(now, months - 1));
const intervalMonths = eachMonthOfInterval({ start: startWindow, end: endWindow });
```

## Fix

fix: exclude partial current month from category trend series (Closes #1269)

## Files changed

- src/lib/insightsUtils.ts | 5 +++--

## Testing

- Change is scoped to the issue; reviewed against surrounding code for correctness.
- Type checking / lint could not be executed locally (node_modules not installed in the working copy), so a CI typecheck is recommended on the PR.

Closes #1269

author: alband
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.15.0) (oldest at bottom):
* #193618
* __->__ #193612

## Author Notes

Adding a new macro to simplify a lot of the python binding.
I could have added a variant that does decref, but it would only remove a small number of skips. So leaving it for now. Happy to add it if anyone wants though!

## Agent Notes

Written by Claude Code:

> `throw python_error()` is how torch hands a pending CPython error back to the
> interpreter: the exception captures type, value and traceback, and
> CATCH_CORE_ERRORS restores them. TORCH_CHECK is not a substitute - it would
> discard the real Python exception, so a KeyError from PyDict_GetItem would reach
> the user as a RuntimeError. This adds a macro that keeps the exception and drops
> the boilerplate around it:
>
>     #define TORCH_CHECK_PYTHON(cond)        \
>       if (C10_UNLIKELY_OR_CONST(!(cond))) { \
>         throw python_error();               \
>       }
>
> so `if (!self) { throw python_error(); }` becomes `TORCH_CHECK_PYTHON(self);`.
> The macro takes no message because the message is whatever CPython already
> raised. Behaviour is unchanged everywhere: the same exception object is thrown
> from the same place.
>
> 249 of the 259 sites were the sole body of an `if`, and the guard had to be
> inverted for each. 236 were rewritten by a throwaway script over shapes whose negation is
> unambiguous - `!x`, `< 0`, `!= 0`, `== -1`, `== nullptr`, and `A && B` by De
> Morgan, which preserves short-circuit order because B runs exactly when A holds
> either way. 13 more were done by hand, mostly guards spanning `||` or wrapped in
> a comment. The remaining 10 keep a raw throw with a reason: they either free a
> reference first (`Py_DECREF(type); throw ...`) or raise an error the line above
> has just set with PyErr_SetString, so there is no condition to collapse.
>
> Three throws of the form `python_error err; err.persist(); throw std::move(err)`
> also keep a raw throw. persist() has to run before unwinding so the error
> survives crossing an autograd engine thread, which the macro cannot express.
>
> UnwindError joins ALLOWED_EXCEPTION_TYPES, scoped to torch/csrc/profiler. It is
> the unwinder's own control flow, caught by name in fast_symbolizer.h and
> unwind.cpp, so a TORCH_CHECK there would break the handlers. It is the last
> thing standing between torch/csrc/profiler and a clean bill.
>
> Deleted from the burn-down block, all four now clean:
>
>     torch/csrc/cuda/**       19 sites
>     torch/csrc/tensor/**     16 sites
>     torch/csrc/xpu/**         6 sites
>     torch/csrc/profiler/**    2 conversions and 1 annotated raw throw, plus
>                               19 UnwindError now allowed by rule
>
> One interaction worth knowing about: `@allow-raw-throw` and NOLINTNEXTLINE both
> want the line directly above the throw. Where they collided, in
> python_function.cpp, the NOLINT moved to a trailing comment on the throw itself.
>
> Test Plan:
>
> ```
> bash -ic 'BUILD_CONFIG spin develop'
> ```
>
> Builds clean. It did not on the first two attempts, which is the point of
> building: the script initially took the guard text from the linter's blanked
> code view rather than the source, so `PyModule_AddObject(module, "_fft", fft)`
> lost its string literal and became `PyModule_AddObject(module, , fft)` at 14
> sites. The script now reads structure from the blanked view and every emitted
> character from the original. The second failure was a dangling `else` in
> python_arg_parser.cpp, where collapsing an `if` consumed the brace its `else if`
> belonged to; the script now refuses any site whose block is followed by `else`.
>
> ```
> python -m pytest -q test/test_indexing.py test/test_numpy_interop.py \
>     test/test_python_dispatch.py test/test_type_promotion.py \
>     test/test_dlpack.py test/test_autograd.py
> ```
>
> 1616 passed, 116 skipped. (test_lstsq is deselected: it needs LAPACK, which this
> build does not have, and it fails the same way on an unmodified tree.)
>
> Exception types are preserved end to end, checked against a built torch:
> `torch.zeros(3)[10]` still raises IndexError, `torch.device(12.5)` and
> `torch.zeros(3).reshape('x')` still raise TypeError. Those paths run through
> converted guards in python_numbers.h and python_arg_parser.cpp.
>
> ```
> spin lint
> ```
>
> RAWTHROW clean. Counting with this PR's linter over all 4450 tracked .cpp/.h
> files and ignoring exclude_patterns, `raw-throw` findings drop from 1314 to
> 1054. Total messages go 1343 to 1071; the extra 17 are orphaned and reasonless
> `@allow-raw-throw` markers that predate this stack and sit in directories that
> are still excluded.
>
> The only lint errors left are 157 CLANGTIDY `file not found` for cuda.h and the
> XPU headers, which this machine does not have - 75 of them reproduce on
> unmodified cuda/xpu files.
>
> Not built locally: 12 of the 79 source files are behind USE_CUDA, USE_XPU,
> USE_DISTRIBUTED or USE_MPS, which this configuration disables - the four
> torch/csrc/cuda files, three torch/csrc/xpu, four torch/csrc/distributed and
> torch/csrc/mps/Stream.cpp. Those need CI.
>
> One deletion worth noting: python_function.h loses a
> NOLINTNEXTLINE(hicpp-exception-baseclass) along with the `if` it guarded. The
> throw now lives inside the macro, and python_error derives from std::exception,
> so the check has nothing to fire on.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary Fixes from a security scan of the frontend (no hardcoded credentials and no SQL/DB access exist in this repo — the risks are all input handling, redirects and dependencies). **Open redirect (high).** `callbackUrl` was taken from the query string and used unvalidated in `router.push(callbackUrl)` / `window.location.href = callbackUrl` on the login page, register page and `GoogleLoginButton`, so `/login?callbackUrl=https://evil.com` sent a freshly authenticated user off-site. New `safeRedirectPath()` accepts only relative same-origin paths: ```ts safeRedirectPath("/dashboard") // "/dashboard" safeRedirectPath("https://evil.com") // "/" safeRedirectPath("//evil.com") // "/" ``` **JSON-LD injection / reflected XSS (high).** `ToolSchema` interpolates `JSON.stringify(schema)` into a `` broke out of the script tag. Now `<` is escaped as `\u003c`. **`/api/lock` proxy (high).** The route was an unauthenticated proxy that: interpolated `file.name` straight into `Content-Disposition` (header injection via CRLF/quotes in the filename), interpolated the password into the backend's flat `upw:…, opw:…, mode:encrypt` config string (a password containing `, ` could inject config fields such as `mode:decrypt`), forwarded arbitrary payload sizes, and returned raw backend error text to the client. It now validates types, enforces the same 50 MB limit as `uploadAndDownloadFile`, rejects passwords containing `,`/CR/LF/NUL, sanitizes the download filename, and returns generic errors while logging details server-side. **SSRF surface in url-to-pdf (medium, partially).** `UrlToPdfWorkspace` submitted any string starting with `http` to the conversion service. New `isPublicHttpUrl()` rejects non-http(s) schemes and loopback/private/link-local/metadata hosts before submitting. This is client-side only — **the backend must enforce the same policy**; that's where the actual SSRF fix belongs. **Dependencies.** `npm audit fix` (lockfile only) patches high-severity advisories in `axios`, `pdfjs-dist` (arbitrary JS execution when opening a malicious PDF — directly relevant here), `form-data` and `nanoid`. The remaining 3 highs (`next`, and its `postcss`/`sharp`) need `next@16.3.1`, which was published less than a day ago, so the bump is intentionally left out of this PR. **Defense in depth.** Baseline response headers (`X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy`, HSTS) via `next.config.ts`; `/admin` and `/admin/content` now gate rendering on `user?.role === "admin"` instead of relying only on a redirect inside `useEffect` (the admin APIs are still enforced by the backend). `npm run build` and `npx tsc --noEmit` pass; `npm run lint` fails only on pre-existing `no-explicit-any` errors, none in the touched lines. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/a27711a01fed40c8ab15d559cbc31e21 Requested by: @gimesha-adikari

## Résumé

Défaut confirmé en UAT (sévérité faible) : le taux de marge n'est pas calculé de la même façon sur deux écrans, pour la même affaire. Avec des données réelles (960 € devisé, 500 € facturé, 150 € de marge) :
- `/affaires/:id` : « 16 % » (150 / 960 devisé)
- `/marge` : « 30,0 % » (150 / 500 facturé), même montant de marge en euros

Les deux formules sont individuellement défendables (marge sur le devisé vs marge sur le facturé), mais présentées sans distinction — aucun des deux libellés ne précisait sur quelle base. Un artisan qui compare les deux écrans pour la même affaire voit deux pourcentages différents sans explication.

**Choix retenu (parmi les deux proposés par le rapport)** : libeller explicitement chaque écran plutôt qu'aligner les calculs — aucun changement de chiffre déjà affiché ailleurs dans l'app.

**Correctif** :
- `/affaires/:id` : « Marge brute » → « Marge brute (sur devisé) »
- `/marge` : « Taux de marge » → « Taux de marge (sur facturé) », colonne « Marge (%) » → « Marge (% facturé) »
- `/rapports` (même calcul, même ambiguïté potentielle) : « Taux de marge » → « Taux de marge (facturé) »

body:
Closes **A7** — and corrects it. The item said *ingest swallows an indexing failure*. Half of that was already fixed: since 2026-08-11 an ingest that leaves chunks unembedded prints the size of the hole and the recovery command. What was still swallowed is **why**.

That matters because the recovery ingest recommends — `nexus reembed run` — fails at the same place for the same reason. A count does not answer *what do I do*.

## The reason was already stored

`embed_refusals` has kept the backend message verbatim since 2026-08-07. `413 max_seq_length(8192)` is not an error string, it is a prescription: fix the chunking. **The only reader was the corpus view.**

- `embed_health.fetch_refusals(column, tenant=…)` — one aggregate, under **the same policy filter the coverage query uses**. If the two populations differed you would get "hole 45 / refused 3" with no way to explain the gap.
- Ingest output, `nexus status`, and `/status` now print the reasons next to the count, most frequent first, with `… 그 밖의 이유 N종` when the list is truncated.
- A hole with **no** refusal behind it is named separately — those chunks never reached the embedding step, which is a different prescription.

## The wiring test was worthless when first written

It asserted the reason string appeared in stdout. **It passed with the CLI's own output disabled** — structlog writes `embedding_index_failed` and the new warning to the same stream, so the string was there either way. It now asserts the line the CLI itself formats, and was verified by breaking that loop on purpose and watching it go red.

Four DB tests: the reason rides on the result, another tenant's refusals do not leak in, a successful retry takes the count back to zero, and the CLI actually prints it.

author: rmontanana
body:
Fase 3: cerrar la última vulnerabilidad (la que mantiene Security en **C**) y atacar las 26 ramas sin cubrir que quedaron tras #13.

## Seguridad

`scripts/update_coverage.py` construía el comando de lcov concatenando `sys.argv[1]` en una cadena ejecutada con `shell=True`:

```python
subprocess.check_output("lcov --summary " + sys.argv[1] + "/coverage.info", shell=True)
```

Una ruta como `x; rm -rf ~` se habría ejecutado como comando. Se pasa ahora la lista de argumentos y se elimina el shell; de paso, un argumento ausente da un mensaje claro en vez de un `IndexError`.

Verificado: la ejecución normal sigue dando 100.0% y actualizando el badge; con `'build_debug/tests; echo INYECTADO'` el comando **no se ejecuta** —la cadena se trata como ruta literal y lcov falla— y el README queda intacto.

Es el único hallazgo que sostenía el rating de seguridad en C, así que debería pasar a **A**.

## Ramas: 2 de las 26 eran alcanzables

Investigadas una a una con el detalle por línea que expone SonarCloud. Solo dos resultaron ser huecos de test reales, y llevan test:

- **`Discretizer.cpp:51`** — `transform()` usa `std::lower_bound` cuando `direction` es `LEFT`. Ningún discretizador de la librería asigna `LEFT`: los tres ponen `RIGHT`, que además es el valor por defecto. La rama solo es alcanzable a través del miembro `protected`, que es un punto de extensión para subclases externas. El test subclasifica `Discretizer` y fija el único caso en que ambos bounds difieren: una muestra justo sobre un punto de corte.
- **`CPPFImdlp.cpp:116`** — `compute_max_num_cut_points()` redondea `proposed_cuts * X.size()` cuando la propuesta es fraccionaria, así que una fracción suficientemente pequeña cae a cero y `fit()` se salta el bucle de recorte. Merece señalarse el comportamiento que esto documenta: **cero se interpreta como "sin límite", no como "sin puntos de corte"**.

## Las otras 24 no son huecos de test

Se dejan como están, porque su otra rama no puede ejecutarse:

| Sitio | Por qué es inalcanzable |
|---|---|
| `CPPFImdlp.cpp:103` | `X.empty() \|\| y.empty()` va precedida de `X.size() != y.size()`, así que "X no vacío pero y vacío" es imposible |
| `BinDisc.cpp:59,70` | `else if (strategy == UNIFORM)` sobre un enum con exactamente dos valores |
| `BinDisc.cpp:150` | `size() == 1` implica `front() == back()`, ya capturado por la primera condición |
| `Metrics.cpp:59,61,72,74` | Guardas de índice dentro de bucles ya acotados por ese mismo tamaño |
| `Metrics.cpp:23,52` | Condiciones correlacionadas: `indices.empty()` fuerza `start >= indices.size()`, y gcov no puede ejercitarlas por separado |
| `CPPFImdlp.cpp:288,309` | Comprobaciones redundantes: los índices vienen de un `iota` sobre el propio tamaño |
| `Discretizer.cpp:84` | Requiere un tensor fuera de CPU; el código ya lo marca `// LCOV_EXCL_LINE` |

No he tocado esas guardas defensivas: eliminarlas subiría la métrica pero cambiaría la postura de robustez de la librería, y esa es una decisión del maintainer, no un efecto colateral de perseguir un número.

## Verificación

- **148/148 tests pasan** (146 previos + 2 nuevos).
- Build Debug completo.
- Script probado en sus tres caminos: normal, sin argumento e intento de inyección.

body:
## Problem
Sites were heartbeating `agent_version: 0.3.0` regardless of the installed release. The value came from a hardcoded `AgentServiceProvider::VERSION` const that was never bumped past 0.3.0 — the `FlushCommandTest` assertions had frozen it there, so bumping it broke tests. It survived three releases (0.3.1, 0.3.2, 0.4.0).

## Fix
- Resolve the version from `Composer\InstalledVersions::getPrettyVersion('131studios/watchtower-agent')` at runtime, so it tracks the installed git tag automatically and can't go stale again.
- Const kept only as a fallback for environments without Composer runtime metadata (e.g. path repos), bumped to `0.4.1`.
- Tests assert against the resolver instead of a frozen literal; added a resolver test.

## Verification
- 40 tests passing.
- `getPrettyVersion` returns the tag (e.g. `0.4.1`) in a real dist install; `dev-main` only in the package's own checkout.

## Note
This fixes the code. Existing sites keep reporting `0.3.0` until their agent is `composer update`d to a release containing this fix (v0.4.1).

body:
### Motivation

- Prevent upgrade-time `ConstraintError`s by reconciling legacy duplicate logical encounters before adding a unique compound index. 
- Ensure concurrent callers creating the same logical encounter resolve to a single stored row and preserve completion/notes. 

### Description

- Introduce `createAppDatabase` and exported `AppDatabase` type and centralize Dexie schema setup into versions 1–3, with `VERSION_1_STORES` and `VERSION_3_STORES`. 
- Add `reconcileDuplicateEncounters(transaction: Transaction)` to detect and merge duplicate logical encounters deterministically while preserving completion, repointing notes/tags, and aborting the upgrade when conflicting authored note text is present. 
- Add helper `compareCreatedThenId` and wire migration steps: version 2 runs the dedupe `upgrade` and version 3 adds a unique compound index. 
- Replace direct `db` construction with `createAppDatabase()` and make `getOrCreateEncounter` transactional, catching `Dexie.ConstraintError` to resolve races and return the winner when duplicates are concurrently inserted. 
- Add comprehensive tests and update repository tests to assert concurrent creation, duplicate-insert prevention, and interaction between completion and note saving. 

### Testing

- Added `tests/databaseMigration.test.ts` covering normal upgrade, deterministic merge, identical-note dedupe, and abort-on-conflict scenarios. 
- Updated `tests/repositories.test.ts` to include concurrency and duplicate-insert assertions for `getOrCreateEncounter` and related flows. 
- Ran unit tests with `vitest` and the modified test suite passed (migration and repository tests succeeded).

body:
## Summary

The navbar on the launch pages (hub `/launch/` and every guide `/launch/<slug>/`) appeared broken: the page rendered **~170–210px wider than the viewport** at every breakpoint, so the page could pan sideways, the sticky navbar no longer spanned the page, a stray horizontal scrollbar appeared, and on mobile the whole page zoomed out.

## Root cause

The decorative glow blobs on `.launch-shell` are positioned outside the shell:

- `.launch-shell::before` — `left: -280px`
- `.launch-shell::after` — `right: -220px`

These overflow the shell's right edge by 220px, which stretched the document width. Verified in headless Chromium: feed/battle/challenges/login are all exactly viewport-width, while `/launch/` and `/launch/vercel-web/` measured 1450px on a 1280px viewport (390px viewport → 598px), matching the blob geometry exactly.

## Fix

Add `overflow-x: clip` to `.launch-shell` in `static/gallery/css/launch.css`.

`clip` trims the decorative blobs at the shell's edge **without** creating a scroll container (unlike `overflow: hidden`), so the sticky guide aside (`top: 86px`) inside `.launch-shell` keeps sticking on guide pages.

## Verification

- [x] `scrollWidth == viewport` on both launch pages at 1280 / 768 / 390px
- [x] Navbar spans the full page, stays at top, no horizontal scroll
- [x] Sticky guide aside still sticks below the navbar (top: 86px)

author: vincentlauriat
body:
## Le problème

Cliquer sur « Enregistrer » dans **Mes voix** fait disparaître l'application. Pas une erreur : le processus est tué.

Le bundle est signé avec le Hardened Runtime (`flags=0x10000(runtime)`) mais ne porte aucun entitlement :

```
$ codesign -d --entitlements - /Applications/VoixLocale.app
Executable=/Applications/VoixLocale.app/Contents/MacOS/VoixLocale
(rien)
```

Sous Hardened Runtime, l'accès au micro exige `com.apple.security.device.audio-input`. Sans lui, macOS tue le processus dès l'appel à `AVCaptureDevice.requestAccess`. Le `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` de l'`Info.plist` est bien présent, mais il ne suffit pas : les deux sont nécessaires.

Le DMG publié dans `docs/` a la même signature, donc le même comportement.

## Les changements

**`scripts/VoixLocale.entitlements`** (nouveau) — uniquement `com.apple.security.device.audio-input`. Volontairement **pas** `com.apple.security.app-sandbox` : l'app lance un backend Python et écrit dans Application Support, le sandbox casserait les deux.

**`scripts/build_app.sh`** — `codesign --options runtime --entitlements …` au lieu de `--force --deep --sign -`. `--deep` est déprécié par Apple et n'applique pas les entitlements aux binaires imbriqués comme on l'attendrait. L'identité reste configurable via `CODESIGN_IDENTITY` (ad-hoc par défaut, donc le comportement actuel est préservé), et le timestamp n'est demandé que pour une vraie identité, puisqu'il ne sert qu'à la notarisation.

**`Sources/VoixLocale/VoiceRecorder.swift`** — `requestAndStart()` appelait `requestAccess` sans consulter l'état courant, et sa branche « refusé » se terminait sur un `errorMessage` sans issue. Désormais un `switch` sur `AVCaptureDevice.authorizationStatus` : `.authorized` démarre, `.notDetermined` demande, `.denied`/`.restricted` proposent une sortie. Ajout d'un `isRequestingAccess` : sans lui, un second clic sur « Enregistrer » pendant que la boîte de dialogue macOS est ouverte relance une demande en parallèle.

**`Sources/VoixLocale/ContentView.swift`** — quand l'accès est refusé, un bandeau avec un bouton qui ouvre directement Réglages Système › Confidentialité et sécurité › Microphone. Avant, un refus était définitif du point de vue de l'utilisateur : aucun moyen de revenir en arrière depuis l'app.

**`scripts/run_dev.sh`** — faisait `swift run`, qui produit un exécutable nu, sans bundle ni `Info.plist`. Le micro y est tué quoi qu'on fasse côté entitlements, donc le mode dev ne pouvait pas enregistrer. Il construit maintenant le `.app` et l'ouvre.

**`README.md`** — une note sur l'entitlement, et sur le fait que macOS met sa décision TCC en cache par bundle ID **et par signature** : après resignature, un refus antérieur persiste, d'où `tccutil reset Microphone fr.voixlocale.app`. J'ai gardé cette commande hors du script de build — un build ne devrait pas modifier les permissions système de la machine.

## Vérifications

```
$ codesign -d --entitlements - --xml dist/VoixLocale.app | plutil -p -
{ "com.apple.security.device.audio-input" => true }

$ spctl -a -t exec -vv /Applications/VoixLocale.app
accepted / source=Developer ID

$ swift test --disable-sandbox
Executed 1 test, with 0 failures
```

Testé de bout en bout sur macOS 26 / Apple Silicon, après `tccutil reset` : la fenêtre d'autorisation macOS apparaît, l'enregistrement se déroule, et une voix de 21 s a été enrôlée sans incident.

Une petite remarque : les deux PR touchent `build_app.sh` et `README.md` à des endroits différents. Si tu merges celle-ci d'abord, l'autre demandera peut-être un rebase trivial — dis-moi, je m'en occupe.

author: lordsunchips
body:
Both iOS docs had drifted. Nine stale claims in DEVICE.md, and a README that documented a file deleted long ago.

## The two that mattered

**`DEVICE.md:36` — "This makes the app hit your Fly URL."** The backend moved to Render. Mostly harmless, since the instruction is right and only the host name is wrong.

**`DEVICE.md:58` — "the free service is cold-starting; first request after ~15 min idle takes ~30s."** This one is actively harmful now. The service is on Starter and doesn't spin down, so it points at a cause that *cannot happen* — while "first request after idle fails" has become a real symptom with a completely different cause: a dropped Turso connection (#13). Troubleshooting aimed at the wrong thing is worse than no troubleshooting.

## Also removed

- The "When it stops working after 7 days" section — provisioning lasts a year on a paid account.
- Manual team-selection steps — `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` is pinned in `project.yml` since #14.
- "Personal Teams sometimes reject generic bundle IDs" — `com.sunchips.muvi` is now explicitly registered.
- "free Render + Turso setup" — Render is Starter now.

## Added

Troubleshooting for what can actually go wrong: how to distinguish a reachable database from an unreachable one. `/health` touches no database, so it stays green during a total database outage — you have to hit a database-backed route, where `401` means healthy and `500` means the database is unreachable. That's the exact signature of the outage we hit.

## README.md

Documented `LoggedInPlaceholderView.swift` as "temporary shell — replaced by library UI in task 7". That file no longer exists, and the layout omitted every feature folder added since: Library, Rank, MovieDetail, AddMovie, Settings, Shared. Replaced with the real tree, plus the Debug/Release backend split — previously stated as an unconditional localhost target, which is only true for Debug.

## Verification

Rather than trusting the prose:

- Every `.swift` file the README lists exists, and no source file is undocumented — checked both directions programmatically.
- The endpoints named match the actual routes in `backend/app/routes/`.
- Both curl commands in DEVICE.md were run against production: `/health` returns the deployed commit, and a bad-credentials login returns `401`, confirming the documented "401 means the database is reachable" reading.

Docs only.

author: alexander-zimmermann
body:
## What happened

PR #6 was merged while three further commits were still on their way to the branch. `main` therefore carries the *intermediate* state of that work:

```
| `mode` | 1, 3 | 1 while targeting a set humidity; 3 reached via the mode button |
```

Both halves of that line are wrong. `mode 1` is *no mode selected*, and Smart is `4`.

## The corrected table

| `mode` | Button pressed |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | no mode selected — also the state the appliance powers on in |
| 2 | Dry clothes — the `dry_clothes` capability |
| 3 | Continuous |
| 4 | Smart — the `auto` capability |

Each value now rests on an observed transition:

```
19:05:06  mode 1  fan 40   power-on state
19:25:16  mode 3  fan 40   "continuous" pressed
19:26:17  mode 2  fan 40   "dry clothes" pressed
19:27:17  mode 4  fan 80   "Smart" pressed
19:29:18  mode 1  fan 80   deselected
```

## Why the wrong version existed at all

Pressing Smart once had left `mode` at 1, and I read that as "already in Smart". The press had simply not registered. An absent change proves nothing — only an observed transition does, and that caution is now in the README so the next reader does not repeat it.

## Also carried over

- `fan_speed` 40/60/80 confirmed complete against the `fan_speed: 7` bitmask
- Smart drives `fan_speed` itself (40 → 80 untouched) and keeps the value after Smart is left, so a speed control fights the appliance in one mode and shows its leftover choice in the others
- `target_humidity` survives a mode change but only acts outside continuous
