author: hylouis233
body:
## What changes

New Plugin `Hylouis233/document-skills` - a Skill-only portable Agent Plugin bundling four original
workbench Skills: `docx`, `pdf`, `pptx`, `xlsx`.

All guidance in this Plugin was written originally for this contribution. It contains no content
from Anthropic's document skills or any other proprietary skill pack - the docx/pdf/pptx/xlsx
names describe the formats, and the patterns are built around standard open-source Python
libraries (python-docx, python-pptx, openpyxl, pypdf, ReportLab, PyMuPDF) and public format
knowledge.

## User value

Users ask agents for document deliverables and get silent corruption: hand-edited ZIP XML that
no viewer opens, pasted values where spreadsheet formulas belong, screenshot-style PDFs with no
extractable text, decks whose text overflows every slide. The four Skills route each task to the
right tool, enforce the container contracts, and - critically - require re-opening and verifying
the artifact before handing it back.

Example prompt:

```text
Use the document-skills plugin: open sales-2024.xlsx, add a sheet "Summary" with per-region
totals computed by formula, a bar chart of the top 5 products, and currency formatting.
```

Expected result: the agent loads the workbook with openpyxl, inspects sheets and headers, writes
real `SUMIF`/`COUNTIF` formulas, adds a native `BarChart`, applies number formats, and reports
the changed ranges plus the verification it ran.

```text
Use the document-skills plugin: create a PDF one-pager "Q3 launch checklist" that fits exactly
one A4 page.
```

Expected result: generated with ReportLab flowables, measured, and verified with pypdf to be
exactly 1 page with extractable text.

Skill inventory (4 Skills, 13 reference files, 1333 lines):

- `docx` - create (python-docx outline + styles + TOC field), edit (two-tier: structural edits
  vs. safe OOXML surgery), read (pandoc / python-docx), review (symptom-driven repair table),
  mandatory postcheck with optional `soffice` PDF smoke test.
- `pdf` - one-tool-per-job routing: ReportLab for creation, PyMuPDF for extraction/inspection,
  pypdf for split/merge/rotate/watermark/encrypt/forms; text-first rule; page-geometry and
  overflow checks in postcheck.
- `pptx` - seven workhorse slide patterns, narrow in-place editing with asserted shape matching,
  real chart parts over chart pictures, text-fit rules, slide-count and render verification.

author: akifgrape
body:
This platform keeps building controls and then not connecting them, and the pattern is **invisible to every signal the repository has**: the code compiles, its own tests pass, `go vet` is clean, and nothing anywhere says the thing never runs.

| | |
|---|---|
| **#74** | `internal/risk/unwind` — could size what a breached portfolio must shed. Built, tested, never called. From outside, a decider nothing invokes is indistinguishable from one that does not work. |
| **#112** | `internal/prediction/registry` — the MLOPS-01a model gate. Its own doc carries the grep proving nobody imports it. |
| **#471** | `internal/validation` — the SR 11-7 gate whose stated purpose is *"no model serves production without recorded, current validation"*. Zero importers, so **every analytic serves production unvalidated**. |

I found #471 by running this audit **by hand**. That is the argument for the test: the audit works, and nobody was running it.

## What it checks

Every package under `internal/` has at least one importer in the module — production *or* test — or an argued exemption naming the **issue** that will wire it.

Six are dark today, and all six are now named:

| package | tracked by |
|---|---|
| `internal/validation` | #471 — SR 11-7 validation gate |
| `internal/prediction/registry` | #112 — MLOPS-01a model registry |
| `internal/collateral` | #408 — COLL-01 margin/financing plane |
| `internal/risk/pricing/credit` | #113 — credit calibrator, unscheduled |
| `internal/risk/termsource` | #345 — contract-terms store |
| `internal/regulatory/stress` | #471 (Source) — CCAR/DFAST framework |

## What it is not, and must not become

**A dead-code check.** The repository has already ruled on deletion, in the registry's own doc:

> Removing it would freeze a documented three-part design permanently at two thirds and turn "wire it" into "rebuild it".

So the remedy for a failure here is a **tracked exemption**, not `rm`. The error message says that explicitly, so nobody reaches for deletion to make it pass.

**Every exemption names an issue.** One that says "not yet" without saying who is tracking it is exactly how a capability stays dark for a year.

**Why importers rather than callers**: an import is what the toolchain can see cheaply and exactly. A package can be imported and still hold a dead function, which this will not catch — but every case above was dark at the *import* level, because that is what "nobody wired it" actually looks like.

## Proof

Both arms mutation-proven:

```
--- FAIL: TestNoInternalCapabilityIsDarkAndUntracked
    1 internal package(s) have NO importer anywhere in the module — not
    production, not test: [internal/darkprobe]

--- FAIL: TestNoInternalCapabilityIsDarkAndUntracked
    exemption for "internal/already/wired" is stale — the package now has an
    importer, or it no longer exists. Delete the entry
```

The probe package **compiled and vetted clean** — which is the whole point.

The dead-entry arm matters more here than usual: it is what turns this from a list that accumulates into one that empties. When somebody finally wires `internal/validation`, the test tells them to delete its exemption.

Gates: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l`, `golangci-lint` (0 issues), full `test/arch` suite green.

author: nealcaren
body:
Closes #741. Closes #740.

Three footguns from the power-user stress test on `load_congress()`, all of which produced wrong or degenerate results **with no error**. Silent-wrong-result footguns are worse than crashes, so these get guarded. All verified to reproduce on 0.55.0.

## Fixes

**1. `LDA` silently accepted `num_topics > vocabulary` (#741).** A K larger than the vocabulary can never form K distinct word distributions, so the surplus topics collapse to empty/degenerate rows — but LDA fit them anyway with no warning, while `NMF` and `CTM` already raise on the same case. LDA now raises up front:

```python
topica.LDA(num_topics=100, seed=13).fit([["a","b"],["b","c"],["a","c"]], iters=20)
# ValueError: num_topics (100) exceeds the vocabulary size (3): there are not
# enough distinct word types to form that many topics ...
```
`num_topics == vocab` is still allowed. The spectral-init fallback test is retargeted to a valid `K == vocab` degenerate corpus (identical docs → no K independent anchors → `spectral_init` returns `None` → random-init fallback), since `K > vocab` is now rejected before init.

**2. `bootstrap_stability(fit_kwargs=...)` crashed (#740).** The docstring documented a `fit_kwargs` parameter, but the signature was `**fit_kwargs`, so the documented dict form raised `TypeError: LDA.fit() got an unexpected keyword argument 'fit_kwargs'`. There is now a real `fit_kwargs=` dict param (matching `cross_validate`), merged with any inline keywords (inline wins on a clash) — so both `fit_kwargs={"iters": 500}` and inline `iters=500` work.

**3. `bootstrap_stability` silently ignored `k=` when `model_factory=` was given (#740).** The factory owns the topic count and its single argument is the **seed**, not `k`, so `model_factory=lambda k: LDA(k)` built `LDA(num_topics=seed)` — the wrong K, no warning. It now warns when both `k=` and `model_factory=` are passed, and the docstring states the factory argument is the seed.

## Tests
- `test_lda_rejects_num_topics_over_vocab` — K>vocab raises; K==vocab fits.
- `test_bootstrap_stability_fit_kwargs_dict_and_inline_merge` — dict and inline forms both work and agree.
- `test_bootstrap_stability_warns_on_k_with_model_factory` — the silent-k warning fires.
- `test_spectral_falls_back_on_tiny_corpus` retargeted to a valid corpus.

## Gates
- Full `pytest`: **4933 passed, 38 skipped, 0 failed**.
- `cargo test --lib`: **340 passed**.
- `scripts/preflight.sh` (fmt, clippy, stub-sync, model tables): green.

author: julianaliliansouza
body:
Regressao silenciosa em producao, encontrada sondando a API real com o token
do Monte 33 — nao a documentacao.

A Meta depreciou um bloco de metricas organicas em 15/06/2026. Entre elas,
post_impressions_unique, que o MetaInsightsService pedia.

O estrago foi maior que uma metrica: fetchFacebookPostInsights() pedia as
quatro num bloco so (implode), e a Graph API rejeita a chamada INTEIRA quando
uma das metricas nao existe. Resultado: todo post de Facebook sincronizado
desde junho gravou

    alcance       -> null
    impressoes    -> null
    visualizacoes -> null
    engagements   -> 0

Sobreviveram apenas curtidas, comentarios e compartilhamentos, que vem do
objeto do post e nao do /insights. Nunca apareceu como erro porque o catch
gera so Log::warning.

Sondagem, uma metrica por vez, contra a API de producao:

    MORTAS  post_impressions, post_impressions_unique,
            page_impressions, page_impressions_unique, page_fans
    VIVAS   post_clicks, post_engagements, post_video_views,
            post_video_views_unique, post_reactions_like_total,
            post_activity_by_action_type, page_post_engagements,
            page_follows, page_views_total

Nao ha substituto para alcance/impressoes de post. Testados e inexistentes:
views, total_views, post_impressions_organic, post_impressions_organic_unique,
post_impressions_paid. O numero acabou.

O que muda:

1. post_impressions_unique sai da lista.

2. alcance e impressoes viram null EXPLICITO, com o motivo no comentario.
   Melhor campo vazio e honesto do que zero que parece medicao. O painel
   precisa parar de prometer esse numero — isso e trabalho de frontend, em
   separado.

3. fetchFacebookPostInsights() fica resistente a depreciacao: tenta em bloco
   (1 chamada, caso normal) e, se o bloco falhar, refaz metrica por metrica e
   fica com o que responder. Custa N chamadas apenas no dia em que algo
   quebra, e o log passa a dizer QUAL metrica morreu em vez de sumir com
   todas. A Meta vai depreciar de novo; da proxima vez nao derruba as outras.

page_fans ja estava tratado no codigo via followers_count — alguem ja passou
por isso antes.

Levantamento completo em claude/META_API_ESTADO_REAL.md.

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

Per the 2026-08-14 operator ruling on #12 (unparked as engineering, with a guardrail), this validates DR-0005's open ESD/capacitance tension as a measurement study on the real pad cell from #2 (`layout/gds/gf180_tmds_pad_min.gds` — a grounded-gate NMOS clamp, not the diode primitives DR-0005's original text named).

- **Sizing interpretation and model-card mapping stated first** (`nfet` → `nfet_03v3`, gate length grown to the `ESD.pl` 0.8 µm floor) — see `design/esd-capacitance-budget.md` §1.
- **ESD sizing** (design-margin estimate, not qualification): JEDEC JS-001 HBM network (100 pF/1500 Ω) implies a 1.333 A peak current at 2 kV; using a commonly cited (PDK-silent, explicitly marked unsourced) 2–6 mA/µm failure-current-density range for a salicided GGNMOS gives a 222–667 µm required clamp width. CDM is treated qualitatively (turn-on/di-dt requirement; PDK has zero snapback/trigger data — "the source is silent" is reported as the finding, not worked around).
- **Clamp capacitance measured**, not estimated: `sim/esd-clamp-cv` (new testbench + full PVT-matrix record `20260814-193222-dd48630`, 45/45 points ok, `mos` corner set × −40/27/125 °C × ±10 % supply — the same subset convention `sim/cml-driver-eye`'s #11 record already used). Both 0 V and the DR-0002/DR-0006 operating-bias point are reported; the doc states explicitly which one the budget is graded on (operating bias) and why.
- **Pad parasitic measured two ways**: `klt extract --parasitics` (a real capability that has since shipped — `2AMLogic/klayout-tools#217` — correcting the issue's own inherited "not available" framing) gives 0.146 fF for the literal drawn via-landing pad; a PDK-cited analytic estimate (`libs.tech/magic/gf180mcuD.tech`'s own `defaultareacap`/`defaultperimeter` coefficients, cross-validated against the `klt`-extracted number to within 0.3 %) gives 6.4–7.1 pF for a realistic 25×25 µm bond pad (the PDK's own established bond-pad-opening size).

**Verdict: the ESD side is easy — a clamp sized past 2 kV HBM costs well under 1 pF at every PVT corner. The budget is closed, decisively, by the pad's own parasitic capacitance once any realistic bond-pad size is used (>3× the entire 2 pF budget on its own), not by clamp sizing.** This is a materially different finding than DR-0005's original clamp-vs-capacitance framing anticipated.

## Guardrail compliance (hard constraint)

**No file under `spec/` is touched by this PR** (`git diff --stat origin/main -- spec/` is empty). Per the operator's explicit guardrail, this "no intersection under a realistic pad-size assumption" verdict is reported here with its full evidence rather than used to revise DR-0005 or open a new decision-record issue. **This needs to go back to the operator** — the pad-vs-clamp trade-off this finding implies (DR-0005's ≤2 pF figure may need to be revisited against what a real bond pad actually costs, independent of any ESD-clamp sizing trade-off) is a call for the operator, not this PR.

## klt / friction protocol notes

- `klt drc`'s `ESD.*` rule coverage and `klt extract`'s diode-device-class gap are restated from `spec/pad-ring-esd-survey.md` §5/§7, citing the already-filed `2AMLogic/klayout-tools#541` rather than re-filing.
- `klt extract --parasitics` (`2AMLogic/klayout-tools#217`) is a first-order lumped-RC estimate, appropriate for the cross-check use here but not signoff-grade, and only measures geometry that is actually drawn (hence the analytic estimate for the realistic-pad-size case). No new tool gap was found, so no new issue is filed.

## Environment note (repo-infra, not this PR's content)

This session's default `gh`/git credential (installation token, no `.loom/tokens/` pool provisioned for this repo yet) had no write access to `2AMLogic/gf180-tmds-tx` — push and this PR creation both used the operator's own authenticated `gh`/git session (`GH_CONFIG_DIR` unset) per the dispatch instructions. Flagging again per the Curator's prior note so the token pool gets provisioned for this repo.

## Test plan

- [x] `sim/esd-clamp-cv` PVT-matrix run: 45/45 points `ok` (`python3 sim/run_corners.py esd-clamp-cv -j 8`)
- [x] `python3 sim/check_records.py --require-append-only` passes (append-only clean, all 3 records well-formed)
- [x] `bash .github/scripts/lint.sh --require-append-only` passes (shellcheck, python syntax, JSON, evidence lint)
- [x] `python3 -m pytest sim/tests -q` — 70 passed, 255 subtests passed
- [x] `git diff --stat origin/main -- spec/` empty — no spec/ changes under any outcome

Closes #12

body:
Cierra 4 de los 6 endpoints de CxP que faltaban de 29.7. **18 de 22 endpoints** del modulo de compras.

## Endpoints

- `GET /supplier-invoices` (paginado, filtro por status)
- `POST /supplier-invoices`
- `POST /supplier-invoices/{uuid}/match`
- `POST /supplier-invoices/{uuid}/pay`
- `GET /suppliers/{uuid}/balance`

## Decisiones de alcance

**match() concilia contra lo RECIBIDO, no contra lo pedido.** Una OC recibida parcialmente factura menos que su total; comparar contra el total daria un 422 falso. No concilia linea a linea porque el maestro no define tabla de lineas de factura, solo totales (4541-4577). Facturado <= recibido pasa, el exceso es 422: mismo criterio que `receive()` con las cantidades.

**pay() deriva el status de paid_amount** (0 pending, < total partial, = total paid). No hay maquina de estados: el status es funcion pura del importe pagado, para evitar dos fuentes de verdad. Sobrepago 422, pagar una saldada 409.

**Divergencias con el maestro, documentadas en la migracion 000050:**
- `decimal(18,4)` en vez de `NUMERIC(14,2)`, para comparar sin redondeos contra `purchase_order_items`.
- Sin `bank_account_id`: la tabla `bank_accounts` no existe en el repo ni la define el maestro.
- Sin columna `balance` generada: ninguna migracion del repo usa `storedAs`. Se calcula al vuelo.

**Permisos:** `SUPPLIER_INVOICE_PAY` va separado de CREATE y fuera de `operations()`. Quien registra la deuda no la liquida, mismo criterio que APPROVE en las OCs (CU-COM-002). Explicito en ADMIN porque ese rol se compone por spread de los tres metodos.

## Corrige un hallazgo en codigo ya entregado (#34)

`nextFolio()` de `PurchaseOrderService` derivaba el numero de `max('id')`, que es la secuencia **global** de la tabla, no un consecutivo por tenant. Con varios tenants activos los folios saltaban (`OC-000001` -> `OC-000015`). No producia duplicados (el unique lo impide) pero si huecos, que anulan el control de auditoria que justifica numerar.

El test existente asertaba `toStartWith('OC-')`: solo mira el prefijo, nunca habria detectado el salto. Se agrega test de regresion que compara dos folios consecutivos.

## Verificacion

- Suite: **649 passed (2091 assertions)**, +13 respecto a main.
- Pint: **PASS 402 files**.
- `migrate` -> `rollback` -> `migrate` de la 000050, en el PR anterior de esta rama.

## Pendiente

`GET /suppliers/{uuid}/products` va en su propia entrega. `purchase-receipts` (3 endpoints) sigue fuera de alcance; su criterio de reapertura era revisarlo despues de este PR, porque `match` mostraria que forma necesita una recepcion para ser conciliable. **Dato para esa revision: conciliamos por totales, no por lineas.**

author: nicolasalt
body:
## Summary

A repository added as `https://x-access-token:<pat>@github.com/o/r.git` had that token stored verbatim and written into every session clone's `remote.origin.url` — i.e. into `/project/.git/config`, which the agent, every plugin companion CLI, and every future plugin service can read. That is a direct violation of docs/262 requirement 19: a credential is never **persisted** to reach a repository, ShipIt supplies fetch credentials through a credential helper scoped to that remote for the life of the fetch, and **a credential a user happens to type into a repository URL is not kept either**. This strips the credential at every point one can enter or be written, sweeps everything an existing installation already has keyed by that URL, and adds the guard tests whose absence is why the violation stayed open.

> **`docs/262-plugins/checklist.md` is deliberately untouched by this PR.** It is the one file every slice of this feature edits, so a checklist edit is a guaranteed conflict with every concurrent sibling and a PR body conflicts with nothing. The orchestrating session owns that file and folds this record in after merge — which is why the full account of the defect, the fix and the accepted cost lives here rather than there.

## Rationale

**Why no existing test caught it.** Every plugin guard test asserts a container's mounts, environment and network. This credential arrives *inside* a file the mount is supposed to carry, so no mount/env/network assertion can see it. The new guard therefore reads the config file itself, after the real clone path — `repo-git.test.ts` → "no credential is recorded in a git config".

**Why strip-on-add alone is not enough.** Three depths were each independently reachable:

- the entry point — `addRepo`, the URL the user types;
- the two stores that persist a URL — and `RepoStore` had to key **every** method by the stripped URL, not just `add`. Stripping only in `add` stores the clean URL and then leaves `setReady` / `setWarmSessionId` / `get` addressing a row that never existed, which is a repo stuck at status `cloning` forever. `SessionManager.setRemoteUrl` is also written back *from an existing workspace's own origin*, so a legacy checkout could otherwise feed a credential straight back into the DB;
- every write of a remote into a git config — `RepoGit.clone` / `cloneBare` / `setRemoteUrl` / `cloneFromCache`, the fork path, and `setGitRemote`, the one place a user hands ShipIt an arbitrary remote string and it lands in `/project/.git/config` directly.

**What the independent review changed, and the shape of it.** Five further gaps, all reproduced at the source, all in one direction: *the first fix cleaned the key and left everything else keyed by it.*

- **Warm sessions were skipped** — `listAll` filters `warm = 0`, and a warm row is a real checkout the next claim hands to a user. Now `listAllIncludingWarm`.
- **`secrets.repo_url` IS the raw URL** — scrubbing without a re-key both left a credential in the secrets table and silently disconnected the user's saved service and plugin secrets from their repository. `SecretStore.scrubCredentialedRepoUrls` moves them; a key re-entered under the clean URL since wins.
- **Every per-repo directory is named after a hash of that URL** — bare cache, dep cache, and the agent's accumulated per-repo memory. The sweep now carries them across. Since `repoUrlToHash` hashes the *stripped* URL (so a caller still holding the credentialed spelling cannot address a second cache), finding the old directory needs the historical rule, which `startup-tasks.ts` keeps as its own inlined copy — the same reason `sessions.ts` inlines the docs/252 rule: a migration must reproduce a historical layout forever.
- **A distinct credentialed `pushurl`** survived a fetch-only rewrite. `--push` is now passed, and only for a genuinely distinct URL, so a remote without one does not gain a `pushurl` line.
- **The duplicate-row case now merges rather than deletes.** The realistic legacy order has the credentialed row as the trusted, ready, warm-linked one and the clean row as a later untouched shell, so dropping the first silently un-trusted the repository. Trust and readiness win if either row has them; nullable columns fill the survivor's holes.

A sixth finding **widened the strip itself**: `stripUrlCredentials` handles only http(s) userinfo by design, so `?access_token=pw` and `ssh://git:pw@…` were still persisted verbatim by `setGitRemote`. Persistence now uses a separate, stronger `stripRemoteUrlCredentials` — http(s) userinfo, a password in *any* scheme (the ssh **user** stays: `git@` is a login, not a secret), and query/fragment dropped wholesale, which is the judgement `sanitizeRemoteUrlForInventory` already makes. `stripUrlCredentials` is left exactly as it was for display, redaction and the identity key.

**Accepted cost, recorded with the requirement and not re-litigated here:** a remote whose ONLY working auth is an embedded URL credential stops working on the helper path — it degrades to an anonymous fetch. That is now legible **in ShipIt** and not only in the orchestrator's stdout (§1/§2): when the add-repo clone fails and the URL carried a credential, the SSE error says the credential was not stored and names what to do instead. No fallback that keeps the credential was added, because that fallback is what req 19 forbids.

**Limits stated rather than closed:** a per-repo directory is carried across only when the destination does not already exist — where both spellings have one, the clean one is authoritative and the stale twin is left for the ordinary disk sweeps, because merging two caches is not something a boot sweep can do safely. And an scp-style remote (`tok@host:o/r.git`) is still persisted as typed: it does not parse as a URL, and a token pasted where the ssh login goes cannot be told apart from one.

## Changes

- **Entry point** — `services/repos.ts:addRepo` strips a credential typed into the Add-repo field and warns, naming the consequence.
- **Stores** — `repo-store.ts` keys every URL-taking method through a private `key()`, and `scrubCredentialedUrls()` re-keys (merging on collision) and reports each `{from, to}`. `sessions.ts:setRemoteUrl` stores the column credential-free. `secret-store.ts:scrubCredentialedRepoUrls()` re-keys stored secrets.
- **Git-config boundary** — `repo-git.ts` routes `clone`, `cloneBare`, `setRemoteUrl` and `cloneFromCache` through `credentialFreeRemote()`; `services/git.ts:setGitRemote` and `services/session-fork-merge.ts` strip before writing a session clone's config.
- **Legacy sweep** — `startup-tasks.ts:runRemoteCredentialScrub` cleans repo rows, session rows (warm included), each checkout's `.git/config` (fetch *and* push URLs, working tree or bare), stored secrets, and the per-repo directories — wired in `bootstrap-managers.ts` ahead of `runRepoMigration`, with `bareCacheRoot`/`depCacheRoot` exported from `session-dir-factory.ts` so those directories can be addressed by hash. Boot-only and idempotent: a clean installation reads a few small queries and one file per session and rewrites nothing, and an affected one converges in a single restart.
- **Helpers** — `git-utils.ts:stripRemoteUrlCredentials` (the persistence-strength strip) and `hasUrlCredentials` (defined as "the strip changes it", so detector and remedy cannot disagree); `repoUrlToHash` hashes the stripped URL.
- **Legibility** — `api-routes-session-repos.ts` explains the stripped credential in the SSE error when the clone then fails.
- **Tests** — the config guard (`repo-git.test.ts`, including an isolated `cloneBare` probe against a real server that asserts git offered no `Authorization`), the legacy sweep in all its cases (`startup-tasks.test.ts`), the user-typed path (new `services/git.test.ts`), the strip's shapes and the hash (`git-utils.test.ts`), the store's one-row identity (`repo-store.test.ts`), the entry point (`services/repos.test.ts`), the session column (`sessions.

author: vandyckmed-droid
body:
Removes the MOM/BLEND momentum pipeline entirely and replaces it with one modular, reader-configurable scoring system computed in the app at view time.

## The formula system

- **Lookback**: 63 / 126 / 189 / 252 trading days — one window, or a 50/50 blend of two
- **Skip toggle**: excludes the most recent round(lookback/12) sessions (5 / 10 / 16 / 21)
- **Base measure**: mean daily log return over the scoring window
- **Volatility toggle**: divides by the daily volatility of the same window
- **Market residual toggle**: beta vs VTI estimated over the 504 sessions ending at the window's cutoff; scores `return − β·VTI`
- **Sector residual toggle**: two-factor VTI + SPDR sector-fund regression over the same estimation stretch; scores what neither factor explains
- **Default**: `0.5·score(12M, skip 21) + 0.5·score(6M, skip 10)`, vol-adjusted, market-residual, sector residual off

Every setting change re-scores and re-ranks immediately; ranks are always recomputed against the rows on screen, as before.

## What changed where

- **`scripts/build_snapshot.py`**: all MOM/BLEND constants, functions, fields and metadata removed. The pipeline now publishes `benchmarks` (VTI + one SPDR fund per sector, aligned to the shared calendar) in every table at schema 3, with validation that they exist and stay in step with the calendar.
- **`scripts/remetric.py`**: replays the remaining derived metrics, strips the retired mom/blend fields, and gained `--fetch-benchmarks` (13 requests) to attach the factor series to committed data without a full refetch. `data/` was migrated in place with it — same data date (2026-08-13).
- **`web/index.template.html`**: new scoring engine (log-returns cache, OLS betas with 252-observation minimum, all-or-nothing windows) plus a formula-builder sheet behind the ƒ chip. MOM bars, BLEND section, and all related prose/visualizations removed; the charts' grey blind-spot tail now follows the active skip. The formula persists in `localStorage` like the watchlist.
- **`CLAUDE.md` / `README.md`**: invariants and docs rewritten for the new system.

## Verification

- JS engine cross-checked against an independent Python implementation of the spec: exact match (< 1e-12) across 6 configurations × 6 symbols
- Playwright run on the built page: 300 rows scored (297 non-null; the 3 young listings correctly null), toggles re-rank live and match engine-predicted orderings, market toggle locks while sector residual is on, zero console errors
- `remetric.py --check` and full validation pass on all 12 tables

author: proggeramlug
body:
Closes #8092 (the `lint` half).

## Why

Three `lint` steps fail on a **pristine `origin/main` checkout**. `lint` is a required status context, so while that holds it cannot distinguish a good pull request from a bad one, and every merge goes through admin bypass. That is the CLAUDE.md "four ways a gate can be unable to fail" pattern in its most expensive form: the job runs, genuinely reports failure, is required, and therefore trains everyone to ignore it — including for the PR that actually broke something.

Reproduced on a clean detached worktree at `506f4ab11`:

```
check_file_size.sh          2010  crates/perry-runtime/src/timer.rs        (cap 2000)
gc_store_site_inventory.py  property_set.rs:1475 raw generated heap/global store
raw_handle_debt.py          json_tape.rs 22 > ceiling 21
                            object/spill.rs 5 > ceiling 3
```

None of these belongs to any open PR.

## What changed

**`timer.rs` 2010 → 1866.** Its `#[cfg(test)]` scanner seeding/snapshot helpers move to `timer/test_scanner_support.rs`. Re-exported **by name**, not by glob — the call sites are `crate::timer::test_…` in the GC root-scanner tests, and a glob does not propagate through that.

**`property_set.rs` marker relocated.** This store already had a `GC_STORE_AUDIT(POINTER_FREE)` marker; a multi-line `canonicalize_raw_f64_numeric_store_value` call had pushed it 8 lines above the store, outside the inventory's ±6-line window. The marker moves against the store it describes. **Nothing about what is stored or barriered changes** — this is the annotation catching up to a refactor, not a new safety claim.

**Three raw-handle reads converted, no ceiling raised.** `raw_handle_debt_files.txt` is explicit that adding or raising a line is not the fix ("*the honest move is to convert a pair elsewhere and say so in the PR, not to add a line here*"), and `--no-raise-vs` enforces it. So:

- `spill.rs`: across `object_meta_ensure`, and across `js_array_alloc_with_length_exact` (5 → 3, its ceiling).
- `json_tape.rs`: across the `LazyArrayRooted` safepoint (22 → 21, its ceiling).

All three already rooted the pointer and reloaded it afterwards, so this is the same discipline in the form the ratchet can count. `across_mut` additionally makes the pre-call address unnameable, which is the property the manual form cannot enforce.

Baseline 998 → 993. `--update` also tightened three ceilings carrying pre-existing slack — `object_ops/define_property.rs` 3→2, `reflect_support.rs` 4→3, `string/split.rs` 10→7. I checked: no open PR touches those files, so no collateral red. Say the word if you would rather I leave that slack alone.

## Validation

```
./scripts/check_file_size.sh                              OK: no Rust source files exceed 2000 lines
python3 scripts/gc_store_site_inventory.py --self-test    ok
python3 scripts/gc_store_site_inventory.py                passed (1430 files, 286 audited, 90 allowlisted)
python3 scripts/raw_handle_debt.py --self-test            ok
python3 scripts/raw_handle_debt.py                        993 (baseline 993); 110 modules within ceilings
python3 scripts/raw_handle_debt.py --no-raise-vs main     998 -> 993, none raised
cargo check --tests -p perry-runtime                      exit 0
cargo test -p perry-runtime --lib                         2331 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored
```

**The `--tests` check is sabotage-verified**, because the entire `timer.rs` change is `#[cfg(test)]` and a plain `cargo check` would not compile a line of it. Planting a type error in the moved file gives exit 101 with the error attributed to `timer/test_scanner_support.rs:153`, and `Checking perry-runtime` appears exactly once in the log — so the green run compiled the moved module rather than skipping it. Restored and re-verified with a real recompile, not a `git checkout`.

## Expect the rest of CI to stay red

Twelve other contexts — `cargo-test`, `gc-stress`, `ext-link`, `compiler-output-regression`, `e2e-scoped`, both ELF `native-roots-rs4gc` arms, `windows-arm64-build` and others — fail identically on unrelated PRs and are **not** addressed here. They are catalogued in #8092. `cargo-test` in particular fails on the same four `native_emit`/`inprocess` byte-identity tests on every PR I checked, where the only observable delta between the two arms is the embedded translation-unit name.

**The signal to look for on this PR is `lint` going green.** No version bump, no manifest or lockfile change.

Confidence: HIGH Fix confidence is a rating derived from an internal benchmark and includes High, Medium, and Low confidence fixes. It comprises three weighted scores reflecting the safety, effectiveness and cleanliness of Pixee's code changes within a fix. [View Details in Pixee.](https://app.pixee.ai/scans/0534ea03-7f77-49e2-a589-b86860b30b54?fix-finding-id=AaAByorrzUBWdThLjdVc)
--- ## Remediation This change fixes finding AaAByorrzUBWdThLjdVc. ## Details Prevent Command Injection in cmd_lab3 ## Summary Prevent Command Injection in cmd_lab3 ## Vulnerability Description Command Injection occurs when an application passes attacker-controlled data into a system command without strict validation or safe process invocation. This is dangerous because an attacker can append shell metacharacters or additional commands and cause the server to execute unintended operations. Successful exploitation can lead to data exposure, arbitrary code execution, or full host compromise. ## Changes Made The `cmd_lab3` view in `introduction/other_views.py` previously built `nslookup` and `dig` commands by formatting the user-supplied `domain` directly into a command string and executing it through `subprocess.Popen`, which created a command-injection sink. The fix added a strict regular-expression allowlist for `domain` and returns `Invalid domain` when the input does not match a valid hostname pattern. It also changed the command invocation to pass `['nslookup', domain]` or `['dig', domain]` as an argument list and removed `shell=True`, so the lookup utility now receives the domain as data instead of executable shell input. ## Guidance Adherence **Source**: Pixee Knowledge Base Applied the following guidance from the remediation instructions: - **Prevent command injection vulnerabilities by sanitizing inputs and/or validating user input**: Added a strict `re.fullmatch(...)` domain whitelist and early return with `"Invalid domain"` before command construction, which blocks malicious command content as specified in the guidance. - **Avoid constructing the OS command from user-controlled data**: Replaced string formatting (`"nslookup {}".format(domain)` / `"dig {}".format(domain)`) with argument lists (`["nslookup", domain]` / `["dig", domain]`), which prevents shell parsing of injected metacharacters. - **Remove shell-based execution**: Deleted `shell=True` from `subprocess.Popen`, aligning with the guidance’s command-injection remediation by avoiding a shell entirely. No specific preferred library/framework, coding style convention, or new dependency was mandated by the guidance, so those criteria pass by default. The fix is aligned with the security guidance and does not require manifest changes.

body:
Die Entwicklung konzentriert sich auf die nativen Apps: Android und iOS, jeweils Telefon und Uhr. Damit fällt `web/` weg — Spiellogik, Renderer, Chiptune-Synthese, Service Worker, Tests und Icons, rund 3000 Zeilen JavaScript.

Der letzte funktionierende Stand ist der Commit `b4ed73f`:

```sh
git checkout b4ed73f -- web/
```

(Ein Tag `v2.22-mit-pwa` wäre die schönere Form gewesen — der Agent-Proxy dieser Session darf aber nur auf den Arbeits-Branch pushen, keine Tags. Nachträglich: `git tag -a v2.22-mit-pwa b4ed73f -m "…" && git push origin v2.22-mit-pwa`.)

## Was unter der Domain bleiben musste

Zwei Dateien hingen an der laufenden Android-App und wären beim naiven Löschen mitgegangen:

- **Die Datenschutzerklärung.** `docs/index.html` liegt weiterhin unter `/datenschutz/` — genau diese URL steht im Play-Eintrag, und ein toter Datenschutz-Link kann den Eintrag kosten. Dieselbe Seite liegt jetzt zusätzlich auf der Wurzel, damit `dottie.robinrehbein.de` nicht mit einem 404 antwortet.
- **`app-ads.txt`** ist von `web/` nach `docs/` gewandert. Sie trägt die echte AdMob-Publisher-ID; ohne sie fällt die Verkäufer-Verifikation und damit ein Teil der Anzeigen-Nachfrage weg.

`deploy-pages.yml` baut die Site jetzt aus `docs/` statt aus `web/` und läuft nur noch bei Änderungen dort. Die `CNAME`-Zeile bleibt drin — ohne sie wäre die eigene Domain nach dem nächsten Deployment weg. `web-tests.yml` und `store/generate_web_icons.py` entfallen ersatzlos.

## Der Paritäts-Vertrag verliert einen Leser, nicht seinen Zweck

Er gilt jetzt zwischen `:core` und dem Swift-Port — und **jeder** Abschnitt gilt für beide Seiten. Die bisherige Ausnahme für `rng.*` und `trace.*` war nur nötig, weil der Web-Port Kotlins XorWow-Generator bewusst nicht nachbaute.

Die Vektoren selbst ändern sich nicht: Im Diff von `parity/golden-vectors.txt` stehen ausschließlich Kommentarzeilen.

## Dokumentation

README, `ios/README.md`, `ARCHITEKTUR.md`, `PUBLISHING.md` und `parity/README.md` nachgezogen — inklusive der Stellen, an denen die PWA als kostenloser Verteilweg auf iPhones beschrieben war. In `ARCHITEKTUR.md` ist Option B (Kotlin/JS für die PWA) damit hinfällig; Option A ist im selben Zug **billiger** geworden, weil nur noch ein Port nachzuziehen wäre.

## Geprüft

`:core:test`, `testDebugUnitTest` und `assembleDebug` grün, Swift-Syntax geprüft, alle drei Workflow-Dateien parsen. Der iOS-Lauf startet mit diesem Push.

body:
# Integration Health Foundation

## Resumo

Este PR implementa a primeira camada de **Integration Health** do Partsec One Portal.

O objetivo é separar claramente:

* estado administrativo/configuracional da integração;
* saúde operacional;
* atividade atual do pipeline de sincronização.

A implementação utiliza exclusivamente dados já persistidos no PostgreSQL através de `IntegrationSyncLog`, sem executar probes live contra Zabbix, SIEM ou outros sistemas durante a renderização das páginas.

A primeira versão cobre:

* Zabbix;
* SIEM Agents;
* SIEM Vulnerabilities;
* Central de Suporte como integração ainda não monitorada operacionalmente.

---

## Separação entre configuração, health e atividade

`IntegrationConfig.status` continua representando o estado administrativo da integração:

```text
ACTIVE
INACTIVE
ERROR
```

Esse campo não é alterado automaticamente pelos processos de sincronização.

A saúde operacional é calculada separadamente:

```text
INACTIVE
UNKNOWN
HEALTHY
STALE
DEGRADED
ERROR
UNMONITORED
```

A atividade corrente do pipeline também é independente:

```text
IDLE
RUNNING
STUCK
```

Isso permite representar situações como:

```text
health   = HEALTHY
activity = RUNNING
```

sem transformar uma sincronização normal em uma falsa mudança de health.

---

## IntegrationSyncKind

Os logs de sincronização já utilizavam:

```text
integrationType = ZABBIX
integrationType = WAZUH
```

Porém os dois pipelines do SIEM compartilhavam `integrationType = WAZUH`, tornando impossível diferenciar estruturalmente logs de:

```text
SIEM Agents
SIEM Vulnerabilities
```

Foi introduzido:

```prisma
enum IntegrationSyncKind {
  ZABBIX_SNAPSHOT
  SIEM_AGENTS
  SIEM_VULNERABILITIES
}
```

e o campo nullable:

```prisma
syncKind IntegrationSyncKind?
```

em `IntegrationSyncLog`.

O campo é definido somente na criação do log `RUNNING`.

Os updates posteriores para `SUCCESS` ou `ERROR` não alteram `syncKind`.

---

## Compatibilidade com histórico

Não foi realizado backfill.

Logs históricos de Zabbix com:

```text
integrationType = ZABBIX
syncKind = null
```

continuam sendo considerados porque historicamente existiu apenas um pipeline Zabbix.

Logs históricos do SIEM com:

```text
integrationType = WAZUH
syncKind = null
```

não são atribuídos a Agents ou Vulnerabilities, pois são estruturalmente ambíguos.

Nenhuma inferência é feita através do conteúdo de `message`.

---

## Migration

Foi criada a migration:

```text
20260814180000_add_integration_sync_kind
```

Ela adiciona:

```text
IntegrationSyncKind enum
syncKind nullable
índice composto para consultas de health
```

A migration é exclusivamente aditiva.

Não há backfill nem alteração destrutiva.

A migration não foi aplicada manualmente em nenhum banco durante o desenvolvimento deste PR.

---

## Health por pipeline

Cada pipeline utiliza três sinais independentes:

```text
latestAttempt
latestSuccess
latestError
```

`latestAttempt` representa a execução iniciada mais recentemente.

`latestSuccess` e `latestError` representam os eventos concluídos mais recentemente, ordenados por `finishedAt`, com `startedAt` como desempate/fallback.

O health não depende exclusivamente do último row existente.

Exemplo:

```text
10:00 SUCCESS
10:15 ERROR
```

resulta em:

```text
health = ERROR
lastSuccessAt = 10:00
lastErrorAt = 10:15
```

preservando contexto para diagnóstico.

---

## Freshness e STUCK

Os thresholds foram definidos com base na cadência real dos jobs em produção.

### Zabbix

```text
cron:       5 minutos
staleAfter: 15 minutos
stuckAfter: 10 minutos
```

### SIEM Agents

```text
cron:       5 minutos
staleAfter: 15 minutos
stuckAfter: 10 minutos
```

### SIEM Vulnerabilities

```text
cron:       30 minutos
staleAfter: 90 minutos
stuckAfter: 60 minutos
```

As regras de boundary são explícitas:

```text
age == staleAfter → HEALTHY
age >  staleAfter → STALE

age == stuckAfter → RUNNING
age >  stuckAfter → STUCK
```

Um `RUNNING` considerado travado não é alterado no banco.

A condição é interpretada somente em tempo de leitura:

```text
activity = STUCK
health   = ERROR
```

---

## SIEM composto

O SIEM é tratado como integração composta:

```text
SIEM
├── Agents
└── Vulnerabilities
```

Cada componente possui health e activity próprios.

O health agregado é calculado por regra explícita, sem framework genérico de ranking.

Exemplos:

```text
HEALTHY + HEALTHY → HEALTHY

HEALTHY + STALE   → DEGRADED
HEALTHY + ERROR   → DEGRADED
HEALTHY + UNKNOWN → DEGRADED

ERROR + ERROR     → ERROR

UNKNOWN + UNKNOWN → UNKNOWN
```

A atividade agregada segue:

```text
qualquer STUCK   → STUCK
senão RUNNING    → RUNNING
senão            → IDLE
```

O detalhe de Agents e Vulnerabilities permanece disponível separadamente na UI administrativa.

---

## Central de Suporte

Ainda não existe pipeline de sincronização operacional para a Central de Suporte.

Por isso:

```text
configuration = ACTIVE
→ health = UNMONITORED
```

A integração nunca é marcada como `HEALTHY` apenas por estar configurada como ativa.

---

## Segurança e tenant isolation

Foi adicionada:

```ts
getAdminTenantIntegrationHealth(tenantSlug)
```

A query:

1. executa `requirePartsecAdmin()`;
2. somente depois resolve o tenant pelo slug;
3. utiliza internamente o `tenantId` encontrado no banco;
4. consulta apenas logs pertencentes ao tenant resolvido.

A página administrativa também passou a aguardar a autorização antes de carregar os demais dados do tenant.

Nenhum `tenantId` fornecido pelo caller é utilizado como prova de ownership.

---

## UI administrativa

A página:

```text
/admin/tenants/[slug]/integrations
```

agora diferencia visualmente:

```text
Configuração
Saúde operacional
Atividade
```

São exibidos:

```text
última tentativa
último sucesso
último erro
duração
mensagem diagnóstica
```

Para o SIEM, também são exibidos subpainéis separados de:

```text
Agentes
Vulnerabilidades
```

Nenhuma chamada live ao Zabbix ou SIEM é realizada durante a renderização.

A fonte continua sendo exclusivamente o PostgreSQL.

---

## Testes

Foram adicionados testes unitários puros para a policy de Integration Health.

A cobertura inclui:

```text
configuration INACTIVE
configuration ERROR
sem histórico
SUCCESS recente
SUCCESS stale
ERROR após sucesso
RUNNING
STUCK
boundaries exatos
status desconhecido fail-closed
Central de Suporte UNMONITORED
todos os 16 pares da matriz SIEM
activity composta do SIEM
```

Resultado:

```text
55 tests
55 passed
0 failed
```

---

## Validação

Executado com sucesso:

```text
npx prisma format
npx prisma validate
npm test
npm run lint
npm run build
git diff --check
```

Resultado:

```text
Prisma schema válido
55/55 testes aprovados
0 erros de lint
6 warnings preexistentes
build concluído com sucesso
nenhum problema de whitespace
```

---

## Fora do escopo

Este PR não altera:

```text
dashboard customer-facing
relatório executivo
RBAC/autenticação
setup tokens
cron/scheduler
CI/CD
deploy
Central de Suporte sync
```

Também permanecem fora deste PR dois achados operacionais já identificados:

```text
duplicação preexistente de deleteMany em siem-agents-sync.ts
ausência de flock no cron do Zabbix
```

Esses pontos devem ser tratados separadamente.

---

## Resultado

Após este PR, o portal passa a possuir uma fundação consistente para health das integrações, baseada em:

```text
configuração
+
telemetria persistida
+
freshness
+
estado da execução
=
Integration Health
```

sem criar uma segunda fonte de verdade e sem acoplar o carregamento das páginas à disponibilid

author: ryanjosephkamp
body:
The first words ever to leave this list.

They are synthetic comparatives and superlatives — `abacteremicer`,
`abambulacralest`, `abatabler` — built by blind affixation and marked
`validated: true` while their own records said "awaiting validation". You cannot
be *more* abacteremic.

Merriam-Webster was asked about 300 of their stems, by reading the inflections it
records for each stem rather than looking the comparative up as a headword, which
it would never carry. It could rule on 183 and listed the comparative for exactly
one.

**That one is `blameworthy` → `blameworthier`, `blameworthiest`, and it stays.**
16,478 forms were measured; **16,476** are demoted. Never demote what the evidence
vindicated, even when it is one case out of 183.

| | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| valid | 378,891 | **362,415** |
| invalid | 9,275,261 | **9,291,737** |
| **total** | **9,654,152** | **9,654,152** |

The total is the row that matters. Nothing was deleted; words moved sides.

## Not a life sentence — three fixes that had to land first

A demotion here says no dictionary we could reach recognised the word that day. It
does **not** say the word is not English. Three separate mechanisms would have made
it mean exactly that:

**1. `validation_progress.json` was a permanent blocklist.** Every word the nightly
checked was appended and filtered out of every future run, forever. It was already
excluding 2,005 words. Now a dated map with a **180-day cooldown**, migrated by
stamping existing entries with the last run date so they don't all come due at
once, and pruned past the window so it stops growing by 1,000 entries a day.

**2. The prioritiser's pre-filter drops anything over 15 characters** — which covers
**4,932 of the demoted words**. `abdominocutaneousest` would never have been
selected again. The recheck queue bypasses the pre-filter entirely.

**3. 9.29M invalid words at 1,000/day is a 25-year cycle.** The queue takes a
reserved **100 of each night**, oldest-checked first, so these rotate in months
rather than decades.

Every ledger row carries `reversible: yes` and `recheck_queued: yes`, and the queue
file explains itself to anyone who opens it.

## Tripwires fired, as designed

Three of them — the word-count floor and the `twl` and `synthetic` shares. They are
updated with reasoning, not widened. Note `twl` and `pipeline` rose **without
gaining a single word**: the denominator fell by 16,476. The comment now warns
about that. The `synthetic` upper bound stays tight, because a rise there would
mean generated words were being added again.

Published: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ryanjosephkamp/english-openlist/commit/8ad1fe8f39055dbed613630281bd4bc73a7ec8bb

## Verified

- 164 pytest (12 new, all on re-validation eligibility), 52 vitest, typecheck clean
- grand total unchanged — asserted before upload, not assumed
- every demoted word is on the invalid list, off the valid list, and in the queue
- `blameworthier`/`blameworthiest` confirmed still valid
- all three files backed up and verified byte-identical on restore
- site checked in a browser; stale `378,891` purged from the shell, manifest and `/use` examples

author: ibetitsmike
body:
## Summary

Fixes the two CI flake classes that dequeued #3854 from the merge queue twice on 2026-08-14 (runs 31829008751 and 31831156227).

## Background

1. **Bun teardown crash**: in `Test / Unit`, bun 1.3.5 crashed (`Illegal instruction`, exit 132) at process teardown in an isolated `WorkflowRunner.test.ts` run *after every test passed* ("0 fail", panic during shutdown). The same signature dequeued another PR on Aug 13.
2. **Registry publication skew**: during an AWS SDK publish wave, the lockfile-free resolves in `Static Checks` (`check-bench-agent.sh`) and `Smoke / Server` (`npm install` of the packed tarball) requested `@aws-sdk/credential-provider-ini@^3.973.14` seconds before it was visible on the registry (`ETARGET` / "No version matching ... (but package exists)").

## Implementation

- `pr.yml`: isolated unit-test files retry up to 3 times, but **only on signal exits (>= 128)**. Genuine test failures (exit 1) still fail immediately on the first attempt, so no flaky-test masking is possible. The existing `scripts/retry.sh` was not reused here because it retries every nonzero exit.
- `check-bench-agent.sh`, `smoke-test.sh`, `generate-npm-shrinkwrap.sh`: the three registry-facing installs (all resolve fresh from npm) are wrapped in the existing `scripts/retry.sh` with 5 attempts x 60s, enough to ride out a multi-minute publish wave.

Considered and rejected: scoping the smoke-test retry to `SKIP_SHRINKWRAP=1` only. The observed incident hit the *shrinkwrapped* `Smoke / Server` install, so that scoping would leave the observed flake unfixed. Also considered a 3x30 retry budget to match `dist-mac`'s; kept 5x60 because publish waves span minutes and the extra delay only applies to genuinely broken resolution, which lockfile-based jobs never hit.

## Validation

- Behavioral test of the crash-retry loop with a fake `bun` (crash-then-pass recovers; exit 1 fails immediately with a single invocation; persistent crash exits 132 after 3 attempts; clean pass runs once).
- `make static-check`, `shellcheck` on all three scripts, `actionlint`, `zizmor`: all green.
- `check-bench-agent.sh` and `generate-npm-shrinkwrap.sh` run end-to-end locally through the retry wrapper.

## Risks

Low. The unit-test retry cannot mask real failures (exit-code gated). The install retries add up to 4 minutes before surfacing a genuine resolution failure in `Static Checks` / `Smoke` / npm publish; publication skew is far more common than genuine breakage on those lockfile-free paths.

## Description

- `aie.utils.config.aiecc_path()` previously only checked the bundled MLIR-AIE `bin/` directory, then `PATH` — there was no way to point at a specific `aiecc` explicitly. author: tgoodhew
body:
Closes #29. §15 step 11's first slice.

A11Y-9 requires mode changes, connection changes and command results to reach a user who is not looking at the window.

**`StateAnnouncer`** holds the judgement — which transitions are worth interrupting for — and is headless, linked into the test project. It is silent on the first observation, and silent on every staleness tick, which is most of the calls into `Render`. Connection outranks the mode change that arrives with it; coasting outranks the mode change that carries it, because reaching Locked while tracking nothing is §10.3's most useful diagnostic and announcing "Locked to GPS" alone would tell the listener the opposite of what happened. Urgency is derived from the §9.4.3 severity the mode already carries.

**`LiveRegion`** raises `LiveRegionChanged` by hand — declaring `LiveSetting` in XAML is necessary and not sufficient — through `CreatePeerForElement`, since `FromElement` returns null for exactly the announcement that most needs making.

**`CommandOutcomeBar`** announces its own outcome, because the bar is reused and a second failure of the same command changes only the message.

## Verification

- 753 tests pass, 13 of them new; one caught a real bug in the coasting falling edge before it shipped.
- All four CI gates pass.
- MSBuild x64 Debug clean, zero warnings.
- **Ran the app against the receiver on COM3.** `Announcer` is present in the UIA tree carrying "Locked to GPS", and the window is visually unchanged.

Narrator confirmation of each forced transition is the remaining manual half of #29's stated verification method.

author: zacxdev
body:
Makes the **external-only** (`kind='offsite'`) App-store scope actually reachable by a segmented tester cohort. `resolveStoreVisibilityScope` already modelled `public-external`; two blockers meant no cohort could ever land in it. Code only — **no Flipt configuration is touched**.

## What changed

**1. `isExternalListingsPublicEnabled` is now user-aware** (`src/server/services/app-blocks-flag.ts`)

It was a bare `isFlipt(FLAG)` — a global eval (`entityId='global'`, empty context). A Flipt segment can only match on the context it is handed, so a `testers` segment resolved `false` for **every** member and the feature was unreachable by construction. It now mirrors `isAppBlocksEnabled` / `isAppListingsEnabled`: `isFlipt(FLAG, String(user.id), buildFliptContext(user))` when a user is present, and `resolveStoreVisibilityScope` threads its `opts` into that second axis.

Backward compatibility is a hard invariant and is tested three ways:
- **no user → the original global eval, byte-identical** — the mock is asserted to be called with the flag key *alone* (one argument), so entityId/context still fall back to the client's `('global', {})` defaults.
- **a base-enabled flag still resolves `true` for everyone** — anon, in-cohort, out-of-cohort and moderator. A plain base-`enabled` boolean has no rollout rules, so it is immune to whatever entityId/context the eval carries. Adding context can only **add** segmentation.
- **fail-closed** — absent flag / Flipt down → `false` → `none`, with or without a user.

**2. The page gate can now express the scope**

There was no client-side feature for `app-listings-public-external` at all, so `hasAppsStoreAccess` → `resolveAppsPageAccess` returned `notFound` for a viewer whose only qualification was that flag — while the server would have happily served them the offsite catalog. Two changes:
- new `appListingsPublicExternal` entry in `feature-flags.service.ts`, `fliptKey: 'app-listings-public-external'`;
- the **shared** `hasAppsStoreAccess` predicate becomes `appListings || appBlocks || appListingsPublicExternal`. Extended in the one place it lives (PR #3905's consolidation); no call site open-codes anything, and the call-site ledger test was read and kept accurate.

The new term grants **reachability only**. What the viewer then sees is still the server's `StoreVisibilityScope` → offsite listings only; onsite App Blocks stay hidden by the server, not by this gate. It also widens no block-RUNTIME surface — `/apps/installed`, `/apps/run/<slug>`, the author surfaces and the `blocks.*` procs still gate on `appBlocks` alone, asserted in the seam suite.

## Dark-by-default proof

`app-listings-public-external` does not exist in Flipt. `app-blocks-flag.external-scope.test.ts` models exactly that (only the two flags that *do* exist are registered) and asserts each cohort lands where it lands today:

| cohort | scope |
|---|---|
| moderator | `full` |
| app-dev-tester (`app-listings`) | `full` |
| plain logged-in user | `none` |
| would-be external tester | `none` |
| anonymous / no-arg | `none` |

It carries its own control (`the external flag really is absent`) so the block cannot pass vacuously. The pre-existing `app-blocks-flag.test.ts` — including `isExternalListingsPublicEnabled evaluates the plain global flag (no context)` — passes **unmodified**, and `resolveAppsPageAccess.test.ts` is **untouched**.

## The server/client seam

The same flag is evaluated twice per request, by two paths that had never shared a test:

- **server data path** — `isExternalListingsPublicEnabled({user})` → `isFlipt` (**async**) → `resolveStoreVisibilityScope` → the store read procs / REST endpoints.
- **page gate** — `featureFlags.appListingsPublicExternal` → `isFliptSync` (**sync**, plus a static `availability` fallback when Flipt answers `null`) → `ctx.features` → `hasAppsStoreAccess` → `resolveAppsPageAccess`.

Disagreement is silent in both directions: the viewer passes the page gate and gets an empty store, or is 404'd off a catalog the server would serve.

**Decision:** they agree *by construction* for a logged-in viewer — same key, same entityId (`String(user.id)`), same context object (both call the shared `buildFliptContext`). And they fail closed together: an absent flag makes the async `isEnabled` return `false` while the sync `isEnabledSync` returns `null` and falls through to the static availability — which is why the client entry is **`availability: []` and not `['mod']`**. With `['mod']` a moderator's client value would be `true` against a server `false`. That is the entry's whole reason for being `[]`, and it is mutation-tested.

**How it is tested:** `app-blocks-flag.external-scope.seam.test.ts` loads **both real sides** (real `feature-flags.service`, real `app-blocks-flag`, real shared predicate, real SSR resolver) against **one** fake Flipt config that faithfully models the async/sync asymmetry, and asserts the relationship over a 4-config × 4-cohort matrix:

> `resolveAppsPageAccess` grants ⟺ `resolveStoreVisibilityScope() !== 'none'`

with a non-vacuity check that the matrix really produced all three scopes and both gate outcomes, a positive control that the Flipt branch is live, a behavioural key-identity control (a neighbouring key moves neither side; the real key moves both), and a control that the service's 10s feature-flag cache is genuinely bypassed between cases.

**Residual, bounded, and pre-existing:** for an *anonymous* viewer the two evals differ in identity — `'global'`/`{}` on the server vs `'anonymous'`/`{isLoggedIn:'false'}` in the client gate. That is true of `app-listings` and `app-blocks-enabled` today and is invisible for both shapes this rollout uses (a user-property segment, or a plain base-enabled boolean). It bites only under a **percentage/entityId rollout** — which is measured and pinned in a test rather than asserted away, and called out on the flag's doc comment as the shape to avoid.

## Mutation matrix

Every mutant applied to the final tree; each dies on its **own** assertion, not incidentally. Run over `app-blocks-flag{,.external-scope,.external-scope.seam}.test.ts` + `hasAppsStoreAccess` + `resolveAppsPageAccess` + the call-site ledger (149 tests green at baseline).

| # | mutant | killed | representative failing assertion |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `resolveStoreVisibilityScope`: external axis checked **before** privileged | 4 | `A MODERATOR IN THE EXTERNAL COHORT IS STILL full, NEVER NARROWED` — `expected 'public-external' to be 'full'` |
| 2 | axis 1 reads the **external** flag (arm/flag swap) | 19 | `privileged: a MODERATOR resolves full` |
| 3 | axis 2 drops `opts` (global eval, ignores user) | 4 | `non-privileged + external flag ON (in segment) → public-external` |
| 4 | helper **ignores its user argument** (silent revert to global) | 7 | `a SEGMENT-scoped flag matches for an IN-segment user` |
| 5 | helper reads `app-listings` instead (flag swap) | 15 | `reads ONLY the app-listings-public-external key` |
| 6 | helper drops the no-user branch (breaks byte-identical compat) | 2 | `no user → the ORIGINAL global eval, byte-identical (flag key alone)` |
| 7 | predicate `\|\|` → `&&` on the new term | 17 | `the external flag being FALSE cannot revoke either older flag` |
| 8 | predicate drops the new term (revert) | 8 | `the EXTERNAL flag ALONE grants access` |
| 9 | predicate `\|\|` → `??` (whole chain; mixing is a syntax error) | 6 | `{listings:false, blocks:true, external:false} → true` |
| 10 | predicate returns constant `true` | 19 | `a viewer qualifying via NOTHING still gets notFound` |
| 11 | predicate returns constant `false` | 33 | `external-only viewer reaches /apps — NOT notFound` |
| 12 | client entry `availability: []` → `['mod']` | 3 | `the client entry is fail-closed for a MODERATOR when the flag is ABSENT` |
| 13 | client entry `fliptKey` → `'app-listings'` | 10 | `KEY IDENTITY, proven behaviourally: both sides read the SAME Flipt key` |

author: lczako-eng
body:
> *"The top, about how to use this thing, has to be more apparent — easier to use, less words, or it needs to be just easier to read. Animated."*

The old Guide screen was this project's own doctrine failing: **sixteen paragraphs of prose explaining that you do not need to learn anything.** Reading a description of talking teaches nobody how to talk.

## It opens with somebody talking

A real sentence types itself out, then what happens to it appears underneath. Rotates through five.

```
had a steak and a baked potato▌
  ↳ Logged, with its macros, under today.
```

Everything below is cut to one short line per section plus the sentences themselves, which *are* the manual. **798 words on screen down to 459.** The long form still exists in the `guide` **tool**, where a model reads it and prose is the right shape.

## Not one invented number on the answering side

A demo figure on a health product reads as somebody's own data at a glance — and this is the one screen a person is on precisely because they can't yet tell which is which. The reply says what *happens*, which is the part being taught anyway. Tested.

## Reduced motion is obeyed, not approximated

The whole line appears at once and the rotation stops. Somebody who told their phone that movement makes them ill didn't ask for a slower animation — and a manual is exactly the screen where they still need the content. Verified in a browser under both settings.

## And it's reachable without a password — which it never actually was

The Guide is written to need no session and no request for exactly one reason: it's the screen somebody needs most when they *cannot* get signed in. But the gate covered the whole app, so there was no way to open it. A promise made in a comment and not kept in the markup.

There's a link on the sign-in screen now, and a way back.

## Second tab, and called "Say this"

Sixth in a sideways-scrolling row is not apparent whatever the label says — you couldn't see it without scrolling the tabs. And *"Guide"* reads as documentation nobody opens; the screen is sentences you say.

556 tests passing. The reduced-motion test was verified to fail without the check.

author: kamyarshahrestani
body:
`WORKER_IMAGE = "apiary-worker"` (`manager.py:59`) was a dataclass default at `:494` that `cli.py` never overrode, baked into argv at `:585`, and `Spawner.spawn(issue, base_commit)` had no image parameter. So the stack a task declares (#98) had nowhere to go.

## `StackImages`

House convention, matching `MergePolicy` and `InfrastructurePolicy`: a `#:`-documented default, `APIARY_WORKER_IMAGES`, a `from_env()` read once at the call site, a `summary()` printed at startup.

| Stack | Image |
|---|---|
| `python` | `apiary-worker` |
| `node` | `apiary-worker-node` |
| `react` | `apiary-worker-node` |

Node and React share an image deliberately — React web needs Node and nothing else at the toolchain level, and two tags for one Dockerfile would be two things to keep built. The override **merges** over the defaults, so `APIARY_WORKER_IMAGES=node=my-node:dev` cannot silently un-configure Python; a malformed pair raises rather than falling back, because a silent fallback would run the whole ledger on the Python image while the operator believed otherwise. A test asserts the mapping covers `KNOWN_STACKS` exactly — a stack an issue may *declare* but no image can *run* is a task that parses and then cannot be dispatched.

## The refusal happens before the claim

A task whose stack this host has no image for cannot run whatever happens next, so the resolution is done **before `claim()`**: nothing is written, nothing is spawned, and the message names the stack and what to do about it. A claim spent on it would be a claim #35 has to sweep.

When the image *is* mapped but was never built, `missing_image` recognises the `docker create` failure and the reason carries `build_hint`'s exact line:

```
docker build -f Dockerfile.worker.node -t apiary-worker-node .
```

That is the one failure whose fix is a command rather than an investigation — the orchestrator can neither build nor pull, so a human has to. Both cases stay **per-issue defers**, which is only safe because #94 landed first; the ticket's own note says so.

## `Dockerfile.worker.node`

Node 22 **pinned**, copied from the official image rather than Debian's archive (bookworm ships 18). The same major the generated CI workflow pins in #96, so a worker-green result and a CI-green result are talking about one runtime. `org.apiary.stack` label. `~/.npm` owned by uid 10001 with `NPM_CONFIG_CACHE` pointing at it — npm writes a cache on **every** invocation, including ones that install nothing, and an unwritable cache directory fails the command rather than skipping the cache. Same reason `/opt/venv` is chowned in `Dockerfile.worker`.

The entrypoint shim is byte-identical to `Dockerfile.worker`'s, and has to be: the orchestrator dispatches one argv against every worker image, so a shim that drifted between them would be a stack-dependent argument contract.

### Verified against a real build, not asserted

```
v22.23.2 · npm 10.9.8 · git 2.47.3 · Python 3.12.14
uid 10001 · cache=/home/apiary/.npm · cache writable · org.apiary.stack=node
node --test → # pass 1  # fail 0   (no network)
```

`node --test` is #87's chosen first non-Python gate, and it runs green in this image with no registry reachable — which is the whole reason that stack was chosen.

## `docs/security.md`'s argument is rewritten, not patched

The claim was that `Dockerfile.worker` "deliberately bakes in no toolchain" so the `## Verify` command can install what the repo needs at run time. **That does not survive its own section**: a worker is on an `internal: true` network whose only route out is the egress proxy with a static allowlist, so a run-time install is not slow — it is *denied*, in under a second. And the stated intent was stack-agnosticism while the effect was the opposite, because the one toolchain every image did carry was the Python the package itself needs.

Toolchains in the images is therefore a security *improvement*: an image that carries its stack needs no registry at run time, so `APIARY_EGRESS_ALLOW` stops being the thing standing between a green gate and a widened allowlist.

## Supply side

`APIARY_WORKER_IMAGES` is added to compose's orchestrator `environment:` block, which is an **explicit list, not a passthrough** — an override absent from it never reaches a containerised orchestrator, which is the drift `tests/test_security.py` already polices for the token and the proxy variables. A new test joins them.

`SETUP.md` gains **step 4**, before the first run, with the exact build commands — nothing in the repository documented them; they appeared only in a `doctor` fix hint.

## `--stack`

`swarm run --stack node` writes that stack into every planned task, so a Node repository is reachable **before** #103 inverts the refusal. An explicit flag overrides the model's own answer: it is the operator saying what the repository *is*, which the planner cannot infer from an objective.

## Testing

19 new tests, unit and bare CI, plus one `@pytest.mark.docker` smoke test that skips (rather than fails) when the image is not built — building it is a manual host step by design, so "not built here" is a fact about the machine, not a regression. Suite 1112 passed, 23 deselected. The live test was run for real against the built image.

Closes #99

body:
## Summary

Promotes `dev` into `beta` for the next prerelease. This batch aligns `textmode.export.js` with the updated `textmode.js` plugin system and the released `0.17.2-beta.1` core, adds the export API refactor, and updates dependencies and tooling.

> **Note:** This supersedes the accidental `dev` → `main` merge (PR #65). That merge has been reverted: the `main` branch was reset to its prior state, the `v1.7.1` release/tag were removed, and `textmode.export.js@1.7.1` was deprecated on npm with `latest` restored to `1.7.0`. The changes land on `beta` instead, as intended.

## What changed

### Plugin-system alignment

- **Export API via `defineExtension`** — `saveCanvas`, `toImageBlob`, `copyCanvas`, and the format save/to-blob methods are now registered as `textmodifier` value extensions; `exportOverlay` is exposed through a getter. The plugin runtime handles conflict detection and uninstall cleanup, replacing the previous manual `Object.assign` + `delete` pass.
- **Hook subscription decoupled** — Exporters now receive a small `PostDrawSubscription` type (`(callback) => () => void`) instead of reaching into `TextmodePluginContext.registerPostDrawHook`.
- **Synchronous install/uninstall** — `install`/`uninstall` are no longer async.

### Video export

- **Frame-rate-independent bitrate presets** — each preset resolves to a fixed bits-per-pixel budget from export dimensions only; docs/types updated.
- **New `VideoRecorder` tests** for the revised bitrate resolution.

### Housekeeping

- **`TEXTMODE_EXPORT_VERSION` removed** — plugin and JSON exporter read the version from `package.json` (the old `src/version.ts` had drifted to `1.2.1`).
- **Unused overlay styles removed** — the `RangeInput` component and its CSS were deleted.
- **Dependencies & tooling** — `textmode.js` peer range → `>=0.17.2-beta.1 <0.20.0`, devDependency → `^0.17.2-beta.1`, `@textmode/release` → `^0.2.0`; `check`/`prepack` composed locally.

## Version note

The package version stays at `1.7.0`. Merging to `beta` triggers the CI release job; semantic-release computes the prerelease version from git tags and commit analysis (expected `1.7.1-beta.1`).

body:
## What
\`_redact_extra_value\`'s cycle guard and depth-cap guard (added in 406afc6 to close the dict/list/tuple/set extra-redaction gap) both returned the raw, unredacted container when they stopped recursing -- so a secret reachable only via a cyclic back-edge, or nested past the depth cap, still leaked into Sentry breadcrumb data.

## Evidence
Reproduced directly against a real \`logging.Logger\` + real \`sentry_sdk\` capture hook:
\`\`\`
extra={'cyclic': {'self': <cycle>, 'secret': SECRET}}
before fix: {'self': "{...'secret': SECRET}", 'secret': '[REDACTED]'}   # leaked via ['self']
after fix:  {'self': "{...'secret': '[REDACTED]'}", 'secret': '[REDACTED]'}
\`\`\`

## Fix
Both short-circuit branches now return \`_redact_secrets(str(value))\` instead of \`value\`.

- 2 new tests (RED before the fix, GREEN after, bite-proofed via copy-aside/mutate/restore)

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD013 -->

# Pull Request

## Goal

Generalize the existing fail-closed OWNER reply-only closeout for unavailable or synthetic provider-only evidence on the canonical current-PR mapping, without introducing another ref/SHA parser branch.

## Business reason

Reduce repeated governance deadlocks and operator/reviewer time while preserving authenticated repository, mapping, seal, CI, security, and review authority boundaries.

## Scope

- Add one exact byte-equal OWNER authoring form:
  `OWNER NOT-A-BUG: provider-only evidence in this root is unavailable; authenticated live PR state is authoritative.`
- Reuse the existing `validated_duplicate_reply_urls(...)` producer and unchanged consumer interface.
- Validate every generic root independently against trusted connector identity, canonical mapping path, immutable REST/GraphQL root identity, live-head `originalCommit`, sole direct mapping-only successor, material digest equality, and the strict current provider-neutral seal.
- Keep legacy full-ref unavailable-evidence behavior compatible.
- Keep historical stale-seal `OWNER FIXED` parsing, topology, and singleton policy separate and unchanged.
- Document the exact human/machine authority split and operational reply-before-resolve order.

## Out of scope

- No bot-prose interpretation, SHA/ref/token extraction, `classify_commit_ref(...)` use, new parser, regex, schema, service, module, or framework for the generic class.
- No workflow, PR-body schema, mapping schema, runtime, API, OpenAPI, dependency, Caddy, backlog, or provider integration change.
- No authority to waive material/code/workflow/dependency/security findings, current seal, CI, security, coverage, unresolved threads, bot actionables, ancestry, or the wait window.
- No change to historical stale-seal `OWNER FIXED` semantics.

## Files changed

- `scripts/orchestration/pr_review_evidence.py`
- `tests/test_pr_review_material_seal.py`
- `AGENTS.md`
- `RUNBOOK_AGENT.md`
- `docs/orchestration/PR_ORCHESTRATION_CONTRACT_MATRIX.md`
- `docs/ENGINEERING_LESSONS.md`

## Key decisions

- OWNER is the attributable semantic authority that the complete root contains no independent actionable finding beyond unavailable provider-only evidence; automation does not infer that proposition from prose.
- The validator proves only authenticated structural eligibility and current mapping/seal/material facts, fail-closed on ambiguity.
- Generic roots are per-root rather than globally singleton; each requires its own exact sole later OWNER reply.
- Same-root canonical mapping or fingerprint disposition blocks generic reply-only coverage; unrelated canonical records may coexist.
- The legacy full-40-ref form remains readable for historical compatibility but is not the recommended authoring form.

## Tests

- `python3 scripts/orchestration/check_preflight.py` — PASS
- `python3 scripts/orchestration/check_agent_consistency.py` — PASS
- Focused pytest for material-seal, merge-readiness, strict disposition, Phase 2 body, and review-pattern oracles — PASS `[100%]`
- `make validate-changed` — PASS `[100%]`
- `pre-commit run --all-files` — PASS
- Black, Ruff, MyPy, Bandit, `git diff --check`, unmerged/conflict/tracked-worktree inventory — PASS
- Current-head PR CI — pending after PR open; no green/ready/mergeable claim is made here.

## Security notes

- Generic eligibility remains restricted to trusted `chatgpt-codex-connector` roots on the canonical mapping path.
- REST and GraphQL cross-bind repository, PR, numeric comment ID, URL, path, exact unedited body/timestamps, trusted connector user identity, and live-head `originalCommit`.
- Material-path comments and any stale/malformed current seal remain blocking.
- The exact OWNER reply is a human NOT-A-BUG disposition only; it is not provider output, review, scan, approval, PASS, no-findings evidence, or merge authority.
- Architecture and security role passes are GO after fixing root immutability and reply-before-resolve ordering findings.

## Risks / rollback

- Primary risk: an OWNER incorrectly classifies a root as provider-only. Mitigation is one exact auditable per-root reply after reading the complete immutable root; uncertainty requires ordinary FIXED, NOT-A-BUG, or DEFERRED disposition.
- Primary implementation risk: accidental blanket coverage or legacy/stale-seal behavior drift. Deterministic positive/negative real-Git tests cover classifier isolation, multi-root generic behavior, same-root exclusions, strict current seal/topology, API uncertainty, legacy singleton, and stale-seal regressions.
- Rollback is a normal revert of the eventual squash merge; behavior returns to the prior narrower fail-closed reply-only contract.

## Premortem

- Decision: `proceed` after all identified actual-diff risks were closed.
- FIXED: blanket-waiver risk via canonical mapping/current-seal/material-path guards and negative tests.
- FIXED: ref/prose parser reintroduction via classifier-fails-if-called tests.
- FIXED: edited-root risk via strict REST/GraphQL body, timestamp, user, repository, PR, comment, and `originalCommit` binding.
- FIXED: generic/legacy/stale-seal cardinality coupling via multi-root generic and regression tests.
- FIXED: operator ordering ambiguity via explicit post-reply visibility before thread resolution in `RUNBOOK_AGENT.md`.
- Residual: human misclassification remains the intentionally attributable OWNER authority boundary; the validator grants no independent correctness or merge claim.

## Experiment Runner Evidence

- Artifact: `artifacts/orchestration/experiments/results/provider-evidence-unavailable-closeout-oracle-result.json`
- Experiment: `exp-7756530a14e9`
- Result: accepted on `apple-container`; 3/3 immutable oracles returned 0; `mutated_paths=[]`; shared tree untouched; `contribution_kind=none`.
- Image: immutable digest `sha256:5b3abbad998dc1b23f9d99e72a8fde931558401b81a2aec8c5eeeff90b128a70`.

## Lane Start Provenance

- Packet: `artifacts/orchestration/task_packets/f940e00bc4e3.json`
- Starter: `scripts/orchestration/start_pr_lane.sh`
- Required pre-open role order executed: agent-coordinator → logic-agent → philosophy-agent → dev-operator → architecture-specialist → security-auditor.

## Split justification

- Why this PR cannot be split safely: production validator and its normative authority contract must remain reviewable and testable as one closed change.
- Invariant or rollout constraint requiring one PR: code/tests and four authoritative documents must describe the same exact OWNER syntax and fail-closed boundary.
- Follow-up PRs: None.

## Deferred / Follow-ups

None.

## Next best step

Run the mandatory post-open QA → bug-hunter → security-auditor pass, fix any bounded finding in this PR, then perform the exact-material self-review/seal and one mapping-only closeout commit after current main is healthy and one final admission sync is possible.
