seeds that compile on both sides.

(The issue title's "71 of 249" is from `ff3da3e` and has decayed a long way; the
last census on the issue listed 8 `$clo` seeds, and #6819 has since taken
`s0017`.)

## Root cause

A closure captures every free var of its body **by value**, so a fn value it
merely *calls* still has to be the uniform env box the capture read dispatches
env-first against (`make_clo_func`'s `var cap: fn = __env[i]`, or the extra
argument `closure_lift_one` appends). `value_use_idents_expr` — which decides
whether a fn-valued `var` binding is env-boxed — applied its *call-callee*
exclusion inside a nested lambda too, so a call-only use one lambda in left the
local a raw `ExprLambda`. That reached `lower_expr`, whose `ExprLambda` arm
emits `const_func(<cur_fn>$clo)` unconditionally, and no hoist had built that
name → the module bailed.

A nested `function` declaration desugars to exactly that binding
(`var f = <lambda>`), which is how the shape arrives through ordinary source.

Two supporting pieces:

- **The exclusion stays for a value-position `if`/`match`.** That desugars to an
  immediately-invoked 0-param lambda whose body lowers *inline* in the enclosing
  frame, so it captures nothing. Without the carve-out, `s0489`'s i64 array
  element built inside one lost its representation and the seed regressed to
  `did not lower: array literal` — caught by the corpus, not by reading.
- **`cap_type_expr` gains the two arms the capture then needs to type**: a lambda
  init, and the `__mkclo$` marker the lift has already left in its place by the
  time a sibling closure's capture is typed.

## The gate, and the divergence it prevents

A fn capture whose signature carries an `i64` / `u64` / `f64` / `f32` position
keeps its bail (`cap_fn_sig_wide`). It rides the env box under the flat `"fn"`
tag, which carries no signature, so the call inside the hoisted body dispatches
through the arity-keyed `$fn<N>` funcref type and pushes 32-bit args — right on
the register backends, `indirect call type mismatch` on wasm.

That is not theoretical: **without the gate, seed `s0356` compiles and diverges
on wasm** (wasmtime 1, interpreter 0). Trading an honest refusal for a wrong
answer is the hazard this issue has documented five times, so those shapes stay
declined.

The gate answers only what it can *prove* wide, so no capture that admitted
before stops admitting.

## Separate pre-existing bug found on the way (NOT fixed here)

A **fn-typed PARAM** with a wide signature, captured by an escaping closure,
already compiles clean on `main` and traps on wasm:

```fern
function mk(lf: (i64) => boolean): (i32) => i32 {
    return ((x0: i32) => (if (lf(4i64)) { x0 } else { 34i32 }));
}
function main(): i32 { return mk(((y: i64) => false))(3i32) & 63i32; }
```

`FERN_STRICT_IR=1` exits 0; wasmtime traps with `indirect call type mismatch` in
`mk$clo`. The capture read is a LOCAL, so the `FNSIG` / `FNRET` seeding
`lower_func` does for fn-typed params never reaches it, and the argument widths
are not coerced either. Fixing it means carrying a fn value's signature through
the env box — #6324 / #6282 territory, with its own blast radius — so it is
filed as #6862 rather than bundled. The gate above is what stops this PR adding new
entrants to that class.

## Tests

`internal/e2eselfhost/self_host_fn_value_capture_ir_test.go` — 9 cases across
three legs (x86-64, wasm, arm64), each asserting the ANSWER through the value
rather than that the module lowered, and each driven with `runCaptureStrictIR`
so a per-function bail cannot pass the case (#6602):

- nested `function` captured by an escaping lambda
- the same written as an annotated fn-typed local
- a fn value and a scalar captured together
- the captured fn value is itself a capturing closure (a box inside a box)
- the capturing lambda in a closure ARRAY beside a plain one (one container, one
  ABI — #5071)
- the seed shape: the capturing lambda reaches its destination through a generic
  passthrough (`pick`)
- three regression guards: a call-only fn local, a call-only *capturing* one
  (both must stay on `closure_lift_one`'s cheaper direct-call lift), and the
  value-position if/match carve-out reduced from `s0489`

**Mutation checked**: all six positive cases bail on the parent commit
(`FERN_STRICT_IR: … function value <fn>$clo not defined`) and pass on this one,
verified on arm64-darwin and wasm.

## Suites run locally

This is an Apple Silicon Mac, so every Go leg that needs `qemu-x86_64` skips
here; the substance was verified by driving the self-host compiler directly.

- **Verified green**: all 9 test-table cases on `-target arm64-darwin`
  (compiled, linked, run, exit code compared against `bin/fern -interp`) and on
  `-target wasm32-wasi` under wasmtime.
- **Corpus, green**: the 512-seed census + interpreter differential on
  arm64-darwin (table above), and the 336-case conformance corpus through the
  self-host compiler on arm64-darwin — 0 bails, 0 wrong answers, result file
  byte-identical to the base commit's.
- **In flight on CI**: `internal/e2eselfhost` (the primary gate for this change),
  the fixpoints, and the self-host differential legs.

author: danimarin
body:
## El defecto

En Android la MediaSession —pantalla de bloqueo, teclas de auriculares, coche— la gobierna el módulo `player-now-playing` sobre el **ExoPlayer crudo**, así que sus play/pausa **no pasan por el flavour**.

Y `paused` es una prop **controlada**: se quedaba con el último valor puesto desde la UI. Resultado: iconos congelados, el flavour emitiendo `isPaused: false` con el audio parado, y el primer toque del usuario desperdiciado en resincronizar en vez de en hacer lo que pedía.

## El arreglo

`onPlaybackStateChanged` transporta ahora `playWhenReady`, y el flavour reconcilia `paused` contra él.

**Contra `playWhenReady` y no contra `isPlaying`**, que es la parte importante: `isPlaying` se cae también al buffear y al perder el foco de audio de forma transitoria. Siendo `paused` una prop controlada, reconciliar contra él **pausaría de verdad** — y no volvería solo.

En iOS el campo no llega y queda en no-op: allí lo resuelve el command handler.

## De propina, dos correcciones de duración

En el mismo flavour, ambas de DVR:

- `e.duration > 0` en vez de `e.duration`, para no dar por válido un 0.
- al refrescar el progreso, si la duración conocida es 0 se cae a `seekableDuration`, que es la que tiene sentido en DVR.

## Un fallo que apareció al portarlo

Venía parcheado en GUAU, donde llevaba tiempo. Al subirlo con el typecheck limpio del fork salió algo que allí no se veía:

```ts
videoEvents.onPlaybackStateChanged(e);   // el método es OPCIONAL
```

Invocación sin guarda sobre algo que puede ser `undefined`. Corregido con `?.()`. En GUAU no daba la cara porque su typecheck arrastra cientos de errores previos.

## Verificación

| | master | con el cambio |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tsc` | 147 errores | **147** |
| `eslint` (ficheros tocados) | 31 problems | **31** |
| tests | 112 | **112** |

`:react-native-video:compileDebugJavaWithJavac` verde contra RN 0.83.10.

## Alcance

`playWhenReady` es un campo **nuevo y opcional** en el evento → **minor**. Sin breaking changes.

Es el último bloque del patch de GUAU: con este, [#14](https://github.com/startcat/react-native-video/pull/14) y [#15](https://github.com/startcat/react-native-video/pull/15), ese patch puede desaparecer entero.

author: loriz-art
body:
## Why

Onboarding could tell a user something untrue about what had just happened, or leave them holding a control that was not a way out. This is the final prerequisite behaviour slice before the Direction D visual PR, which will consume these states rather than redefine them.

**Behaviour only.** No Direction D styling, no Quickstart redesign, no Settings work, no Paper edits. **Direction D visuals will be implemented separately.**

## Truthful cancellation vs. genuine failure

A cancelled download and a broken one shared `FailureDiagnosis.Kind.downloadFailed`, so stopping a pull yourself produced *"Check your connection"* — advice about a fault that had not occurred. Paper 05.1 state 10 flags exactly this and names `FailureDiagnoser` as the fix site.

- New `.downloadCancelled` kind, severity `.notice` (the user chose it, so it is not painted as a malfunction), action `.retry`, heading `Download stopped`.
- `DownloadManager` records the kind at **every** cancellation site, so no surface has to re-infer the cause from prose.
- Copy states what happened and stops. No connection advice, and deliberately silent about whether a fresh pull reuses bytes already on disk — that is a property of the downloader, not a promise this app can make. **No Pause, no resume claim.**
- Offline stays a third, distinct diagnosis (`.downloadSourceUnavailable` → *Switch source*).

## A reachable `Cancel download` in Step 3

Found during manual verification: nothing inside setup could *ask* for a cancellation. Onboarding is a full-window sheet, so `DownloadStrip` sits behind it for the entire transfer — a 63%-complete download had no exit but quitting the app. The recovery path existed and was correct; it was simply unreachable.

- `Cancel download` on the Step 3 card, wired to `downloads.cancelDownload(alias: coordinator.selection.alias)`.
- Shown only while the matching job is running; gone once it settles.
- Repeat presses are inert — the optimistic flip to `.cancelled` lands on the same run-loop turn, but a second press would re-signal a process mid-SIGTERM and arm a second hard-kill timer.
- **No keyboard shortcut**, deliberately: `.defaultAction` would put a destructive action on Return on a screen whose job is waiting, and Escape already means "retreat within Step 2, else leave setup".
- Identifier `Quickstart.Download.Cancel`, label naming *which* download, hint stating the consequence.

## Retry, and the route back to choosing

- Retry targets the same intended model and creates **no duplicate job** — `retryDownload` dismisses the terminal record before starting the next child, and refuses to overlap a running pull or a live process.
- The failure card's only route back was *"browse all models"*, which sent everyone to the catalogue even if they had never opened it, and which **ejected the user from setup entirely after a load failure** (a crashed serve makes the wizard ineligible, so returning to `phase .idle` closed the sheet).
- It now returns to the micro-stage the user actually left — **shortlist, Browse All, or Review Download** — naming its destination, and clears the terminal server state so the move stays inside onboarding.
- **Selection, search query, filter, sort and scroll anchor are all preserved** across the failure and the return.

## Pre-flight: disk and memory

- Insufficient disk **interposes before the pull starts**; `Cancel` returns to the exact Step 2 origin, and `Continue anyway` remains available. Warn-only is retained per Paper 05.1 state 12 and existing `DiskSpaceProbe` behaviour — it is not turned into a hard gate.
- The warning no longer attributes the flat 2 GiB pre-flight floor to *"<model> weights + safety margin"*; it says the number is a flat setup floor, not the size of the chosen model.
- Incompatible/insufficient memory blocks the invalid action before download or start, in every list context, and the disabled primary keeps its neutral verb. The alias stays selected — only its actionability changes.
- Declining the pre-load memory guard returns to the exact origin.

## Missing engine

`refreshBinary()` always ran a real `ServerLocator` re-resolution, but when the engine was still absent it changed nothing observable — the one control on that screen read as a dead button.

- `refreshBinary(userInitiated:)` records a `BinaryRecheck` (found + attempt count) and the overlay states the result.
- Repeated checks are audibly and visibly distinct; the success branch reads differently again.
- No invented cause, no promised retry schedule. Launch and Settings refreshes leave no "you rechecked" state behind.
- Recovery stays in the existing window architecture — no separate architecture change was required.

## Relaunch, and what is never fabricated

- A relaunch that finds setup unfinished now says so: the welcome primary reads **`Continue setup`** and the screen states that nothing was carried over.
- **Nothing is carried forward** — no selection, no job record, no phase — so a fake active transfer, percentage, ETA or Step 3 state is impossible by construction rather than by remembering to avoid it (Paper 05.1 state 18: *"The copy promises a fresh download, never a resume."*).
- **Pending Ready keeps precedence**: an unconfirmed Ready flow still reopens on its own model rather than the welcome hero, and still never claims the model is up on this launch (PR #1917 behaviour, pinned against regression here).
- Skip leaves setup owed and still resumable; completion retires the resume record, across relaunch.

## Preserved

The merged four-step model, persistent Ready, `Start chatting`, and the in-window model-selection flow from #1917 / #1931 are unchanged and covered by regression assertions. Cached and uncached successful paths both verified end to end.

## VoiceOver — five contracts

Two of the five did not exist: a cancellation replaced the control the user had just pressed, and a genuine failure arrived with no interaction at all — both in silence.

| Contract | Status |
|---|---|
| Cancellation announcement | Added + covered |
| Genuine-failure announcement | Added + covered |
| Every repeated Recheck result | Covered (string + wiring) |
| Successful Recheck result | Covered (string + wiring) |
| Back control naming its destination | Spoken label added + covered |

Every recovery arrival announces through one helper, composed from the same diagnosis kind the card renders from, so speech and pixels cannot drift. The Back control gained an explicit spoken label with the leading arrow stripped — VoiceOver reads U+2190 aloud as "left-pointing arrow".

Coverage is split honestly: the strings are pure functions asserted directly; the *wiring* is asserted at source level, because `VoiceOverAnnouncer.announce` posts into AppKit's accessibility bus and returns `Void`. This matches the existing pattern in `OnboardingCompletionBehaviorTests`, and the guard was negative-checked — deleting the announce call fails the test.

## Verification

- **60 focused recovery tests pass** (`OnboardingRecoveryBehaviorTests`).
- **Build passes; AX identifier gate passes.** `verify-recommendation-tiers`, `verify-conversation-ordering` and `verify-chat-timeout` all pass.
- **Live manual passed** against an isolated build with the real bundled sidecar (unique bundle id, isolated `HOME`, Application Support, prefs and cold model cache): cancellation, retry, genuine failure, all three Back destinations, incompatible memory, Missing Engine + Recheck, relaunch, pending Ready, cached and uncached success, `Start chatting`, and Light/Dark at 1440x900, 1000x700 and 720x560.
- **VoiceOver was automated-only and was NOT verified with a screen reader.** The tester does not use VoiceOver.
- **The low-disk warning could not be safely produced live** and is automated-only.
- **The full suite has one known unrelated failure** — `MarkdownLinkPerformanceTests` → "Adjacent links keep their own hit targets" (`rects.count → 3` vs `2`) — which **reproduces on clean `upstream

author: mvicenzi
body:
The flash_attn branch added the positional encoding to the input features before the qkv projection, full-width, so it flowed into `v` as well and acted as content rather than as an attention bias. The dense branch already injected it per-head into `q` and `k` after the projection. The two paths computed different operators, and everything trained with `enable_flash=true` used the wrong one. Both paths now use the dense semantics. This matches WarpConvNet's current SpaceAttention, where RoPE is applied to `q`  and `k` only. 
 
Separately, `backbone_kwargs()` now walks the MRO and raises on kwargs a backbone cannot honour instead of dropping them silently. That silent drop is why `encoding_range` never reached the encoder and ran at `125.0` instead of the configured `320`. Same class of bug in `from_config()`: unknown JSON keys were ignored. Both are now errors, which exposed seven parameters (encoding_dim, feature_dim, apa, view, image_h, image_w, min_lr) that were read but settable from nowhere. Every existing config sets them to their dataclass defaults, so no past run was affected.

 A full 100-epoch rerun against the pre-fix baseline, scored with the probe suite at all ten checkpoints, favors the fix.

In addition:

- Probe suite runs in one process (`probes/run_probes.py`). Each stage was re-reading and re-inflating the same ~7 GB features file; `load_features` now happens only once and gets saved in memory. 
  - `collect_probes.sh` drives extraction + probes across a run's checkpoints under a loop. It can be used to automatically collect results as a training jobs progress.

author: ulysses-lima-alltech
body:
## Resumo
Piloto reportou "Erro ao baixar dados offline" ao tocar em "Manter dados Offline" na tela da OS, com `NativeStatement.finalizeAsync has been rejected -> database is locked`.

Causa raiz: o banco SQLite offline usa WAL mode mas nao tinha `busy_timeout` configurado. Qualquer sobreposicao entre duas escritas concorrentes (ex: download manual rodando junto com a sincronizacao automatica do outbox de aplicacoes pendentes) falhava na hora em vez de esperar a transacao anterior liberar.

## Mudancas
- `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000` na abertura do banco (`offlineStorage.ts`).
- `useOfflineSync`'s outbox agora checa `isOfflineDownloadInProgress()` e adia a sincronizacao se um download estiver em andamento, evitando a colisao na origem em vez de so contar com o timeout.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` e `npx eslint` no app mobile
- [ ] Piloto confirmar em campo que "Manter dados Offline" nao falha mais com esse erro

author: victrsantos
body:
Continuação do #17 (já em produção). Dois blocos: o assistente passa a **ler o arquivo**, e a biblioteca passa a ser **visível para toda a empresa**.

## 1. Catalogar a partir do conteúdo

A descrição deixa de partir do zero. Ao escolher o arquivo, o conteúdo é lido e o campo já nasce com um rascunho para revisar; as perguntas da entrevista vêm com respostas sugeridas deduzidas do mesmo conteúdo — confirmar é mais rápido que escrever.

**A extração roda no navegador**, não no servidor: o arquivo já está na máquina de quem publica, e mandá-lo para uma API route esbarraria no limite de ~4,5 MB de body da Vercel. Sobe só o texto, alguns KB.

- **PDF** — pdf.js, primeiras 12 páginas. O worker é empacotado como asset local, então passa na CSP (`worker-src 'self'`).
- **PPTX** — o arquivo é um zip de XML; o texto sai dos elementos `<a:t>` com jszip, o que evita trazer um parser de Office inteiro para ler algumas strings.
- **.ppt antigo** (pré-2007) não é zip: o diálogo orienta salvar como .pptx.
- **Áudio** — um trecho inicial vai para `/transcribe` (Whisper). Cortar bytes funciona em MP3 e WAV; em M4A o índice pode ficar no fim do arquivo e o corte sai ilegível.

Nenhuma dessas falhas bloqueia o cadastro: a interface diz o que aconteceu e o preenchimento manual continua valendo. Rotas novas: `/draft` e `/transcribe`.

**Verificado sobre o `.pptx` real que já está na biblioteca** (`scripts/try-assistant-prompt.ts`, que baixa o arquivo e roda os prompts de verdade): 3.615 caracteres extraídos, rascunho correto sobre comparação de custos de carteiras. Com conteúdo rico o assistente nem pergunta — vai direto aos metadados; com conteúdo escasso, 2 de 3 perguntas vêm com sugestão e a terceira fica vazia porque não havia base (período de validade).

Vale registrar um erro que o teste pegou: a primeira versão do prompt ficou tão conservadora que devolvia **todas** as sugestões vazias, anulando a feature. A instrução foi recalibrada para deduzir quando há base razoável.

Corrige de passagem: o tipo do arquivo enviado ao assistente era sempre `"pdf"` em uploads, mesmo para áudio.

## 2. Acesso aberto à empresa

`canViewBibliotecaComercial` passa a nascer `true` nos defaults, então colaboradores novos já entram com acesso sem depender de alguém ligar a flag. Publicar continua restrito.

**As permissões já foram aplicadas em produção** (`scripts/grant-biblioteca-comercial-managers.mjs`): 79 de 79 colaboradores com visualização e 5 curadores com gestão — Ana Daldegan, Patrick Corrêa, Fernando Damasceno, Carlos Pessoa e Paulo Ribeiro. O script não revoga ninguém e é idempotente.

Junto vai uma correção que evitaria um estrago: em `apply-access-permissions.mjs`, `canManageBibliotecaComercial` vinha da base como `false` sem a salvaguarda que `canManageRegrasComerciais` já tinha — rodar aquele script **revogaria a permissão dos cinco curadores**. Agora o valor atual é preservado.

## Atenção na revisão

**O conteúdo dos documentos passa a ser enviado à OpenAI.** No arquivo real da biblioteca, o texto extraído inclui patrimônio alocado, instituição e composição de carteira. O prompt proíbe copiar esses dados para a descrição — e não copiou —, mas eles trafegam na requisição. Se materiais com dado de cliente forem comuns aqui, vale decidir com compliance antes de ampliar o uso.

## Verificação

- `typecheck`, `lint` e `build` limpos (seguem apenas os dois warnings antigos, alheios a esta feature).
- `AuthContext.test.tsx` atualizado para o novo default e passando (13/13).
- As 3 suites que falham no repo (`token.test.ts`, `ManageCollaborators.import.test.ts`, `WorkflowSubmissionModal.test.tsx`) continuam falhando por motivos pré-existentes, já confirmados contra `main` num worktree limpo.
- Dependências novas: `pdfjs-dist` e `jszip`, ambas carregadas sob demanda — `/documents` cresceu 1,8 kB no first load.

author: michelledelossantos1067
body:
## Backend

### Fix crítico: GeminiService no parseaba la respuesta de Gemini
- El deserializado leía `"contents"` (plural) del lado de la *respuesta*, pero Gemini responde con `"content"` (singular) dentro de `candidates[].content.parts[].text`. Esto iba a fallar apenas la API respondiera correctamente, sin importar que la key estuviera bien configurada.
- El *request* body sí usa `contents` (plural), que es lo correcto de ese lado.

### Modelo actualizado
- `gemini-2.0-flash` → dado de baja por Google (shutdown 1 de junio 2026), nunca tuvo cupo en el free tier.
- `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` → ya no disponible para API keys nuevas.
- Actualizado a `gemini-3.6-flash`, probado y devolviendo respuestas completas.

### Confianza en predicciones
- El nivel de confianza (`Alta`/`Media`/`Baja`) se calculaba con un umbral absoluto de muestras (`>=6`, `>=3`), lo que hacía matemáticamente imposible llegar a `Media`/`Alta` cuando `LookbackWeeks` era bajo, sin importar la calidad de los datos.
- Ahora se calcula como cobertura relativa a las semanas de historial solicitadas.

### Seguridad
- Se removieron credenciales reales (Gemini API Key, SMTP password, JWT secret key) que estaban hardcodeadas en `appsettings.json` y quedaron expuestas en el historial de git. Reemplazadas por placeholders; las credenciales fueron rotadas.

## Frontend

- Nueva página de **Insights IA** que consume el endpoint de Gemini para generar recomendaciones de stock, promociones y menú.
- Render de la respuesta con `react-markdown` (antes se mostraban los símbolos `**`, `##`, `*` crudos en pantalla).
- Agregados los links de navegación a **Predicción** e **Insights IA** en el header de las páginas del owner.

author: andreadiazcorreia
body:
Admin dispute resolutions (`admin-settled`, `admin-canceled`, `admin-took-dispute`) were applied unconditionally: the status changed with no dispute in local state, and a dispute payload could materialize a resolved dispute on its own. They now
require local dispute state to back them, are not re-applied to an already-resolved dispute, and a payload can no longer re-point a tracked dispute at a different id. A dropped message raises no notification and does not navigate.

`admin-canceled` gets its own terminal status (`canceled-by-admin`, already rendered by the trade widgets) and the `handleEvent` case it was missing. It is no longer indistinguishable from a plain cancelation, and no longer reaches session deletion through the bond-cancel reconciler, which was only ever meant for `Action.canceled`. These orders stay under the "canceled" filter.

Resolution messages across the six locales now attribute the outcome to the admin and ask the user to confirm in their wallet, instead of stating that funds moved: the app reads neither the wallet nor the escrow.

Also documents that `MostroFSM` is not wired in — nothing imports it, and status is derived by `OrderState._getStatusFromAction`.

15 new tests across intake guard, status filter and resolution messages.
540 tests pass, `flutter analyze` clean.

author: blueman82
body:
## Summary

Adds `hooks/scripts/lib/graph_readiness.sh` — a pure read-only readiness
query over `progress.json`'s durable execution graph (`graph.nodes` /
`graph.edges` / `graph.joins`, added by PR #379).

- Usage: `bash hooks/scripts/lib/graph_readiness.sh <path-to-progress.json> <node-id>`
- Prints `ready` or `blocked` to stdout (nothing else), exits 0 when ready,
  1 when blocked (fail-closed, including on any missing-arg/missing-file/
  unparseable-JSON case).
- Readiness predicate: a node is ready iff every incoming edge's `from`
  node has `outcome` in `{done, skipped}` (terminal-success). If the node
  is a join target in `graph.joins` with `mode: "all"`, that join's
  `inputs` list is used instead of raw edges.
- Never writes `progress.json` or any other file — the orchestrator
  remains the sole writer of graph state via `als_atomic_progress_update`,
  once per wave. This is advisory query tooling invoked by the
  orchestrator via `Bash`, not a hook, scheduler, or daemon.

Also adds a new `stale` node `status`/`outcome` enum value — a dispatched
node whose worker went idle without reporting, distinct from a definitive
`failed` outcome or an in-flight `running` one — added additively to
`graph_contract.test.sh`'s existing enum assertion.

## Tests

- `hooks/scripts/tests/graph_readiness.test.sh` (new): single-predecessor
  blocked/ready, two-input `mode:"all"` join blocked/ready, `failed` vs
  `skipped` predecessors, and the new `stale` value inside a join — each
  case paired with an explicit negative control (a fixture that legitimately
  flips the verdict).
- `hooks/scripts/tests/graph_two_unit_fanout.test.sh` (new): end-to-end
  A||B->C fan-out/join acceptance shape, invoking `graph_readiness.sh`
  directly across three simulated wave states (neither done, one done,
  both done) — proves the join blocks until both fan-out inputs are
  terminal-success and releases once they are.
- `hooks/scripts/tests/graph_contract.test.sh` (modified, additive only):
  `stale` added to both the `status` and `outcome` `IN(...)` allowlists.
  Regression-verified still PASSing.
- `hooks/scripts/tests/exec_bit_invariant.test.sh` (modified): added the
  manifest entry for the new `hooks/scripts/lib/graph_readiness.sh`
  (100755 — its call sites in both new test files invoke it as a direct
  path via `bash "$HELPER"`, not a `source`, per that test's own rule).
  This closes a fail-closed-hook-boundary regression this PR would
  otherwise have introduced; confirmed passing (FAILED count 0) after
  the fix.

## Out of scope (follow-up)

Wiring `graph.nodes` to `work_units` is explicitly **not** done in this
PR — that sync is a separate follow-up.

author: jopetty
body:
Stacked on [#281](https://github.com/allenai/olmo-eval/pull/281) (`helmet-plus-recall`) — base is that branch, so this diff shows only the incremental work.

Extends the HELMET integration beyond recall: adds the five ICL tasks and two of the three LongQA tasks, at standard HELMET's 4k–128k lengths. `helmet_all__{size}` now spans 8 tasks across three categories.

| category | tasks | lengths |
|---|---|---|
| recall | `json_kv` | 4k–2m (from #281) |
| longqa | `infbench_qa_eng`, `infbench_choice_eng` | 4k–128k |
| icl | `trec_coarse`, `trec_fine`, `banking77`, `clinic150`, `nlu` | 4k–128k |

These are kept HELMET-namespaced rather than factored into standalone tasks (as RULER was in #276): the length-controlled construction — shot count per length tier, shuffled integer labels, truncation to a token budget — is HELMET's, not a property of the underlying datasets, so they aren't interchangeable with a generic `narrativeqa` or `banking77` task.

## Commits

Each is independently reviewable; metric infrastructure is separate from the tasks that use it.

- `bbcda0c` ICL tasks
- `77472c0` ICL length caveat + measurement script
- `af0bbda` ROUGE-L F1/recall scorers and metrics
- `555bd0f` `infbench_qa_eng`
- `56f7b74` `infbench_choice_eng`

## Things worth a reviewer's attention

**Three ICL source datasets no longer load.** `datasets` 4.0 dropped script-based loading, which HELMET relies on via `trust_remote_code`. `CogComp/trec` and `xingkunliuxtracta/nlu_evaluation_data` are repointed to the Hub's auto-converted `refs/convert/parquet` branches; `banking77` to `legacy-datasets/banking77`, since `PolyAI/banking77` hosts only the loading script and no data. Split sizes and label counts were verified against the values HELMET hardcodes (6/50/77/151/68).

**ICL prompts render ~20% short of nominal.** HELMET fit its shot counts against a Llama-2-era tokenizer, so under Olmo 3 they come out at 0.78–0.85× — `icl_*__4096` is really ~3.2–3.5k tokens, `__131072` is ~104–108k. The counts are kept verbatim anyway so results stay comparable to published HELMET; the shortfall is documented in `helmet_tasks.py`, and `scripts/internal/calibrate_helmet_icl_shots.py` measures it (or generates Olmo-3-calibrated counts, if we ever decide comparability isn't worth it). Note this leaves ICL inconsistent with `json_kv`, which *is* Olmo-3-calibrated — a `helmet_all__4096` average mixes a 4.1k-token task with ~3.3k-token ones.

**LongQA truncates with a fixed reference tokenizer (Llama 2, ungated mirror)**, not the model under test. That's what makes every model see the same text, and it matches HELMET. Same nominal-vs-realized caveat as above.

**Two suite-semantics changes vs #281.** `helmet_all__*` now aggregates *category* suites via `AVERAGE_OF_AVERAGES` rather than flat-averaging tasks — otherwise ICL's five tasks would outweigh recall's one 5:1. And it's only registered where more than one category exists: above 128k only `json_kv` extends, so a combined suite there would be a rename of `helmet_recall__*` whose composition silently differs from the same name at shorter lengths, which is how a length sweep becomes a misleading trend line. Use `helmet_recall__*` for the extended tiers.

**Two deliberate deviations from a literal port of `load_infbench`**, both measured rather than assumed:
- HELMET's `>=65536`-token filter is skipped — it's a no-op (shortest InfiniteBench story is ~78k reference tokens, and HELMET itself calls it "just a sanity step"), which lets us sample first and truncate only the rows we keep instead of tokenizing all 351 book-length contexts.
- Truncation is memoized per distinct context, since 351 questions come from just 69 stories.

Demos are still drawn from the full pool, not the sampled subset, so they don't depend on how many instances are evaluated.

## Verification

- **ROUGE** matches HELMET's `calculate_metrics` byte-for-byte across 5 cases (multi-reference, no-overlap, empty prediction).
- **`InfbenchChoiceScorer`** agrees with HELMET's `choice_post_process` on all 11 cases tried — bare/lowercase/trailing-period letters, prefixed (`Answer: B`), embedded (`The answer is B. Paris`), wrong, and empty.
- **ICL answer parser** is byte-identical to HELMET's `parse_output` across 11 cases.
- **ICL correctness**: each instance's demo labels match that instance's own label permutation and the `answer` field agrees (20/20); deterministic per seed; demo label balance correct.
- **LongQA truncation** lands exactly on budget (3886/3886 at 4k, 65326/65326 at 64k).
- `rouge-score` is the only lockfile addition — verified no other package versions moved.
- ruff, ty, and all 820 existing tests pass.

## Known caveat

`infbench_choice_eng` can render slightly over nominal at the smallest tier (~4109 vs 4096 tokens at 4k) because the options block eats into HELMET's fixed 200-token prompt reserve. This is faithful — HELMET budgets both InfiniteBench subsets identically at `size - 200 - 10` — and is 0.3% at 4k, less above.

## Not included

`narrativeqa` and both Summ tasks (`infbench_sum_eng`, `multi_lexsum`) are LLM-judged in HELMET — `gpt-4-score`/`gpt-4-f1` are their *primary* metrics, so they need judge integration rather than another metric. That's one coherent follow-up.

author: jkreileder
body:
## What

`minimumReleaseAge: "3 days"` (line 66) does not hold back GitHub Actions digest
refreshes, and the blanket `digest`/`pin` automerge rule fires on them immediately. A
compromised upstream action would have landed in CI within hours, with no hold and no
human review.

From Renovate's [minimum-release-age
docs](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/main/docs/usage/key-concepts/minimum-release-age.md):

> Datasources whose timestamps reflect when the matched version was first released (such
> as `github-tags` for digest-pinned GitHub Actions) cannot detect re-published content.
> If an existing tag is force-pushed to new commits, the digest update ages against the
> original release date, so it may pass Minimum Release Age immediately.

`internalChecksFilter: strict` only helps if the payload breaks CI, which a targeted
attack would avoid.

## Scope

I checked each update type against the docs' support table rather than blanket-disabling
automerge:

| Path | Gated today? | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub Actions `digest` | no — ages against original release date | **automerge off** |
| Docker Hub image `digest` | yes — `tag_last_pushed` restarts the hold | unchanged |
| GHCR / Quay `digest` | yes — no timestamp, held under default `timestamp-required` | unchanged |
| `pin` / `pinDigest` | no | unchanged — see below |
| pre-commit hooks | — | unchanged |

`pin` and `pinDigest` are deliberately left alone: both freeze what a reference already
resolves to rather than repointing it, so holding them back would only prolong the
less-safe unpinned state. The pre-commit rule is left alone too — the config comment shows
that was a considered decision.

The new rule gets its own `groupName` so a held actions-digest PR doesn't drag the image
digests out of automerge with it.

## Note on the report's suggested fix

The SAST report proposed adding `"minimumReleaseAge": "3 days"` inside the digests rule.
That's a no-op — it's already inherited from line 66, and inheriting it is exactly what
doesn't work here.

## Verification

`renovate-config-validator --strict` passes at 44.17.0, the version pinned in
`.pre-commit-config.yaml`. (A bare `npx renovate` resolves to an older build that rejects
the existing `managerFilePatterns` fields — worth knowing if you validate by hand.)

author: macieklamberski
body:
This PR adds `surfaceParkedMarkup`, a transform that replaces a lazy-loader container with the original embed markup parked inside it.

A publisher network runs an in-house loader that swaps every third-party embed for `<div class="load-later load-later-vendor-{host}" data-url="{url}" data-content="{percent-encoded original markup}">` and rebuilds it on scroll. A reader runs no JS, so the div renders nothing, and because it holds no text either, `stripEmptyTags` deletes it. The embed arrives as nothing at all, with no link left behind.

`data-content` is the complete original element, so decoding it hands the pipeline exactly the markup every resolver and the cite pass are already written against. Nothing in the transform names a platform: it matches the container, decodes, and replaces. The vendor half of the class is the host with its dots stripped and varies per publisher, so keying on it would mean chasing spellings for no gain. YouTube alone appears as `youtube`, `youtubecom` and `wwwyoutubecom`.

The payload is encoded twice over and both layers have to come off. The outer one is percent-encoding; underneath, the attribute values still carry HTML entities, so `src="https%3A//…/embed/ID%3Fversion=3%26amp%3Brel=1"` only yields the real url if the decoded string goes back through the parser. Reading it with a regex gives a src whose separators are `&`, which no resolver matches.

What the containers become:

- YouTube gets a youtube placeholder holding the id, the canonical watch url, the poster and the player's own 640x360.
- Omny, Spotify and Spreaker get their own placeholders. Their payloads hold the embed iframe, while the container's `data-url` is the page url their resolvers refuse, so these three only work through the markup.
- Twitter, X, TikTok, Instagram and Bluesky have no resolver in the repo, so their quotes stay quotes: the tweet text with its author, date and links, the TikTok caption with its handle and sound, the Instagram permalink, the Bluesky post text. Readable content in place of an empty div.
- Facebook stays nothing. Its payload is `<div class="fb-video" data-href>`, an empty div that nothing claims, so it is deleted exactly as a native Facebook embed is today.

Nothing is added to `embedCarriers`, because a url-only path would have nothing to handle. All 1,589 containers I could read carry `data-content`: 1,048 across the 23 corpus feeds that carry the class, and 541 live across blackamericaweb, bossip, hiphopwired, cassiuslife, newsone, praiseindy and praiserichmond. None carries only `data-url`.

Feeds carrying each vendor class in the corpus: `twittercom` 22, `wwwyoutubecom` 22, `wwwinstagramcom` 19, `youtube` 16, `youtubecom` 8, then Spotify, TikTok, Omny, Bluesky, Facebook, Spreaker and `xcom` at one to five each. `div.load-later` itself is 23 feeds. This is one network's own code and not a plugin anyone else installs, so that population is effectively capped and not growing.

The container's url is kept as a last resort: when the recovered markup states no http url in any attribute, it is appended as a link so the post stays reachable. That never fired on any of the 1,589 containers, since all of them hold a working url somewhere in the payload. I left it in because the failure it covers is a post nobody can reach, and the cost is one attribute walk over markup that only exists inside a container.

Instagram overlaps with #548, which adds `instagramLazyEmbedResolver` for `div.load-later-vendor-wwwinstagramcom[data-url]`. This transform dissolves the container before any resolver sees it, so that selector becomes unreachable once both land and #548's blockquote resolver picks up the recovered quote instead. I left #548 alone so it can merge on its own terms; whichever lands second should drop the lazy selector.

Assignee: [kmmuntasir](https://linear.app/kmmuntasir/profiles/kmmuntasir)

## Summary

Implements `SLYK-0180` — `backend/src/services/dispatcherClient.ts`, slykboard's only outbound path to the dispatcher, per `docs/agentic-automation/07-dispatcher-contract.md` and `03-security.md`.

- `postToDispatcher<T>(path, body, options?)`: serializes the payload **once**, injects a uuid-v4 `idempotencyKey`, and HMAC-SHA256-signs the exact raw bytes with `SLYKBOARD_DISPATCHER_TOKEN` → `X-Slykboard-Signature`. All retries send the identical byte string (re-serialization would break the signature on key-ordering differences).
- `DispatcherError` with `path` / `status` / `detail` (`status: 0` = network-unreachable).
- **Retry semantics**: 5xx and network errors retry 3× with 1s/5s/30s exponential backoff; 4xx never retries; `204` resolves `undefined`, other 2xx parses JSON.
- **Observability**: pino log per attempt — `direction`/`path`/`method`/`status`/`durationMs` + `ticketId`/`traceId` when known. Token and bodies never logged; error details truncated at 200 chars per `03-security.md` § Logging.
- **Test-scaled backoff**: `SLYKBOARD_DISPATCHER_BACKOFF_SCALE` env multiplier (tests use 0.01 → 10ms/50ms/300ms) plus per-call `backoffScale` option — no real 30s waits in CI.

## Testing

`backend/src/services/dispatcherClient.test.ts` — 10 tests against a real `node:http` listener on a random port (scripted status sequences, request recording):

- signs the exact raw bytes (listener recomputes HMAC over received bytes) + success log fields
- nested ticket payloads signed byte-identically
- retries on 500 then succeeds — byte-identical bodies, stable idempotencyKey across attempts
- gives up after 3 retries (4 total attempts) → throws `DispatcherError`
- does NOT retry on 400 (single request) / 409
- 204 → `undefined`
- fresh uuid-v4 `idempotencyKey` per call
- retries on connection-refused → `DispatcherError` status 0
- fails fast without agent-mode config (no request sent)

**Results**: dispatcherClient 10/10 ✅ · full backend suite 930/930 (49 files) ✅ · typecheck both workspaces ✅ · lint/prettier — no new issues (19 lint errors + 11 prettier warnings pre-exist on `main`, all in untouched files) · frontend 1071/1072 (the 1 failure reproduces identically without this branch — pre-existing env-wiring issue, backend-only change)

Closes [KMM-18](https://linear.app/kmmuntasir/issue/KMM-18/slyk-0180-dispatcherclient-service-hmac-signing-retry-logging)

author: skabou
body:
## What this adds

The pathway pipeline is stateless: topic in, pathway out, and the run is forgotten. This adds the other half of the loop — what the student actually did, distilled into a profile that feeds the next generation.

```
topic ─▶ propose ─▶ verify ─▶ graph ─▶ plan ─▶ widget
                                        ▲                │
                                        │                ▼
                              student_profile ◀── interactions (append-only)
```

## The pieces

- **`supabase/schema.sql`** — `pathway_sessions`, an append-only `interactions` stream, `student_profiles`, and a `component_mastery_rollup` view. Append-only is enforced by a trigger rather than convention.
- **`lib/student/profile.ts`** — distillation. Deliberately *no* model call: mastery is Laplace-smoothed accuracy discounted by hint rate, so it is explainable to a teacher ("3 of 4, one hint") and cheap enough to recompute after every widget.
- **`lib/pathway/generate.ts`** — `planPathway` takes an optional profile and injects the weakest components plus demonstrated misconceptions into the planning prompt.
- **`app/learn`** — a student-facing surface with voice intake, alongside the teacher-facing builder on `/`. Same pipeline, same grounding, different audience.
- **`api/telemetry`, `api/student`** — event ingest and anonymous learner creation.

## It is additive

No existing behaviour is removed. Across the four existing files touched, the diff deletes 8 lines and every one is re-emitted in extended form — `onComplete` still fires, the stream loop still runs, `planPathway` just gained a parameter.

Widgets emit events through React context rather than props, so `WidgetRenderer({ spec })` is unchanged and telemetry is inert on `/`. Adding `session` to `PathwayEvent` was caught by the exhaustive reducer switch in `use-pathway-stream.ts`, which is working exactly as intended.

Without Supabase env vars configured, every one of these paths no-ops and the app behaves exactly as it does today.

## Verified

```
POST /api/student   -> anonymous learner
POST /api/pathway   -> 3.NF.A.1, 6 steps, fraction-area-model, session persisted
POST /api/telemetry -> 202, wrong answer + misconception recorded
profile             -> mastery 0.25 (2 attempts, 0 correct), accuracy 0%,
                       confirmedMisconceptions: ["thinks parts need not be equal"]
```

Regenerating the same topic for that student then produced a plan whose **first** listed misconception was "thinks the parts of a fraction do not need to be equal in size" — the one the student had actually demonstrated.

`pnpm build` and `tsc --noEmit` both clean.

## Notes for review

- **`pnpm-lock.yaml` is not included.** It was regenerated locally against a package proxy that quarantines recent releases, so committing it would churn unrelated versions. `pnpm install` after merge.
- Two dependencies added, no existing versions changed: `@supabase/supabase-js`, `motion`.
- Env vars: `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`. The service role key bypasses RLS and is guarded by a `server-only` import.

## Not included

Telemetry is wired into `SwiperFlashcard` only; `FractionAreaModel` still needs its call sites. The pathway is stored as JSONB rather than normalized tables — the Zod schemas are moving fast and this avoids chasing them with migrations. The mastery rollup keys off `interactions.learning_component_id`, a real indexed column, so analytics do not depend on the blob.

author: tanghyd
body:
Based on #31. First of the per-entity splits that #27 set up.

Each of these three entities had its columns declared twice: once in `app/models` as the table, once in `app/schemas` as the class the API used. The two disagreed about which fields a caller must send, because one schema served create, update and response at the same time and so marked almost every field optional.

Each entity now has one module in `app/models` holding the whole family:

| class | what it is |
|---|---|
| `XBase` | the shared field declarations and the input leniency |
| `X` | the table — it takes the plain name that used to belong to the schema |
| `XCreate` | what a caller must send, which is what the columns say |
| `XUpdate` | every field optional again, for a partial update |
| `XPublic` | the response, with `id` required |

The hand-written `from_dbx()` converters are gone: `XPublic.model_validate` reads the ORM object directly. `app/models/types.py` now holds the field types that pin the request and response shapes; `app/schemas/base.py` re-exports them for the schemas that are not converted yet.

The map routes declare `MapCreate` and `response_model=MapPublic`, so the OpenAPI document describes their request and response instead of a bare object.

```
POST /maps  request   before {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": true}
                      after  {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/MapCreate"}
POST /maps  201       before {}
                      after  {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/MapPublic"}
```

**One field is deliberately looser than its column.** `w3cstats.user_id` is `NOT NULL`, but the w3champions sync builds the stats before it knows the user, so `W3CStatsCreate` leaves it out and the service supplies it.

**Verified against the previous head of the stack**

- 91 of 91 GET responses byte-identical, both checkouts on one shared database.
- 93 of 93 write steps identical, including the map create, update, search and delete steps and the numeric-cell case the xlsx import relies on.
- 81 tests pass; ruff clean.
- Table dump: no column, type, nullability, key or foreign key differs. The three tables list `id` after the inherited columns now, because a base class declares its fields first. Column order carries no meaning here and the migrations are unchanged.

author: ehrlinger
body:
Completes the eight-task plan in `docs/plans/2026-08-14-hvtirlifetables-implementation.md`. Tasks 1–5 merged in #1; this is the rest.

## What's here

- **Task 6** — `tests/testthat/test-vintage.R`, the Tier 4 vintage-discrimination tests, plus a README section on `hmatched` units.
- **Task 7** — the release gate: `_pkgdown.yml` and a full CRAN Cookbook audit.
- **Task 8** — `HANDOFF.md` and design-spec status brought up to date.

## Why Task 6 exists

These tests catch exactly one regression: **a refactor that silently ignores `vintage`.** That failure would pass every other test in the suite — invariants, the `_STATUS_` regression, and even the study's own SAS acceptance check, which uses a single vintage. Three of the four blocks fail under it; the fourth is an honest 27-stratum evaluability sweep that doesn't claim otherwise.

## Release gate

Built from a clean `git archive` export, checked **with** the manual:

| | |
|---|---|
| `R CMD check --as-cran` | 0 errors, 0 warnings, **1 NOTE** |
| The note | `New submission` — unavoidable for a package not yet on CRAN |
| Plain `R CMD check` | `Status: OK` |
| PDF + HTML manual | both build (so no raw Unicode in `.Rd`) |
| Tarball | 30,779 bytes (limit 5 MB) |
| Check time | 49.7s (budget 10 min) |
| Tests | 434 assertions, output pristine |
| `.sas7bdat` in the export | zero |

## Two judgement calls worth a reviewer's attention

**`hmatched` is per year regardless of `scale=`.** This follows `usmatchd.sas:227`, which assigns `_HAZARD` with no `SCALEF` multiplication, rather than the design spec and the macro's own header comment at line 47 — both of which claim the opposite. Bit-fidelity to the macro is the acceptance criterion. Documented in the README and recorded as the one deliberate spec deviation.

**The pkgdown site URL is deliberately not in `DESCRIPTION`.** `pkgdown::check_pkgdown()` wants it there; `R CMD check --as-cran` fetches every `DESCRIPTION` URL and the gh-pages site is not published, so adding it produces a 404. The two checks cannot both pass until the site is live. Resolved in favour of the release gate; the coupling is recorded in `_pkgdown.yml` so the next person doesn't rediscover it by breaking the gate.

## Still outstanding, by design

- **Tier 3 SAS acceptance** — reproducing a real `%usmatchd` run to 1e-12, reported per stratum. PHI-adjacent, so it lives in the study's `R_parity`, not here.
- **CI** — blocked. CRAN's `TemporalHazard` is 1.1.0 while `DESCRIPTION` requires `>= 1.2.0`; any workflow fails at dependency install. The bound is real — the evaluator calls `hzr_decompos_g3()`, absent in 1.1.0.

author: tohaua
body:
## Why

Every Release run emits:

> Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24: `mathieudutour/github-tag-action@a22cf08...` (v6.2)

The action is pinned at its latest release (v6.2), and even its default branch still declares `using: node20` and hasn't changed since June 2024 — so there is no upstream version to bump to. The only fix is to replace the action.

## What

Swap `mathieudutour/github-tag-action` for [`ietf-tools/semver-action`](https://github.com/ietf-tools/semver-action) (`v1.11.0`, Node 24, actively maintained).

`semver-action` only **computes** the next version; it doesn't create the tag. So this also adds an explicit lightweight-tag push step, preserving the previous design where the `resolve` job creates the tag that the `goreleaser`/`docker` jobs check out via `refs/tags/${version}`.

## Behavior preserved

- `minorList: feat` / `patchList: fix, perf` mirror the previous angular-preset bumping (`feat`→minor, `fix`/`perf`→patch, everything else no release). Explicit lists avoid the action's broader defaults (which also bump on `refactor`/`test`).
- `noNewCommitBehavior: silent` + `noVersionBumpBehavior: silent` leave the `next` output **empty** when nothing qualifies (verified in the action source) — matching the old empty-`new_tag` → `proceed=false` "nothing to release" path.
- Dry run still computes the version without tagging or releasing.
- `push:` tag trigger path is unaffected.

## Verification

- Dispatch Release with `dry_run: true` from `main`: the compute step logs the next version, no tag is pushed, jobs are skipped.
- Dispatch a real release after a `fix:`/`feat:` commit lands: `resolve` pushes the new tag, `proceed=true`, and `goreleaser`/`docker` run.

author: fponticelli
body:
Closes #155.

Clicking a button **inside** an open popover could close it. Dismissing an overlay calls `els.anchor?.focus()` to restore focus to its trigger; that trigger is outside every *sibling* layer, so the sibling's `focusin` watcher read the engine's own bookkeeping as a user interaction and dismissed too.

## Direction chosen — option 2, implemented as a scoped re-entrancy counter

The issue listed three directions. What the code says about each:

**Chosen: restrict the `focusin`-driven outside path so focus moves originating from a layer's own machinery do not count.** There is nothing on a `FocusEvent` that identifies its origin — no `relatedTarget` pattern separates "the engine restored the trigger" from "the user Tabbed to the trigger" — so the origin has to be *declared* at the source. `utils/engine-focus.ts` is that declaration: a depth counter raised across the synchronous `.focus()` call, and `watchInteractOutside`'s `handleFocus` (and only `handleFocus`) returns early while it is up. Every focus move the overlay machinery makes as its own bookkeeping now goes through it:

| site | file |
| --- | --- |
| teardown restore to the anchor | `utils/overlay-engine.ts` (used by `menu`/`menubar`/`context-menu`/`select`/`combobox`/`searchable-select`) |
| `dismiss.extra` restore to the trigger | `components/popover.ts` |
| focus trap activate + release | `utils/focus-trap.ts` (`dialog`/`drawer`/`alert-dialog`) |
| focus-on-open | `utils/overlay-engine.ts` (defensive — see below) |

**Rejected — a re-entrancy flag suppressing outside-interaction dispatch generally.** Same mechanism, wrong blast radius: it would also mute the `pointerdown` path, and a real click *can* land during a teardown (`popover`'s `extra` runs `anchor.focus()` synchronously inside the outside handler, so app code on `focusin` runs while the engine is still unwinding). Muting a genuine click there is exactly the over-suppression the issue warns about. The guard therefore gates the focus path only, and there is a test that a pointerdown delivered mid-restore still dismisses.

**Rejected — ordering the cascade so a dismissal's side effects settle first.** Ordering does not help: the sibling is not being offered the original pointerdown, it is being offered a *new* `focusin` event that the engine itself generated. Deferring the cascade changes when that event is observed, not whether. To fix the bug, ordering would have to swallow the event — i.e. it collapses into suppression anyway, with a worse (asynchronous) suppression window.

### The suppression window, stated precisely

The guard is held for **one synchronous turn**, and that turn is the whole **synchronous transitive closure** of the `.focus()` call — *not* just the call itself. `HTMLElement.focus()` dispatches `focus`/`focusin` synchronously from inside itself, so every `focusin` listener the move triggers runs while the counter is up, including arbitrary **consumer** code and the full TEA `send`/reduce/commit cycles it drives. That is not narrowable: there is no point between "raise the counter" and "`focusin` listeners run" at which it could be lowered.

**The safety-relevant half holds.** No *user* event can be delivered into the window — there is no `await`, timer or microtask in it, so the event loop is never free to run. Nothing a user did is ever suppressed.

**The accepted cost is consumer re-entrancy.** An app `focusin` listener that itself moves focus during an engine restore has its own (non-engine) move swallowed too. Measured: with a listener that calls `elsewhere.focus()` when the upper popover's trigger receives the restore, the final state is `activeElement: elsewhere | lower open: true` — an open popover with focus resting outside it. On `main` the lower popover would have dismissed. The state is **recoverable**: the guard is released the moment the outermost engine call returns, and the next genuine focus move dismisses as usual (verified).

### The rest of why the window is narrow rather than a blunt mute

- **`pointerdown` is never gated**, so a genuine click during a teardown still dismisses every layer it is outside of.
- **It is depth-counted, not a boolean** — a trap release nested inside an overlay restore must not clear the guard early for the outer move.
- **User-driven moves stay out of it even where the engine picks the destination**: the focus trap's Tab/Shift+Tab wrap and the roving/list-navigation focus in `roving.ts`/`table.ts`/`pagination.ts`/`tags-input.ts` are deliberately *not* wrapped — a layer the user Tabs out of must still dismiss.

## Accepted consequence: a modal no longer excludes a non-modal layer beneath it (#171)

Because the popover is no longer dismissed when a dialog's focus trap activates, a **programmatically** opened modal can coexist with a fully interactive non-modal layer. Measured (jsdom probe, and independently in real Chromium by the reviewer):

```
popover open: true | positioner aria-hidden: null | positioner inert: false | activeElement: dlg-action
```

The popover's positioner is not `aria-hidden`, not `inert`, and is Tab-reachable from inside the modal (via the `focus` nested-layer aspect in `focus-trap.ts`). **A modal that does not exclude the layer beneath it is not really modal** — that is the a11y cost, and it is stated here rather than left implicit.

**It is kept, for three reasons.**

1. **The cause is elsewhere and pre-existing.** The exemption comes from the FLAT `nested-layer.ts` registry: a lookup has no notion of which layer asked, so a modal's `hide`/`focus` sweep exempts *every* registered layer, nested inside it or not. `nested-layer.ts`'s own module comment already documents this shape of limit for the `outside` aspect; this is the same limit landing on `focus` + `hide`.
2. **`main` reaches the same state.** What this PR removed was only an *accidental* mitigation — the trap's own `focusin` misread as a user interaction, i.e. the very defect being fixed — and an unreliable one. Measured both ways with a jsdom probe:

   | modal content | popover after a programmatic modal open, pre-PR (guard removed) | post-PR |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | has a focusable control | dismissed (the accidental mitigation) | stays open, interactive |
   | **no focusable control** | **stays open, interactive** | stays open, interactive |

   So the state is reachable on `main` today with a focusable-free modal. This PR widens the set of configurations that reach it; it did not create it.
3. **The narrow patch is worse.** Having `pushFocusTrap` dismiss the dismissable layers below it regresses nested dialogs: the inner dialog's trap pushes *before* the inner dialog's own dismissable layer, so it would dismiss the OUTER dialog.

It is narrow: it needs a **programmatic** modal open. A `pointerdown` on the dialog's trigger goes through the un-gated pointer path and dismisses the popover first.

The real fix is the per-layer registry that `nested-layer.ts` already names as the shape that removes the flat-registry limits ("is this nested inside *me*?"). Filed as **#171**. The consequence is named in the test title, explained in a comment above it, and **asserted** (`aria-hidden` null, `inert` absent), so a future change that fixes it flips a deliberate assertion rather than quietly passing.

## Tests

`test/components/overlay-nested-layer.integration.test.ts` — the existing case `a pointerdown inside the lower sibling popover dismisses the upper one` now runs at the **production default** `restoreFocus: true` on both popovers (the `restoreFocus: false` workaround, added purely to isolate the outside-click path from this bug, is gone) and asserts the upper dismisses **and the lower survives**. That is the headline test.

`test/components/overlay-engine-focus.integration.test.ts` (new) — one app per focus-moving site:

- `a click inside a popover does not close that popover when it dismisses a layer above` — popover + **menu** above it, menu trigger outside the popo

body:
## Summary

Closes `/tools edit`, the second-to-last remaining Step 21 backlog row (`docs/PLAN.md` §13), continuing directly from the audit (#132), revive (#133), and delete (#134) slices already merged.

Unlike those three prior slices, this one required resolving two new architectural questions:

### 1. Reusing `tool_edit.go`'s own vetted safety checks, not duplicating them

`tools.ToolEdit.Run`'s own flow depends on two **unexported** `internal/tools` helpers — `parseManifest` and `checkManifestSafety` — that enforce §19.8's egress-allowlist and structural-exfiltration hard blocks on the edited result. Every prior slice (audit/revive/delete) was built entirely from *exported* functions `internal/app`'s `toolsLister` could call directly.

Rather than widen `internal/tools`' exported surface around a security-sensitive check just for this one caller, `ToolsLister.EditTool` constructs a real `tools.ToolEdit{Dir, Allow, AllowAll}` value and calls its `Run` method directly through the generic `Tool` interface — reusing the entire vetted code path, safety check included, instead of duplicating any part of it.

### 2. Threading the egress allowlist through without a breaking constructor change

`EditTool` needs `config.Tools.Egress.Allow`/`AllowAll`, which `toolsLister` never previously carried. Growing `NewToolsLister`'s existing signature would have broken its one production call site plus ~26 existing test call sites. Instead, added an additive `NewToolsListerWithEgress(dir, enabled, allow, allowAll)` constructor; `NewToolsLister` is now a thin wrapper over it (`allow=nil, allowAll=false`), so every pre-existing call site keeps compiling unchanged.

### 3. A new multi-line slash-command input convention

`/tools edit` needs three human-typed fields (`name`, `old_string`, `new_string`) that don't fit a single space-separated line. `parseToolsEditArg` recognizes:

```
/tools edit <name>
<old_string, one or more lines>
---
<new_string, zero or more lines>
[replace_all]
```

Typed via the TUI's existing `ctrl+j`-inserts-newline mechanism (never submits); `slash.Parse`'s single-space-cut behavior already lets this multi-line string survive intact into `runToolsCommand`.

No confirmation gate is needed (unlike delete): `tool_edit.go`'s own hard blocks already refuse anything dangerous before a byte reaches disk, and the resulting demotion to `unverified` is itself the safety net.

## Files changed
- `internal/tui/tools.go` — `ToolsLister` gains `EditTool`
- `internal/app/toolslister.go` — `EditTool` impl + `NewToolsListerWithEgress`
- `internal/app/app.go` — production call site updated to thread egress config
- `internal/tui/toolscmd.go` — `parseToolsEditArg` + dispatch branch
- `internal/tui/toolscmd_internal_test.go` — `fakeToolsLister.EditTool`, `typeToolsEditAndEnter` helper, dispatch tests, `parseToolsEditArg` table (12 cases)
- `internal/app/toolslister_test.go` — real `t.TempDir()` round-trip tests (10 new cases)
- `docs/PLAN.md` — closed the `/tools edit` row, new Bitácora entry

## Testing
- `gofmt -l .` clean
- `go build ./...` OK
- `go vet ./...` clean
- `go test ./...` green across all 25 packages
- `go test -race ./internal/tui/... ./internal/app/...` green
- `TestTUINoImportaHTTP`/`TestProviderNoImportaPresentacion` (§6.1 architecture boundary) explicitly re-run and passing

## Remaining Step 21 work
`/tools create [--force]` is the one remaining backlog row — needs its own governance-gate UI design (structured multi-field input or text-based manifest spec, plus the `--force` bypass-and-log behavior), a separate increment.

author: brandonrc
body:
## Summary

Four related 1.8.0 bugs across blob lifecycle, storage accounting and proxy-cache catalog correctness. They are grouped because three of them share one root cause — a column or a query that means something different from what its consumer assumes — and the fourth (S3) is a one-method parity fix that the streaming conversions keep widening.

Fixes #3285
Fixes #3286
Fixes #2927
Fixes #3305

---

### #3285 — blob GC readiness gate can never open

`backend/src/services/manifest_blob_refs_backfill.rs`

The gate (`any_live_manifest_missing_refs`) was strictly **wider** than the backfill candidate set (`select_unbackfilled_manifests`): the gate `UNION`ed in `oci_manifest_refs.child_digest` for every tagged parent, while the candidate query selected only *tagged* digests — and an index child carries no tag of its own. A child without `manifest_blob_refs` rows therefore pinned the gate `true` with no way for any backfill to clear it. The startup backfill logged `candidates_scanned=0 edges_inserted=0` while `BLOB_GC_ENABLED=true` stayed a permanent no-op; storage GC still hard-deleted the soft-deleted `artifacts` rows, so the database converged while object storage grew without bound (the reporter kept an external SQL + S3 `DeleteObjects` job and reclaimed 2.27 TiB of 3.44 TiB by hand).

Both queries — plus the new diagnostic — are now built from one shared relation (`LIVE_IMAGE_MANIFEST_SET_SQL` → `unbackfilled_live_manifests(alias)`), so "the gate can only be held closed by something the backfill also selects" is structural rather than a convention. A unit test asserts the three query builders all contain that relation byte-for-byte.

The shared set adds index children, but **only** where a live `artifacts` row in the *same repository* sits at `oci-manifests/<child_digest>`. That is the locality proof the original design was missing: the module docs correctly refused to backfill a bare `oci_manifest_refs` edge because on a shared cloud namespace it would import another repository's manifest and later authorize digest fallback through the wrong repository. An `artifacts` row is proof this repository actually committed that body (both the push path and the proxy path write it), so reading it back is safe. `idx_artifacts_storage_key` already exists, so the join is an index scan — **no migration**.

Consequently a merely-referenced child is now in **neither** set. This is the proxy case the issue called out: a proxy cache legitimately holds only the architecture it was asked for, so the arm64 child of a tagged index can never be backfilled, and it no longer gates. With no manifest body there are no local blobs attributable to it that a sweep could wrongly reclaim. Nested indexes are excluded from the child arm by the same structural guard #1409 applies to tagged indexes.

Also adds the operator escape hatch the issue asked for: `list_live_manifests_missing_refs` (bounded by `LIMIT`), wired into the scheduler's per-tick gate warning so it names up to 20 `digest@repository` pairs instead of leaving the operator to reconstruct both queries by hand.

**Interaction with open PR #3385** (`fix/gc: singleton-lease the scheduled storage GC tick`): both touch `scheduler_service.rs`, but different regions — #3385's hunks end at the storage-GC `lease.release()` around old line 412, and mine is a 10-line insert inside the existing blob-GC `Ok(true)` arm around old line 448, roughly 35 lines later. No textual conflict at 3 lines of context, and no shared symbol: #3385 adds a `SchedulerLease` around `run_gc()` and a migration (196, which this PR does **not** claim), while this PR only enriches an existing `tracing::warn!`. Whichever lands second should be a clean rebase; if it is not, the correct resolution is to keep both.

### #3286 — storage accounting double-counts OCI layers

`backend/src/services/storage_stats_service.rs`, `backend/src/services/oci_migration_reindex.rs`

`REPO_OBJECT_UNION_SQL` unioned live `artifacts` with `oci_blobs` on the premise (from #3134) that a Docker/OCI repository contributes only a few KiB of manifests through `artifacts`. It does not: `artifacts.size_bytes` for an image manifest is `oci_v2::manifest_total_size(body)` — `config.size` plus the sum of `layers[].size`, the aggregate **image** size — written that way deliberately because GC, quota and scanning enumerate that table. Every layer was therefore counted once through the inflated manifest row and again through `oci_blobs`: 3097 GB of `unique_bytes` against 1.14 TiB of real bucket usage, a 2.7x over-report on a metric an operator reasonably reads as deduplicated physical usage.

`oci-manifests/%` rows are excluded from the physical union. Of the three directions the issue offered, this is the one that does not move any other invariant:

- **Rewriting `artifacts.size_bytes` to the object size was rejected on purpose.** That is the column `RepositoryService::check_quota` sums, so it would have silently loosened every OCI repository's quota — a behaviour change with no upgrade signal.
- **Quota enforcement is unchanged in both directions.** `check_quota` reads the live logical `SUM` over `artifacts` and never consulted this accounting layer (#2056 §7).
- **Upgrade impact:** reported storage drops sharply on OCI-heavy instances at the next stats refresh. That is the correction landing, not data loss; nothing is deleted. Stated explicitly in the CHANGELOG.
- The manifest JSON documents themselves are no longer counted — a bounded, documented undercount (~164 MB across 56k manifests on the reporting instance, ~0.01%), since no column holds their true object size.
- `PATH_REF_UNION_SQL` is deliberately **unchanged**: it drives the *logical* per-path tree, where an image node is expected to weigh the image, and it excludes layer blobs entirely, so it has no double count to correct. A test pins that asymmetry so a future edit does not "helpfully" align them.

The same conflated column also produced the `oci_migration_reindex` false positives the issue mentions: its cheap pre-read guard compared the 4 MiB *object* cap against the image size and skipped 8,069 ordinary manifests with `manifest body exceeds 4194304 bytes (got 322036591); refusing to buffer`. `oci-manifests/%` rows now skip that pre-read guard and are bounded by the unconditional post-read `body.len()` cap like every other manifest — the authoritative check was always the second one.

A `const _: () = assert!(prefix_matches("oci-manifests/"))` guard pins the SQL literal to `storage::keys::OCI_MANIFEST_STORAGE_PREFIX`, the same pattern `storage_gc_service` uses.

### #3305 — proxy-cache catalog backfill cannot repair the placeholder it races

`backend/src/services/proxy_catalog.rs`

`record_proxy_download` is awaited **inline on the request** and inserts a `size_bytes = 0` / NULL-checksum placeholder so the first download counts (#2537). `spawn_lazy_catalog_backfill` runs detached and therefore normally *loses* that race, and its `ON CONFLICT` arm bumped only `last_accessed_at` — so the losing backfill returned without ever writing the real size, checksum or content type, and nothing else repaired the row. The #2218/#2270 self-healing was inert for exactly the pre-catalog entries it exists for, and storage accounting read zeros for them (which is why this sits next to #3286).

The conflict arm now repairs a row that is still a placeholder and continues to leave every authoritative row untouched. The predicate requires **both** `size_bytes = 0` and a NULL checksum, mirrored in Rust as `is_placeholder_catalog_row` so it has one testable statement: a genuinely cached zero-byte object carries its checksum and is never mistaken for a placeholder.

**This builds on #3289 and does not undo its bounding.** The semaphore, the `try_acquire_owned`, and the threaded-through `CacheMetadata` are untouched — a backfill skipped under saturation still simply retries on the next hit. #3289 made the backfill more likely to *win* the race;

author: umanggarg28
body:
The agent proposes edits to its own skills and you approve them — but nothing ever checked whether an approved edit **helped**. `skill_hn_ai_summary` is on **version 12**. Twelve edits, zero evidence.

## What it does

Runs are stamped with the skill version that produced them (the same move that made `by_model` work), scorecards slice `by_version`, and `compare_versions` grades the two most recent versions:

> `v7 → v8` **regressed** `-2` · *Cost per run regressed 102%; contract compliance worse by 17%.* (9 vs 6 runs)

**The verdict is computed, never model-generated.** The model wrote the edit; letting it grade its own edit reintroduces exactly the unverified self-report the rest of the harness exists to remove.

## Most of this PR is refusing to answer

Driving it against real data produced three unrelated skills all "regressing" with ~2000% guard-fire increases. That wasn't three bad edits — it was three bugs, each of which would have shipped a confident lie:

**1. Events had no task attribution.** `_events_between` windowed purely by time, and the heartbeat interleaves tasks. One reflection tick looping on one skill put **214 guard fires (216 of 236, all on Aug 10) inside every other task's window.** Events now carry a `task` stamp via `events.task_context`; cross-task events are excluded; guard counts predating the stamp are reported but never scored.

**2. Every version boundary straddles the Aug 1 model swap**, so cost deltas were measuring the swap, not the edit. Runs are filtered to the newer version's model; pre-tracking runs group under `""` and compare against nothing.

**3. Infra failures counted against edits.** `partial` runs are excluded — a six-day mail outage is not an edit's fault.

Plus a floor of 3 clean runs a side, else `inconclusive`.

**After all three corrections, every live comparison reads `inconclusive`.** That is the honest answer, and I'd rather ship that than the version of this PR that told you your edits broke three skills. Real verdicts appear as runs accumulate under the current model.

## Backfill

Version history records when each version went live, so pre-stamping runs are attributed by timestamp (`infer_skill_version`) instead of waiting days. Runs older than the first archived version belong to version 0 and are never credited to the first edit.

## Frontend

A `SkillEvolution` panel on each eval scorecard: `v3 → v4`, verdict badge (reserved status color + icon + word, never color alone), the score, the plain-language headline, per-metric deltas, and the run counts it's based on.

## Boy-scout

- `_RunAggregate` — the five metric properties were duplicated across two aggregates; a third was about to be added.
- `_apply_usage` — the append and retrofit paths in `tasks.py` had byte-identical copies of the same field mapping, which is how a retrofitted run would have silently lost the new version stamp.

## Gates

ruff clean · pyright 0 errors · `tsc --noEmit` clean · vite build clean · 1191 passed, 32 skipped · coverage 69.53%
