author: luisgamas
body:
## The bug

A conversation started on Codex **from the phone could not be opened anywhere else**: Codex Desktop (and an IDE, and `codex resume`) reported it as not available.

**Codex grants exactly one writer per thread**, held for as long as that thread is loaded in a process. The bridge kept one long-lived `codex app-server`, so every conversation the phone had ever touched stayed locked — on the reporter's machine by an app-server process that had been idle for two days.

## What changed

The app-server now lives **for the turn**, and is released as soon as no turn is in flight; the next turn re-attaches with `thread/resume`.

Measured against codex-cli 0.147.0, running two app-servers against one thread:

| Attempt | Result |
|---|---|
| Second client resumes while the bridge holds the thread | `already has an active writer` |
| Holder calls `thread/unsubscribe`, second client retries | **still refused** — replies `{status:'unsubscribed'}` but the thread stays in `thread/loaded/list` and the writer stays held |
| Holder's process exits, second client retries | resumes immediately |

So ending the process is the handover. Cost: ~250 ms respawn + ~200–750 ms resume (upper end on a 7 166-line rollout), once per turn.

Same root cause, same set:

- a turn whose thread another Codex client holds **names that client** instead of surfacing the protocol error; a rollout deleted elsewhere continues in a fresh thread instead of dead-ending;
- `thread/start` sets `threadSource: 'user'` — every first-party Codex client does, the app-server otherwise leaves it unset;
- the conversation's **name is mirrored** onto the Codex thread (`thread/name/set`), so it is no longer untitled there;
- a **restarted bridge adopts the persisted native session** instead of opening a new one behind a history the phone still shows;
- the **access mode rides on every resume**, so changing it mid-conversation applies from the next turn — closes that `FOR-DEV` item (verified live: the rollout's `turn_context` flips from `never`/`read-only` to `on-request`/`workspace-write`).

Mobile carries one copy fix: the Session info sheet said the ids were for "the agent's CLI"; they open the agent's desktop app too, and the hint now names the one condition that matters.

## Verification

- Bridge suite **657 passing** (was 649; 8 new tests), `tsc` clean, prettier clean.
- Mobile **1038 passing**, `flutter analyze` clean, l10n regenerated.
- **End-to-end against the real CLI**: a turn through the patched adapter → the process is gone once it completes → another client opens the conversation → a second turn resumes the same Codex thread and answers. The reverse conflict was driven live too and reports the friendly message.

## Docs / spec synced in the same set

`architecture/02a` §5.8.8 (new *the other direction* subsection + `adoptNativeSession`), `02a` implemented-agents list, `02b` Codex approval transport, `00-index` convergence row, `bridge/docs/agents.md` (new *Codex holds one writer per thread* section, wired-agents table, naming), `bridge/FOR-DEV.md`, both CHANGELOGs.

Mirrors the earlier `WebExtractorKit` and `LLMClientKit` lifts.

author: ddvdozuki
body:
## What broke

`terraform-aws-modules/eks/aws` 21.25.0 was published 2026-08-14T20:49:45Z and raised its aws provider floor from `>= 6.52` to `>= 6.59`. `terraform/physical` constrained the module as `~> 21.0`, which accepts any 21.x, so every fresh `tofu init` picked up 21.25.0 and failed against the committed `.terraform.lock.hcl` (aws 6.56.0):

```
Could not resolve provider hashicorp/aws: locked provider
registry.opentofu.org/hashicorp/aws 6.56.0 does not match configured version
constraint >= 3.29.0, ..., >= 6.56.0, >= 6.59.0
```

Not env-specific. Any stack doing a fresh physical init could not resolve providers at all, so it blocked every infra change touching physical.

## The fix

Pin the module to exact `21.24.0` - the version that resolved and applied cleanly on production stacks earlier the same day, before 21.25.0 existed. This leaves the aws provider where it is. The alternative, refreshing the lockfile to aws >= 6.59, is a fleet-wide provider bump and does not belong in a hotfix.

## Verification

Reproduced and fixed locally, both directions:

- at the current constraint, `tofu init -backend=false` fails with the error above
- with this pin, init succeeds, resolving eks **21.24.0** against aws **6.56.0**

The lockfile is untouched, so the provider-lock platform-coverage property is unaffected.

## Note for operators

author: nagwww
body:
## What

Follow-up to #26. That PR filled the 2026 gap in `iam_credentials` but left `s3_leaks` ending at `2025-09`, on the basis that the 2026 bucket leaks I'd found were Azure and R2 rather than S3. That conclusion was wrong — it reflected the shape of my searches, not the state of the world. A second sweep aimed specifically at S3 turned up two named 2026 exposures.

| Date | Org | Scale | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jun 2026 | **Carla** (car rental aggregator, 180 countries) | ~48,000 booking confirmation PDFs | [Cybernews](https://cybernews.com/security/carla-car-rental-data-leak/) |
| Mar 2026 | **Fatal Model** (Brazil's largest escort platform) | 18M+ records, 3.5M files, ~700 GB | [Website Planet](https://www.websiteplanet.com/news/fatalmodel-leak-report/) |

**Carla** — discovered 3 June 2026 by the Cybernews research team. Booking confirmations exposed names, emails, phone numbers, booking numbers, rental dates, costs and pickup locations. The bucket was live, taking several hundred new files a day. Access was restricted after notification and no misuse was found. Worth noting the specific risk: rental dates tell an attacker exactly when someone's home is empty.

**Fatal Model** — reported 24 March 2026 by Jeremiah Fowler. Two non-password-protected databases (the logging DB alone ~14.7M records / ~19.17 GB) plus AWS cloud storage holding 3.5M+ files at ~700 GB. Escort photos, application and development files, admin access tokens, user device data, names, emails and user IDs. The logging database was secured on discovery, but the AWS storage stayed open until a responsible disclosure notice was sent — and that logging database also exposed the AWS access keys for the storage account, which is why this one straddles both tables.

## Verification note, and what this PR does not claim

Network egress to news domains is still blocked in this environment, so as with #26 I could not open any source page directly; details come from search results and Link Check confirms the URLs resolve.

That caveat earned its keep here. On this sweep the search layer returned, with confident dates attached, several incidents that are **not** 2026 and are excluded:

- **Artwork Archive** (421 GB, misconfigured S3) — actually July 2021
- **PeopleGIS / 80+ US municipalities** and **Cosmolog Kozmetik** (567k customers) — both 2021
- **IMDataCenter** — surfaced as "January 2026", actually July 2025
- **HireClick** (5.7M resume files, open S3) — February 2025
- **Xobin** (523k applicants) — August 2024, and Google Cloud Storage rather than S3

Each was checked against a second search before being dropped. The two entries in this PR are the ones whose 2026 dates held up.

I would **not** treat `s3_leaks` as complete for 2026 even now. Two named exposures across eight months is well below this list's historical rate, and the same search bias that hid these two from the first pass may still be hiding others. Anyone with unrestricted network access sweeping Cybernews, Website Planet and Hackread month by month would likely find more.

## Checks

- `python scripts/generate_readme.py --check` reports Readme1.md in sync with incidents.yaml
- `Readme1.md` changes are generated only — two new rows at the top of the S3 table
- Categories reuse existing vocabulary (`Travel & Hospitality`, `Technology`)

author: dhk
body:
## Summary

Closes #104.

`claude-opus-5` was missing from `pricing.py`'s `RATES` while it was the default model, so ~99% of turns on a current machine were unpriced. `estimate_cost_usd` correctly returned `None` rather than a silent `$0.00`, so surfaces rendered `?` — but that left the cost half of the tool blank behind a UI where every other column stayed fully populated. `trend` showed a run of `?` days next to a couple of priced older ones.

Three changes, the last two structural:

**1. The rate.** `claude-opus-5` at $5/$25 per MTok, verified against Anthropic's published pricing the same way `claude-sonnet-5`'s entry was for #47 — not inferred from the 4.x line.

**2. Unpriced models name themselves.** Parsing records *which* model id had no rate (`Unit.own_unpriced_model` → `Turn.unpriced_models` → `TranscriptTailer.unpriced_models()`), and the live table, `chapters`, `chapters --all`, `rollup`, `trend`, and the trend HTML report all name it. This is the part that matters most for preventing a repeat: "some models unpriced" reads identically at 0.1% and at 99%, and never hinted which one-line `RATES` entry was missing — which is why the gap survived weeks.

The names go in a **table caption**, not the ~12-char cost cell, where a model name just gets ellipsized (`claude-opus…`). Verified against a synthetic transcript:

```
│          │ TOTAL  │  240,000 │  6,000 │      $0.9250 │
│          │        │          │        │ (some models │
│          │        │          │        │    unpriced) │
└──────────┴────────┴──────────┴────────┴──────────────┘
   Unpriced (no rate in pricing.py, shown as "?"): claude-opus-6
```

**3. A variant id never silently inherits the base rate.** `rate_for` split on `-`, so a bracketed context variant (`claude-opus-5[1m]`) returned `None` even with the base model priced. It now resolves — but only for models flagged `flat_long_context`, i.e. confirmed to serve their full context window at standard pricing. Anything else stays deliberately unpriced, and only a token-count marker counts as a context variant, so a suffix like `[fast]` (priced well above standard) can't be mistaken for one and billed at half its real cost.

The `unknown_model_cost` flag stays alongside the model names rather than being replaced by them: cost can be unknown for reasons that name no model, such as an unreadable subagent transcript. Collapsing the two would make "no names" mean "everything priced", which is wrong.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest` — 628 passed, 1 skipped (18 new tests across `test_pricing.py`, `test_transcript.py`, `test_trend.py`, `test_cli.py`)
- [x] `python -m compileall -q work_ledger`
- [x] Coverage 78% against CI's `--cov-fail-under=65`
- [x] Ran the real CLI against a synthetic transcript, not just tests: the Opus 5 day went from `?` to `$0.9250` in both the live table and `trend`, and both named the remaining unpriced model
- [x] Rebased onto current `main` (post-#102) — no conflicts

Docs updated per `CLAUDE.md`'s placement rule: `ROADMAP.md` (Quality/Infra), `docs/architecture.md` (the `pricing.py` seam and its two new structural rules), `docs/commands.md` (what `?` means and how to fix it).

## Deliberately not included

The rollup **CSV** output already carries `unknown_model_cost` but not the model names — adding a column is a breaking format change that seemed worth asking about rather than assuming. The `--json` output does carry the names.

body:
## What changed
- replace transaction-level model samples with one point-in-time `Opportunity` row per `(company_id, next executable session)`
- collapse same-company source rows on the same publication day before market lookups, then merge Friday/weekend/holiday slices that still resolve to the same execution session
- use the latest public trigger in the opportunity as the PIT decision boundary and build one aligned forward label
- keep every canonical source event untouched and persist `trigger_event_ids` on the training row for provenance
- aggregate newly public trigger counts/values/actors/semantics/topics instead of choosing one arbitrary source row
- use company-balanced LightGBM sample weights by default so prolific filers do not dominate train/validation loss
- report raw trigger count, aggregated trigger count, opportunity row count, and trigger-per-opportunity statistics
- document the architecture in `docs/opportunity-dataset.md`

## Why
The first real insider-only baseline had 136,184 transaction-level rows and the permutation null exposed heavy pseudo-replication: the fitted model produced only 426 executable trades while randomized score assignment produced ~1,521 trades because many high scores were clustered on duplicate/near-duplicate same-company opportunities. The correct ML unit is the tradable opportunity, not an individual Form 4 transaction line.

## Point-in-time safety
- canonical event storage is unchanged
- company/security mapping remains fail-closed
- one opportunity is formed only from events public before the same conservative next-session execution point
- historical feature builders still filter to `public_time <= opportunity decision_time`
- one forward label is attached only after the PIT feature snapshot is complete
- Congress remains disabled by default

## Expected next physical test
Rebuild the same 41-ticker LightGBM development baseline into a fresh output directory, compare raw trigger count vs opportunity row count/runtime, then rerun validation-rank and permutation-null diagnostics on the new artifacts.

body:
## 1. User/business problem

A market leasing profile (renewal probability, downtime, free rent, TI, LC — the assumptions that drive rollover) has always been model-scoped. Every new acquisition means re-typing the firm's standard leasing assumptions by hand, with no way to keep them consistent across a portfolio or update them once and have new deals start from the current version.

## 2. Why this belongs in the acquisition workflow

Priority 1 of the milestone: finish and harden the growth curve library, then extend the exact same pattern to the next reusable assumption family. This is that next family — market leasing profiles are the second of four planned (growth curves done, this one, then expense/category, then acquisition/disposition/debt).

## 3. Existing infrastructure reused

- The model's own `PUT /models/:id/market-leasing/:code` (unchanged) is what actually writes a profile — applying a template only calls it with seeded values, exactly like growth curves.
- `requireCapability`/organization-scoping pattern, identical to every other organization-owned resource in this codebase.
- The `escalationSchema`/`recoveryConfigSchema`/`rentBasisEnum` validation already defined in `@cre/domain-models` for the model-level profile schema — reused as-is for the template body, not reimplemented.
- Refactored, not duplicated: `GrowthCurveLibraryCard` became a generic `TemplateLibraryCard` (Organization admin UI) and `Collection` gained generic `librarySegment`/`templateToDraft` props (AssumptionsTab.tsx) instead of copy-pasting another ~150-line component and another growth-curve-shaped branch. Both template families — and every one still to come — now share one implementation.

## 4. What remains deliberately unbuilt

- Expense/category templates and acquisition/disposition/debt templates — next slices, same pattern.
- No validation that a template's `marketRentGrowthCurve` code actually exists anywhere — same as the model-level profile itself, which is validated nowhere at the database layer either; a dangling reference is caught by the engine's existing `GROWTH_CURVE_NOT_FOUND` diagnostic at calculate time, and a template doesn't invent a stricter rule than the row it's templating.

## 5. Exact tests run

- `tests/market-leasing-profile-templates.test.ts` — 11 tests: upsert-by-code create/edit, field defaults, organization scoping both directions, unauthenticated refusal, and a provenance block (applying a template records `source_template_code`/`source_template_name`, a hand-typed profile records neither, a later edit that omits the fields preserves them, deleting the library template afterward leaves the model's copy untouched).
- Load-bearing check: reverted just `upsertMarketLeasingProfile`'s provenance columns with the tests in place — the 3 provenance-dependent tests failed exactly as predicted (`expected null to be 'office-standard'`); restored, all 11 pass.
- `e2e/assumptions.spec.ts` — new test drives the real flow: create a template in the org admin screen → open a model → start a new market leasing profile from it → confirm the seeded draft (forced into the raw JSON view — see finding below) carries the values and `sourceTemplateName` → save → confirm the grid row reads `Library: <name>`.
- `e2e/organization-admin.spec.ts` — extended for the new card's visibility (owner's `model:write` sees it, reviewer doesn't); the existing growth-curve test was rescoped to its own card once a second library card existed on the same page.
- Regression coverage on the refactor itself: `e2e/assumption-grid.spec.ts` (22 tests, incl. "every collection that can be a grid is one") and `e2e/accessibility.spec.ts`'s assumptions-tab sweep, both re-run clean against the generalized `Collection`/`Organization.tsx`.
- Full gate: `pnpm -w typecheck`, `pnpm -w lint`, `pnpm -w format:check`, `pnpm check:docs` (1261→1272 tests, 200→201 browser, migrations 21→22), `pnpm check:migrations`, full `vitest run` (1272/1272).

**A real gap caught in review of my own diff, before it shipped:** market leasing has a structured `RecordEditor` (growth curves doesn't), which initializes from `editingRecord`, not `draft`. A naive port of `beginFromTemplate` would have silently opened the structured form blank on "Start from library," discarding everything the template seeded. Separately, `RecordEditor.submit` only forwards fields its own spec knows about — so even with `editingRecord` fixed, saving through the structured form would have silently dropped `sourceTemplateCode`/`sourceTemplateName`. Both are fixed: the raw JSON view opens explicitly (with `editingRecord` filled too, so switching to the structured form doesn't open blank), and provenance injection moved into the shared `save` mutation itself so it survives regardless of which form the analyst actually submits from.

## 6. Zero-cost impact

None. No new dependency, no infrastructure, no external service.

## 7. `ENGINE_VERSION`

No change. Nothing in `calculate()`'s own code path is touched — `source_template_code`/`source_template_name` are descriptive columns the engine never reads.

## 8. Commercial-gap documentation

`docs/commercial-gap-analysis.md` item 13 updated: two of four planned template families now reusable and traceable, with the shared pattern (organization-scoped code-addressable table, `TemplateLibraryCard`, copy-not-reference apply with provenance snapshot) named explicitly as what the remaining two extend rather than reinvent.

author: zgrether
body:
One measured performance problem plus four bounded items. **Do not merge** — opened for review as the spec asked. Five commits, one per item.

## Item 1 — the region hypothesis is dead, and so is the depth hypothesis

Prod Supabase is `us-west-2` (Oregon), confirmed. But the depth story doesn't survive your three measurements either.

| call | depth (#935) | measured |
|---|---|---|
| `games.bracketDraw` | 1 | 459ms |
| `games.pickWinner` | 4 | 806ms |
| `competitions.faceBootstrap` | 3 | 997ms |

Solving the first two: `base + 1L = 459`, `base + 4L = 806` → **L ≈ 116ms per level, base ≈ 343ms per request.** So "~200ms each across four levels" is **refuted** — there's a large fixed per-request cost and a smaller per-level one.

**The decisive number is `bracketDraw`: depth 1, and still 459ms.** That's the floor. Taking `pickWinner` from depth 4 to depth 2 buys ~230ms of 806ms and cannot get below ~460ms. Depth is real and it is not the story — which is why the depth reduction is **not** in this PR.

**The score-entry control, answered from the code.** `scores.upsertEntry` is `trip_members` → `games` → upsert: **depth 3**, one level below the pick's 4. If depth explained the felt difference, a score entry would be ~690ms, not 150ms. My prediction, stated so your control run can refute it: **a score entry will measure in the same 500–700ms band and still feel instant**, because #15's outbox writes the cell before the mutation settles. The pick had no such thing, so its round trip was fully exposed. The difference was never speed; it was whether anything was on screen while you waited.

**Why `faceBootstrap` is 997ms.** It runs `competitions`, then five parallel branches. A pick can only have changed the `leaderboard` branch — `teams`, `assignments`, `games` and `myDelegateGameIds` are all invariant under a winner write. But they're parallel, so they cost requests and payload rather than depth, and #10 requires `faceBootstrap` over `leaderboard`-alone anyway. Behind the coalescer and behind an optimistic mark, it leaves the felt path entirely.

**What shipped: the optimistic pick.** CLAUDE.md #1's shape — `setData` in the handler, invalidate to re-pull server truth as the rollback, no `onMutate`. `applyPick` writes the one column the server writes and everything downstream stays derived by `resolveDraw`, so an optimistic pick and a fetched one travel one code path. Both invariants hold for free and are pinned against `applyPick` directly: **#924** (a stale optimistic winner is dropped by `winnerOf`) and **#925** (clearing writes one column, the final's pick survives, re-picking the same entrant brings it back).

Two details that aren't incidental:
- `pendingPicks` — only the last in-flight pick reconciles. Otherwise tapping two matches quickly is a visible flicker: the first pick's refetch is already on the wire when the second is applied, and it lands carrying state that predates it.
- `cancelRefetch: false` — a second invalidation during an in-flight refetch otherwise cancels it and the first response never reaches the cache (verified mechanism, `invalidateCancelsRefetch.test.ts`).

**Still needed from you** (I can't log into bbmi.app): tap→mark and tap→settled, before and after, with a score entry on the same device and session as the control.

## Item 2 — rounds 2+ centre on their feeding pair

The old layout used `justify-around`, which is *mathematically* the same answer when every column and card is the same height. Two things broke the coincidence:

1. The round **heading** was a flex child of the distributing column, so it was spaced along with the matches — round 1 distributed 5 items, round 2 distributed 3.
2. Card heights weren't equal. A bye row, a pending row and a competitor row render different content, so a column with byes was shorter and everything below drifted.

Offsets now live in `bracketLayout.ts` as pure functions, and `cardHeight` is asserted to equal the sum of the parts the markup renders — grow a row without updating it and a test fails rather than the bracket quietly drifting. Verified as a **relationship**, not fixed numbers: at every size 4→16, each match's centre equals the midpoint of its two feeders', and the final is centred on the first round's extent. Plus a render test that the offsets reach the DOM — the old numbers were never wrong, they just weren't being used.

## Item 3 — the field count, cause named

**The Field's 6 was correct; the data was wrong.** Manhattans had 8 assignments, 6 of whom were still trip members.

| team | assigned | still a member | orphaned |
|---|---|---|---|
| Centurions | 8 | 8 | 0 |
| Manhattans | 8 | 6 | **2** |

**Scope: 4 orphans in all of production**, across both Playground trips — and they're **four distinct ghost users** (each trip has its own placeholder named Brad and Rob), not two people twice.

**The writer set is three, and two leaked:**

| writer | deletes `trip_members` | cleared assignments | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tripMembers.remove` | yes | no, and never called the orphan-guest cleanup either | **leaked** |
| `ghostCrew.remove` | yes | only via `delete_orphan_guest_user` | **leaked when the guest survives** |
| `merge_guest_to_real_user` | yes | yes, collision included | safe |

**Why this is NOT a trigger, which is the part worth reading.** A `DELETE ON trip_members` trigger would cover every writer at once — the better instinct in general, and wrong here. The merge deletes a membership row as PK-collision resolution at offset **~422** of its body and repoints `team_assignments` at **~4646**. A trigger would fire mid-merge and destroy the guest's assignments thousands of characters before the merge hands them to the real account — silently dropping a new user's cup team at signup. **The one writer that is currently correct is the one the structural fix would have broken.**

So: a shared helper in the two app paths, the merge left alone, and a **source guard** (CLAUDE.md #21's idiom) so a future third app-side writer fails a test — a behavioural test cannot fail for code nobody has written yet. Migration 120 clears the 4 orphans keyed on the *condition*, so it's a no-op on a fresh DB and replays from zero.

Also worth knowing: `team_assignments_user_id_fkey` is ON DELETE CASCADE, so an assignment only strands while the *user* survives — and `delete_orphan_guest_user` swallows `foreign_key_violation`, so any guest with RESTRICT-referenced history survives and keeps theirs. Every production orphan was exactly that kind.

## Item 4 — why the consolation toggle was lost

**Never dropped, never connected.** The whole chain existed — `consolation` in `BracketConfig`, validated, passed to `buildDraw`, rendered by `BracketBoard`, handled by `bracketPlacements`, defaulted to false. Nothing anywhere set it to true, so it had been permanently false since #927 built the surface around it. A handoff gap, not a regression: the plumbing shipped without its tap.

**One instruction deliberately not followed.** The spec asked for the 3rd/4th distribution rows to be "structurally absent" when the toggle is off. The engine says otherwise: `placementPoints` averages a tie group across the places it **spans**, and its own worked example is `[9,6,4,2]` with two tied at 3rd getting `(4+2)/2 = 3` each. So with the toggle off, the two semi losers tie at 3rd spanning places 3–4 and **both values are already consumed**. Hiding those rows would zero the 4th and quietly change what every existing non-consolation bracket pays — contradicting the spec's own (correct) observation that the current split is the averaging doing exactly what it should. The rows stay; what the toggle changes is what the bracket can **tell apart**, not what it pays. Pinned by a test asserting the averaging directly, so the next reader finds the reason rather than the instruction.

## Item 5 — one formula, every round

Your open question, answered: a first-round match **does** award something, and "1st: 7, 2nd: 4"

author: p-linnane
body:
`brew generate-advisories-api` builds the concatenated `BREW-*` advisory index for formulae.brew.sh from a checkout of Homebrew/advisory-database, mirroring that repository's `AdvisoryIndex` (kept in step): matched records without a comparable range are skipped, output is grouped by formula and deterministic, and mixed schema versions fail the build.

This is the first half of serving the index from formulae.brew.sh/api instead of a raw git URL: the site's CI gains a generate-advisories job running this command, after which `brew vulns` flips its `DATA_URL` and Homebrew/advisory-database stops committing the 67 MB generated file. Output was verified byte-identical to the existing `rake advisories:concat` over the full 20,918-record corpus.

author: fishygeek91
body:
## Summary

Closes #44.

Adds `TraceBuffer.applyCount` (lifetime live-cursor `applyOne` count) so the frozen-lane `syncLanes` regression can assert a **second seek past freeze is a true no-op** (zero applies), not only that final `eventIndex` / `work` match. The old #14 bug produced the same final state after overshoot+rewind, so the previous test would not catch a reintroduction.

Does not change photo-finish freeze semantics or `syncLanes` clamp behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

Issue #44 has no checkboxes. Implied AC from the issue body:

- [x] **Spy `applyOne` / seek apply count (or equivalent) on a frozen lane** — public `TraceBuffer.applyCount` getter; incremented only in private `applyOne` after a successful `applyOneTo`. `appendChunk` index-state pass is not counted. Tests use `race.laneBuffer(lane).applyCount` (no `vi.spyOn`).
- [x] **Two `syncLanes` past freeze** — existing test still does `seek(5)` then `seek(8)` after `setFinishVertex(1)`.
- [x] **Second sync is a no-op (zero applies)** — after `seek(8)`, frozen-lane `applyCount` is unchanged. Running lane `applyCount` increases (control so a stuck-at-zero counter cannot pass).
- [x] **Not merely `eventIndex` matches** — original `eventIndex` / `work` / `lanePhotoFrozen` asserts kept; apply-count asserts added.
- [x] **Do not reopen #14 / do not change freeze semantics** — `syncLanes` untouched.

## Deviations

- First seek past freeze may apply more than `eventIndex`: live `settleWork[finish]` is unset until the first crossing (`appendChunk` indexes `indexState` only), so `syncLanes` may overshoot then recap. That first-crossing recap is intended. The test asserts `applyCount` delta `>= eventIndex` on the first seek, and **zero additional applies** on the second.
- Roadmap #29: tick issue #44 when this merges (reviewer confirms on merge).

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck`
- [x] `npx vitest run` — 910 tests, 84 files
- [x] `npm run lint` (ESLint + Prettier `--check` clean)

author: mikalstill
body:
Closes out phase 5 of the distro matrix CI, which is the final phase of
that programme. Documentation only — no code changes.

## What changed outside this diff

`Can merge` was added to the "Develop branch" ruleset's required status
checks (ruleset `20783686`) before this commit was written. The live
ruleset was diffed against a pre-change snapshot: exactly one field
moved, and the `sf-can-skip-merge-queue` bypass survived intact.

That is the step which turns the seven-distro matrix from something
that *runs* in the merge queue into something that can *stop* a merge.
This PR is therefore the first one to face a genuinely gating
`Can merge`, which makes it a self-test of the thing it documents.

## Why the two-step order mattered

`Can merge` only reports on `merge_group` events, so requiring it before
a merge group had ever run would have blocked every merge on a branch
with no protection to fall back to. Hence `Can enqueue` alone on
2026-08-12, and `Can merge` added on 2026-08-15.

The gap that left was not theoretical, and the docs now say so rather
than describing it as a pending step. `Can enqueue` is gated
`!= 'merge_group'`, so inside a merge group it skips — and a skipped job
reports success, satisfying the sole required check. Both #493 and #496
merged exactly thirty one seconds after that skip, with the matrix still
running.

## The regression the queue caught

#493 was picked as a deliberately trivial verification merge (a
pre-commit pin bump). The matrix it triggered found that Renovate's #488
had reverted phase 1's `debian:bullseye` base to `trixie`, raising the
shipped binary's glibc floor from 2.30 to 2.39 and silently dropping
Rocky 9, Ubuntu 22.04 and Debian 12. Rocky 9 said so in as many words:

```
nothing provides libc.so.6(GLIBC_2.39)(64bit) needed by instar-0.3.0-1.x86_64
```

No pull-request job could have caught it — they all run on one modern
distro where a 2.39 floor is invisible. Fixed in #496, whose queue run
went 7/7 green. That red arrived seventeen minutes after #493 was
already on `develop`, which is the argument for this PR.

## Also here

- Replaces the `Can merge` recipe in `docs/development.md`. The old one
  PUT the `GET` response back unchanged, which carries fields outside
  the update schema (`id`, `_links`, `"parameters": null` on rules that
  take none). The replacement was verified to produce the exact payload
  applied to the live ruleset, and warns that omitting `bypass_actors`
  silently drops the bypass team.
- Marks the master plan and the `docs/plans/index.md` row Complete, and
  corrects three disagreeing status claims across the two files.
- Closes 5b and 5e by observation rather than inspection: the testdata
  token demonstrably reaches `merge_group` (all seven containers fetched
  testdata and ran the full stestr suite), and the nightly config export
  proposed the ruleset unprompted in #495.
- Records measured wall clock: the fan-out is ~76 minutes, consistently
  across both runs. The surrounding build ranged 24–116 minutes with
  cache state and dominates the end-to-end number.

## Left open on purpose

The flakiness-cascade risk. Fourteen matrix entries across two runs is a
thin sample for a gate that now blocks *all* merges when one distro goes
flaky, and the master plan's mitigation — temporary `continue-on-error`
on an entry that fails twice consecutively, rather than holding the
queue — is now the operative one.

## Test plan

- `pre-commit run --all-files` clean.
- Live ruleset read back and diffed field-by-field against the
  pre-change snapshot; only `required_status_checks` differs.
- No code changes, so the matrix run on this PR is exercising the gate
  rather than the diff.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

The shadow-constructor flip evaluation, finally run. All five correctness gates
it was waiting on closed on 2026-08-04 (#4579/#4581/#4582/#4604 merged, #4580 a
documented negative result), so this PR is the decision measurement.

**Verdict: `enable_shadow_construction` stays `False`, and `KCT_BOARD06_SHADOW`
stays `"0"`.** Shadow-ON buys +5 coupled pairs and loses the board — it fails
its own CI gate on four separate assertions and costs 2.16x the wall-clock
against a job already running a median 24.5 min of a 30-minute ceiling.

This is outcome (b) from the issue's acceptance criteria: a documented negative
result (the #4580 pattern). Comments, docs and one test docstring only — **no
behaviour, defaults or artifacts change.**

## Method

Two repeats per arm on `main @ fa18a25b` (i.e. **after** #4791 and its #4840
per-net-class width fix), in a fresh worktree with `uv run kct build-native`
run first (`C++ backend: available (version 1.0.0)`, build version 19):

```bash
# arm A (default)
PYTHONHASHSEED=42 KCT_SHADOW_DEBUG=1 uv run python \
  boards/06-diffpair-test/generate_design.py --step route --seed 42
# arm B
KCT_BOARD06_SHADOW=1 PYTHONHASHSEED=42 KCT_SHADOW_DEBUG=1 uv run python \
  boards/06-diffpair-test/generate_design.py --step route --seed 42
# board quality, both arms, via the CI gate itself:
uv run python scripts/ci/check_diffpair_coverage.py boards/06-diffpair-test \
  --skip-route --seed 42
# independent cross-check (project convention):
kicad-cli pcb drc --refill-zones --format json -o <out>.json <artifact>.kicad_pcb
```

Runs were **serial** (never concurrent) so the wall-clock column is comparable.

## Determinism / provenance of each number

Per the issue's determinism AC, here is which surface each figure came from:

| Figure | Source | Determinism |
|---|---|---|
| `coupled-ok` by name, per-pair class | `[coupled-pair-report]` lines, shadow phase | deterministic; identical across repeats |
| decline count (46), `[coupled-tail]` (33), `[coupled-channel]` (10) | `KCT_SHADOW_DEBUG=1` counters | deterministic; identical across repeats |
| DRC error count, per-rule split, reach, pour connectivity | full-regen artifact via `check_diffpair_coverage.py --skip-route` | **paired mode-for-mode** — see below |
| `kicad-cli` errors / clearance / unconnected | full-regen artifact via `kicad-cli pcb drc --refill-zones` | same artifacts as the row above |
| wall-clock | `/usr/bin/time -p` on `--step route` | timing, 2 samples per arm |
| CI job wall-clock | 10 consecutive **green** `main` runs, GitHub API | observational |

**Mode pairing.** Both shadow-ON repeats landed in the documented **Mode B**
(35 DRC / 19 `diffpair_clearance_intra` / 18-of-21 reach) — all three mode
signals mutually consistent, so this is not a Mode-A-vs-Mode-B mix-up. Stronger
than that: within each arm the two artifacts are **byte-identical modulo
`(uuid …)`** — 424 uuid lines differ, **zero** geometry lines
(`diff | grep -c uuid` = 424 of 424 changed pairs, both arms). So the compared
rows are single-mode, not a lucky draw. Shadow-OFF landed on the documented
committed/CI floor (18 DRC = 9 skew + 9 continuity, 21/21) both times.

## Results

| | shadow OFF (default) | shadow ON (`KCT_BOARD06_SHADOW=1`) |
|---|---|---|
| `coupled-ok` | **0/9** | **5/9** |
| `[coupled-follow] declined` | n/a (no shadow phase) | **46** |
| `[coupled-tail]` lines | n/a | 33 |
| signal reach | **21/21** | **18/21** (MIPI_D0+, MIPI_D0-, USB_CC1) |
| `kct check` DRC errors | **18** (allowlist 18) | **35** (allowlist 18) |
| diff-pair violations | 18 (baseline 18) | **31** (baseline 18) |
| — `diffpair_clearance_intra` | 0 | 19 |
| — `diffpair_length_skew` | 9 | 6 |
| — `diffpair_routing_continuity` | 9 | 6 |
| pour connectivity (copper-union) | **PASS** | **FAIL** — +3V3 in 3 disjoint groups (largest 9/11), GND in 5 (largest 118/122) |
| `kicad-cli` errors | 444 / 444 | 639 / 646 |
| — of which `clearance` | 11 / 11 | 169 / 176 |
| `kicad-cli` unconnected items | **0 / 0** | **9 / 9** |
| `--step route` wall-clock | 745.2 s / 739.9 s | 1649.8 s / 1570.6 s |
| negotiated phase | 491.6 s / 485.3 s | 789.6 s + 59.2 s planning + 187.4 s re-run |
| **CI gate exit code** | **0** | **2** |

**Coupled-ok by name** (identical on both ON repeats — the AC's "by name, not
count" requirement; a count match can hide one pair gained and another lost):

| pair | shadow OFF | shadow ON |
|---|---|---|
| MIPI_CLK | joint-A\*-plateau | **coupled-ok** |
| MIPI_D0 | joint-A\*-plateau | guide-missing |
| PCIE_RX | joint-A\*-plateau | **coupled-ok** |
| PCIE_TX | joint-A\*-plateau | shadow-declined-blockage |
| USB2_D | joint-A\*-plateau | **coupled-ok** |
| USB3_RX1 | joint-A\*-plateau | shadow-declined-blockage |
| USB3_RX2 | joint-A\*-plateau | shadow-declined-blockage |
| USB3_TX1 | joint-A\*-plateau | **coupled-ok** |
| USB3_TX2 | joint-A\*-plateau | **coupled-ok** |

**The vacuity trap is live in this data and does not rescue shadow-ON.**
`diffpair_length_skew` *drops* 9 → 6 and `diffpair_routing_continuity` 9 → 6
under shadow-ON, which reads as an improvement until you notice
`diffpair_clearance_intra` goes 0 → 19 and reach drops. Read `coupled-ok` and
reach alongside the counts, as the board README instructs.

## Re-verifying the two named blockers

**Blocker 1 — USB_CC1 corridor contention: RE-VERIFIED, and worse.** The
corridor-yield planner states it itself, on both repeats:

```
[corridor-yield] 3 net(s) left unconnected by the main strategy: USB_CC1, MIPI_D0+, MIPI_D0-
  [corridor-yield] USB_CC1 stays unroutable with every coupled corridor lifted -- not a corridor-competition failure
  [corridor-yield] MIPI_D0+ is sealed in by MIPI_CLK
[corridor-yield] planning took 59.2s; 1 pair(s) to yield
[corridor-yield] 1 pair(s) yielded their corridor: MIPI_CLK; re-running the main strategy for the freed nets
[corridor-yield] reach 18 -> 18 of 21 net(s); yield reverted
```

Note the last line: the #4463 recovery that used to buy back MIPI_D0 **now
reverts**. Shadow-ON lands at **18/21**, not the 19/21 recorded on 2026-08-02 —
a regression against the previous measurement, and 3 nets short of the board's
`REQUIRED_SIGNAL_REACH`. It still pays 59 s of planning and a 187 s re-run for
that null result.

**Blocker 2 — wall-clock: RE-VERIFIED, and the CI margin has SHRUNK.**
Shadow-ON costs **2.16x** shadow-OFF locally (1610.2 s vs 742.6 s, means of two
repeats). The comment's quoted "14m22s–20m42s" green-run band is now stale —
ten consecutive green `ci.yml` runs on `main` (2026-08-14) measure the
`diffpair-routing-regression` job at:

```
24.65, 24.82, 17.92, 24.70, 24.38, 25.20, 24.40, 24.05, 24.60, 22.20  (min)
min 17.9 | median 24.5 | max 25.2   vs   timeout-minutes: 30
```

Step-level, the single `Re-route board + check diff-pair coverage` step is
**23m30s** of that (setup is only ~65 s). That is **~5.5 min of margin at
shadow-OFF**. Applying the measured 2.16x to that step puts shadow-ON near
**51 min — roughly 21 min past the ceiling.** Raising `timeout-minutes` is
explicitly *not* the fix the issue asks for, and would in any case only buy time
to ship a board that fails the gate; `ci.yml` is untouched by this PR.

**Blocker 3 — pour connectivity (NEW, not on the 2026-08-02 list).** The
stranded nets break the copper-union audit (`REQUIRE_POUR_CONNECTIVITY`,
#3509): +3V3 splits into 3 disjoint pad groups, GND into 5. This fails the CI
gate independently of DRC count and reach, and matches the `kicad-cli`
cross-check finding 9 unconnected items where shadow-OFF has 0.

**Net effect on the gate:** shadow-OFF exits **0**; shadow-ON exits **2** on
four separate assertions (reach, pour connectivity, diff-pair violation
baseline, total DRC allowlist). The trade is not close and it is not a tuning
question.

## Changes

- `src/kicad_tools/router/diffpair.py` — replaced the stale 2026-08-02
  WALL-CLOCK/blocker block above `enable_shadow_construction` with the dated
  #4800 A/B table, the by-name coupled s

author: n24q02m
body:
### 💡 What
Added a specific, disabled state handling for `syncloop.StateNeedsResync` in the system tray menu. The "Sync now" button is now disabled during this state with the tooltip: "Sync broken: run 'better-drive sync --resync' to fix".

### 🎯 Why
Previously, if a user was in the `StateNeedsResync` error state, they might not know how to resolve it just by looking at the tray UI. By explicitly disabling the sync action and providing the exact CLI command in the tooltip, we make the error state actionable and significantly reduce user frustration.

### 📸 Before/After
**Before:** The "Sync now" button might either have an unhelpful generic tooltip or fail silently when in a broken sync state, giving the user no guidance.
**After:** The "Sync now" button correctly disables itself during `StateNeedsResync` and its tooltip provides the exact command needed to fix the issue: `better-drive sync --resync`.

### ♿ Accessibility
This improves the usability of error states by ensuring users have contextual, actionable feedback rather than hitting a dead end in the UI.

body: ## Jira Ticket [OSDEV-3233](https://opensupplyhub.atlassian.net/browse/OSDEV-3233) --- ## Summary of Changes Updates the data-center extended fields to match the current Master Dataset Schema, adds the two grouping fields, and deprecates the fields the schema dropped. **Backend — `api/models/extended_field.py`:** - Added 12 schema fields: `wue_units`, `onsite_power_generation` (utility usage); `non_data_area(_units)`, `number_of_floors`, `footprint(_units)`, `building_area(_units)`, `land_area(_units)`, `number_of_buildings` (building info). - Added 2 grouping fields: `is_group` (yes/no) and `data_center_group_id` (string). - Removed `overall_area` / `overall_area_units`, which the updated schema replaces with `building_area` / `land_area` / `footprint`. - Updated both `DATA_CENTER_FIELDS` (which drives `FIELD_CHOICES` and `RAW_DATA_FIELDS`) and `DATA_CENTER_NUMERICAL_FIELDS`, so the new measures are handled as numbers in `create_extendedfield`. - No ingestion changes needed: the fields ride the generic extended-field pipeline for list upload, legacy API and v1/SLC. **Migration:** reused the existing unmerged `0224_facilitylistitem_ai_usage_notes_and_more.py`, updating the `choices` in both `AlterField` operations (`extendedfield` and `historicalextendedfield`). Choices metadata only — no DB column change. **Frontend:** - `ProductionLocation/constants.jsx`: added the new fields to their groups (measures paired with their `unitsField` so value and units render together), removed `overall_area`, and added a new **Grouping** group. - `data_center_group_id` renders as a **link to the group's profile** (`/production-locations/`), resolved against the current origin — so "this data center's group is at .../production-locations/A2" is one click away. Implemented as a `renderValue` in the field config (JSX stays in the `.jsx` constants file) and applied in the data-point builder; `DataPoint.value` already accepts a node. - `Contribute/DataCenterFields/`: helper descriptions for every new field, and **`is_group` renders as a checkbox** rather than a text input, since it is a yes/no question. **Note on the checkbox value:** it is stored as the string `'true'` (checked) or `''` (unchecked), not a boolean. `parseContribData` filters the payload with lodash `isEmpty`, which treats both `true` and `false` as empty — a real boolean would be silently dropped and never reach the API. Leaving it blank when unchecked also matches the schema, where the field may be true, false or blank. --- ## Type of Change - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [x] Backend change (API, database, business logic) - [x] UI / frontend change - [ ] Architectural change (affects structure, contracts, or shared modules) - [ ] Refactor (no functional change) - [ ] Breaking change (existing functionality may not work as before) - [ ] Documentation / tooling only --- ## Testing `__tests__/utils/ProductionLocationDetailsGeneralFieldsUtils.test.js`: - `data_center_group_id` renders as a `Link` with `to === '/production-locations/'` and the id as its text. `__tests__/components/DataCenterFields.test.jsx`: - `is_group` renders as a checkbox, unchecked by default; checking it sets `'true'`; unchecking clears it to `''`. `__tests__/utils/slcValidationSchema.test.js`: - `isGroup` accepts empty, `'true'` and `'false'`; rejects anything else. Manual end-to-end: submitted an SLC contribution with a group id, approved the moderation event, and confirmed the value appears on the production-location page as a link (note the index refresh is not immediate — the value shows once the facility is reindexed). --- ## Known TODO Items - `data_center_group_id` is a **staging mechanism**: it records group membership as contributed data until the grouping model exists. A follow-up script will read these ids to create the groups and wire up the relationships; the grouping model tickets (OSDEV-3083 – OSDEV-3087) remain the end state. - Because these are extended fields, the group values are contributor-asserted and multi-valued — nothing enforces "one facility belongs to one group", and the group id is not validated against an existing OS ID (a typo links to a non-existent profile). The migration script will need a conflict-resolution rule. - Existing `ExtendedField` rows stored under `overall_area` / `overall_area_units` are not deleted by this change; they simply stop rendering. Clean-up with a data migration only if any were created during testing. - Unchecked `is_group` means "blank / not stated" rather than an explicit `false`. If product wants an explicit answer, a Yes/No radio would express `false` directly. - The schema doc still lists `number_of _servers` with a stray space; the codebase uses `number_of_servers`. Worth correcting so collectors' column headers match. - Screenshots to be attached after a local run. --- ## Checklist ### Implementation - [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines and naming conventions. - [x] I have removed debug logs, commented-out code, and unused imports. - [x] Any AI-assisted code (e.g., Claude) has been reviewed, understood, and adapted to fit our codebase. - [x] I have considered backward compatibility and migrations where applicable. ### Testing & Validation - [x] I have manually tested the change in a local/dev environment. - [x] I have added or updated unit tests for the new/changed behavior. - [ ] All existing tests pass locally. - [ ] For UI changes: I have included screenshots or a recording, and verified responsive/cross-browser behavior. - [x] For backend changes: I have validated API contracts, error handling, and edge cases. - [ ] For architectural changes: I have documented the design decision and notified affected teams. ### Documentation & Communication - [x] I have updated relevant documentation (README, ADRs, inline comments, API docs). - [ ] I have updated the Jira ticket status and added any relevant notes. ### Final Review - [x] I have performed a self-review on my PR and I am presenting my best work for my peers to review. author: qnox
body:
## Problem

Candidate construction repeatedly decoded inline-body plans: method-bytecode reads, disassembly, and invoke-site analysis for the same declaration. Scratch classpaths also forced fresh `Classpath` instances and discarded warm package/class caches.

## Fix

- Cache decoded plans in a per-instance LRU.
- Share plans process-wide only for the exact complete archive/jimage classpath composition. A plan is composition-dependent because a multifile facade lookup can read a shadowable part from another entry; it is not an owner-entry-local fact.
- Compositions containing mutable directory entries remain instance-local.
- Any active stub overlay disables plan caching because an overlay can replace a facade part even when it does not replace the facade owner.
- Keep the full plan key: owner, source name, body descriptor, physical parameter slots, and default-bridge descriptor.
- Never memoize a transient body/bridge read failure; a successfully decoded negative remains cacheable.
- Route javac output and generated Java signature stubs through a scoped in-memory overlay so the common harness classpath remains reusable. Kotlin dependency-module directories remain real classpath entries because their package/facade catalog is semantically required.

## Validation

- Added `inline_plan_cache_is_scoped_to_the_complete_archive_classpath`, proving identical immutable compositions share, different part-bearing compositions do not, and directory compositions have no global cache.
- Existing overlay regression remains green; caching is now disabled for every active overlay, including independently overlaid multifile parts.
- Focused post-rebase unit tests pass.
- Full CI is the merge gate.

author: aipropsoftware
body:
## What

Drop an address in the map search and, alongside the zoning X-ray, Pencil now shows **"What's selling nearby"** — recorded sales within ~¾ mile: address, closed price, sale date, building sf, $/sf, distance, a neighborhood median $/sf (when ≥4 sales carry building size), and green "Sold" pins on the map.

## Every price is real

Each record is a deed transfer read live from a government source — no estimates, no invented listings. Where no county publishes machine-readable sales, the panel says exactly that instead of guessing.

Probe-verified sources (runner-verified live queries, 2026-08-14):

| Coverage | Source | Query shape |
|---|---|---|
| New York City | NYC Dept. of Finance rolling sales (Socrata) | bbox `$where`, residential tax classes 1–2 |
| Nashville / Davidson Co. | Metro Assessor parcels (MapServer) | envelope |
| Philadelphia | OPA property records (Carto) | PostGIS radius |
| **All of Florida** (incl. Miami) | FL DOR statewide parcel roll | point+distance (envelope 400s on this layer); dates shown at the year+month precision the state publishes |

## Hardening

- Server-side `where`/`orderBy` degrade gracefully; the client re-filters ($40k floor drops quitclaims) and re-sorts newest-first regardless
- Data canary now watches all four sources using the app's exact query shapes at points verified to have sales
- `sales_near` usage event tracked; sale pins clear when the X-ray closes
- probe scripts (`scripts/sales-probe.ts` + workflow) kept for the next coverage round

author: metaneutrons
body:
## Summary

- make device deletion atomic and enforce database-owned cascade/set-null behavior
- add normalized content dependency tracking, append-only audit enforcement, FK indexes, and singleton default constraints
- serialize and checksum migrations so multi-replica startup is deterministic and fails closed
- introduce explicit read, write, and transaction boundaries with safe retry semantics across server database access
- harden audited admin mutations, authentication, telemetry, rollout, settings, assets, and dashboard reads

## Root cause

Device deletion performed several independent statements and omitted OTA event rows. A foreign-key violation therefore stopped the delete after earlier cleanup statements had already committed. More broadly, referential actions and retry semantics were split between application code and the database, allowing partial mutations and ambiguous write retries.

## Impact

Existing installations receive forward-only migrations at startup. Device-owned history is removed atomically, assignments are safely detached, referenced providers/assets cannot be deleted, audit rows are append-only, and database failures are surfaced instead of producing partial or misleading state.

## Validation

- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm db:check`
- `pnpm i18n:check`
- `pnpm test` (256 tests)
- `pnpm lint` (0 errors; 10 existing warnings)
- production build and Docker image build
- PostgreSQL 18 fresh install, cloned production upgrade, concurrent migration, checksum-tamper, cascade/set-null/restrict, and append-only audit tests

body:
## What changed

- Added an immutable SQLite composition store binding one qualified reasoning artifact to the exact run, task, and approved-task digest.
- Rejected unresolved questions, reserved-field collisions, missing bindings, task drift, conflicting rebinding, and stored-data integrity failures.
- Added an optional scheduler payload resolver so preview and execution consume the same deterministic enriched payload.
- Kept tool selection, effect matching, policy, approval, typed execution, and evidence outside model control.
- Documented the Phase 4B boundary and current non-goals.

## Why

Phase 4A could produce a strictly validated proposal but intentionally could not feed it into runtime execution. This slice adds the durable, fail-closed composition boundary required to carry qualified content into governed tools without granting the model dispatch authority.

body:
## Alcance

- Frontera de comunicaciones futuras: `DOCUMENTED_ONLY`; fuente canónica: ADR-0017.
- Separa conceptualmente destinatarios paciente y profesional. El modelo actual no contiene `recipientKind`, por lo que no autoriza entrega.
- Toda capacidad futura exige autorización explícita por canal y finalidad, revalidada de forma fail-closed antes de cualquier intento.
- Taxonomía conservadora: `CHANNEL_UNAVAILABLE`, `DELIVERY_NOT_CONFIRMED` y `NO_RESPONSE`.
- Está prohibido inferir recepción, comprensión, conducta, riesgo o estado clínico a partir de resultados técnicos.
- Implementación, proveedor, automatización, migraciones y dependencias añadidas: cero.

## Rutas y estadísticas

- `docs/adr/0017-future-communications-boundary.md`: +238 / -0
- `docs/architecture/gas2-ownership-boundaries.md`: +3 / -3
- `docs/decision-register.md`: +10 / -0
- `docs/audit/gas2-claims-register.md`: +1 / -0
- `docs/audit/gas2-evidence-index.md`: +35 / -1

## Validación

- PostgreSQL 16.14 aislado, base inicialmente vacía, 14 migraciones, seed exclusivamente sintético y estado de migraciones actualizado.
- `pnpm test`: 530/530 (401 unitarias, 103 integración, 26 tooling).
- E2E local: `NOT_EXECUTED` bajo la excepción documental; no se declara PASS. El CI remoto debe aprobar 74/74.
- Trazabilidad: 36 claims, referencias resueltas y drift Markdown/CSV 0.
- `pnpm format:check`, lint, typecheck, tooling, trazabilidad, checker de governance evidence, referencias locales, build y `git diff --check`: PASS.
- `pnpm audit --prod`: no cero esperado; advisories heredados 5 high y 2 moderate; atribuibles a P09: 0. No hay cambios de dependencias ni lockfile.

## Decisiones y gaps abiertos

- Permanecen pendientes DEC-003, DEC-005 y DEC-013–DEC-017: base jurídica, retención, proveedor/IAM, incidentes, continuidad, autorización de piloto y operación.
- GAP-DCB-023 (safety del motor futuro) y GAP-DCB-024 (validación clínica/human factors) permanecen abiertos y sin aceptación de riesgo residual.
- No se declara cumplimiento jurídico, clínico, MDR ni institucional.

`REAL DELIVERY / DATA / PILOT / PRODUCTION = NO_GO`
